title: Author and verify the dated shelf cards for Journey III (relativity)
description:
# Author and verify the dated shelf cards for Journey III (relativity)

**Epic:** `am-ep-discovery-33u` · **Batch:** batch-e · **Priority:** P1 · **Plan sections:** §5.1–5.4, §9.4, §3.9 (paper 3 margin), §22.1 (traceability only)

## Background

Journey III asks: how could you stop assuming that everyone shares the same time? Its shelf is the richest and the most dangerous for hindsight. By the end of 1904 Lorentz had the full transformation mathematics, and Poincaré had discussed the conventionality of simultaneity, described synchronization with light signals, and named the principle of relativity. The journey must show exactly what was on the table and what was different about taking both postulates physically, without ridiculing the ether program, which reproduces the formulas and is not declared refuted by the kinematics alone.

The relativity paper cites no one, so "the paper cites or asserts it" is almost always false here; the paper's own assertions (the magnet-and-conductor asymmetry, the unsuccessful attempts to detect motion relative to the light medium) are recorded as category-3 notes without implying citations. Einstein-knowledge evidence, when used, is cited separately: for example his later statements to R. S. Shankland that Fizeau's experiment and stellar aberration weighed more with him than Michelson–Morley.

Anachronism controls: Michelson–Morley is not the documented sole cause of the paper; spacetime diagrams are Minkowski's 1908 aid; the train-and-embankment picture is Einstein's 1917 illustration; contraction is not what a camera sees.

Three other surfaces read these cards rather than restating their numbers, so the cards' verification state has visible consequences: SR-09's Bradley comparison row (`am-sr-09-doppler-aberration-rabd`) shows "awaiting verification" and no number until `bradley-1729-aberration` is verified; the §§7–8 readings (`am-sre-readings-s7-s8-lpje`) quote the same card's figures; and the Michelson–Morley shelf instrument (`am-disc-shelf-michelson-fizeau-dauq`) shows the 1887 observational bound as a cited value from `michelson-1887-null-result`, never as a dataset and never as a computed output. The transcriptions those surfaces need live here, on the cards, and nowhere else.

## Scope

In scope: one verified HistoricalPremise record per card below, with the fields and rules of `am-disc-knowledge-cards-iw8j`; the dynamo-context note; category-3 notes; Einstein-knowledge evidence where cited; the primary-source verification queue, including the transcriptions SR-09, the §§7–8 readings, and the Michelson–Morley shelf instrument read; the list of later items kept off the shelf.

Out of scope (owned elsewhere): card rendering and rules (`am-disc-knowledge-cards-iw8j`); the chain (`am-disc-journey-iii-chain-hpr7`); shelf instruments and their computations (`am-disc-shelf-michelson-fizeau-dauq`); SR-09's aberration computation and its labels (`am-sr-09-doppler-aberration-rabd`); the Fizeau, Kaufmann, Bucherer, and Ives–Stilwell datasets (`am-data-fizeau-1851-tgl8`, `am-data-kaufmann-1902-1906-52ya`, `am-data-bucherer-1908-w3mf`, `am-data-ives-stilwell-1938-61lp`); paper 3 margin entries (`am-sr-margin-entries-tn4l`); the Bern page's clock-coordination argument (`am-disc-bern-bridge-6euz`); the human knowledge-boundary review (`am-disc-batch-h-exit-audit-r8xq`).

## Requirements

Store records under `content/historical-premises/` (journey-neutral card ids in lowercase kebab case, `<first-author>-<year>-<topic>`; this bead's cards may be grouped in `content/historical-premises/relativity/`). Each record carries the standard fields of `am-disc-knowledge-cards-iw8j`: `sources[]` as printed, `date` (`earliest`, `latest`, `latestYear`, `precision`), `proposition`, `limits`, `status`, `admittedStages[]`, `paperCitesOrAsserts` where verified, `einsteinKnowledgeEvidence` only with its own citation, and `verification` (`verifiedBy`, `verifierKind`, `date`, `method`, `evidenceLocator`, `printedCitation`, `discrepancies[]`, `reviewRecordId`).

| Card id | Date (`latestYear`) | Proposition | Limits to state | Status | Candidate citation (verify) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `galileo-1632-ship` | 1632 (1632) | The laws of mechanics look the same below decks whether the ship moves uniformly or not | Mechanics only | available | G. Galilei, *Dialogo* (1632), Second Day |
| `maxwell-1865-equations-ether-frame` | 1865, 1873 (1873) | Maxwell's equations, with light traveling at $c$ relative to the ether in the period's interpretation; they do not keep their form under $x' = x - vt$, $t' = t$ | The ether framing is interpretation; the change of form is demonstrated by the shelf instrument, not asserted | available | J. C. Maxwell, Phil. Trans. 155 (1865) 459; *Treatise* (1873) |
| `faraday-1832-induction` | 1831–1832 (1832) | Moving the magnet or moving the coil produces the same induced current for the same relative motion, while the theory of the period explains the two cases with two mechanisms | The same current to the precision of the observations; the two classical accounts agree to first order in $v/c$. The dynamo-patent remark is context, never evidence of Einstein's path. Category 3: the paper's introduction opens with this asymmetry (queue item Q4) | available | M. Faraday, Phil. Trans. 122 (1832) 125 |
| `bradley-1729-aberration` | 1729 (1729) | Stars show an annual aberration of about 20 arcseconds, explained by the finite speed of light combined with the Earth's orbital motion | Carries Bradley's printed figures, not a modern number: his ratio of the speed of light to the Earth's orbital speed (about 10,210 to 1) and his light time from the Sun (about 8 minutes 12 seconds), from which the implied angle of about $20.2''$ is computed by `aberration`, never stored on the card; the modern computation ($20.4956''$ at 29.789 km/s) belongs to SR-09 and is labeled there (queue item Q1) | available | J. Bradley, Phil. Trans. 35 (1727–1728, issued 1729) 637 |
| `fizeau-1851-drag` | 1851 (1851) | Light in moving water is dragged by about the fraction $1 - 1/n^2$ of the water's speed (Fresnel's coefficient) | Measured and explained within Fresnel's ether theory; not derived kinematically until later | available | H. Fizeau, C. R. 33 (1851) 349; extended account Ann. Chim. Phys. (3) 57 (1859) 385 |
| `michelson-1887-null-result` | 1881, 1887 (1887) | No ether wind is detected to second order in $v/c$ | A null result within the stated precision; the 1881 experiment's sensitivity was later questioned, and the 1887 experiment is the decisive one. Carries the 1887 paper's printed figures: the effective path, the wavelength count, the expected shift, and the reported upper bound (queue item Q2). Category 3: the paper's introduction refers in general terms to unsuccessful attempts to detect the Earth's motion relative to the light medium, without naming an experiment (queue item Q4) | available | A. A. Michelson, Am. J. Sci. (3) 22 (1881) 120; A. A. Michelson and E. W. Morley, Am. J. Sci. (3) 34 (1887) 333 |
| `fitzgerald-1889-contraction` | 1889, 1892 (1892) | Bodies moving through the ether contract along the motion by $\sqrt{1 - v^2/c^2}$, which would hide the wind | A dynamical hypothesis about bodies in the ether | available | G. F. FitzGerald, Science 13 (1889) 390; H. A. Lorentz, Versl. Kon. Akad. Wet. Amsterdam 1 (1892) 74 |
| `lorentz-1895-local-time` | 1895 (1895) | A fictitious "local time" $t' = t - vx/c^2$ makes the equations of moving systems correspond to those of systems at rest to first order in $v/c$ | First order; a calculational variable in Lorentz's framework | available | H. A. Lorentz, *Versuch einer Theorie der electrischen und optischen Erscheinungen in bewegten Körpern* (1895) |
| `poincare-1898-measure-of-time` | 1898 (1898) | The simultaneity of distant events is fixed by convention, chosen for convenience | How explicitly the 1898 essay describes light-signal synchronization is settled at the original, and the proposition follows the text (queue item Q3); the operational light-signal procedure for moving observers is the 1900 card | available | H. Poincaré, Rev. Métaphys. Morale 6 (1898) 1 |
| `poincare-1900-local-time` | 1900 (1900) | Lorentz's local time is what moving observers obtain when they synchronize clocks by exchanging light signals and assume equal travel times each way | The ether is retained | available | H. Poincaré, Arch. Néerl. (2) 5 (1900) 252 |
| `lorentz-1904-transformation` | 1904 (1904) | The full transformation with contraction, applied to a contractile electron, with the ether kept | A dynamical interpretation with local time as an auxiliary variable; the transformations of charge density and velocity were not yet exact (completed in Poincaré's June 1905 note) | available | H. A. Lorentz, Proc. R. Neth. Acad. Arts Sci. 6 (1904) 809 |
| `poincare-1904-st-louis` | 24 September 1904 (1904) | "The principle of relativity" named as one of the general principles of physics | A programmatic statement in a lecture | available | H. Poincaré, Bull. Sci. Math. (2) 28 (1904) 302 |
| `kaufmann-1901-electron-mass` | 1901–1903 (1903) | The inertia of fast electrons rises with speed; Abraham's rigid electron and Lorentz's contractile electron compete to explain it | The interpretation of the data was contested; the three papers' volumes and pages are settled at the originals (queue item Q5) | available | W. Kaufmann, Nachr. Ges. Wiss. Göttingen (1901, 1902, 1903); M. Abraham, Ann. Phys. (4) 10 (1903) 105 |
| `poincare-1905-june-note` | 5 June 1905 (1905) | The group property of the transformations and corrected transformations of charge density and velocity | Appeared before the relativity paper's receipt (30 June 1905) but after the 1904 cutoff | parallel-work | H. Poincaré, C. R. 140 (1905) 1504 |

**Einstein-knowledge evidence to attach** (always category 2, always cited separately, queue item Q6): R. S. Shankland's reports of conversations in which Einstein said that the observations of stellar aberration and Fizeau's measurements on light in moving water had influenced him most (R. S. Shankland, Am. J. Phys. 31 (1963) 47), attached to the Fizeau and Bradley cards.

**Worth proposing (queue item Q7):** W. Voigt (1887, Göttinger Nachrichten), a transformation that keeps the wave equation's form; J. Larmor (1897, 1900, *Aether and Matter*), a transformation to second order with time dilation. Either card is added only after its original is checked; both are available by 1904 and bear on what "the transformation was already known" means.

**Kept off the shelf** (timeline, margin, or world check only): Poincaré's Palermo paper (received July 1905, published 1906); Laue (1907), deriving Fizeau's coefficient from velocity addition; Minkowski (1908); Kaufmann's 1905–1906 data; Bucherer (1908); Einstein's 1917 train illustration; Lorentz's later acknowledgment that he had regarded local time only as an auxiliary quantity (*The Theory of Electrons*, 2nd ed., 1916; queue item Q8), which belongs in the margin; Ives–Stilwell (1938); muon lifetimes (1941); flown clocks (Hafele and Keating, flights in 1971, published 1972); satellite clocks.

### The primary-source verification queue

The queue is a declared list in `content/historical-premises/relativity/verification-queue.yaml`, each entry `{ id, question, cards[], sourceToConsult, landsIn, status }` where `status` is `open`, `resolved`, or `narrowed` and `landsIn` names the exact field the answer writes. The record shape is registered as an additive schema item with `am-disc-knowledge-cards-iw8j` (requested with `br comments add`), and each shelf bead owns its own queue file and entries. A card whose queue items are still `open` carries no `verification` record, so the publication gate keeps it out of a production build and the reading surfaces above keep saying "awaiting verification."

| Queue item | Question to settle at the original | Cards | Lands in |
|---|---|---|---|
| Q1 | Bradley's printed figures: his ratio of the speed of light to the Earth's orbital speed (about 10,210 to 1), his light time from the Sun (about 8 minutes 12 seconds), and the wording of the aberration he reports | `bradley-1729-aberration` | `limits` as transcribed figures with their printed units, plus `verification.printedCitation`; the implied angle is computed by `aberration` from the transcribed ratio and never stored |
| Q2 | The 1887 paper's printed quantities: the effective path (about 11 m), the statement that it is about $2\times10^{7}$ wavelengths, the expected shift (0.4 fringe), and the reported upper bound (the plan's recollection: less than one-twentieth, and probably less than one-fortieth, of the expected shift) | `michelson-1887-null-result` | `limits` as transcribed printed figures with the page; read by `am-disc-shelf-michelson-fizeau-dauq` as a cited card value, never retyped there and never styled as a dataset |
| Q3 | How explicitly Poincaré's 1898 essay describes light-signal synchronization, as against the conventionality of simultaneity | `poincare-1898-measure-of-time` | `proposition` and `limits`; a narrowed item states what the essay does not say and leaves the operational procedure to the 1900 card |
| Q4 | Paper 3's own assertions on the facsimile: the introduction's magnet-and-conductor asymmetry, and its general reference to unsuccessful attempts to detect motion relative to the light medium, with the printed wording | `faraday-1832-induction`, `michelson-1887-null-result` | `paperCitesOrAsserts` (`{ paper, anchor, note }`), with a note that the paper cites no one |
| Q5 | Kaufmann's 1901, 1902, and 1903 papers: volumes and pages as printed | `kaufmann-1901-electron-mass` | `sources[]`, `verification.printedCitation` |
| Q6 | Shankland, Am. J. Phys. 31 (1963) 47: the pages and the reported wording of what Einstein said about aberration and Fizeau | `bradley-1729-aberration`, `fizeau-1851-drag` | `einsteinKnowledgeEvidence` with its own citation, or the item is narrowed to "no evidence attached" |
| Q7 | Whether Voigt (1887) and Larmor (1897, 1900) can be cited from their originals, and exactly what each transformation preserves | candidate new cards | new cards with full records, or the item is narrowed to "not added" with the reason |
| Q8 | Lorentz's 1916 acknowledgment about local time: the edition, page, and printed wording | no shelf card (later) | the margin entry owned by `am-sr-margin-entries-tn4l`, reported with `br comments add` |

Resolving a queue item follows the card rules: read the scan page, never run OCR locally (AGENTS.md), record volume, pages, and dates exactly as printed, and file every difference from the plan's research queue in `verification.discrepancies` and with `br comments add`. `verifierKind: agent` is admissible with a checkable `evidenceLocator`; when a named historian checks a card, the check is a `history` review record from `am-edit-review-records-hofz` (reviewer role `history-reviewer` in `docs/OWNERS.md`) referenced from `verification.reviewRecordId`. Neither substitutes for the human knowledge-boundary review recorded in `am-disc-batch-h-exit-audit-r8xq`.

## Technical Approach

- Write and verify the fourteen records; open the queue with all eight items and close them as the originals are consulted; record volume, pages, and dates exactly as printed.
- Where an original contradicts the plan's date or proposition, correct the card, record the difference in `verification.discrepancies`, and raise it with `br comments add`.
- Tell the consuming beads when a card's state changes: `br comments add am-sr-09-doppler-aberration-rabd` and `br comments add am-sre-readings-s7-s8-lpje` when `bradley-1729-aberration` is verified or corrected, and `br comments add am-disc-shelf-michelson-fizeau-dauq` when `michelson-1887-null-result` is.
- Attach `admittedStages` from the Journey III record's stage ids; until those ids exist, list the intended stages by name (the nagging fact, two postulates, the measurement procedure, the Galilean test, simultaneity, Fork A, the move, the consequences, Fork B, waves and the light complex, charge and the electron, the world check).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Fourteen verified records exist with every standard field; the June 1905 Poincaré card is `parallel-work`.
- [ ] Every queue item is `resolved` or `narrowed` before the relativity paper is published; a card with an open queue item carries no verification record, so the production-profile publication gate fails if it is cited.
- [ ] The Poincaré 1898 proposition matches the original text after verification.
- [ ] Bradley's card carries his printed ratio and light time as transcribed figures, carries no stored angle, and states that $20.50''$ is a modern computation owned by SR-09; a fixture card storing an angle fails.
- [ ] The Michelson–Morley card carries the 1887 printed effective path, wavelength count, expected shift, and reported upper bound, and the shelf instrument shows them as cited card values with no dataset styling.
- [ ] Einstein-knowledge evidence appears only with its own citation and never merges with availability; category-3 notes never imply that the paper cites anyone.
- [ ] Later items are recorded for the timeline and margin and not attached to shelf stages; Lorentz's 1916 acknowledgment is reported to `am-sr-margin-entries-tn4l`.
- [ ] The shelf audit and anachronism lint pass (no "spacetime diagram," "Minkowski," "light cone," or "train and embankment" in card text outside labeled later-lens fields).

## Test Plan

### Unit and integration tests

- `content/historical-premises/relativity/relativityShelf.test.ts`, against the real schemas and validators: schema validity; dates and statuses; verification records with non-empty evidence locators and printed citations; ids match `<first-author>-<year>-<topic>`; Einstein-knowledge evidence separate and cited; category-3 notes present on the Faraday and Michelson–Morley cards and containing no citation keys; the anachronism vocabulary scan; the Lorentz 1904 and FitzGerald cards contain none of a short list of evaluative words ("failed," "wrong," "mistaken," "naive").
- `content/historical-premises/relativity/bradleyCard.test.ts`: the Bradley card carries the ratio and the light time as transcribed figures; it stores no angle in any field; computing the implied angle from the transcribed ratio through `aberration` gives $20.2022''$ (relative $10^{-9}$); a fixture card whose ratio is changed yields a different computed angle, which proves no literal is used; the string "20.50" appears nowhere on the card.
- `content/historical-premises/relativity/verificationQueue.test.ts`: the queue file validates; every `cards[]` entry resolves; a card with an `open` queue item and a `verification` record fails, naming the card, the queue item, and the repair; a `narrowed` item requires a non-empty explanation; Q8's entry names no card and resolves to a margin report.
- Compiler integration with the real card rules and epistemic checks: a fixture stage citing `poincare-1905-june-note` without acknowledgment is rejected, and accepted with it; a production-profile build citing an unverified card fails the publication gate and passes once the record is present; a draft-profile build shows the "Unverified research-queue card" marker, which is absent from production-profile HTML.

### End-to-end tests

- `e2e/journey-iii-shelf.spec.ts`, run through the browser harness (`am-test-e2e-harness-bqmh`) once `/discover/special-relativity` renders the shelf: confirm date order and the parallel-work flag; open the Fizeau card and see the cited Shankland evidence as a separate section; open the Faraday card's "What the paper itself cites or asserts" section; open the Bradley card and read the transcribed figures with the verification summary; follow a backlink to a journey stage and return; JavaScript disabled, 320 px, and print lanes.

### Structured logging

JSONL to `artifacts/test-logs/journey-iii-shelf/<log-run-id>.jsonl` with `timestamp`, `suite`, `logRunId`, `testId`, `beadId`, `cardId`, `latestYear`, `status`, `verified`, `verifierKind`, `hasEinsteinEvidence`, `hasCategory3Note`, `queueItem`, `queueStatus`, `discrepancyCount`, `expected`, `actual`, `tolerance`, `comparisonKind`, `buildProfile`, `browser`, `viewport`, `jsEnabled`, `outcome`, `durationMs`, `message`. Failing browser tests retain a screenshot, trace, DOM snapshot, and console log; a failing validator run retains the offending record path and the diagnostic under `artifacts/test-logs/journey-iii-shelf/<log-run-id>/`.

## Considerations and Pitfalls

- Treat Lorentz and Poincaré with precision and respect. The Lorentz cards must not be phrased as failures, and how far Poincaré's view departed from Lorentz's is a historians' question for the margin, with citations.
- Keep the dynamo-patent remark as context; Galison's argument about clock coordination belongs on the Bern page, labeled as an argument.
- That the equations do not keep their form under a Galilean substitution is demonstrated by the shelf instrument, not asserted.
- A 1729 measurement and a modern constant differ by about 1.5 percent. The card carries Bradley's figures and the instrument labels its own computation; neither is called the other's value, and neither is called an error.
- Checking a citation means looking at the scan page; never run OCR locally.

## Dependencies

Blocked by:
- `am-disc-knowledge-cards-iw8j`: card schema, validators, publication gate, and rendering; it also registers the verification-queue record shape.
- `am-cm-anachronism-lint-dl2`: card text is linted for unlabeled anachronisms.

Unblocks:
- `am-disc-journey-iii-chain-hpr7`: the chain cites these cards.
- `am-dod-relativity-105y`: the relativity definition of done requires every shelf card dated and sourced.
- `am-disc-desk-1904-9hgd`: the desk's premise catalogue lists every shelf card.
- `am-sr-09-doppler-aberration-rabd`: its Bradley comparison row reads `bradley-1729-aberration` and its verification state.
- `am-sre-readings-s7-s8-lpje`: the §§7–8 readings quote the same card's transcribed figures, and their numeric-trace test compares against it.

Unblocks, added as an edge in review: `am-disc-shelf-michelson-fizeau-dauq`, whose Michelson–Morley instrument shows the 1887 observational bound as a cited value from `michelson-1887-null-result`.

title: Build Journey IV: two ledgers, the fork, the check against the world, doors, and exercises
description:
# Build Journey IV: two ledgers, the fork, the check against the world, doors, and exercises

**Epic:** `am-ep-discovery-33u` · **Batch:** batch-d · **Priority:** P1 · **Plan sections:** §9.1, §9.5, §8.4, §3.6, §7.2, §7.3, §14.5 (traceability only)

## Background

Journey IV: **can emitting light change inertia?** Three printed pages make the argument short, and brevity makes a missing premise easy to hide, so this journey is reviewed with the same seriousness as the long ones. The route imports exactly one 1905 result with provenance, the relativity paper's §8 light-energy transformation, and never assumes its conclusion: the body's internal energies stay symbolic, and the additive-constant premise is stated as a premise rather than disguised as a theorem. The formula $E = mc^2$ does not appear in the paper; the paper says that a body giving off energy $L$ as radiation loses mass $L/V^2$.

The journey is labeled "A route you could take." Its shelf is "the end of 1904, plus paper 3."

The journey record carries the one sentence that states its move for readers with no physics background (`move.r0Summary`). The fifteen-minute mass–energy tour (`am-tour-15min-mass-energy-nqz1`) renders it verbatim by journey id, so it must be true at R0, keep the slow-motion identification and the paper's premises, and contain no mathematics, no symbols, and no "conversion" language.

## Scope

In scope: the complete Journey IV record `content/arguments/journeys/mass-energy.yaml` for `/discover/mass-energy`, including `move.r0Summary`.

Out of scope (owned elsewhere): shelf cards (`am-disc-journey-iv-shelf-ff7g`); ME-01 to ME-03 and the 1906 box extension, with their presets, modes, tapes, and prompts (`am-me-01-two-ledgers-g1re`, `am-me-02-coefficient-dtmi`, `am-me-03-system-boundary-0arb`, `am-me-03-box-extension-kiei`); the no-algebra entrance (`am-me-first-encounter-kejt`); energy-source card values (ME-03 and `massEnergy.ts`); the framework and the move summary guard (`am-disc-journey-framework-umbg`); placing the predict-perturb-explain task at the end of the reading chapter (`am-disc-ppe-teachback-wnp7`, which references this record); the `physics-math` review that makes the summary `reviewed` (a named physics reviewer; the paper's physics review `am-me-review-physics-1t2l`).

## Requirements

**The nagging fact.** "A body that emits light in one direction recoils. If it emits equal pulses in opposite directions it does not recoil, and yet something about its motion has changed, because the two pulses carry different energies to a moving observer."

**The first honest question.** "If I already know how the energy of a light pulse changes between frames, what does energy conservation force me to say about the body that emitted it?"

**Admitted import.** The record lists `einstein-1905-light-complex-energy` in `admittedImports`, and every stage that uses it shows the import card with its provenance and a link to the relativity paper's §8.

### The chain (front door; ME-01, ME-02)

Tape, preset, and mode ids below are cited exactly as the instrument beads register them.

1. **The deliberately minimal experiment.** A body at rest emits two equal pulses in opposite directions; the symmetry removes recoil from the rest-frame bookkeeping and isolates an energy change.
2. **Two ledgers (ME-01, teaching tape "the two pulses," `the-two-pulses`).** With $L$ the total emitted energy in the rest frame, $E_0, E_1$ the body's energies before and after in that frame, and $H_0, H_1$ in a frame moving at $v$: the pulses carry $\tfrac{L}{2}\gamma\left(1 - \tfrac{v}{c}\cos\varphi\right)$ and $\tfrac{L}{2}\gamma\left(1 + \tfrac{v}{c}\cos\varphi\right)$ in modern notation, summing to $\gamma L$ for every emission angle. At $v = 0.6c$ ($\gamma = 1.25$) the pulses carry $0.25L$ and $1.0L$ at $\varphi = 0°$, $0.4375L$ and $0.8125L$ at $60°$, and $0.625L$ each at $90°$, always $1.25L$ in total. The printed form uses $V$ for the speed of light and writes the factor as a square root; the concordance notes that Einstein's $\beta$ is the modern $\gamma$. Balances: $E_0 - E_1 = L$ and $H_0 - H_1 = \gamma L$.
   - Rotating the emission axis in ME-01 is a `setup-change` (a new identified run with a different emission geometry): the reader watches each pulse energy change while the sum $\gamma L$ does not.
   - Changing the moving observer's speed is an `observer-change`: the run id and event ids stay the same, and nothing restarts.
3. **The subtraction.** $(H_0 - E_0) - (H_1 - E_1) = L(\gamma - 1)$; every cancellation is a selectable operation. $E_0, E_1, H_0, H_1$ stay symbolic or carry explicitly arbitrary offsets that cancel; they are never initialized with $Mc^2$ or $\gamma Mc^2$.
4. **The stated premise.** Each frame-energy difference equals the kinetic energy plus the same additive constant before and after emission. The source asserts this; the cancellation is not an independent derivation of the assertion (the margin presents Ives 1952 and Stachel and Torretti 1982).
5. **The low-speed expansion with its domain visible (ME-02, teaching tape "toward low speed," `toward-low-speed`).** $K_0 - K_1 = L(\gamma - 1) \approx \tfrac12\frac{L}{c^2}v^2$. At $v = 0.6c$ the exact difference is $0.25L$ and the quadratic approximation $0.18L$; the reader moves toward low speed and watches the coefficient stabilize. Four outputs stay distinct: the exact difference; the quadratic approximation; the finite-speed proxy $2L(\gamma-1)/v^2$, which exceeds $L/c^2$ by about $\tfrac34(v/c)^2$ at small speed (1.3889 $L/c^2$ at $0.6c$; 1.00756305, 1.00007501, and 1.00000075 at 0.1, 0.01, and 0.001 of light speed, with $\gamma - 1$ evaluated in cancellation-free form); and the limiting coefficient $L/c^2$, a typed `analytic-limit` at $v = 0$.
6. **The move.** Identifying the limiting coefficient of $v^2/2$ as a mass loss of $L/c^2$ within the admitted premises, marked in the derivation chain (from `am-me-equations-0mgx`). The page distinguishes the positive mass lost, $M_{\text{before}} - M_{\text{after}} = L/c^2$, from the signed change $\Delta M = -L/c^2$.
7. **The generalization.** The paper's statement that the mass of a body is a measure of its energy content, separated from the specific radiation argument and from the later modern formulation.

### The move's R0 summary (`move.r0Summary`)

- **Text** (authored here; editors may refine the wording through review, keeping every property below): "Seen by an observer moving past, the body carries less energy of motion after giving off light than before, at the same speed, just as a slightly lighter body would when the motion is slow, so, within the paper's stated premises, giving off energy lowers the body's mass by an amount set by that energy."
- **Properties that must survive any rewording:** one sentence; no mathematics and no symbols (the framework's guard); at most 100 words; the comparison at the same speed seen by a moving observer; the lighter-body identification limited to slow motion (the move identifies the limiting coefficient, so "exactly" at every speed would overclaim); the paper's stated premises acknowledged; the amount set by the energy given off; none of the fifteen-minute tour's forbidden terms ("E = mc," "mc²," "converts," "turns into energy," "bomb," "reactor").
- **Review state.** This bead records the summary as `reviewState: draft` and never sets `reviewed`. A named physics reviewer records a `physics-math` review record covering the journey record's revision; only then may `reviewed` be set, which the review-status check of `am-edit-review-records-hofz` verifies. Until then the production and preview builds of the mass–energy fifteen-minute tour fail `tour-move-summary-missing`, by design.

### The forks (after the move)

**Fork 1: which account to give of the same bookkeeping.**

- (a) *Poincaré 1900:* the center-of-mass theorem fails for radiation unless the radiation is treated as a fictitious fluid carrying mass $E/c^2$. Worked honestly as bookkeeping. Outcome `empirically-equivalent-not-refuted`, with the scope note: "for the center-of-mass bookkeeping of emission and absorption treated in Poincaré's 1900 paper." Proponent card: `poincare-1900-fictitious-fluid`.
- (b) Energy itself has inertia. Outcome `papers-route`.

**What fork 1 varies.** It declares `varies: proposed-explanation` from the closed set of `am-disc-journey-framework-umbg`: both branches keep the same bookkeeping and the same $E/c^2$, and they differ on what account to give of it, a fictitious fluid introduced to save the center-of-mass theorem against energy itself having inertia. The reader's sentence, shown above the branches: "This fork is about two accounts of the same bookkeeping, not about which quantity to measure." The fork varies no measurement choice and neither branch uses `dead-end-on-constraint`, so `fork-measurement-choice-cannot-dead-end` has no application here, and branch (a)'s `scopeNote` already names the observable class the framework requires, the center-of-mass bookkeeping of emission and absorption treated in Poincare's 1900 paper.

**Fork 2: does inertia belong to energy as such, or only to the field?** The fork declares `varies: assumption` from the same closed set: the branches disagree about a premise, not about which account to give of one bookkeeping. The reader's sentence, shown above the branches: "This fork is about how far the claim reaches, not about the arithmetic."

- (a) *Electromagnetic mass:* a charged body's field adds to its inertia, so inertia is a property of field energy rather than of energy in general. Worked from the shelf card `thomson-1881-electromagnetic-mass`, whose own note already records that the coefficient depends on the electron model. Outcome `undecided-on-available-evidence`, with the `insufficiency` sentence: "The 1904 shelf carries no measurement of a body whose non-electromagnetic energy changes by enough to weigh, so it cannot separate a claim about field energy from a claim about energy as such." Its `whatWouldDecide` resolves to the nuclear mass-defect measurement of Cockcroft and Walton (1932), which is later evidence and is already the dated later comparison this journey's check-against-the-world stage names, so `fork-undecided-already-decidable` cannot fire.
- (b) The inertia of a body depends on its energy content, whatever form that energy takes. Outcome `papers-route`.

Branch (a) is neither a dead end nor a target. Electromagnetic mass was a serious quantitative programme, Kaufmann's deflection data were read as bearing on it, and what 1904 lacked was not a better account of it but a body whose non-field energy could be weighed. `am-disc-journey-iv-shelf-ff7g` is required to represent electromagnetic mass fairly, and this fork is where the reader meets it.

**The exhaustive case for `undecided-on-available-evidence`.** This journey's branches use `empirically-equivalent-not-refuted` and `papers-route`, and branch (a) is not re-typed to the fifth outcome, because Poincare's account and the paper's agree on the bookkeeping within that scope rather than being undecidable on the evidence. Wherever this bead's content, branch copy or tests switch on `outcome.type`, the fifth value carries its own case rather than falling through: the per-outcome copy names it, and the record test walks all five values and ends in the framework's `const _exhaustive: never = type`, so a missing case is a typecheck failure rather than a blank branch. Fork 2's branch (a) carries the fifth outcome as a shipped and fully worked branch, and a fixture branch exercises it as well, so the case is never met by leaving a shipped branch unworked: the fifth outcome is not a place to hide a branch nobody worked out.

### Check it against the world (ME-03)

- **Framing.** These cards compute what the relation implies from cited modern energy values on `modern-si-2019`. They are consequences, not tests: the mass changes are far too small to weigh outside nuclear processes. The first quantitative nuclear checks (Cockcroft and Walton 1932; Bainbridge 1933) are dated later evidence on the timeline and are named here as such. The framing is rendered from the typed `boundary` object each card carries in `am-me-03-system-boundary-0arb` (`systemBefore`, `systemAfter`, `matterCrossesBoundary`, `radiation.disposition`, `referenceFrame`, `energyFigure` and `closedButNotIsolated`), not restated as prose in this record: the stage reads those fields, so the cards whose `matterCrossesBoundary.crosses` is true say so in the reader's own words, and the cards whose `closedButNotIsolated.value` is true render that sentence. A stage that authored a boundary sentence of its own would put one fact under two owners, and the instrument bead already owns it.
- **Cards,** each computed live by ME-03's owner from its cited value through its registered preset (with a build-time static worked example without JavaScript):
  - `me-03-card-radium`: one radium-226 alpha decay releases about 4.87 MeV, so a mole of radium loses about 5.23 mg of mass in that single step. The paper's own remark was conditional: a test might succeed with bodies whose energy content varies strongly, such as radium salts.
  - `me-03-card-sun`: the Sun radiates about $3.83\times10^{26}$ W, so it loses about $4.26\times10^{9}$ kg (about four million tonnes) every second.
  - `me-03-card-coal`: burning a kilogram of coal (about 24–35 MJ) loses $(2.67\text{–}3.89)\times10^{-10}$ kg, about 0.27–0.39 μg. The plan's "less than a nanogram" holds per gram, not per kilogram; the corrected figure is used.
  - `me-03-card-candle`: a candle of about 80 W (a cited value stated as an assumption) loses about 3.20 ng per hour through the energy it emits.
  - `me-03-card-bulb`: a 100 W bulb running for a year loses about 35.1 μg.

### What Einstein actually wrote

Jumps to the paper's two-ledger passage, the subtraction and kinetic-energy identification, the low-speed expansion, the general statement, and the radium remark, each lighting its named weave predicate from the carried instrument state or showing the static pointer; the import card links to the relativity paper's §8.

### Doors

- **Front door:** the paper's argument above.
- **Side door, arithmetic (required):** the no-algebra entrance, first-encounter record `entrance-mass-energy` (`am-me-first-encounter-kejt`, rendered at `#entry-mass-energy`), entered with host `returnTo` and `continueTo` targets: two before-and-after accounting sheets with unknown internal quantities as covered boxes, where subtracting the sheets shows the inaccessible details are not needed. $Mc^2$ is never placed inside a covered box.
- **Side door, programmer (required):** the photon-in-a-box argument (`am-me-03-box-extension-kiei`, mode `me-03:box-1906`, teaching tape "the 1906 box," `the-1906-box`). A box of mass $M$ and length $\ell$ recoils at $E/(Mc)$ for a time $\ell/c$ and shifts by $E\ell/(Mc^2)$, so mass $E/c^2$ must have moved with the light if the closed system's center of mass stays put. It is labeled "Einstein's 1906 argument, crediting Poincaré 1900," with its approximations stated (rigid box, nonrelativistic box motion, transit time $\ell/c$). The door's premises are shelf cards: `maxwell-1873-radiation-pressure` for the momentum $E/c$ carried by radiation (its momentum clause cites the verified first explicit source) and `poincare-1900-fictitious-fluid` for the center-of-mass theorem of a closed system that Poincaré set out to save. The 1906 paper is cited as the source of the route, never as a premise, and the argument is never merged into the 1905 ledger.
- All three doors arrive at the same equation id, the paper's mass-loss statement ($L/V^2$ in the printed notation), and the page says so.

### Exercises

Instrumented (four; the framework requires two to five):
1. **Mass lost by a 100 W bulb in a year** (numeric: $100 \times 3.156\times10^{7}$ J divided by $c^2$, about $3.5\times10^{-8}$ kg; reference from `massEnergy.ts` on `modern-si-2019`).
2. **Show the $\cos\varphi$ cancellation** (expression equivalence: $\tfrac12\gamma\left(1 - \tfrac{v}{c}\cos\varphi\right) + \tfrac12\gamma\left(1 + \tfrac{v}{c}\cos\varphi\right)$ against $\gamma$, with declared variables $\varphi \in [0, \pi]$ and $v/c \in [-0.95, 0.95]$).
3. **Compute the recoil displacement of the box** (numeric: $E\ell/(Mc^2)$ for the authored $E$, $\ell$, $M$ stated in the prompt; reference `photonInBox` in `massEnergy.ts`).
4. **What the finite-speed proxy is and is not** (numeric: at $0.6c$ the proxy is $2(0.25)/0.36 \approx 1.389\,L/c^2$ against the limit $L/c^2$; plus an explanation part).

Explanation item (one):
5. Explain why the equal-and-opposite emission was chosen.

### The predict-perturb-explain task (`ppeTask`, id `ppe-mass-energy`)

- **Prompt:** "A body's unknown internal energy appears in both ledgers; which subtraction removes it, and which premise makes the subtraction useful?"
- **Predict:** the reader chooses which difference removes the unknown energies (candidates: $E_0 - E_1$; $H_0 - H_1$; $(H_0 - E_0) - (H_1 - E_1)$), stored locally and never scored.
- **Perturb:** in ME-01, use the premise probe ("the additive constant is allowed to change") and change the observer's speed, through the instrument's action contract, and watch which conclusion survives.
- **Explain:** an explanation part with comparison criteria (the unknown internal energies cancel in the difference of differences; the conclusion about mass needs the stated premise that each frame-energy difference is kinetic energy plus the same constant; relaxing the premise leaves the subtraction true but no longer about inertia).
- `am-disc-ppe-teachback-wnp7` places this same record at the end of the mass–energy reading chapter (the whole paper); its id follows that bead's `ppe-<paper slug>` pattern.

## Technical Approach

- Author the journey record referencing the shelf cards and the admitted import; ME-01 to ME-03 presets, modes, and the teaching tapes above; the box extension's mode and tape for the programmer door; derivation-chain step ids with the move marked (from `am-me-equations-0mgx`); weave predicates; exercises; the predict-perturb-explain task; the door equation id; `move.r0Summary` with `reviewState: draft`.
- World-check cards bind the exact quantity ids of ME-03's card outputs; no literals.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The journey validates as `complete`; its only post-1904 premise is the admitted import, shown with provenance.
- [ ] `move.r0Summary` passes the framework's guard, keeps the properties listed above, contains none of the tour's forbidden terms, and is recorded as `draft`; this bead never sets `reviewed`.
- [ ] No ledger value is initialized with $Mc^2$ or $\gamma Mc^2$ (tested against the ME-01 snapshot).
- [ ] The additive-constant premise is stated as a premise.
- [ ] Exact, quadratic, proxy, and limit outputs are displayed distinctly, with $0.25L$ against $0.18L$ at $0.6c$.
- [ ] Rotating the emission axis creates a new identified run; changing the observer speed keeps run and event ids.
- [ ] The fork's branch (a) is labeled empirically equivalent within its stated scope and not refuted.
- [ ] Fork 1 declares `varies: proposed-explanation` and fork 2 declares `varies: assumption`; each renders the reader's plain sentence above its branches; and the fifth outcome is carried by fork 2's branch (a) as a worked branch as well as by an exercised case in this bead's outcome handling.
- [ ] The journey carries two forks, which is what the framework's completeness check requires of a `complete` journey, and fork 2's branch (a) cites the shelf card `thomson-1881-electromagnetic-mass`, an `insufficiency` sentence, and a `whatWouldDecide` resolving to Cockcroft and Walton 1932, so `fork-undecided-already-decidable` does not fire.
- [ ] The check-against-the-world stage's framing is projected from the typed `boundary` fields of `am-me-03-system-boundary-0arb`, and a boundary sentence authored in this journey record fails a static check.
- [ ] Energy-source cards compute from cited values through their registered presets, are framed as consequences rather than tests, and the coal card shows the corrected magnitude; Cockcroft–Walton and Bainbridge appear as dated later evidence.
- [ ] Three doors end at the same equation id, the box door carries its 1906 label and credit and cites its two premise cards, and the page states that the routes meet.
- [ ] Four instrumented exercises, one explanation item, and the predict-perturb-explain task work.

## Test Plan

### Unit and integration tests

- `content/arguments/journeys/massEnergy.test.ts`, with the real compiler, framework checks, and `massEnergy.ts`: validation as `complete`; the import rule; door equation ids and the entrance-record door; the box door's premise cards resolve; every cited preset, mode, and tape id resolves; exercise roles and counts; references: 100 W for $3.156\times10^{7}$ s gives $3.5115\times10^{-8}$ kg; the proxy at $0.6c$ is 1.388889; the cancellation identity holds at the checker's sample points; `photonInBox` with $E = 1$ J, $\ell = 1$ m, $M = 1$ kg gives $1.11265\times10^{-17}$ m.
- `forkContract.massEnergy.test.ts`, against the real schema and this journey's record: fork 1 declares `varies: proposed-explanation` and fork 2 declares `varies: assumption`; a missing `varies` fails with `fork-varies-missing` naming the fork id; branch (a)'s `scopeNote` names an observable class; a walk over all five `outcome.type` values compiles with no default arm; and a fixture branch typed `undecided-on-available-evidence` passes only with `insufficiency` and a `whatWouldDecide` resolving to a dated item after 1904, such as Cockcroft and Walton 1932, which is also the rule fork 2's shipped branch (a) passes under.
- `moveSummary.massEnergy.test.ts`: the summary passes `moveSummaryGuard`; the fifteen-minute tour's `symbolScan` with the mass–energy concordance finds no symbol label (none of "c²", "c^2", "L/", "γ", "Mc", "mc", "V²"); its word count is at most 100 (logged); it contains "slow" and "premises"; it contains none of "E = mc," "mc²," "converts," "turns into energy," "bomb," "reactor," and "exactly"; `reviewState` is `draft` in the committed record unless a covering `physics-math` review record exists (checked through the real review-status check).
- `ledgers.massEnergy.test.ts`: at $0.6c$, pulse energies $0.25L$ and $1.0L$ at 0°, $0.4375L$ and $0.8125L$ at 60°, $0.625L$ each at 90°, total $1.25L$ at every angle (relative $10^{-12}$); the proxy 1.00756305, 1.00007501, and 1.00000075 at 0.1, 0.01, and 0.001 of light speed (relative $10^{-8}$); the zero-speed coefficient is the typed `analytic-limit`.
- `worldCheck.massEnergy.test.ts`: card mass changes derive from their cited inputs (radium 5.229 mg per mole from 4.871 MeV; Sun $4.259\times10^{9}$ kg/s from $3.828\times10^{26}$ W; coal $2.670\times10^{-10}$ and $3.894\times10^{-10}$ kg for 24 and 35 MJ; candle 3.204 ng per hour at 80 W; bulb 35.11 μg over a Julian year; relative tolerance $10^{-3}$); an uncited card fixture is refused.
- `worldCheckFraming.massEnergy.test.ts`: the check stage's framing strings are projected from each card's typed `boundary` object in `am-me-03-system-boundary-0arb`; a static scan finds no boundary sentence authored in this journey record; changing a fixture card's `matterCrossesBoundary.crosses` or `closedButNotIsolated.value` changes the rendered framing; and the Sun, coal and candle cards render their matter-crosses note while the radium and bulb cards render the closed-but-not-isolated sentence.
- `noncircularity.massEnergy.test.ts`: a historical ledger fixture initialized with $E_0 = Mc^2$ fails `circular-rest-energy`; the adversarial fixture "the low-speed proxy is the exact mass coefficient at every speed" fails at $0.6c$.
- `commandClasses.massEnergy.test.ts`: axis rotation yields a new `runId`; an observer speed change keeps `runId` and every event id and consumes nothing.

### End-to-end tests

- `e2e/journey-iv.spec.ts`, run through the browser harness (`am-test-e2e-harness-bqmh`): walk the ledgers; rotate the axis by typed entry and confirm the sum is unchanged; change the observer speed and confirm the run identity; select each cancellation; step toward low speed; read the move marker and its summary; take both fork branches; read the check cards and their framing; follow the import link to relativity §8 and back; enter through each side door and reach the same equation; answer exercises 1 and 2; complete the predict-perturb-explain task and reload; lanes keyboard only, 320 px, reduced motion, JavaScript disabled (static worked examples, the summary, and both branches readable), WebKit.

### Structured logging

JSONL to `artifacts/test-logs/journey-iv/<log-run-id>.jsonl` with `timestamp`, `suite`, `logRunId`, `runId`, `testId`, `beadId`, `journeyId`, `stageId`, `forkId`, `branchId`, `varies`, `outcomeType`, `doorId`, `instrumentId`, `presetId`, `modeId`, `tapeId`, `instanceId`, `snapshotVersion`, `commandClass`, `quantityId`, `expected`, `actual`, `tolerance`, `comparisonKind`, `constantSetId`, `executionLabel`, `resultStatus`, `moveSummaryReviewState`, `moveSummaryWordCount`, `browser`, `viewport`, `jsEnabled`, `outcome`, `durationMs`, `message`. Failing browser tests retain a screenshot, trace, DOM snapshot, and console log.

## Considerations and Pitfalls

- Do not begin by asserting that each pulse is "mass converted to energy."
- The mass of a closed system is conserved; the body's rest mass falls because energy left it.
- Two equal opposite pulses have nonzero invariant mass as a system; that is a later modern explanation, not a hidden premise of 1905.
- The 1906 box is a later argument and is labeled so; it never enters the 1905 ledger.
- The summary's "when the motion is slow" is load-bearing: the move identifies the low-speed coefficient, and the finite-speed proxy exceeds it.

## Dependencies

Blocked by:
- `am-disc-journey-iv-shelf-ff7g`: verified cards and the admitted import.
- `am-disc-journey-framework-umbg`: skeleton, route, and the move summary schema and guard.
- `am-disc-exercise-checker-i4h2`: exercises.
- `am-me-01-two-ledgers-g1re`: the ledgers and the "the two pulses" tape.
- `am-me-02-coefficient-dtmi`: the low-speed coefficient, the move, and the "toward low speed" tape.
- `am-me-03-system-boundary-0arb`: the check against the world, its card presets, and the typed `boundary` fields the check stage's framing renders from.
- `am-me-first-encounter-kejt`: the arithmetic side door.
- `am-me-03-box-extension-kiei`: the programmer side door (batch-d, like this journey).

Unblocks:
- `am-dod-mass-energy-oxh2`, `am-disc-cross-journey-exercises-j53n`, `am-tour-evening-and-course-5kcb`, `am-disc-batch-h-exit-audit-r8xq`.
- `am-tour-15min-mass-energy-nqz1`: renders this record's `move.r0Summary`.
- `am-disc-ppe-teachback-wnp7`: places this journey's predict-perturb-explain record.
- `am-ver-no-circularity-audit-6vj`: the circularity audit covers the ledgers (the paper's physics review `am-me-review-physics-1t2l` runs after that audit, so it can review the summary).

title: Author and verify the dated shelf cards for Journey IV (mass-energy)
description:
# Author and verify the dated shelf cards for Journey IV (mass-energy)

**Epic:** `am-ep-discovery-33u` · **Batch:** batch-d · **Priority:** P1 · **Plan sections:** §5.1–5.3, §8.4, §9.5, §3.6, §3.9 (paper 4 margin), §14.4 (traceability only)

## Background

Journey IV asks: can emitting light change inertia? Its shelf is "the end of 1904, plus paper 3." The September 1905 argument may import the relativity paper's §8 result that a light complex's energy transforms exactly like its frequency, and the journey shows that import's provenance instead of hiding it. This is the one journey where an admitted 1905 result is a legitimate premise. The import card is encoded with status `available`, `latestYear` 1905, and an `admittedImport` declared by the mass–energy journey; the card rules accept it only there and never on the `/1904` desk.

The shelf must also represent real prior work fairly (Poincaré's 1900 "fictitious fluid," Hasenöhrl's cavity radiation, electromagnetic mass) without adjudicating priority on a card, and without importing the later slogan $E = mc^2$, which does not appear in the paper; the paper says that a body emitting energy $L$ as radiation loses mass $L/V^2$.

Verification has a hard deadline here: the mass–energy paper is the Batch D delivery, and `am-disc-knowledge-cards-iw8j` rule 3 fails every production and preview build in which a published journey cites a card without a verification record. The open research questions are therefore tracked as a named queue, not as scattered parenthetical notes.

## Scope

In scope: one verified HistoricalPremise record per card below, with the fields and rules of `am-disc-knowledge-cards-iw8j`; the admitted-import card with provenance; the paper's own citations where present; the primary-source verification queue; the list of later and world-check items kept off the shelf.

Out of scope (owned elsewhere): card rendering and rules (`am-disc-knowledge-cards-iw8j`); the chain (`am-disc-journey-iv-chain-wwrz`); energy-source world-check cards for ME-03 (`am-me-03-system-boundary-0arb`); paper 4 margin entries (`am-me-margin-entries-kfg5`); timeline cards (`am-disc-timeline-xzef`); the relativity paper's §8 transcription itself (`am-edn-translation-relativity-s6-s10-qkn` and `am-sre-equations-2g3h`, which this card links to); the human knowledge-boundary review (`am-disc-batch-h-exit-audit-r8xq`).

## Requirements

Store records under `content/historical-premises/` (journey-neutral card ids in lowercase kebab case, `<first-author>-<year>-<topic>`; this bead's cards may be grouped in `content/historical-premises/mass-energy/`). Each record carries the standard fields of `am-disc-knowledge-cards-iw8j`: `sources[]` as printed, `date` (`earliest`, `latest`, `latestYear`, `precision`), `proposition`, `limits`, `status`, `admittedStages[]`, `paperCitesOrAsserts` where verified, `einsteinKnowledgeEvidence` only with its own citation, and `verification` (`verifiedBy`, `verifierKind`, `date`, `method`, `evidenceLocator`, `printedCitation`, `discrepancies[]`, `reviewRecordId`).

| Card id | Date (`latestYear`) | Proposition | Limits to state | Status | Candidate citation (verify) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `maxwell-1873-radiation-pressure` | 1873, 1884 (1884) | Radiation falling on a surface exerts a pressure numerically equal to its energy density (Maxwell); electromagnetic energy flows as Poynting described; a pulse of energy $E$ therefore carries momentum $E/c$ | Classical field result. The momentum clause cites the source that first states $E/c$ explicitly, settled at the originals (queue item Q1); if that source is later than Poynting, the clause becomes its own card | available | J. C. Maxwell, *A Treatise on Electricity and Magnetism* (1873), vol. 2, art. 792; J. H. Poynting, Phil. Trans. 175 (1884) 343 |

Poincaré, Arch. Néerl. (2) 5 (1900) 252 |
