# Audit the relativity paper against the per-paper definition of done

**Epic:** `am-ep-relativity-electrodynamics-afj` · **Batch:** batch-g · **Priority:** P1 · **Plan sections:** §17.7, §19.3 G, §21 (traceability only)

## Background

A paper is done when nine independent conditions hold together, not when its instruments merely work. This audit closes *Zur Elektrodynamik bewegter Körper* (`ap-17-891`) against the per-paper definition of done and against Batch G's exit evidence: all ten sections covered, sign and frame checks passing, and the difficult final sections treated with the same depth as the opening. Each item is judged separately; none is aggregated into a score. The audit also closes the loop on the corrections found while polishing the relativity beads (printed-text verifications and owner gaps), so none of them reaches launch silently.

## Scope

In scope: producing `docs/audits/dod-special-relativity.md` with a verdict (`met`, `not met`, or `not yet observable`) and evidence for each item; running the checks that can only be run once everything exists (rendered embeds for every instrument, the corrections register); filing or linking beads for gaps.

Out of scope: doing the missing work (owned by the linked beads); site-wide launch criteria (`am-launch-readiness-audit-sc9b`).

## Requirements

1. **Provenance receipt** `docs/provenance/ap-17-891.md`: typed dates (date-line "Bern, Juni 1905"; received 30 June 1905, with the printed receipt line "(Eingegangen 30. Juni 1905.)"; published 26 September 1905), the page map from PDF pages to journal pages 891-921, sections, and equations, comparison witnesses (Collected Papers Vol. 2 document 23, the Augsburg facsimile, a Wikisource revision), and translation credits.
2. **Source layers** share one SHA-256 and pass edition tests: pinned facsimile, reviewed diplomatic ledger, German edition, English edition, gloss units for the required sections (`am-edn-gloss-relativity-na8d`), and the many-to-many alignment; the source manifest reports every block covered.
3. **Readings and equations:** every paragraph, heading (including `part-1` and `part-2`), footnote, and closing block from the introduction to the closing has R0-R3 (from `am-srk-readings-intro-s2-00vk`, `am-srk-readings-s3-odqp`, `am-srk-readings-s4-s5-njsh`, `am-sre-readings-s6-c5i4`, `am-sre-readings-s7-s8-lpje`, `am-sre-readings-s9-s10-3myq`); every displayed equation has a record with a semantic tree, concordance entries, a spoken form, authored R0-R3 texts, a passing dimension check, and a derivation chain with the move marked where the paper derives it (`am-srk-equations-30cq`, `am-sre-equations-2g3h`); every instrument caption of SR-01 through SR-13 has R0-R3 (`audit-readings.ts` report).
4. **Results and misconceptions:** every result has a results card with decoder and a probe whose named preset resolves (`am-sr-results-cards-k9ck`, fourteen cards); the ledger has at least five entries with instruments (`am-sr-misconceptions-cyci` has eight), each with resolving presets and anchors.
5. **Instruments:** SR-01 through SR-13 each have an explicit dispatcher case, an instance-scoped owner, a tape identity, passing fixtures, named preset scenarios, an honest execution label, `notModeled`, predict mode or a recorded exemption, show-the-code, an action contract, an embed route, a 320 px layout, keyboard operation, and reduced motion (`audit-instruments.ts` report). The mode tests pass with run ids: SR-04's `sr-04:1904` (`sr-04.mode1904.test.tsx` and its 1904-mode lane) and SR-02's `sr-02:apparatus` (`sr-02.apparatus.test.tsx`, with the resolution withheld and shown). The control-tape audit shows "the boost to 0.6c" (`the-boost-to-0.6c`) present. The instruments whose interaction primitives were proved in Batch D on runtime-fixture evaluators have re-run the exported family parity suite (`src/experiments/interactions/parity.suite.ts`) against their real owners, each cited by `logRunId`: SR-01 and SR-03 against `events.ts`, SR-08 against `fields.ts`. A parity run recorded with `ownerSource: runtime-fixture` is not evidence for this item. **Rendered embeds:** run the `am-inst-embed-route-rnyg` host-fixture lane parametrized over every `embeddable: true` relativity manifest at the audited commit and record one run id per instrument (attribution, execution label, `notModeled` line, parameters honored, no cookies or third-party requests).
6. **Discovery journey:** Journey III has its front door (§3's functional equation) and at least one side door (the constructed map), the no-algebra first encounter (`am-srk-first-encounter-471z`, also embedded by record id `entrance-special-relativity` as the arithmetic side door, with every door arriving at the §3 transformation), the nagging fact embedding `sr-02-apparatus-nagging-fact`, every shelf card dated and sourced (`am-disc-journey-iii-shelf-5z6q`, including Bradley's printed figures on `bradley-1729-aberration`, verified against the paper and kept distinct from SR-09's modern computation), every fork with a worked non-paper branch that fails on a stated constraint or is honestly marked equivalent (Lorentz's ether kinematics is marked equivalent in its formulas), and every check step computing live from accepted snapshots (`am-disc-journey-iii-chain-hpr7`).
7. **Margin:** records (a) through (h), the reception and confirmation records, and every confirmation cited by a relativity reading are present with primary sources and a named human acceptance (`am-sr-margin-entries-tn4l`).
8. **Tour:** the fifteen-minute tour exists and a reader with no physics background completed it and stated the paper's claim in one sentence (`am-sr-review-reader-qff7`).
9. **Gates and editorial acceptance:** `verify-content`, typecheck, lint, format, build, `ubs --diff`, the WASM artifact test, the scenario runner for `special-relativity`, and the Playwright suites (`am-srk-e2e-4qkd`, `am-sre-e2e-xmj6`) are green at the audited commit; German fidelity (`am-edn-review-german-relativity-0sr`), R2 readability (`am-sr-review-reader-qff7`), and the physics review (`am-sr-review-physics-omj8`) are recorded with reviewer names in the receipt. The German source review's scope includes the relativity gloss units of `am-edn-gloss-relativity-na8d`, because that review depends on the gloss and covers it in one pass; item 2's gloss units therefore need no separate German review, and this item records the one review record that covers both the translation and the gloss. The physics review record covers Journey III's `move.r0Summary` as well as the equation chains, so item 6's move and item 8's tour both rest on reviewed physics.
Every review record cited here is scoped to the audited revisions; a record that names a superseded revision is a gap, not evidence.

**Batch G exit evidence:** all ten sections covered (manifest report); the sign and frame test list (field transforms, invariants, general force law, Doppler, aberration, light-complex factors including the corrected discriminating fixture, mirror balance and interception at normal and oblique incidence, neutral conductor, analytic continuity, both electron conventions); depth parity confirmed in the physics reviewer's record for §§6-10 relative to §§1-5, stated qualitatively, never as a numeric score. The Batch E exit record (`am-srk-exit-audit-4owh`) is cited.

**Corrections register:** a section listing each correction raised during bead polishing with its resolution evidence or an open bead: the printed $4\pi$ in §9's $\rho$ and its SI conversion; the §1 concession footnote (margin record (g)) versus the plan's rigid-body description; the §3 printed use of $\varphi$; the §10 relations as printed; Bradley's figures on the Journey III card `bradley-1729-aberration` (verified against *Phil. Trans.* 35, 637), its check step, and SR-09's "modern computation" label; the owner of the teaching tape "the boost to 0.6c"; in `am-ref-waves-r53`, oblique mirror incidence and the SR-10 countermodel (specified in round 2), the mirror-frame ledger, and the label of the aberration fixture; in `am-ref-fields-6l9`, analytic continuity, analytic plane-wave residuals, and the general force law (specified in round 2), SR-02's excess through `gammaMinusOne`, and the moving-sphere total charge; in `am-ref-kinematics-tjq`, the Galilean deviation and medium increment helpers (specified in round 2) and the near-light shortfall helper; SR-04's `sr-04:1904` mode for the `/1904` desk and SR-02's apparatus mode for Journey III's nagging fact; the missing pre-1905 light-speed constant set in `am-ref-constants-xik`; harmonized frame-tagged quantity ids in the registry, with no legacy spelling (`lightSpeed`, bare `propagationAngle`, `lightComplexEnergy`, `chargeDensity`, or the retired electron-mass ids) surviving in any relativity manifest, scenario, tape, or equation record.

**Optional studios:** the status of `am-srk-sphere-clock-studio-lpxr` and `am-sre-field-lines-studio-4882` (present with run ids, or not built), recorded without changing the nine verdicts.

## Technical Approach

- Build the audit from machine reports (`verify-content.ts`, `audit-readings.ts`, `audit-instruments.ts`, `audit-misconceptions.ts`, the control-tape audit, `scripts/run-scenarios.ts`, test JSON reports, JSONL summaries, receipt fields) and human records; write the verdicts; commit the audit with evidence links.
- Validate every link with `scripts/validate-audit-evidence.ts` (created by `am-srk-exit-audit-4owh`), extended with link kinds for review records, embed-lane run ids, and parity-suite run ids with their `ownerSource`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The audit record has all nine items, the Batch G exit section, the corrections register, and the optional-studio status, each with a verdict and resolvable evidence.
- [ ] Rendered-embed evidence exists for each of SR-01 through SR-13, or the item is `not met` with a linked owner.
- [ ] Item 5 cites a real-owner parity run for SR-01, SR-03, and SR-08, each with `ownerSource` naming the real evaluator; a run recorded against a runtime fixture fails the evidence validator.
- [ ] Item 9 names the single German review record that covers both the translation and the gloss units, and the physics review record that covers Journey III's move summary.
- [ ] No item is marked met without concrete evidence; gaps link to open beads with owners; human review records are scoped to the audited revisions.
- [ ] The close reason lists each verdict and the audited commit hash.

## Test Plan

### Unit and integration tests

- `scripts/validate-audit-evidence.ts` over the committed record: every evidence link (files, test ids, run ids, review records, content ids, bead ids, embed-lane run ids, parity-suite run ids) resolves; fixture records with an unresolved link, a `met` verdict without evidence, a missing instrument in the embed list, a parity citation whose `ownerSource` is `runtime-fixture`, and a stale review record each fail with the line number.

### End-to-end tests

- Re-run `am-srk-e2e-4qkd`, `am-sre-e2e-xmj6`, and the parametrized embed-route lane at the audited commit and record the run ids.

### Structured logging

- `artifacts/test-logs/audit-dod-special-relativity/<log-run-id>.jsonl`: `timestamp`, `suite`, `logRunId`, `testId`, `beadId` (`am-dod-relativity-105y`), `paper`, `instrumentId` (for embed evidence), `outcome`, `durationMs`, `message`, and `extra: {dodItem, verdict, evidenceLink, linkKind, resolved, correctionId, reviewRecordId, revision, ownerSource}`.
- A failing validation run retains the audit record, the resolved evidence table, and the failing links as evidence.

## Considerations and Pitfalls

- Human review records are scoped to revisions; if content changed after a review, the audit notes which ids need re-review.
- Keep the nine dimensions separate in presentation and in any summary.
- A correction that is "known" but not resolved is a gap, not a footnote.
- One review record covering two artifacts (the translation and its gloss) is still one scope statement: the audit records which block and unit ids it names, not merely that the reviewer signed.

## Dependencies

Blocked by: `am-srk-exit-audit-4owh` (Batch E evidence); `am-sr-margin-entries-tn4l`, `am-sr-misconceptions-cyci`, `am-sr-results-cards-k9ck` (items 4 and 7); `am-sre-readings-s6-c5i4`, `am-sre-readings-s7-s8-lpje` (item 3); `am-sre-e2e-xmj6` (item 9); `am-sr-review-physics-omj8`, `am-sr-review-reader-qff7`, `am-edn-review-german-relativity-0sr` (editorial acceptance); `am-disc-journey-iii-shelf-5z6q`, `am-disc-journey-iii-chain-hpr7` (item 6); `am-edn-gloss-relativity-na8d` (item 2); `am-inst-embed-route-rnyg` (item 5 rendered embeds); `am-inst-show-the-code-4brv` (item 5); `am-edit-review-records-hofz` (the cross-projection review record for this paper's claim).

Unblocks: `am-launch-readiness-audit-sc9b`, `am-companion-dissertation-record-nbvv`, `am-disc-capstone-relativity-t8hg`, `am-found-prereq-audit-71ot`, `am-a11y-disabled-reader-rounds-jkjr`, `am-edit-comprehension-rounds-tcgi`, `am-test-real-device-check-iju4`, `am-a11y-reviewed-narration-r28u`, `am-later-language-editions-sp4e`.

title: Write the comprehension-testing protocol, consent materials, and rubric
description:
# Write the comprehension-testing protocol, consent materials, and rubric

**Epic:** `am-ep-editorial-13x` · **Batch:** B · **Priority:** P0 · **Plan sections:** §1.7, §1.9,
§7.1, §14.5, §17.1, §17.5, §17.6, §19.7, §21 (traceability only)

## Background

The fifth release question is whether an explanation helps a reader overcome the obstacle it was
written for (§17.1). Only people can answer it. The plan specifies a practical, humble protocol
(§17.5): recruit readers across different starting points; participation is voluntary, accessible,
and compensated where feasible; collect no diagnosis, credential, or placement score; run five to
eight participants per contrasting route as a problem-discovery design, not a statistically powered
claim; state the targeted change in understanding before each session; measure understanding with a
rubric rather than satisfaction; record the precise stumbling point with the passage or action id;
fix recurrent barriers first; and publish the scope of tested routes and known barriers without ever
claiming the site can teach every person. Perceived and measured learning can diverge (Deslauriers
and colleagues, PNAS 116, 2019), so satisfaction, confidence, time on page, and completion are not
substitutes for understanding.

The protocol governs every human reader session in the project: the slice and per-paper
comprehension rounds, the cross-paper verification rounds, the full acceptance scenario for Brownian
motion (§17.6), the fifteen-minute tour tests, the disabled-reader co-design sessions, and the final
product test at launch. It also supplies the observation format for the innovation stop rules
(§19.7): several capabilities expand "only after" observed readers resolve the obstacle, so the
protocol must record that observation in a form those beads can cite.

Because so many beads read these documents mechanically, the protocol owns two small pieces of code
as well as the prose: the participant-code parser every consumer uses, and the shared structural
test that validates round reports against the templates. Both paper slugs and route ids contain
hyphens (`brownian-motion`, `no-algebra`, `full-derivation`, `low-cost-phone`), so a naive split on
hyphens misreads a code; the parser exists so that mistake is made once, in one place, and caught by
tests.

It also owns one audit, for the same reason. The site says the five accomplishments overlap and are
not a ladder, and that a reader pursuing any of them never hits a dead end. That is a claim about
records, and a claim about records can be checked before a single participant is recruited.

## Scope

In scope: the protocol document, ethics and consent materials, facilitator script, rubric and
observation sheet, route definitions, participant code and reuse rules, the participant-code parser,
per-paper question banks, the stop-rule observation form, the preregistration template for
comparative experiments, templates for round reports and the public summary, the shared round-report
structural test, a structural test of the protocol itself, the five-accomplishment rubric and its
reach-sets, and the reachability audit `scripts/audit-reachability.ts`.

Out of scope, owned elsewhere: running rounds (`am-edit-comprehension-round-brownian-slice-vihm`,
`am-edit-comprehension-rounds-brownian-864m`, `am-edit-comprehension-rounds-mass-energy-tec7`,
`am-edit-comprehension-rounds-relativity-jdp3`, `am-edit-comprehension-rounds-light-quanta-vr69`,
`am-edit-comprehension-rounds-tcgi`); the Brownian acceptance scenario
(`am-bm-acceptance-scenario-vjn4`); accessibility co-design sessions
(`am-bm-slice-a11y-codesign-3xuq`, `am-a11y-disabled-reader-rounds-jkjr`); the final product test
(`am-launch-final-product-test-nzhn`); naming facilitators (`am-gov-owners-and-reviewers-hte`);
structured review records and the backfill of earlier session evidence
(`am-edit-review-records-hofz`); the support ladder itself and its stage defaults
(`am-disc-journey-framework-umbg`); the voice-lint engine and its vocabulary file
(`am-edit-voice-lint-trmf`); the coverage ledger whose input format the audit writes
(`am-cm-coverage-ledger-0ip`); the gate chain the audit registers a step in
(`am-scaf-quality-gates-ci-4xx`).

## Requirements

1. **Participants:** starting points to recruit: no algebra or graph fluency; rusty preparation;
non-native English; technically trained but physics-unfamiliar; strong mathematical preparation;
disabled readers using their own assistive setups; people on low-cost phones. No diagnosis,
credential, or placement score is collected. Personas (programmer, physician, engineer, student,
reader with no algebra) are editorial lenses; participants are never asked to identify with one.
2. **Routes:** `no-algebra` (first encounter, bridges, overview and show-every-step readings,
fifteen-minute tour); `nonvisual` (screen reader or other assistive technology, keyboard or switch
access, textual equivalents, action contracts, no graphics); `full-derivation` (full explanation and
show-every-step readings, derivation chains, source faces, equation interaction); `low-cost-phone`
(the reader's own or a provided inexpensive phone on a mobile network). These four ids are the only
route ids; every report, participant code, and review record uses them verbatim.
3. **Ethics and consent:** plain-language consent in accessible formats (a screen-reader-friendly
document, a large-print version, and an easy-read summary); the right to stop at any time without
explanation; data minimization (notes pseudonymized; recordings only with separate consent and never
stored in the repository); a retention period for notes and recordings set with the user's approval
and stated on the consent form; compensation policy; accommodations (breaks, remote or in-person,
the participant's own devices and assistive setups); a separate consent for delayed revisits; a
distress or discomfort procedure (pause, offer to stop, no pressure to continue). Follow
institutional review rules where an institution is involved, and equivalent practice otherwise.
4. **Participant codes and reuse:** codes of the form `<paper>-<route>-<YYYYMMDD>-<nn>` (for example
`brownian-motion-nonvisual-20270412-03`); the key linking codes to people is held by the facilitator
outside the repository. A participant who took part in a round on a paper is not recruited for the
final product test of that paper, and verification rounds use fresh participants where the barrier
was blocking, so learning effects do not hide a barrier.
   - **The parser.** `src/testing/docs/participantCodes.ts` exports `parseParticipantCode(code)`,
   returning `{paper, route, date, index}` or a typed failure, and `formatParticipantCode(parts)`.
   It resolves the code from the right, because both the paper slug and the route id contain
   hyphens: the last segment is `<nn>` (two digits), the one before it is `<YYYYMMDD>` (eight
   digits, a real calendar date), the next segment or segments form a route id from the closed list
   in requirement 2, and everything remaining is the paper slug, which must be one of
   `light-quanta`, `brownian-motion`, `special-relativity`, `mass-energy`,
   `molecular-dimensions`, or the slice form `brownian-motion-slice`. Anything else fails with a
   readable reason. Every consumer uses this function instead of its own pattern:
   `am-edit-review-records-hofz` (`scripts/backfill-review-records.ts`),
   `am-bm-acceptance-scenario-vjn4`, `am-launch-final-product-test-nzhn`, and the round beads'
   report validation.
5. **Session procedure per tested lesson:** state the targeted change in understanding in advance
(template sentence: "After this lesson the reader can …"); a brief pre-explanation question; observe
the interaction with neutral, non-leading prompts; ask for an explanation afterward; present a
different case (transfer); optional delayed revisit. Include the plan's probes: explain what a
formula predicts before and after interacting; identify which assumptions support a conclusion;
distinguish a simulation result from an observation.
6. **Rubric:** Meaning (can the reader say what is measured or compared?); Mechanism or argument
(can the reader explain the connection rather than describe the animation?); Prediction (can the
reader handle a changed value, geometry, or direction?); Assumptions (can the reader name a
condition under which the inference would need revision?); Evidence (can the reader distinguish an
observed dataset from a simulated consequence?); Navigation (can the reader locate the source and
obtain the missing explanation unaided?). The rubric is applied by a human observer; free text is
never graded by keywords.
7. **Stumbling-point codes:** `undefined-symbol`; `omitted-inference`; `misleading-visual-cue`;
`inaccessible-control`; `too-much-at-once`; each recorded with a passage anchor or action id.
8. **Stop-rule observation form** (§19.7): for a capability whose expansion waits on observed
readers (for example the missing-step explorer on the variance argument, the baseline and variant
comparison, the identifiability comparison, predict mode, show-the-code, the misconception ledger,
the gloss face for paper 4), record the capability id, the obstacle, how many participants met it,
how many resolved it and returned to the argument, and the facilitator's note. The form never
becomes a score.
9. **Question banks:** per paper, at least four questions per route, each with the anchor or action
id it targets, drawn from the chapter-end tasks, for example: two microscope traces look equally
restless, what additional comparison distinguishes different diffusion coefficients; a lamp gets
brighter below threshold, which output should not increase; two transformed events have a larger
spatial separation, why is that not a rod measurement; which subtraction removes the unknown
internal energy and which premise makes it useful.
10. **Comparative experiments:** a preregistration template stating outcome, assignment, exclusions,
analysis, and uncertainty in advance; with small traffic, report descriptive observations only.
11. **Templates:** a round report (pseudonymized, with rubric observations, targeted-change
outcomes, stumbling points with codes and ids, stop-rule observations, facilitator id, and date); a
public summary of tested routes and known barriers for the About page, with no universal teaching
claim.
    - The round report begins with front matter carrying `paper`, `route`, `date`, `buildCommit`,
    and `anchors` (the anchors and action ids the session exercised). The route-freshness check of
    `am-edit-comprehension-rounds-tcgi` and the review-record backfill of
    `am-edit-review-records-hofz` read exactly these fields, so the template and the shared
    structural test define them once.
12. **The shared structural test.** `src/testing/docs/roundReports.test.ts` belongs to this bead and
validates every report under `docs/comprehension/rounds/` against the template: required sections,
the front matter of requirement 11, route and paper values from the closed lists, participant codes
that `parseParticipantCode` accepts, a facilitator id shaped like an owners-table id, and no
personal data. Round beads add their reports to the corpus it validates; they never fork the test.

13. **The five accomplishments as a rubric, and as a reachability audit.**

The site names five things a reader may be trying to do today, and insists they overlap rather than
rank. That is currently a statement of values with nothing behind it. It becomes a rubric with two
halves: what counts as a meaningful outcome for each, and **what must stay within reach** while a
reader pursues it. This is a second instrument, not a replacement: requirement 6's six dimensions are
what a human observer scores during a session, and this table records what the participant was trying
to do and what the records must keep available while they try.

| Accomplishment | A meaningful outcome in a round | What must remain within reach |
|---|---|---|
| Appreciate | The participant explains why the question mattered and what was surprising about the answer | A concrete example and the original passage |
| Explain | The participant reconstructs the main reasoning in words, a picture, or a small table | Definitions, the assumptions in force, and a bridge to the symbols |
| Predict | The participant anticipates how a specified change affects an observable, and says why | Units, a numerical example, and the model that applies |
| Derive | The participant reproduces the mathematical steps and identifies each premise | Every intermediate step, any alternative derivation, and the printed notation |
| Critique | The participant separates what follows, what is suggested, what has been measured, and what remains undetermined | Countermodels, uncertainty, primary sources, and later qualifications |

Two uses, and they are different:

- **In a round.** Each participant is asked at the start what they are trying to do today, in ordinary
  words, and the session record stores the accomplishment they chose. The middle column is the
  outcome the facilitator scores against, per participant per argument, beside the six rubric
  dimensions. No participant is told they achieved a "level", and the accomplishment is never stored
  as a property of the person, only of the session. A participant may change it mid-session, and that
  is recorded as information about the material.
- **As an audit, before rounds run.** The right column names records that already exist, so it can be
  checked mechanically. `scripts/audit-reachability.ts` walks every argument node and reports, in the
  input format of `am-cm-coverage-ledger-0ip`, which of the five reach-sets does not resolve:
  - *Appreciate*: the passage's `example` action (`am-read-passage-actions-vbe`) and a source anchor.
  - *Explain*: R1 and R2 readings, plus at least one resolving `FoundationLink`.
  - *Predict*: an instrument whose outputs carry units, plus a printed check or a golden scenario.
  - *Derive*: a `DerivationChain` reaching the node's target with no step missing its R1 reason, plus
    every alternate route exported for that target, plus the printed notation form.
  - *Critique*: a fork branch or countermodel case, the node's `limitations`, its `sources[]`, and any
    reception links naming its result.
  A node with an unresolved reach-set is reported, not failed. It is an authoring gap the
  comprehension rounds would otherwise discover one participant at a time.
- **Scheduling.** The protocol document, its materials, the parser and the two structural tests do not
  wait for anything. The audit walks the compiled corpus, so it lands once the compiler exists and
  registers a reporting step in the gate chain of `am-scaf-quality-gates-ci-4xx`; it never blocks the
  recruitment the rest of this bead enables.

14. **The support ladder is an empirical question, not a settled one.**

`am-disc-journey-framework-umbg` gives every stage a support ladder: `workedExample`,
`partialComparison`, optional `prediction`, `explanation`, `transferCase`, with a direct path to the
explanation at every point. The ladder is right. What is missing is a written commitment that **the
default position on that ladder is measured here, not assumed**, and the reason it matters.

- There is no defensible general rule that minimal guidance is best, and there is no defensible
  general rule that it is worthless. The two studies most often used as slogans do not settle it:
  - Klahr and Nigam (2004), on elementary science instruction, found direct instruction more
    effective for initial acquisition **in the task they tested**.
  - Schwartz and Martin (2004), in statistics, found value in an invention activity **as preparation
    for subsequent learning**.
  - Different populations, different tasks, different outcome measures. Record both citations in the
    bibliography with role `secondary`, verify author, year, journal and pages against the articles
    before either is cited in a published protocol document, and record a null finding if a detail
    does not check out. Neither is quoted to a reader; they are recorded here so a later agent cannot
    reopen this as a matter of opinion.
- **What the protocol therefore does.** For each argument tested, the round records the support level
  the participant actually needed to reach their chosen accomplishment: which rungs they used, in
  which order, whether they went straight to the explanation, and where they stopped. The middle
  column of requirement 13 decides whether the accomplishment was reached; the ladder record says
  what it took.
- **What the protocol therefore forbids.** No protocol document, report, or visitor-facing string may
  claim that discovery learning, productive struggle, or minimal guidance is generally superior, or
  that direct instruction is. The claim the site is entitled to make is narrower and more useful:
  *for this argument, readers in these rounds needed this much support.* That phrasing is the one the
  consolidated findings of `am-edit-comprehension-rounds-tcgi` use, and the ban is registered as a
  rule set with `am-edit-voice-lint-trmf` so the About page and the tested-routes summary cannot
  drift into a pedagogy claim.
- **What changes as a result.** A journey stage whose rounds show readers consistently going straight
  to the explanation has its authored default support raised for that stage, recorded with the round
  ids that justified it, by the bead that owns the stage. A stage whose rounds show readers using the
  partial comparison productively keeps it. Neither is a sitewide setting: the ladder default is per
  stage, and the evidence is per stage.
- Nothing here is scored, ranked, or stored against a participant, and the consent materials and
  privacy rules of requirement 3 are unchanged.

## Technical Approach

Write `docs/comprehension/protocol.md` and `docs/comprehension/materials/`
(`consent-plain-language.md`, `consent-screen-reader.html`, `consent-large-print.md`,
`consent-easy-read.md`, `facilitator-script.md`, `observation-sheet.md`, `routes.md`,
`participant-codes.md`, `stop-rule-observation.md`, `preregistration-template.md`,
`question-banks/<paper-slug>.md`, `round-report-template.md`, `public-summary-template.md`). Add
`src/testing/docs/participantCodes.ts` and the two structural tests. The parser is pure and has no
filesystem or network dependency, so every consumer can import it cheaply. Add
`scripts/audit-reachability.ts`, a pure function over the compiled corpus plus a CLI, with its shared
report utilities beside the other audits, and register its gate step as a reporting step.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The protocol and all materials exist and cover every requirement above.
- [ ] Consent materials exist in the accessible formats listed.
- [ ] The rubric dimensions and the five stumbling-point codes appear verbatim on the observation
sheet.
- [ ] Question banks exist for all four papers with at least four questions per route, each naming
its target anchor or action id.
- [ ] The stop-rule observation form and the preregistration template exist.
- [ ] `parseParticipantCode` exists, is exported, and is the only participant-code parser in the
repository (proven by a static test).
- [ ] A structural test confirms the protocol's required sections and the templates' required
fields, and `roundReports.test.ts` validates the reports directory.
- [ ] The protocol document contains the five-accomplishment rubric with both columns, presented
beside the six observation dimensions and never as a ladder, and the session record stores the chosen
accomplishment per session and per change, never against a person.
- [ ] `scripts/audit-reachability.ts` reports, per argument node, which of the five reach-sets does
not resolve, in the coverage ledger's input format, and runs in the gate chain as a report rather
than a failure.
- [ ] On the Brownian §§4–5 fixture corpus the audit resolves all five reach-sets, and a seeded node
with its `limitations` removed is reported as failing the Critique reach-set.
- [ ] The protocol records, per participant per argument, which support rungs were used, in what
order, and where the participant stopped.
- [ ] Klahr and Nigam (2004) and Schwartz and Martin (2004) exist as bibliography records with role
`secondary` and a verification note; neither is cited in a published document before its details are
verified.
- [ ] The voice lint fails a seeded "discovery learning works better", "productive struggle is
essential" and "direct instruction is more effective" in any protocol, report or visitor-facing
string, and passes the per-stage phrasing.
- [ ] A support-default change to a journey stage records the round ids that justified it, and a
change with no round ids fails review.

## Test Plan

### Unit and integration tests
`src/testing/docs/comprehensionProtocol.test.ts`:
- the protocol contains headings for participants, routes, consent, participant codes and reuse,
procedure, rubric, accomplishments and reach-sets, stumbling-point codes, stop-rule observations,
question banks, comparative experiments, support-ladder evidence, and templates;
- the observation sheet lists all six rubric dimensions and all five codes verbatim, and the
accomplishment table's five rows with both columns;
- each question bank has at least four questions per route, and every question line carries an
anchor (`#s<n>…`) or action id (`<instrument>:<action>`) placeholder;
- the round report template contains the fields rounds beads validate (front matter with paper,
route, date, build commit and anchors; routes, participant codes, facilitator id, date, rubric
observations, chosen accomplishment, support rungs used, stumbling points, stop-rule observations,
findings with bead links);
- a privacy scan of `docs/comprehension/` finds no email addresses, phone numbers, or participant
codes in example text other than the documented fictitious example;
- no document in `docs/comprehension/` presents the five accomplishments as ordered levels.

`src/testing/docs/participantCodes.test.ts`:
- `brownian-motion-nonvisual-20270412-03` parses to paper `brownian-motion`, route `nonvisual`, date
`2027-04-12`, index 3;
- `brownian-motion-full-derivation-20270412-01` parses correctly, proving a hyphenated route beside
a hyphenated paper slug;
- `brownian-motion-slice-low-cost-phone-20270412-11` parses to the slice paper and the
`low-cost-phone` route;
- `mass-energy-no-algebra-20270412-7` fails (index not two digits);
- `brownian-motion-nonvisual-2027-04-12-3` fails (the hyphenated date form), with a message naming
the expected form;
- an unknown route (`brownian-motion-skimming-20270412-03`) and an unknown paper
(`browian-motion-nonvisual-20270412-03`) each fail naming the closed list;
- `20270230` fails as an impossible date;
- `formatParticipantCode(parseParticipantCode(code))` returns the original string for every valid
fixture;
- a static scan finds no other regular expression matching the code shape outside this module.

`src/testing/docs/roundReports.test.ts`: a fixture report with complete front matter passes; missing
`buildCommit`, an unknown route, a participant code the parser rejects, a facilitator id containing
an at sign, and an embedded email address each fail with the file and line.

`src/testing/docs/reachabilityAudit.test.ts` (real compiler, real fixture corpus):
- all five reach-sets resolve for the Brownian §§4–5 nodes;
- removing the node's `limitations` reports Critique; removing the `example` action reports
Appreciate; removing the units from an instrument output reports Predict; removing a chain step's R1
reason reports Derive; removing the only resolving `FoundationLink` reports Explain;
- the report validates against the coverage ledger's input schema;
- the audit never fails the build, and its exit code is 0 with findings present.

`src/testing/docs/sessionRecord.test.ts`: an accomplishment is stored per session with a timestamp
and a change history; a fixture attempting to store it against a participant identifier fails schema
validation.

`src/testing/docs/supportLadderRecord.test.ts`: rungs used, order, and stopping point round-trip; a
support-default change without round ids fails the review-record check of
`am-edit-review-records-hofz`.

`voiceLint.integration.test.ts` (addition): the pedagogy-claim rule set, with one failing fixture per
banned claim and a passing per-stage phrasing.

### End-to-end tests
A dry run of one session with an internal volunteer is recorded in
`docs/comprehension/materials/rehearsal.md` as a facilitation rehearsal (not counted as a round),
noting any procedure changes it caused.

No browser lane belongs to a protocol document. The reachability audit runs in the gate chain
(`am-scaf-quality-gates-ci-4xx`) over the fixture corpus, and its report is compared with a golden
file so a regression in reachability is visible in the same run that introduced it.

### Structured logging
The structural tests write `{timestamp, suite: "comprehension-protocol", logRunId, testId, beadId,
file, check, outcome, message}` to `artifacts/test-logs/comprehension-protocol/<log-run-id>.jsonl`,
and the round-report test writes the same shape with `suite: "round-reports"` to
`artifacts/test-logs/round-reports/<log-run-id>.jsonl`. A failing structural test retains a copy of
the offending document under `artifacts/test-logs/<suite>/<log-run-id>/evidence/<testId>/`, copied
and never deleted. Session reports themselves are Markdown with pseudonymous participant codes.

The audit writes `{timestamp, suite: "comprehension", logRunId, testId, beadId, paper, argumentId,
accomplishment, reachSet, resolved, missingTarget, rule, outcome, durationMs, message}` to
`artifacts/test-logs/comprehension/<log-run-id>.jsonl`, and its report is retained under
`artifacts/audits/reachability/<tool-run-id>/`, named with a tool run id because it is a tool
execution whose artifacts persist.

Round records log `{sessionId (a per-session code, never a person), paper, argumentId,
accomplishmentChosen, accomplishmentChanged, rungsUsed, rungOrder, stoppedAt, outcomeReached,
facilitator}` beside the standard fields. No free-text participant response is ever written to a log.

## Considerations and Pitfalls

- Never grade free text by keywords; the rubric is applied by a human observer.
- Keep sessions short and respectful; difficulty should come from the ideas, not the procedure.
- An incorrect explanation is information about the product, never a judgment of the participant.
- Recruitment takes time; publishing the protocol early in Batch B lets the slice round recruit
while the slice is finished.
- The parser is deliberately strict. A code that does not parse is a recording error to fix at the
source, never something a consumer works around with its own pattern.
- The five accomplishments are not five levels, and the rubric must never be laid out as a ladder in
the protocol document or in a report. A mathematician choosing Appreciate is doing what the site
invited.
- The reachability audit checks that something **resolves**, not that it is good. A resolving
foundation link to a thin lesson still reports as resolved; the rounds are what test quality.
- Do not let the audit become a build gate. A node missing a countermodel is an authoring queue item,
and failing the build on it would push authors toward stub countermodels.
- The two studies are recorded to close a debate, not to open one. Neither is evidence about this
site's readers, and the protocol must not present them as such.
- The temptation after a good round is to generalize. "Readers understood the variance argument
better after inventing a statistic" is a finding about one argument and a handful of readers; a
sentence about how people learn is not.
- A participant who changes accomplishment mid-session has told you something valuable about the
material. Record it as a property of the argument, never of the person.

## Dependencies

Blocked by: `am-gov-repo-bootstrap-p5t` (repository and `docs/` exist).

Proposed in review (no edge exists yet; each is a prerequisite of the reachability audit only, not of
the protocol document, the materials, the parser or the two structural tests):
- `am-cm-compiler-core-oa7`: the compiled argument nodes, chains, foundation links and instrument
outputs the audit walks.
- `am-cm-coverage-ledger-0ip`: the input format the audit's report is written in.
- `am-scaf-quality-gates-ci-4xx`: the gate registry where the audit registers a reporting step.
- `am-edit-voice-lint-trmf`: the pedagogy-claim rule set is registered there rather than kept here.

Unblocks: `am-bm-acceptance-scenario-vjn4`, `am-bm-slice-a11y-codesign-3xuq`,
`am-a11y-disabled-reader-rounds-jkjr`, `am-edit-review-records-hofz` (its backfill script uses
`parseParticipantCode`), `am-edit-comprehension-round-brownian-slice-vihm`,
`am-edit-comprehension-rounds-brownian-864m`, `am-edit-comprehension-rounds-mass-energy-tec7`,
`am-edit-comprehension-rounds-relativity-jdp3`, `am-edit-comprehension-rounds-light-quanta-vr69`,
`am-edit-comprehension-rounds-tcgi`. A bead of the separate iPhone app plan
(`am-app-at-sessions-n6vj`) also uses this protocol; app work never delays a website batch.

title: Run the first comprehension rounds on the Brownian reference slice
description:
# Run the first comprehension rounds on the Brownian reference slice

**Epic:** `am-ep-editorial-13x` · **Batch:** B (after the slice exit demonstration) · **Priority:**
P1 · **Plan sections:** §17.5, §17.6, §19.2, §19.7 (traceability only) · **Human gate**

## Background

The reference slice (Brownian motion §§4–5 with the required explanation of the diffusion
coefficient) is the first place a reader can meet the whole product: a source passage, its
translation, readings at every depth, semantic equations, instruments driven by a real seeded owner,
the no-algebra entrance, the nonvisual actions, and the return stack. The Brownian acceptance
scenario (`am-bm-acceptance-scenario-vjn4`) runs the plan's five-step scenario with one reader
unfamiliar with algebra and a nonvisual check before the architecture freeze. These rounds are
broader: five to eight participants per contrasting route, measured with the protocol's rubric, so
recurring barriers show up before three more papers copy the same patterns.

They also supply the observations the innovation stop rules wait for (§19.7): the missing-step
explorer expands beyond the variance-of-a-sum step "only after observed readers resolve the obstacle
and return" (`am-reason-missing-step-explorer-rsl4`); predict mode expands beyond the slice only
after observed readers show it resolves a misunderstanding (`am-inst-predict-mode-ti7m`);
show-the-code and the misconception callouts are P1 innovations with the same condition; and the
no-algebra first encounter is the pattern the other papers reuse (`am-bm-first-encounter-fjvh`).

## Scope

In scope: recruiting under the protocol; running rounds on the four routes against a recorded slice
build; recording rubric observations, stumbling points, and stop-rule observations; filing and
triaging findings; a follow-up round verifying fixes for blocking barriers; converting the reports
into structured review records.

Out of scope, owned elsewhere: the protocol, its materials, the participant-code parser, and the
shared round-report structural test (`am-edit-comprehension-protocol-ouih`); the §17.6 acceptance
scenario (`am-bm-acceptance-scenario-vjn4`); accessibility co-design of individual actions
(`am-bm-slice-a11y-codesign-3xuq`); rounds on the complete Brownian paper
(`am-edit-comprehension-rounds-brownian-864m`); cross-paper consolidation
(`am-edit-comprehension-rounds-tcgi`).

## Requirements

1. **Build under test:** a production build of the slice at a recorded commit (with the WASM
artifact digest), served locally or through a protected, authorized preview; never a public
deployment made for the study without the user's authorization.
2. **Routes and size:** `no-algebra`, `nonvisual`, `full-derivation`, and `low-cost-phone`, each
with five to eight participants recruited across the protocol's starting points; participant codes
per the protocol, in the form `<paper>-<route>-<YYYYMMDD>-<nn>` with the paper part
`brownian-motion-slice` for these rounds, validated by `parseParticipantCode`
(`src/testing/docs/participantCodes.ts`).
3. **Targeted lessons** (the targeted change is stated in advance for each):
   - zero signed average is not no movement: for the four displacements $-3, -1, +1, +3$ the signed
   mean is 0 while the mean square is 5, so the typical size is $\sqrt{5} \approx 2.24$, and that is
   why the square is the useful summary;
   - the square-root time dependence of the typical displacement, $\lambda_x = \sqrt{2Dt}$, and
   where it appears in §5;
   - the viscosity comparison: doubling viscosity halves the diffusion coefficient and changes the
   RMS displacement by $1/\sqrt{2} \approx 0.707$, not by one half;
   - the variance-of-a-sum step (cross terms vanish) in the missing-step explorer;
   - distinguishing a simulated trajectory from observed data, and why programmed motion does not
   independently prove molecules exist;
   - navigation: locating the §4 and §5 source passages and returning to the interrupted sentence.
   Questions come from the Brownian question bank, including "two microscope traces look equally
   restless; what additional comparison distinguishes different diffusion coefficients?"
4. **Stop-rule observations:** for the missing-step explorer, predict mode on BM-01, show-the-code,
the misconception callouts, and the first-encounter pattern, record the protocol's stop-rule
observation form.
5. **Findings:** every stumbling point recorded with its code (`undefined-symbol`,
`omitted-inference`, `misleading-visual-cue`, `inaccessible-control`, `too-much-at-once`) and anchor
or action id; each finding filed as a bead or bead comment against the owning bead (the generalized
component when the barrier is architectural); blocking barriers fixed and verified in a follow-up
round with fresh participants on the affected route.
6. **Reports:** `docs/comprehension/rounds/<YYYY-MM-DD>-brownian-motion-slice-<route>.md` using the
protocol template, pseudonymized, with front matter carrying `paper`, `route`, `date`,
`buildCommit`, and `anchors` (the anchors and action ids exercised, read by the route-freshness
check of `am-edit-comprehension-rounds-tcgi`), the facilitator id from `docs/OWNERS.md` with role
`comprehension-facilitator`, and the date.
7. **Review records:** each round is recorded as a `comprehension-round` review record
(`am-edit-review-records-hofz`) citing its report in `sessionRef`. Rounds that happen before that
bead lands are converted by its backfill script, which accepts only protocol participant codes and
owners-table facilitator ids, so reports must be written in that form from the first session.

## Human Gate

Recruitment, facilitation, and observation require people. Agents may prepare the build, session
plans, task cards, and anchors list; analyze de-identified notes; file findings; and draft review
records for the facilitator to confirm. Close this bead only when all four routes have a completed
round, every finding is triaged, blocking barriers have a verification result, and each report names
its facilitator id and date. Agents never close it on their own judgment, never sign a review
record, and never simulate participants.

## Technical Approach

Prepare a session plan per route that lists the targeted changes, the question bank items, and the
exact anchors and actions, so the report front matter can be filled mechanically. Before sessions,
run the slice e2e suite (`am-bm-slice-e2e-sbqu`) in every lane on the same commit and fix known
automated failures first.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Round reports exist for the four routes on the recorded slice build, and
`src/testing/docs/roundReports.test.ts` passes on them.
- [ ] Every stumbling point has a code, an anchor or action id, and a linked bead or comment.
- [ ] Stop-rule observations exist for each capability listed in Requirement 4.
- [ ] Blocking barriers show a verification result or an explicit open status.
- [ ] Review records exist for each round, naming a facilitator listed in `docs/OWNERS.md`.
- [ ] No personal data is stored in the repository.

## Test Plan

### Unit and integration tests
`src/testing/docs/roundReports.test.ts` (owned by `am-edit-comprehension-protocol-ouih`, shared
across round beads) validates each report: the template's required sections, front matter with
paper, route, date, build commit, and anchors, route and paper values from the protocol's closed
lists, participant codes that `parseParticipantCode` accepts, and no personal data. This bead adds
its reports to that corpus and forks no second test.
### End-to-end tests
The pre-session slice e2e run in every lane, with log run ids attached to the session plan. When a
finding is reproducible in the browser, its fix adds an automated regression to
`am-bm-slice-e2e-sbqu` or `am-bm-e2e-complete-gmdb`.
### Structured logging
Session reports are Markdown. The pre-session runs log JSONL as in the slice suite; the structural
test logs `{timestamp, suite: "round-reports", logRunId, testId, file, check, outcome, message}` to
`artifacts/test-logs/round-reports/<log-run-id>.jsonl`, retaining a copy of a failing report under
that run's evidence directory.

## Considerations and Pitfalls

- Do not coach participants toward answers; record where the page failed them.
- Small samples reveal problems; they do not estimate effect sizes.
- Improve the explanation before adding a feature; a stop-rule observation that the obstacle was not
resolved is a reason to revise, not to expand.
- These rounds must not delay `am-bm-slice-retrospective-pp09`; architecture-relevant findings are
filed against the generalized components as soon as they are observed.
- A participant who says the animation "shows molecules hitting the particle" has met a real
instrument problem, not a comprehension failure: the slice's simulated trajectory is a consequence
of assumptions, and the page must say so.

## Dependencies

Blocked by: `am-edit-comprehension-protocol-ouih` (procedure, materials, participant-code parser,
and the shared report test), `am-bm-slice-exit-demo-5922` (the demonstrated slice),
`am-gov-owners-and-reviewers-hte` (facilitator ids), `am-edit-review-records-hofz` (the
`comprehension-round` record type and the backfill rules).

Unblocks: `am-edit-comprehension-rounds-brownian-864m` (the complete-paper rounds build on these
findings), `am-edit-comprehension-rounds-tcgi` (cross-paper consolidation).

title: Run comprehension rounds on the complete Brownian motion paper
description:
# Run comprehension rounds on the complete Brownian motion paper

**Epic:** `am-ep-editorial-13x` · **Batch:** C (after the Brownian definition of done) ·
**Priority:** P1 · **Plan sections:** §8.2, §17.5, §19.3 (Batch C), §19.7, §21 (traceability only) ·
**Human gate**

## Background

Batch C completes the Brownian paper: osmotic pressure, the force balance, the diffusion
coefficient, the full §2 argument, the independent inference route, measurement bias, and the
kitchen real-data mode (§19.3). The slice rounds tested §§4–5; these rounds test what the complete
paper adds, and they re-test the slice routes on the finished paper so the findings from
`am-edit-comprehension-round-brownian-slice-vihm` can be confirmed fixed. They run as soon as the
paper meets its definition of done, while the mass–energy, relativity, and light-quanta papers can
still learn from the result.

These rounds also supply stop-rule observations for the Batch C innovations (§19.7): identifiability
and the observation-error comparison ("unknown information is visible and the uncertainty
calculation remains valid"), the baseline and variant comparison
(`am-reason-hold-fixed-comparison-xgxw`), and the kitchen real-data mode ("the access need is
tested").

## Scope

In scope: rounds on the four routes against the complete Brownian paper; rubric observations,
stumbling points, and stop-rule observations; findings and follow-up verification; review records.

Out of scope, owned elsewhere: the protocol, its materials, the participant-code parser, and the
shared round-report structural test (`am-edit-comprehension-protocol-ouih`); the slice rounds
(`am-edit-comprehension-round-brownian-slice-vihm`); the non-physicist R2 review and fifteen-minute
tour test (`am-bm-review-reader-x77h`); cross-paper consolidation
(`am-edit-comprehension-rounds-tcgi`).

## Requirements

1. **Build under test:** a production build of the complete paper at a recorded commit, served
locally or through a protected, authorized preview.
2. **Routes and size:** `no-algebra`, `nonvisual`, `full-derivation`, and `low-cost-phone`, five to
eight fresh participants per route (not reused from the slice rounds), recruited across the
protocol's starting points, with participant codes in the protocol's form validated by
`parseParticipantCode`.
3. **Targeted lessons** (stated in advance):
   - osmotic pressure of suspended particles as the same kind of pressure as dissolved molecules
   (§1), and the free-energy argument (§2);
   - the drift–diffusion balance and the diffusion coefficient $D = RT/(N\,6\pi k P)$ in Einstein's
   notation (his $k$ is the viscosity of the liquid and $P$ is the particle radius; the modern
   symbols appear only in the modern-notation layer), and why a more viscous liquid gives slower
   spreading: doubling the viscosity halves $D$ and changes the RMS displacement by $1/\sqrt{2}
   \approx 0.707$, not by one half;
   - inference of $N$ from observed displacements with an honest interval, and why the historical
   inference must not hide a modern Boltzmann constant in its data;
   - identifiability: radius and molecular number cannot both be recovered from diffusivity alone;
   - measurement bias: localization noise and drift change the naive estimate;
   - the Exner velocity trap and the Nägeli fork in Journey II, labeled as a route one could take
   and never as mockery of either man;
   - the slice lessons re-tested for regressions.
   Questions come from the Brownian question bank.
4. **Stop-rule observations:** identifiability and observation-error comparison, baseline and
variant comparison, the kitchen real-data mode, and any slice capability whose earlier observation
was "not resolved."
5. **Slice follow-up:** each slice finding is marked fixed, still present, or not applicable.
6. **Findings:** every stumbling point recorded with its code and anchor or action id; findings

# Run comprehension rounds on the complete light-quanta paper

**Epic:** `am-ep-editorial-13x` · **Batch:** F (after the light-quanta definition of done) · **Priority:** P1 · **Plan sections:** §3.3, §5.3, §8.1, §9.2, §17.5, §19.3 (Batch F), §19.7, §21 (traceability only) · **Human gate**

## Background

The light-quanta paper is the most anachronism-prone of the four. Popular accounts open with the "ultraviolet catastrophe" (Ehrenfest's phrase from 1911), say Planck had already proposed light quanta (he had proposed energy elements for material oscillators, not radiation behaving as independent quanta), and claim that the photoelectric effect proves photons. The paper itself is a heuristic: in the Wien regime, the entropy of dilute monochromatic radiation depends on volume the way the entropy of an ideal gas of independent particles does, and Einstein draws a restricted inference from that analogy, then tests its consequences on fluorescence, the photoelectric effect, and ionization. Batch F's exit evidence asks that all nine sections be covered, that the Wien limitation be visible, that energy and rate controls be demonstrably distinct, and that the Planck branch be worked fairly (§19.3). These rounds test whether readers on every route come away with that restricted, honest claim.

## Scope

In scope: rounds on the four routes against the complete light-quanta paper; rubric observations, stumbling points, and stop-rule observations; findings and follow-up verification; review records.

Out of scope, owned elsewhere: the protocol (`am-edit-comprehension-protocol-ouih`); the non-physicist R2 review and fifteen-minute tour test (`am-lq-review-reader-5alq`); cross-paper consolidation (`am-edit-comprehension-rounds-tcgi`).

## Requirements

1. **Build under test:** a production build of the complete paper at a recorded commit, served locally or through a protected, authorized preview.
2. **Routes and size:** `no-algebra` (the first encounter "independent objects in half a space," the fifteen-minute tour, overview and show-every-step readings), `nonvisual` (ratio entry or half, same, or double choices instead of resizing a volume; channel selection instead of dragging energy), `full-derivation`, and `low-cost-phone`, five to eight participants per route across the protocol's starting points.
3. **Targeted lessons** (stated in advance):
   - what the wave description explains well (LQ-01) and why the paper does not claim that light is not a wave;
   - independent placement: the probability that $n$ independent objects are all found in a sub-volume $v$ of $v_0$ is $(v/v_0)^n$, while objects locked together give $v/v_0$, which shows that independence is the premise (LQ-05);
   - the volume dependence of the entropy of dilute monochromatic radiation in the Wien regime: §4 prints $S - S_0 = \frac{E}{\beta\nu}\lg\frac{v}{v_0}$ ("lg" is the natural logarithm), and §6 rewrites it as $S - S_0 = \frac{R}{N}\lg\left[\left(\frac{v}{v_0}\right)^{\frac{N}{R}\frac{E}{\beta\nu}}\right]$ to compare it with the §5 form for $n$ independent points, $S - S_0 = R\frac{n}{N}\lg\frac{v}{v_0}$; the comparison reads the radiation as $n = \frac{N}{R}\frac{E}{\beta\nu}$ independent quanta of energy $R\beta\nu/N$, and the analogy stops outside the dilute Wien regime (LQ-04, LQ-06);
   - honest spectral coordinates: an energy density per unit frequency and one per unit wavelength are different functions, so relabeling the axis does not preserve the density (LQ-03);
   - energy versus rate in the photoelectric apparatus: brighter light changes how many electrons leave, not the maximum energy of each, so a brighter lamp below threshold should not increase the stopping potential (LQ-08; question bank: "a lamp gets brighter below threshold; which output should not increase?");
   - the printed check of about 4.3 V for $\nu = 1.03\times10^{15}\,\mathrm{s^{-1}}$ as a reproduction of what Einstein printed from his constants (in the printed gram-equivalent representation, 4.34 V), and Millikan's 1916 measurements as later evidence, not something on the 1904 shelf;
   - the fork between Planck's oscillator energy elements and radiation behaving as independent quanta, worked fairly;
   - notation: in paper 1, $L$ is the speed of light, $\beta$ is Wien's constant (modern $h/k_B$), $P$ is the work function, and $N$ is Avogadro's number.
4. **Stop-rule observations:** predict mode on LQ-08, show-the-code on LQ-03 or LQ-04, and the misconception callouts ("the photoelectric effect proves photons," "Planck already proposed light quanta," "the ultraviolet catastrophe drove the 1905 paper").
5. **Findings:** every stumbling point recorded with its code and anchor or action id; findings filed against owning beads; blocking barriers verified in a follow-up round with fresh participants. Record explicitly any participant explanation that turns the heuristic into a proof or imports photon vocabulary as a premise, because those are anachronism findings as well as comprehension findings.
6. **Reports and records:** `docs/comprehension/rounds/<YYYY-MM-DD>-light-quanta-<route>.md` with front matter (paper, route, date, build commit, anchors), facilitator id, and date; one `comprehension-round` review record per round.

## Human Gate

Recruitment, facilitation, and observation require people. Agents may prepare builds, session plans, and anchors lists; analyze de-identified notes; file findings; and draft review records. Close this bead only when all four routes have a completed round, every finding is triaged, blocking barriers have a verification result, and each report names its facilitator id and date. Agents never close it on their own judgment, and never simulate participants.

## Technical Approach

Prepare session plans per route listing targeted changes, question bank items, and anchors, grouped by the paper's three movements (the radiation difficulty and entropy argument, §§1–6; the applications, §§7–9). Before sessions, run `am-lq-e2e-x7z0` in every lane on the same commit.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Round reports exist for the four routes on the complete paper.
- [ ] Every stumbling point has a code, an anchor or action id, and a linked bead or comment.
- [ ] Stop-rule observations exist for the capabilities in Requirement 4.
- [ ] Anachronism findings are recorded separately and sent to the owning content beads.
- [ ] Blocking barriers show a verification result or an explicit open status, and review records exist for each round.
- [ ] No personal data is stored in the repository.

## Test Plan

### Unit and integration tests
`src/testing/docs/roundReports.test.ts` (owned by `am-edit-comprehension-protocol-ouih`) validates every report (required sections, front matter, pseudonymous codes only).
### End-to-end tests
The pre-session `am-lq-e2e-x7z0` run in every lane, with log run ids attached to the session plan; reproducible findings add regressions to that suite.
### Structured logging
Session reports are Markdown; the pre-session runs and the structural test log JSONL per the standard (`suite: "round-reports"` for the structural test, `artifacts/test-logs/round-reports/<log-run-id>.jsonl`).

## Considerations and Pitfalls

- A participant who says the simulator "shows there is a threshold" has met the circularity the plan warns about: a simulator programmed with a threshold is not evidence that nature has one. Record whether the page made that distinction visible.
- The closing sections (§§7–9) are where explanations thin out; check that each route reaches them.
- If a page, caption, or session plan shows the §4 entropy law with an extra factor $R/N$ in front of $\frac{E}{\beta\nu}$, file it as a physics finding against the owning content bead: with $\beta = h/k_B$, $\frac{E}{\beta\nu}$ already has the dimension of entropy, and the factor $R/N$ appears only in the §6 rewriting, where the exponent carries $N/R$.
- Do not coach participants; small samples reveal problems and do not estimate effect sizes.

## Dependencies

Blocked by: `am-edit-comprehension-protocol-ouih` (procedure, materials, and the round report template), `am-dod-light-quanta-7as8` (the complete paper), `am-gov-owners-and-reviewers-hte` (facilitator ids), `am-edit-review-records-hofz` (the `comprehension-round` record type).

Unblocks: `am-edit-comprehension-rounds-tcgi` (cross-paper consolidation).

# Run comprehension rounds on the complete mass-energy paper

**Epic:** `am-ep-editorial-13x` · **Batch:** D (after the mass–energy definition of done) ·
**Priority:** P1 · **Plan sections:** §8.4, §9.5, §17.5, §19.3 (Batch D), §19.7, §21 (traceability
only) · **Human gate**

## Background

The mass–energy paper is the first complete paper and is deliberately short (three journal pages),
so it proves the complete-paper contract cheaply (§19.3). Its argument is two energy ledgers, one
subtraction, and one small-speed coefficient: a body emits two equal light pulses in opposite
directions; the energy bookkeeping is done in two frames using the relativity paper's §8
light-energy transformation (imported with its provenance shown); subtracting the two ledgers
removes the unknown internal energy; and the leftover difference, expanded for small speeds, has the
form of a kinetic energy with the mass reduced by $L/V^2$ in Einstein's notation (emitted energy
$L$, light speed $V$). The site must reach that result without assuming it: no body energy may be
initialized as $E_0 = Mc^2$ or $\gamma Mc^2$.

The paper is reviewed with the same seriousness as the long ones, and its rounds come early, in
Batch D, so what readers find hard about ledgers, frames, and approximations can improve the
relativity and light-quanta writing that follows. These rounds also supply the stop-rule observation
for the gloss face of paper 4 (§19.7: "each resolves an observed misunderstanding in testing").

## Scope

In scope: rounds on the four routes against the complete mass–energy paper; rubric observations,
stumbling points, and stop-rule observations; findings and follow-up verification; review records.

shared round-report structural test (`am-edit-comprehension-protocol-ouih`); the non-physicist R2
review and fifteen-minute tour test (`am-me-review-reader-l6iy`); cross-paper consolidation
(`am-edit-comprehension-rounds-tcgi`).

## Requirements

1. **Build under test:** a production build of the paper at a recorded commit, served locally or

2. **Routes and size:** `no-algebra` (the first encounter "two accounting sheets and one
subtraction," the fifteen-minute tour, the overview and show-every-step readings), `nonvisual`,
`full-derivation`, and `low-cost-phone`, five to eight participants per route recruited across the

3. **Targeted lessons** (stated in advance):
   - why subtracting the two ledgers removes the unknown internal energy, and which premise makes

   - which result is imported from the relativity paper (§8) and why it is shown with provenance

   - the small-speed coefficient: the exact expression, its Taylor expansion, and the low-speed
   proxy are different claims, and the proxy is not the exact coefficient at every speed (ME-02);

   MJ and so loses about 0.27–0.39 μg (about 0.3 μg) of mass;

   Einstein's question, not as a proof that "mass is energy" in every modern sense;
   - reading the paper's German through the gloss face (word-level gloss of the whole paper).
4. **Stop-rule observations:** the gloss face for paper 4, predict mode on ME-01, show-the-code on
ME-02, and the misconception callouts.
5. **Findings:** every stumbling point recorded with its code and anchor or action id; findings

6. **Reports and records:** `docs/comprehension/rounds/<YYYY-MM-DD>-mass-energy-<route>.md` with

`src/testing/docs/roundReports.test.ts` passes on them.

failing report retained under that run's evidence directory).

or an explanation that hides the subtraction; record which, and send circularity concerns to the
physics reviewer and to `am-ver-no-circularity-audit-6vj` as well as to the content owner.

title: Run comprehension rounds on the complete relativity paper
description:
# Run comprehension rounds on the complete relativity paper

**Epic:** `am-ep-editorial-13x` · **Batch:** G (after the relativity definition of done) ·
**Priority:** P1 · **Plan sections:** §3.5, §8.3, §9.4, §17.5, §19.3 (Batches E and G), §19.7, §21
(traceability only) · **Human gate**

## Background

The relativity paper has two halves, and the plan insists that the difficult closing sections
(§§6–10) receive the same depth as the familiar opening (§19.3). Its kinematics (introduction and
§§1–5) turn simultaneity into a measurement procedure for distant clocks, construct the
transformation rather than hand it over, and separate event coordinates from rod and clock
measurements. Its electrodynamics (§§6–10) transform the field equations component by component in
Gaussian units, treat Doppler shift and aberration, the finite light complex, the moving mirror,
charge and current densities, and the electron's work and deflection with the source's force
convention beside the modern one. Batch E's exit evidence already asks that a reader distinguish
event separation from a rod measurement (recorded by `am-srk-exit-audit-4owh`); these rounds test
both halves of the finished paper with the protocol's full rubric and routes.

These rounds also supply the stop-rule observation for the countermodel workbench (§19.7: the
baseline and variant comparison plus a fair countermodel case expand only once "the interface
distinguishes changed premises from changed representation"), whose first case is relativity
(`am-reason-countermodel-workbench-t07q`).

## Scope

In scope: rounds on the four routes against the complete relativity paper; rubric observations,
stumbling points, and stop-rule observations; findings and follow-up verification; review records.

Out of scope, owned elsewhere: the protocol, its materials, the participant-code parser, and the
shared round-report structural test (`am-edit-comprehension-protocol-ouih`); the Batch E exit
evidence (`am-srk-exit-audit-4owh`); the non-physicist R2 review and fifteen-minute tour test
(`am-sr-review-reader-qff7`); cross-paper consolidation (`am-edit-comprehension-rounds-tcgi`).

## Requirements

1. **Build under test:** a production build of the complete paper at a recorded commit, served
locally or through a protected, authorized preview.
2. **Routes and size:** `no-algebra` (the first encounter "the signal that leaves at 0 and returns
at 10," the fifteen-minute tour, overview and show-every-step readings), `nonvisual` (named events
chosen from tables instead of diagram points, axis and component selection instead of rotating
arrows), `full-derivation`, and `low-cost-phone`, five to eight participants per route across the
protocol's starting points, with participant codes in the protocol's form validated by
`parseParticipantCode`. Each route covers both halves of the paper, so a round may be split into a
kinematics session and an electrodynamics session with the same participants; both sessions share
one participant code and one report.
3. **Targeted lessons** (stated in advance):
   - synchronizing distant clocks by a light-signal procedure (SR-01), and why "simultaneous" needs
   a definition;
   - two transformed events with a larger spatial separation are not a rod measurement (SR-03;
   question bank: "why is that not a rod measurement?");
   - constructing the transformation from stated requirements, including the Galilean shelf step,
   without assuming the Minkowski interval as a historical premise (SR-04, mode `sr-04:1904`);
   - velocity composition never exceeding $V$, including the non-collinear case with rotation
   (SR-06);
   - the field transformation as a change of description of one situation, with the
   magnet-and-conductor case agreeing only to first order in $v/c$ in the pre-relativistic
   descriptions: in the magnet's rest frame the coil's charges feel $q\,\mathbf{v}\times\mathbf{B}$,
   and in the coil's rest frame that effect is the electric field $\mathbf{E}' =
   \gamma\,\mathbf{v}\times\mathbf{B}$ (SR-02, SR-07, SR-08);
   - Doppler and aberration, the energy of a finite light complex versus its frequency ratio, and
   the moving mirror (SR-09, SR-10, SR-11);
   - the electron's transverse and longitudinal coefficients as consequences of a stated force
   convention (SR-13);
   - notation: Einstein's $\beta$ is the modern $\gamma$, his $V$ is the light speed, his $\tau$ is
   the moving-frame time rather than the modern proper time, and §3's printed auxiliary $x' = x -
   vt$ is a Galilean coordinate that the modern-notation layer gives a distinct glyph.
4. **Stop-rule observations:** the countermodel workbench, the baseline and variant comparison where
used, predict mode on SR-03 and SR-06, show-the-code on SR-04, and the misconception callouts (for
example "Michelson–Morley made Einstein do it" and contraction versus what a camera sees).
5. **Findings:** every stumbling point recorded with its code and anchor or action id; findings
filed against owning beads; blocking barriers verified in a follow-up round with fresh participants.
Record separately whether barriers cluster in §§6–10, because that half is most at risk of thinner
explanation.
6. **Reports and records:** `docs/comprehension/rounds/<YYYY-MM-DD>-special-relativity-<route>.md`
with front matter (`paper`, `route`, `date`, `buildCommit`, `anchors`), the facilitator id from
`docs/OWNERS.md` with role `comprehension-facilitator`, and the date; one `comprehension-round`
review record (`am-edit-review-records-hofz`) per round, citing its report in `sessionRef`.

## Human Gate

Recruitment, facilitation, and observation require people. Agents may prepare builds, session plans,
and anchors lists; analyze de-identified notes; file findings; and draft review records. Close this
bead only when all four routes have completed rounds covering both halves, every finding is triaged,
blocking barriers have a verification result, and each report names its facilitator id and date.
Agents never close it on their own judgment, never sign a review record, and never simulate
participants.

## Technical Approach

Prepare separate kinematics and electrodynamics session plans per route listing targeted changes,
question bank items, and anchors. Before sessions, run `am-srk-e2e-4qkd` and `am-sre-e2e-xmj6` in
every lane on the same commit. Collect the Batch E exit observations from `am-srk-exit-audit-4owh`
as prior evidence for the kinematics lessons.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Round reports exist for the four routes, each covering kinematics and electrodynamics, and
`src/testing/docs/roundReports.test.ts` passes on them.
- [ ] Every stumbling point has a code, an anchor or action id, and a linked bead or comment.
- [ ] Stop-rule observations exist for the capabilities in Requirement 4.
- [ ] The report states whether barriers cluster in §§6–10.
- [ ] Blocking barriers show a verification result or an explicit open status, and review records
exist for each round.
- [ ] No personal data is stored in the repository.

## Test Plan

### Unit and integration tests
`src/testing/docs/roundReports.test.ts` (owned by `am-edit-comprehension-protocol-ouih`) validates
every report: required sections, front matter, closed-list route and paper values, parseable
participant codes, and no personal data. This bead adds its reports to that corpus.
### End-to-end tests
The pre-session `am-srk-e2e-4qkd` and `am-sre-e2e-xmj6` runs in every lane, with log run ids
attached to the session plans; reproducible findings add regressions to those suites.
### Structured logging
Session reports are Markdown; the pre-session runs and the structural test log JSONL per the
standard (`suite: "round-reports"`, `artifacts/test-logs/round-reports/<log-run-id>.jsonl`, with a
failing report retained under that run's evidence directory).

## Considerations and Pitfalls

- Spacetime diagrams are a later geometric aid (Minkowski 1908); a participant who can follow only
the diagram, not the paper's measurement procedure, has found a gap in the historical route.
- Gaussian units in §6 are a unit-system choice, not a different physics; confusion there usually
points to the notation concordance's unit-conversion marker, which is a different operation from a
symbol rename and from a substantive modernization.
- Do not coach participants; small samples reveal problems and do not estimate effect sizes.
- Lorentz's ether with local time reproduces the same formulas within the tested scope; a
participant who says so has not made a mistake, and the branch must not be shown as refuted.

## Dependencies

Blocked by: `am-edit-comprehension-protocol-ouih` (procedure, materials, parser, shared report
test), `am-dod-relativity-105y` (the complete paper), `am-gov-owners-and-reviewers-hte` (facilitator
ids), `am-edit-review-records-hofz` (the `comprehension-round` record type).

Unblocks: `am-edit-comprehension-rounds-tcgi` (cross-paper consolidation).
