- `am-cm-checks-semantic-lic` imports this module for its `unsupported-math-command` rule, so the renderer and the checker never disagree.

### Trust callback and denial collector

- Allow `\htmlData` only when the trust context's `attributes` object has exactly one key, `data-term` or `data-op`, whose value parses as a `TermId` or `OperationId` from `src/content/ids.ts` (grammar defined by `am-eq-expression-tree-8kl`).
- Allow `\htmlClass` only when the class string is exactly one token from the enumerated role classes `am-role-energy`, `am-role-time-rate`, `am-role-space-geometry`, `am-role-material`, `am-role-statistical`, `am-role-field`, `am-role-quanta`, imported from the single role enum that the registry's `colorRole` field validates against (`am-not-quantity-registry-2f7`, `am-design-semantic-color-8vbq`). Never use a looser pattern.
- Deny everything else, including `\href`, `\url`, `\includegraphics`, `\htmlStyle`, and `\htmlId`.
- Each render call creates a fresh denial collector. The callback records every denied context, and `renderStatic` throws a build failure after rendering if any denial was recorded, because KaTeX itself renders the denial as error-colored text instead of throwing.

### Authored multi-line display form

Long displays (for example paper 4's $K_0 - K_1 = L\left\{\frac{1}{\sqrt{1 - (v/V)^2}} - 1\right\}$ in a narrow column, and multi-step field transformations) must not shrink below legibility, overflow the page, or be broken at a point a renderer guesses.

- **The record carries the form.** An `Equation` record may carry the authored layout hints defined and validated by `am-eq-expression-tree-8kl`: `layout.breaks[]`, naming the node ids after which the display may break, and the optional `layout.alignAt`, naming the node whose glyph starts each aligned row (usually the relation symbol). The hints are authored, never computed.
- **This bead renders them.** When a form carries layout hints, `renderStatic` emits the display as aligned rows (a KaTeX `aligned` environment generated from the hints by `am-eq-latex-generation-hc3`), with the same term and operation markers as the single-line form, so selection, colors, and spoken forms are unaffected. Ids are identical across the single-line and multi-line renderings.
- **Who consumes it.** Equation cards (`am-eq-colorized-component-1z8`), derivation steps (`am-eq-derivation-renderer-9gd7`, whose over-wide step equations render from this authored form and never invent breaks), print (`am-plat-print-3orn`, whose `print-overflow` report fires only for a display wider than the printable width **with no authored multi-line form**, so every report has a resolution path in the record), and share cards (`am-design-og-images-pwok`).
- **No renderer-invented breaks.** This bead never inserts a line break, never rewrites a fraction into a solidus form, and never scales a display down to fit. A display that is too wide and has no authored form renders as-is and is reported by its consumer, so the repair happens in the equation record.

### Build failure

- Any KaTeX `ParseError`, strict violation, allowlist violation, tokenizer error, refused provenance, or recorded trust denial fails the content build. The diagnostic names the equation or passage id, the form (printed, modern, or alternate-form id), the color mode, a bounded excerpt of the offending LaTeX (at most 200 characters), and the sanitized KaTeX message or rule id. Raw error strings are never shipped to readers.
- After rendering, the output is scanned for the `errorColor` sentinel, and any occurrence fails the build (defense in depth behind the collector).

### No raw LaTeX in readers' text

- Inline math in prose (readings, captions, footnotes, term definitions, misconception text) is rendered at build time.
- `scanStaticOutput(buildDir)` parses each built page with an HTML parser and inspects text nodes only. It fails on unrendered math delimiters (`$…$`, `\(…\)`, `\[…\]`) or LaTeX control sequences, and on the error-color sentinel in any style.
- Excluded from the text scan: `<annotation encoding="application/x-tex">` content inside KaTeX MathML, `<script>` and `<style>` elements, and code listings explicitly marked by show-the-code (`<pre data-code-listing>`). There is no blanket exemption; a literal dollar sign or backslash in prose is authored through an explicit escape that the scanner recognizes.

### Static output

Every displayed equation appears as KaTeX HTML plus MathML in the initial HTML of its route, and the page reads correctly with JavaScript disabled.

### Ledger parity

- **Why.** The reviewed-ledger validator (`am-edn-ledger-validator-edv`, Batch A) parses ledger mathematics with its own settings in `src/content/ledger/ledgerMathSettings.ts`: `throwOnError: true`, `strict: "error"`, `trust: false`, an empty macro table, `maxExpand: 1000`, and `maxSize: 20`. The shared publication configuration only arrives in Batch B, so without a parity check, ledger-valid mathematics could fail late at publication.
- **Region check.** Every math region accepted under the ledger settings, in every `public/papers/transcripts/*-reviewed.txt` present and in the committed fixture ledgers under `src/testing/fixtures/ledgers/`, must render under `src/equations/katex/config.ts`. It goes through `renderStatic` with provenance `authored-inline`, so the command allowlist applies.
- **Ledger keys, not slugs.** `am-edn-ledger-validator-edv` keys the sections of `ledger-config.yaml` by `ledgerKey`, so the parity corpus reads a ledger's math settings by its bibliographic key: `ap-17-132`, `ap-17-549`, `ap-17-891`, `ap-18-639`, and for the companion both `ap-19-289` (the 1906 dissertation) and `ap-34-591` (the 1911 correction). The `molecular-dimensions` route slug maps to two ledger keys and is therefore never used to look up ledger settings; a lookup by slug alone fails the test with a message naming the two keys.
- **Cap check.** The ledger caps must be no looser than the publication caps: ledger `maxExpand` and `maxSize` are at most the publication values; the ledger macro table is empty; ledger `trust` is `false`; and ledger strictness is `"error"`.
- **Failures.** A region that fails names the ledger key, the file, the line, and the rule. The repair is either a reviewed allowlist addition or a transcription question raised with `br comments add`, never a retyped formula.

### Client rendering

- Allowed only for genuinely dynamic expressions (for example previews inside derivation steps that cannot be precomputed). It loads lazily, uses the same configuration and allowlist modules, and never enters the initial reading route bundle.
- Reader-entered text (exercise answers, notebook entries) is never passed to KaTeX as LaTeX. A preview of a reader's expression renders from a parsed expression tree through generated LaTeX that still passes the allowlist.

### Assets and size

- KaTeX CSS is self-hosted and wired to the KaTeX font files that `am-design-themes-typography-288q` subsets and hosts, with stable fallback metrics so deferred math activation keeps cumulative layout shift at or below 0.1.
- **Glyph manifest.**
  - `renderStatic` records every code point it emits, grouped by KaTeX font face (for example `KaTeX_Main-Regular`, `KaTeX_Math-Italic`, `KaTeX_Size3-Regular`, `KaTeX_AMS-Regular`). It derives the face from each output text node's KaTeX font classes.
  - Code points from every form, both color modes, inline prose math, and multi-line renderings are included.
  - The records go into a build glyph manifest that the font subsetting of `am-design-themes-typography-288q` consumes, so no subset can omit a glyph the corpus renders.
  - A test renders the fixture corpus and asserts every recorded code point is present in the shipped subset for its face.
- Record rendered HTML bytes per equation and per reading face, and separately the bytes of MathML `<annotation>` payloads, which repeat the input LaTeX including markers. This output counts toward the 250 kB gzipped budget per paper reading face enforced by `am-read-detail-axis-sfc` and `am-plat-perf-budgets-s3ww`. If annotations threaten the budget, replace annotation text with the plain-mode LaTeX of the same form through a tested DOM transform, never by string substitution on LaTeX.

## Technical Approach

- Adapt the donor `LatexRenderer.tsx`, `TextWithLatex`, and `HudText` (extracted with license notices by `am-scaf-extract-ui-components-c31`) into `src/equations/katex/renderStatic.ts`. It is a pure function that runs the provenance check and allowlist scan (through the shared tokenizer), then KaTeX with the shared config and a fresh denial collector, then the sentinel scan, and returns markup or a typed failure. Thin server components insert the precomputed markup.
- The compiler (`am-cm-compiler-core-oa7`) calls `renderStatic` for every variant it needs (printed, modern, and alternate forms; plain and colorized; single-line and, where hints exist, multi-line) and stores the HTML in route-local payloads, so no client component imports KaTeX for static content.
- `src/equations/katex/scanStaticOutput.ts` runs after the production build in the quality gate chain; `am-cm-audit-scripts-d34` also calls it from `scripts/verify-content.ts`.
- Keep the donor's `biome-ignore` justification pattern for `dangerouslySetInnerHTML`, limited to markup produced by `renderStatic`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] All fixture equations and every equation in the first corpus render at build time in printed and modern notation, and in every alternate form, with HTML plus MathML present.
- [ ] The strict function rejects a strict violation (a raw `ä` in math mode) with its code in the diagnostic, and admits `htmlExtension` only for trusted generated markers.
- [ ] A malformed fixture fails the build with an actionable, sanitized message naming the record.
- [ ] Every construct in the security fixture list fails the build, including trust denials that KaTeX renders without throwing.
- [ ] The allowlist module is the single source of permitted commands, its scan uses the single shared tokenizer of `am-eq-latex-generation-hc3`, and `am-cm-checks-semantic-lic` imports the allowlist (verified by an import test once that bead lands).
- [ ] An equation record carrying layout hints renders as aligned rows with the same term and operation ids as its single-line form, and no renderer-invented break appears anywhere in the output.
- [ ] The raw-LaTeX scan passes on the full static output and fails on seeded leaks (`$\frac{a}{b}$` in prose; `\alpha` in a figure caption); the sentinel scan fails on a seeded unsupported-command rendering.
- [ ] The initial reading route loads no KaTeX JavaScript, verified by the shared initial-route bundle check owned by `am-scaf-nextjs-app-bu2`; a lazily loaded client renderer, if present, shares the configuration and allowlist modules.
- [ ] With JavaScript disabled, equations on a Brownian §§4–5 page are visible and their MathML is present in the DOM.
- [ ] The size report lists bytes per equation, per reading face, and for annotations, and the glyph manifest covers every emitted code point by face.
- [ ] The ledger parity corpus test passes: every ledger-valid math region renders under the publication configuration, ledger settings are looked up by `ledgerKey` (both companion keys covered), and the ledger caps are no looser than the publication caps.

## Test Plan

### Unit and integration tests

- `renderStatic.test.ts`: display and inline rendering; MathML present; allowed `\htmlData` and `\htmlClass` markers pass; output is byte-identical across two runs.
- `strict.test.ts`: the `htmlExtension` exception path; a raw `ä` in math mode fails naming `unicodeTextInMathMode`; a strict code missing from the exceptions table fails; the table matches the documentation.
- `trust.security.test.ts`: each input fails the build with its rule id: `\href{javascript:alert(1)}{x}`, `\url{https://example.org}`, `\includegraphics{x.png}`, `\htmlStyle{color:red}{x}`, `\htmlId{x}{y}`, `\htmlData{onclick=x}{y}`, `\htmlData{term=eq-s3-d4.t.viscosity, op=eq-s3-d4.op.denominator}{y}` (two keys), `\htmlData{term=not an id}{y}`, `\htmlClass{am-role-energy extra}{x}`, `\htmlClass{am-role-unknown}{x}`, `\def\x{y}\x`, `\gdef\x{y}`, `\let\x=\frac`, `\newcommand{\x}{y}`, and nested expansion beyond `maxExpand`. For each trust case the test also calls bare KaTeX with the same trust function and asserts that it did **not** throw, which proves the collector is necessary.
- `maxSize.test.ts`: `\rule{500em}{500em}` fails the allowlist in an ordinary record; in a named record where a size command is allowlisted, the rendered size is capped at `maxSize`.
- `commandAllowlist.test.ts`: through the real shared tokenizer, the scan catches a forbidden command inside braces, a subscript, `\text{}`, and an environment body, and a forbidden environment name; a tokenizer error fails with the record id; `authored-inline` input containing `\htmlData` fails; `reader-input` provenance is refused; the allowlist snapshot matches.
- `multilineForm.test.ts`: a fixture record with `layout.breaks[]` and `layout.alignAt` renders aligned rows; the term and operation ids of the multi-line rendering equal those of the single-line rendering; a record without hints renders on one line and no break is inserted; the rendered rows are byte-identical across two runs.
- `buildFailure.integration.test.ts`: a malformed equation in a temporary fixture corpus makes the real compiler exit non-zero with the expected diagnostic.
- `scanStaticOutput.test.ts`: flags leaked delimiters and control sequences in prose and in a `<figcaption>`; ignores `<annotation encoding="application/x-tex">`, `<script>`, `<style>`, and `<pre data-code-listing>`; flags the sentinel color.
- `glyphManifest.test.ts`: rendering the fixture corpus records code points per KaTeX face, including a `KaTeX_Size3-Regular` delimiter, inline prose math, and a multi-line rendering, and every recorded code point is present in the shipped subset for its face.
- `ledgerParity.corpus.test.ts`: every math region accepted by `ledgerMathSettings` in the present reviewed ledgers and the fixture ledgers renders under the publication configuration; settings are read by `ledgerKey`, with `ap-19-289` and `ap-34-591` both exercised and a lookup by the `molecular-dimensions` slug failing with a message naming both keys; the ledger caps, macro table, trust, and strictness are no looser than the publication values; a seeded fixture region using a command outside the allowlist fails with its ledger coordinates.

### End-to-end tests

- `e2e/equations/static-math.spec.ts` in the JavaScript-disabled lane of `am-test-e2e-harness-bqmh`: load a fixture paper reading face; assert visible KaTeX HTML and a `<math>` element for each displayed equation; run the same text-node scanner in the page and assert no unrendered LaTeX and no sentinel color; at 320 px, a display with an authored multi-line form renders its rows and the page does not scroll horizontally.
- Layout stability in the Chromium lane: cumulative layout shift at or below 0.1 during initial load with fonts cold (the layout-shift API is Chromium-only; WebKit lanes assert visible math without the metric).
- Failures retain a screenshot, DOM snapshot, console log, and the generated LaTeX of the failing record.

### Structured logging

Build diagnostics are JSON lines with `recordId`, `anchor`, `form` (`printed`, `modern`, or an alternate-form id), `layout` (`single-line` or `multi-line`), `colorMode`, `provenance`, `stage` (`provenance`, `tokenize`, `allowlist`, `katex`, `strict`, `trust`, `sentinel`, `scan`), `rule`, `ledgerKey` (for parity failures), `excerpt` (at most 200 characters), and `message`. Tests write through `src/testing/log/logger.ts` to `artifacts/test-logs/equations-katex/<log-run-id>.jsonl` with the standard fields (`timestamp`, `suite`, `logRunId`, `testId`, `beadId`, `outcome`, `durationMs`, `browser`, `viewport`, `jsEnabled`, `message`); failures retain the offending generated LaTeX file.

## Considerations and Pitfalls

- The donor sets `strict: false`. Publication here wants errors on nonstandard input, so every strictness exception must be deliberate and tested.
- KaTeX's non-throwing trust denial is the most likely silent failure in this bead; the collector and the sentinel scan exist because `throwOnError` does not cover it.
- `maxSize` caps silently. Never cite it as the reason an oversized construct "fails"; the allowlist is what fails it.
- A second LaTeX tokenizer here would eventually disagree with the one that validates author markers; import the shared one.
- MathML and a spoken-form label can double-announce. The pattern is decided in `am-eq-spoken-forms-w4f` and confirmed on real assistive technology by its human-gate follow-up, so this bead must not hard-code ARIA that forecloses it.
- An automatic line break is a rendering guess about meaning: it can split a radicand or separate a factor from its group. Breaks are authored in the record or they do not happen.
- The companion has two ledger keys. Looking up ledger settings by route slug would silently read the wrong printing's caps.
- Upgrading KaTeX changes markup and possibly glyph metrics. Pin the version through `am-gov-decision-stack-versions-6ax`, rerun the golden, layout, strict, and collector tests on upgrade, and re-verify the three behaviors in Background.

## Dependencies

Blocked by (each edge exists in `br dep list`):
- `am-eq-latex-generation-hc3`: the LaTeX being rendered, the marker grammar the trust callback enforces, the aligned-row generation for multi-line forms, and the brace-aware tokenizer the allowlist scan imports.
- `am-scaf-extract-ui-components-c31`: the donor LaTeX renderer, extracted with license notices.
- `am-edn-ledger-validator-edv`: the ledger math settings the parity corpus test compares against, keyed by `ledgerKey`.
- `am-cm-compiler-core-oa7`: the compiler calls `renderStatic`, and the build-failure test runs the real compiler.
- `am-design-themes-typography-288q`: the self-hosted KaTeX font files and fallback metrics the layout check and glyph test need.
- `am-test-e2e-harness-bqmh`: the JavaScript-disabled, 320 px, and layout lanes.

`am-cm-id-scheme-8bn`, `am-gov-decision-stack-versions-6ax`, the layout hints of `am-eq-expression-tree-8kl`, and the JSONL logger of `am-test-logging-standard-l3cp` are reached transitively through `am-eq-latex-generation-hc3` and the compiler.

Unblocks:
- `am-eq-colorized-component-1z8`: the interactive layer over static markup.
- `am-eq-spoken-forms-w4f`: accessible names over the rendered formula.
- `am-eq-derivation-renderer-9gd7`: step lists with precomputed KaTeX markup, including authored multi-line displays.
- `am-design-og-images-pwok`: static signature equations on share cards.
- `am-edn-review-packet-ee9t`: German review packets render displays through the shared KaTeX configuration.
- `am-plat-security-f644`: site-wide hardening builds on this trust policy.
- `am-plat-print-3orn`: printed equations come from the static output, and its `print-overflow` report resolves through the authored multi-line form.

Unblocks, added as an edge in review: `am-cm-checks-semantic-lic` imports the command allowlist for its `unsupported-math-command` rule.

title: Author foundations: functions and graphs, derivatives, partial derivatives, exponentials, logarithms
description:
# Author foundations: functions and graphs, derivatives, partial derivatives, exponentials, logarithms

**Epic:** `am-ep-foundations-z1e` · **Batch:** batch-c · **Priority:** P1 · **Plan sections:** §6.4, §7.5, §8.1, §8.2 (traceability only)

## Background

Four papers lean on the same small calculus toolkit: reading a family of curves, local sensitivity, what is held fixed in a partial derivative, dimensionless exponents, and logarithms that turn products into sums. These nodes are written for the physician who has not used a derivative since 1998 and for the programmer who distrusts "obviously," and each is anchored in a passage that needs it.

Two findings from light-paper review r2 bear on these nodes. The 1905 prints write "lg" for the natural logarithm, which modern readers would take for a base-10 logarithm. The light paper's §5 derives the logarithm in Boltzmann's principle from the fact that probabilities of independent systems multiply while entropies add, which is exactly this node's concrete entry point.

## Scope

Nodes owned here (canonical ids from `am-ep-foundations-z1e`):

| Id | Concrete entry point | What the reader can do afterward |
|---|---|---|
| `foundation:functions-graphs` | A table of paired measurements | Read axes, inputs, outputs, slope, and a parameterized family |
| `foundation:derivatives` | Move one control a little and compare the output | Interpret local sensitivity with units |
| `foundation:partial-derivatives` | Change temperature while holding volume fixed | State what is held fixed and why it matters |
| `foundation:exponentials` | Repeated proportional changes | Read growth, decay, and dimensionless exponents |
| `foundation:logarithms` | Turn repeated multiplication into addition | Understand why independent probability products give additive entropy |

Owned elsewhere: integration and the Taylor expansion node (`am-bm-slice-foundations-f5z9`; this bead adds the binomial-series extension to it as a separate section record, as that bead expects); hyperbolic functions (`am-found-linear-geometry-7w15`); the bridges `foundation:bridge-a-graph` (`am-bm-slice-foundations-f5z9`) and `foundation:bridge-mathematical-punctuation` (`am-found-zero-algebra-rest-oipl`).

## Requirements

**Worked examples.**
- **Functions and graphs.** The radiation spectrum at several temperatures as a parameterized family (light §§1–4); a table of RMS displacement against time becoming a $\sqrt{t}$ curve (Brownian §5); the light paper's predicted straight line of stopping potential against frequency, whose slope does not depend on the metal (light §8).
- **Derivatives.** The stopping potential rises by $h/e \approx 4.14\times10^{-15}$ V per hertz of frequency (light §8); $\partial f/\partial t$ as the local rate of change of a density (Brownian §4); velocity as a ratio of differentials (relativity §5); the low-speed expansion's leading term (mass–energy).
- **Partial derivatives.** $(\partial s_\nu/\partial\rho_\nu)_\nu = 1/T$ with frequency and volume held fixed (light §3); $\partial n/\partial x$ versus $\partial n/\partial t$ (Brownian §§3–4); the chain rule for transformed derivatives (relativity §6).
- **Exponentials.** $e^{-\beta\nu/T}$ with a dimensionless exponent (light §4); the Gaussian $e^{-x^2/(4Dt)}$ (Brownian §4).
- **Logarithms.**
  - $\ln(f^n) = n\ln f$ for independent points (light §5).
  - Inverting Wien's law with a logarithm (light §4).
  - The free-energy term $N_p\ln V$ (Brownian §2).
  - Why a function that turns products into sums must be a logarithm: if $S = \varphi(W)$, $S_1 + S_2 = S$, and $W_1W_2 = W$, then $\varphi(W_1W_2) = \varphi(W_1) + \varphi(W_2)$, so $\varphi = C\ln W + \text{const}$ (light §5).
  - **Notation note:** the 1905 prints write "lg" for the natural logarithm; modern ISO notation reserves "lg" for $\log_{10}$. The node shows both glyphs on the same example ($\lg 2$ printed means $\ln 2 = 0.6931$, not $\log_{10}2 = 0.3010$).
- **Taylor expansion extension** (a section record owned here, rendered inside `foundation:taylor-expansion`, whose node record belongs to `am-bm-slice-foundations-f5z9`).
  - The binomial series $(1 - x)^{-1/2} = 1 + \tfrac12x + \tfrac38x^2 + \tfrac{5}{16}x^3 + \tfrac{35}{128}x^4 + \cdots$ for $|x| < 1$, applied to $\gamma = (1 - v^2/c^2)^{-1/2}$.
  - At $v/c = 0.6$ ($x = 0.36$), the partial sums of $\gamma - 1$ are 0.18, 0.2286, 0.24318, and 0.247773 against the exact 0.25. The quadratic 0.18 is mass–energy's $0.18L$ fixture beside the exact $0.25L$, so a retained term, a neglected term, and a range of usefulness are all visible.
  - At $v/c = 10^{-4}$ ($x = 10^{-8}$) the exact $\gamma - 1 = 5.0000000375\times10^{-9}$, and the first term $5\times10^{-9}$ matches it to a relative $7.5\times10^{-9}$ (the next term's share, $0.75x$). This value is reproduced only by a cancellation-free evaluation with `expm1` and `log1p`; subtracting 1 from a rounded $\gamma$ in double precision returns $5.0000001917\times10^{-9}$ and a relative difference of $3.83\times10^{-8}$, five times too large. The node shows both routes and says which is trustworthy.
  - Planned callers: relativity §4 and mass–energy.

**Constructions.** A table-to-plot builder; a "nudge the control" sensitivity demo that reports the change and the ratio with units; a held-fixed toggle that shows two different partial derivatives of the same function; a repeated-proportional-change table; a product-to-sum table for logarithms with a toggle between "ln" and the printed "lg". Each has a textual equivalent.

**Prerequisites and stopping points.** Every prerequisite is typed `{foundationId, kind}` (`am-cm-schemas-argument-llm`).
- Functions and graphs rest on "a graph as a record of paired quantities" (`proof-edge` prerequisite `foundation:bridge-a-graph`).
- Derivatives rest on "a rate as change per unit of something".
- Logarithms rest on "how many times you multiply".
- Partial derivatives require derivatives (`proof-edge`).
- Logarithms and exponentials name each other as `cross-link` prerequisites, not as a proof circle, so the acyclicity check ignores that pair.

**Calling passages and return captions.** Captions follow the rule in `am-found-library-infra-002t`: this bead records captions for callers that already exist in the node's `returnCaptions[]`, and later callers put theirs on their own link records.
- This bead authors captions for callers that exist when it lands: the Brownian reference slice (§§4–5) and the Brownian readings through §3.
- It records as `plannedCallers` in the registry: light §§1–5 and §8, relativity §§5–6, and mass–energy.

## Technical Approach

- Records under `content/foundations/`; constructions use the instrument platform's controls and action contracts; numeric examples come from evaluator fixtures where possible and are compared through `src/units/tolerance.ts` (`am-ver-tolerance-module-ho90`); registry entries flipped to `authored` in the same change.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Five complete records with all parts and stopping points, registered under their canonical ids with this bead as owner.
- [ ] Each held-fixed example names the fixed quantities explicitly.
- [ ] The logarithms node carries the "lg" note and the product-to-sum derivation.
- [ ] The binomial-series extension renders inside the Taylor node without editing the slice bead's record, and states the cancellation-free evaluation rule with both computed values.
- [ ] Captions exist for every existing caller (in the node's `returnCaptions[]` or on the caller's link record); planned callers are recorded; every prerequisite carries its `kind`.
- [ ] Constructions have textual equivalents and keyboard operation; print and no-JavaScript renderings are complete.

## Test Plan

### Unit and integration tests
- `foundCalculus.numbers.test.ts`: quoted values through `src/units/tolerance.ts`: $h/e = 4.135667697\times10^{-15}$ V s; $\ln 2 = 0.693147$ against $\log_{10}2 = 0.301030$; the logarithm identity $\ln(f^n) = n\ln f$ for $n = 10$, $f = 1/2$ ($-6.931472$).
- `foundCalculus.logarithm.property.test.ts`: a property test that the product-to-sum construction satisfies $\ln(W_1W_2) = \ln W_1 + \ln W_2$ for random positive inputs.
- `foundCalculus.binomial.test.ts`: partial sums $0.18$, $0.2286$, $0.24318$, $0.247773$ at $x = 0.36$ against the exact $0.25$; at $v/c = 10^{-4}$, the cancellation-free route gives $\gamma - 1 = 5.0000000375\times10^{-9}$ and a relative difference of $7.500000\times10^{-9}$ to the first term, while a planted naive evaluation ($1/\sqrt{1 - x} - 1$) gives $5.0000001917\times10^{-9}$ and $3.833\times10^{-8}$ and fails the assertion, so the test documents why the stable route is required.
- `foundCalculus.records.test.ts`: compiler checks for registry entries, link-record captions, prerequisite typing (`cross-link` versus `proof-edge`, and a prerequisite missing `kind` rejected), and voice lint.
- Failure evidence (the failing example id, expected and actual values, and the evaluation route used) is written beside the log and retained.

### End-to-end tests
- From Brownian §4 (reference slice), open `foundation:partial-derivatives`, toggle what is held fixed, and return to the exact step.
- From Brownian §5, open `foundation:functions-graphs`, build the plot from the table with keyboard only, and return.
- Open `foundation:logarithms` with JavaScript disabled and assert the "lg" note renders.

The light-paper routes into these nodes (for example from light §3) are exercised by `am-lq-e2e-x7z0`, not here.

### Structured logging
- JSONL to `artifacts/test-logs/found-calculus/<log-run-id>.jsonl` with `timestamp`, `suite`, `logRunId`, `testId`, `beadId`, `foundationId`, `callingAnchor`, `expected`, `actual`, `tolerance`, `outcome`, `viewport`, `jsEnabled`, `message`; failure evidence retained.

## Considerations and Pitfalls

- Never write "obviously" or "clearly."
- Keep "rate" and "sensitivity" explanations unit-bearing; a slope without units is not an explanation.
- Never render a printed "lg" as $\log_{10}$ in a modern form.
- Never quote a low-speed expansion figure obtained by subtracting 1 from a rounded $\gamma$; the digits that matter are the ones that cancel.

## Dependencies

Blocked by:
- `am-found-library-infra-002t`: rendering, the registry, and link-record captions.
- `am-bm-slice-foundations-f5z9`: integration, Taylor expansion, and the graph bridge these nodes link to.

Unblocks:
- `am-found-prereq-audit-71ot`: the audit covers these nodes.
- `am-found-fields-light-cv3o`: its `foundation:functions-graphs` and `foundation:derivatives` prerequisites are proof edges, so that cluster waits for this one.
- `am-lq-equations-s1-s4-9gl5`, `am-srk-equations-30cq`, `am-sre-equations-2g3h`: chain tool links resolve to these nodes.
- `am-lq-readings-intro-s2-n0bq`, `am-lq-readings-s3-s4-k923`, `am-lq-readings-s5-s6-deq6`, `am-lq-readings-s7-s9-yorj`, `am-srk-readings-s3-odqp`, `am-srk-readings-s4-s5-njsh`, `am-sre-readings-s6-c5i4`, `am-bm-readings-intro-s1-s3-l3tp`: these readings link these nodes.
- `am-disc-desk-1904-9hgd`: the 1904 desk's shelf explanations link these nodes.

description:
# Author foundations: frames and events, fields and waves, electromagnetism needed here, momentum and energy of light

**Epic:** `am-ep-foundations-z1e` · **Batch:** batch-d · **Priority:** P1 · **Plan sections:** §3.3 (Introduction, §§1, 8), §7.2 (relativity first encounter), §7.5, §8.3, §8.4, §9.4–§9.5 shelves (traceability only)

## Background

The relativity paper opens with a moving magnet and a conductor, defines simultaneity through light signals, transforms fields and waves, and computes the energy of a light complex. The mass–energy paper follows the energy of two light pulses. The light paper's introduction contrasts continuous fields with discrete matter and notes that optical observations record time averages. Its §1 treats electrons bound by restoring forces as "resonators" that absorb and emit waves, and its §8 uses charges, potentials, and electron volts. Readers without an electromagnetism course need exactly these four nodes, and no more, to follow the claims.

**Batch note.** `am-me-readings-69bo` (Batch D) already depends on this bead for the momentum and energy of light, so this bead must land before the mass–energy paper, not only before relativity. It is labeled batch-d for that reason.

## Scope

Nodes owned here (canonical ids from `am-ep-foundations-z1e`):

| Id | Concrete entry point | What the reader can do afterward |
|---|---|---|
| `foundation:frames-events` | Several clocks record local occurrences | Distinguish coordinate description, measurement procedure, and optical reception |
| `foundation:fields-waves` | Values across space sampled at successive times; frequency, wavelength, phase; the Doppler effect for sound | Understand phase, frequency, amplitude, direction, and local field quantities |
| `foundation:electromagnetism-needed-here` | A charge, a current, a field, and a detector; Maxwell's equations in words | Follow the paper's claims without a complete prior E&M course |
| `foundation:momentum-energy-light` | Radiation pressure and the momentum $E/c$ of a light pulse | Follow papers 3 and 4 |

Owned elsewhere: vectors, dot and cross products (`am-found-linear-geometry-7w15`); work and energy (`am-found-transport-thermo-smv3`); electrical unit systems (`foundation:unit-system-1905`, `am-found-quantities-magnitudes-igxe`).

## Requirements

**Worked examples (verified by test).**
- **Frames and events.** A signal leaves clock A at 0, reflects at B, and returns to A at 10. The synchronization procedure assigns B's reflection the time 5, a stated convention rather than a direct measurement of an unknowable one-way time. An event differs from its reception: a flash at B is seen at A later than it happened.
- **Fields and waves.**
  - $\lambda\nu = c$, so 600 THz corresponds to about 499.7 nm.
  - Phase $kx - \omega t$ with $k = 2\pi/\lambda$ and $\omega = 2\pi\nu$, keeping cyclic $\nu$ distinct from angular $\omega$.
  - Intensity as a time average: the average of $\cos^2$ over a period is $\tfrac12$, so what an optical observation records is not the instantaneous square (light introduction, LQ-01).
  - A point source of 1 W spreads its power over spheres, $I = P/(4\pi r^2) = 0.0796$ W/m² at 1 m and one quarter of that at 2 m.
  - The Doppler effect for sound differs for a moving source and a moving listener because air is a medium (a foundation analogy, never a proof about light).
- **Electromagnetism needed here.**
  - Forces $q\mathbf{E}$ and $q\mathbf{v}\times\mathbf{B}$; potential difference and the electron volt.
  - A charge bound by a restoring force oscillates, absorbs, and emits waves of its own frequency, which is what the light paper's §1 calls a resonator.
  - Maxwell's equations in words: charges are sources of electric field; there are no magnetic charges; a changing magnetic field produces a circulating electric field; currents and changing electric fields produce a circulating magnetic field. Together they describe waves traveling at $c$.
  - The magnet-and-conductor case, where pre-1905 theory explains the same current by two different mechanisms.
- **Momentum and energy of light.**
  - 1 W of light absorbed pushes with $1/c \approx 3.34\times10^{-9}$ N, and twice that when reflected.
  - A pulse of energy $E$ carries momentum $E/c$; two equal pulses emitted in opposite directions carry zero total momentum.
  - Dated measurements of radiation pressure (Lebedev 1901; Nichols and Hull 1901–1903) and Poynting (1884) appear as dated context.

**Constructions.** A small event ledger with two clocks (with a table); a wave sampler with phase, frequency, and wavelength readouts and an instantaneous-versus-averaged intensity toggle; a separate sound-Doppler toy; a charge-and-field arrow view with a force readout; a radiation-pressure calculator. Each has a textual equivalent and keyboard operation. Where a construction would embed an instrument preset that is not yet registered (for example LQ-01 or ME-01), the node shows its static worked example with the library's status line.

**Prerequisites** (typed `{foundationId, kind}` entries, the shape defined in `am-cm-schemas-argument-llm`):
- `foundation:quantities-units` (`am-found-quantities-magnitudes-igxe`), `foundation:functions-graphs`, and `foundation:derivatives` (both `am-found-calculus-6agg`) as `kind: "proof-edge"`. All three are authored in Batch C, and this bead depends on both authoring beads, because the build refuses a proof-edge prerequisite whose target is still `planned`.
- `foundation:vectors-components` (`am-found-linear-geometry-7w15`, Batch E) as `kind: "cross-link"`. Under the rule in `am-found-library-infra-002t`, a cross-link to a `planned` node renders as "available later", never fails the build, and is reported by `am-found-prereq-audit-71ot` until the node is authored. No proof route in these nodes depends on vectors, so this bead does not wait for Batch E.

**Calling passages and return captions.** Captions follow the rule in `am-found-library-infra-002t` for `FoundationLink {foundationId, callingAnchor, returnCaption?}` records (`am-cm-schemas-argument-llm`): this bead records captions for callers that already exist in the node's `returnCaptions[]`, and later callers put theirs on their own link records. This bead authors captions only for callers that exist when it lands. It records the following as `plannedCallers`; those beads author their captions when they link:
- the relativity introduction and §§1, 6, 7, 8, and 9;
- SR-01, SR-02, and SR-08 to SR-12;
- ME-01, ME-03, and the mass–energy readings;
- the light introduction, §1 (resonators), and §8 (potentials);
- LQ-01.

**Stopping points.**
- Event: "something that happens at one place and one time."
- Field: "a value assigned to every place."
- Charge: "the property that makes electric forces."
- Light's momentum: "the push a beam gives when absorbed."

## Technical Approach

- Records under `content/foundations/`; numbers referenced from `am-ref-constants-xik` and, where live, from `am-ref-events-yvl` and `am-ref-waves-r53` fixtures; registry entries flipped to `authored` in the same change.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Four complete records with all parts and stopping points, registered under their canonical ids with this bead as owner.
- [ ] The synchronization example states the convention explicitly; the sound analogy is labeled as an analogy with its limit; the time-average example is present.
- [ ] Quoted numbers match tests; constructions have textual equivalents; captions exist for every existing caller (in the node's `returnCaptions[]` or on the caller's link record); planned callers are recorded.
- [ ] Every prerequisite carries `kind`: the three proof-edge prerequisites resolve to authored nodes, and the cross-link to `foundation:vectors-components` renders "available later" until `am-found-linear-geometry-7w15` authors it.

## Test Plan

### Unit and integration tests
- Numeric checks: 499.65 nm at 600 THz; $1/c = 3.3356\times10^{-9}$ N per watt (twice for reflection); the midpoint assignment 5; the $\cos^2$ period average 0.5 to $10^{-12}$; $P/(4\pi r^2) = 0.0795775$ W/m² at 1 m and $0.0198944$ at 2 m.
- Every numeric comparison calls `withinTolerance` from `src/units/tolerance.ts` (`am-ver-tolerance-module-ho90`) with the tolerance stated beside the value.
- Wording check that the sound Doppler example carries its analogy label.
- Compiler checks for registry entries, link-record captions, and typed prerequisites: a fixture that retypes the vectors cross-link as `proof-edge` fails the build while `foundation:vectors-components` is `planned`, and a fixture prerequisite without `kind` is rejected by the schema.

### End-to-end tests
- Open `foundation:frames-events` in the drawer from a fixture calling passage, step through the ledger by keyboard, and return with scroll restored.
- Open `foundation:momentum-energy-light` standalone, compute the push for 1 W, and read the table equivalent; repeat with JavaScript disabled.
- The mass–energy, relativity, and light routes are exercised by those papers' content lanes.

### Structured logging
- JSONL to `artifacts/test-logs/found-fields-light/<log-run-id>.jsonl` with `timestamp`, `suite`, `logRunId`, `testId`, `beadId`, `foundationId`, `callingAnchor`, `expected`, `actual`, `tolerance`, `outcome`, `viewport`, `jsEnabled`, `message`; failure evidence retained.

## Considerations and Pitfalls

- Never conflate what a distant camera sees with a simultaneous coordinate measurement.
- Keep Gaussian and SI conventions labeled when field formulas appear.
- Time-averaged intensity is a statement about observation; it is not evidence for or against light quanta.

## Dependencies

Blocked by:
- `am-found-library-infra-002t`: rendering, the registry, typed prerequisites, and link-record captions.
- `am-found-calculus-6agg`: authors `foundation:functions-graphs` and `foundation:derivatives`, which these nodes list as proof-edge prerequisites.
- `am-found-quantities-magnitudes-igxe`: authors `foundation:quantities-units`, a proof-edge prerequisite of these nodes.

Unblocks:
- `am-found-prereq-audit-71ot`: audits these nodes, their typed prerequisites, and their backlinks.
- `am-me-readings-69bo`, `am-lq-readings-intro-s2-n0bq`, `am-lq-readings-s3-s4-k923`, `am-lq-readings-s5-s6-deq6`, `am-lq-readings-s7-s9-yorj`, `am-srk-readings-intro-s2-00vk`, `am-sre-readings-s6-c5i4`, `am-sre-readings-s7-s8-lpje`, `am-sre-readings-s9-s10-3myq`: these readings link these nodes.
- `am-lq-equations-s1-s4-9gl5`: its chain tool links and equation readings link the fields-and-waves and electromagnetism nodes.
- `am-disc-desk-1904-9hgd`: the 1904 desk's objects link these nodes.

title: Build the foundation library routes, drawer, backlinks, return captions, and proof-route checks
description:
# Build the foundation library routes, drawer, backlinks, return captions, and proof-route checks

**Epic:** `am-ep-foundations-z1e` · **Batch:** batch-b · **Priority:** P0 · **Plan sections:** §1.5 item 2, §6.4, §6.8, §7.5, §15.1, §16.2, §16.3, §19.4 reader-shell closure (traceability only)

## Background

Unfamiliar mathematics must open into an explanation with a worked example, a picture or manipulable construction, and a route back to the exact interrupted argument. The foundation library is that route. It must work in two ways:
- as a drawer inside the reader, so the return stack keeps the paragraph, selected expression, laboratory state, and scroll position;
- as standalone pages at `/foundations` and `/foundations/[concept]`.

The reader shell's closure condition applies here too: a deep-linked passage survives face switching and foundation return.

The library is shared by four papers authored across Batches B to H by different agents. Two structural choices keep that safe:
- A **registry** of canonical ids (defined in `am-ep-foundations-z1e`) fixes every node's identity and single owner before its content exists.
- **Return captions** come from the caller's link record or from the node's `returnCaptions[]`, under one precedence rule, so a later paper never has to edit a foundation record owned by another bead.

A third structural choice belongs here for the same reason. Every foundation and every bridge requires "one worked example", and nothing says what an example is made of, so the shape would be left to each of the nine authoring beads. The five-part shape below lands with the registry, before the cluster beads author content, so it costs one decision rather than nine revisits.

## Scope

In scope:
- routes and index; drawer mode;
- registration of the `foundation` clarification kind in the reader's closed kind registry;
- the registry file and its validation;
- rendering of `Foundation` records and zero-algebra bridge records;
- the five-part worked-example contract, its rendering, and its validation in this bead's compiler projection;
- the transfer-case content contract and its coverage findings;
- link records and computed backlinks; per-link return-caption validation;
- stopping-point display and "deeper derivation available" markers;
- print and no-JavaScript rendering; accessibility of embedded constructions;
- tests.

Out of scope: authoring foundation content (the cluster beads and `am-bm-slice-foundations-f5z9`); the `Foundation`, `FoundationLink`, `WorkedExample`, and typed-prerequisite schemas themselves (`am-cm-schemas-argument-llm`, which adds the structured worked example with a schema-version bump at this bead's request); the return stack, its store, and the `?open=` parser (`am-read-return-stack-oxa`); the compiler's acyclicity check itself (`am-cm-checks-epistemic-o7n`); the `support` ladder field and its stage semantics on journeys (`am-disc-journey-framework-umbg`, which consumes this contract); the voice-lint engine and its vocabulary file (`am-edit-voice-lint-trmf`); search indexing (`am-plat-search-index-snx1`); the prerequisite dead-end audit (`am-found-prereq-audit-71ot`).

## Requirements

- **Registry.** `content/foundations/registry.yaml` lists all 46 canonical ids from `am-ep-foundations-z1e` (36 nodes, 10 bridges), each with `id` (`foundation:<slug>`), `kind` (`node` or `bridge`), `cluster`, `ownerBead`, `status` (`planned` or `authored`), and `plannedCallers` (anchor ids expected from later papers).
  - The compiler fails on a duplicate id, an id without exactly one owner, a record whose id is not in the registry, an `authored` entry without a record, and a record whose kind differs from its registry entry.
  - This bead creates the registry with all 46 entries `planned`; owning beads flip their entries to `authored` in the same change that adds the record.
- **Routes.** `/foundations` lists every authored node grouped by cluster with its concrete entry point, and lists bridges in a separate "Explain from the beginning" group. `/foundations/[concept]` renders one node or bridge, where `[concept]` is the id's slug. One canonical URL per id; planned entries return not-found, never a placeholder page. Drawer deep links on reader routes use `?open=foundation:<slug>`, the form used by `am-bm-slice-foundations-f5z9`.
- **The `foundation` clarification kind.** `am-read-return-stack-oxa` owns a **closed** registry of clarification kinds and names this bead as the registrar of `foundation`. This bead therefore calls `registerClarificationKind("foundation", { parseId, render, staticHref, title })` exactly once, at module scope of the foundations feature:
  - `parseId` accepts `foundation:<slug>` where `<slug>` is the id's slug under the id grammar of `docs/CONTENT_IDS.md` (lowercase words and digits joined by hyphens, a dot only between two digits), resolves it against the registry, and returns the canonical `foundation:<slug>` id; an unknown, planned, or malformed slug returns no value so the return stack ignores the `?open=` value rather than opening an empty drawer;
  - `render` draws the record in the companion column or bottom sheet described under Drawer mode;
  - `staticHref` returns `/foundations/<slug>`, which is what a no-JavaScript reader follows and what print uses;
  - `title` returns the node's learning objective heading for the drawer header, the compass entry, and the browser history entry.
  - Registering the kind twice throws in development and fails a test, per the return-stack contract. No other bead registers `foundation`, and this bead registers no other kind (`example` and `obstacle` belong to `am-read-passage-actions-vbe`).
- **Record rendering.** Learning objective; compact explanation; full explanation; one worked example in the five-part shape below; an optional instrument or manipulable construction (by instrument id and preset id, following the action contract); a textual equivalent; prerequisites (links); the stated stopping point; backlinks. If a referenced instrument or preset is not yet registered, the construction renders its static worked example with a visible "interactive version not yet available" status, never a broken embed.

### A worked example has five authored parts

The most valuable part of a good example is the part an author is least likely to write unprompted, so `WorkedExample` is a structured record with five required parts, added to the `Foundation` entity by `am-cm-schemas-argument-llm` with a schema-version bump (the pattern `am-read-notebook-tde` uses for `ArgumentNode.recap`; requested with a `br comments add` note). This bead owns the rendering and the projection-time validation.

| Part | What it holds |
|---|---|
| `question` | The specific thing this example settles, in one sentence, naming the quantity |
| `given` | The information the reader starts with: the numbers, the units, and what is held fixed |
| `plausibleFirstThought` | **One reasonable first move a reader actually makes here**, stated without irony, with one sentence on why it is reasonable |
| `decisiveStep` | The calculation or comparison that settles the question, with its arithmetic shown |
| `limitation` | Where this example stops: what it does not show, and what changes at a realistic scale |

`plausibleFirstThought` is the part that earns the change. The editorial voice already forbids "obviously", "clearly" and "it is easy to see" (`am-edit-voice-lint-trmf`), on the reasoning that a reader at "Show every step" would not be there if it were easy. An example that shows only the correct move breaks that rule structurally rather than lexically: it implies the move was the natural one. Naming the reasonable first thought is the same fair-hearing discipline the site applies to Nägeli and Exner, applied to the reader.

Worked values in existing content, authored by the beads that own those records and shown here as the shape:

- The Brownian entrance (`am-bm-first-encounter-fjvh`): `question` is whether four observations summing to zero show no movement; `given` is $-3, -1, +1, +3$ units, labeled authored and not measured; `plausibleFirstThought` is "add them up, which gives zero, so nothing moved"; the `decisiveStep` compares mean absolute displacement 2 with mean square 5, and doubling to 4 and 20; `limitation` says the four entries are an arithmetic illustration and that the real growth law needs many independent steps.
- `foundation:ratios-scaling` (owned by `am-found-quantities-magnitudes-igxe`): `plausibleFirstThought` is "doubling the viscosity halves the displacement", the site's own adversarial fixture, and the `decisiveStep` shows the change is $1/\sqrt{2} = 0.70711$.

Rules:

- `limitation` may not be empty. An example with no stated limit is an example claiming to be general, which no example is.
- `plausibleFirstThought` may not be phrased as a mistake the reader should not have made. The voice lint gains a small rule set for it: no "of course", no "many people wrongly", no "the naive answer". It is registered with `am-edit-voice-lint-trmf`, not kept here, so no parallel deny list exists.
- The `decisiveStep` is **revealable immediately**. It renders inside a native disclosure open by default at Detail "Show every step" and closed at "Overview" and "Full explanation", with a control that opens it in one action. There is no gate, no attempt counter, and no record of whether the reader opened it. Struggling first is never required and revealing is never counted.
- The five parts render in order, statically, in print, and without JavaScript, where the disclosure is the browser's own.

### Transfer changes a condition, not a number

`am-disc-journey-framework-umbg` carries `support.transferCase` on every stage and owns that field. Its content contract belongs here, because a transfer case is a worked example with one condition moved, and the foundations projection is where examples are validated:

- A transfer case changes something **structural**: a different statistic, a different pair of events, a different system boundary. Changing only the numbers is not a transfer case, and the coverage pass reports it as `transfer-not-structural`.
- The three cases the site already has the instruments for:
  - after explaining mean square, ask about mean absolute displacement (BM-01, whose statistic control offers it as an `estimator-change`, and the entrance's own arithmetic module `src/reader/entrances/signedDisplacements.ts`);
  - after explaining contraction, ask for a different pair of endpoint events (SR-03, whose rod measurement is exactly a choice of two named events);
  - after an energy ledger, change the chosen system boundary (ME-03, whose boundary is a control).
- **Feedback contract.** The authored response to a transfer case names two things explicitly: **what remains valid** from the original example, and **which newly introduced condition changes the answer**. A response that only states the new answer fails the coverage pass with `transfer-feedback-incomplete`. This is what turns a transfer case from a second exercise into an account of what the reader now understands.
- Both findings are written in the input format of `am-cm-coverage-ledger-0ip`, the format this bead's other coverage output already uses.
- Transfer feedback is never scored and never recorded as competence, consistent with this bead's "No tests or scores" requirement below.

- **Zero-algebra bridges.** A bridge record renders its small obstacle, concrete bridge, and "readiness shown without a test." "Explain from the beginning" in the reader lands on a bridge, never on another paragraph of abstract vocabulary. A bridge carries the same five-part worked example as a node.
- **Link records and backlinks.** Every reference to a foundation from a reading, equation tool link, derivation step, instrument caption, or "What is getting in the way?" response is a `FoundationLink` record `{foundationId, callingAnchor, returnCaption?}` (the shape defined in `am-cm-schemas-argument-llm`), stored with the calling record and authored by its owner.
  - The compiler computes backlinks from link records; each backlink shows the calling anchor, a short context, and the caption.
  - **Return-caption precedence**, the contract this bead enforces when it computes backlinks: the link's `returnCaption` is used when present; otherwise the node's `returnCaptions[]` entry for the same `callingAnchor`; a link with neither caption fails the build; a link whose own caption and the node's entry for that anchor both exist and differ fails the build; a node `returnCaptions[]` entry whose anchor has no link is flagged as stale.
  - **Typed prerequisites.** Prerequisites are typed `{foundationId, kind: "proof-edge" | "cross-link"}` (the field name is `kind`, as landed in `am-cm-schemas-argument-llm`; a prerequisite without `kind`, or with `kind: "proof"`, is rejected by the schema). A link from a calling passage, or a prerequisite of `proof-edge` type, to a `planned` or unknown id fails the build. A prerequisite typed as a `cross-link` to a `planned` id renders as "available later" and is reported by `am-found-prereq-audit-71ot` until its target is authored. Cross-link prerequisites never enter a proof route's acyclicity check.
- **Return captions.** Authored per calling passage, naming the right quantity and what is held fixed there (for example, "Back to light quanta §3: $\partial\varphi/\partial\rho$ with volume and frequency held fixed").
- **Drawer mode.** Opening a foundation from the reader uses the companion column on desktop and a bottom sheet on phones; the return stack and compass restore the exact sentence, expression, laboratory state, and scroll position; one action closes all side explanations.
- **Proof routes.** Where a foundation is a tool in a selected proof route, the page shows the route back to entry assumptions and marks deeper derivations as available; concept-map cross-links are displayed as cross-links. A reader may stop at an understood result.
- **Print and no-JavaScript.** Full static HTML; drawers degrade to real links produced by the kind's `staticHref`; print expands essential parts, including the decisive step and the limitation, and never prints a collapsed heading alone.
- **No tests or scores.** Nodes never quiz the reader or record competence.

## Technical Approach

- Pages under `src/app/foundations/`; rendering components under `src/reader/`; registry, worked-example, transfer-case, link-record, backlink, and caption validation in the content compiler's route projection.
- The drawer uses the return-stack store from `am-read-return-stack-oxa`, and the `foundation` kind is registered against that bead's `registerClarificationKind` API; foundation pages consume only compiled, route-local payloads.
- `FoundationLink`, `WorkedExample`, and the typed prerequisite shape are imported from the shared schemas of `am-cm-schemas-argument-llm`, never redeclared here.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The registry exists with all 46 canonical ids, kinds, owners, and statuses, and its validation rules fail on the fixture violations listed below.
- [ ] The registry's node, bridge and id totals come from the canonical id table of `am-ep-foundations-z1e` rather than from a number typed here; a fixture registry holding 45 entries against that bead's 46-row table fails with both counts named.
- [ ] Index and node routes render every authored foundation and bridge statically; planned ids return not-found.
- [ ] The `foundation` clarification kind is registered exactly once with `parseId`, `render`, `staticHref`, and `title`; `?open=foundation:<slug>` opens the drawer for an authored id and is ignored for an unknown, planned, or malformed one; a second registration fails.
- [ ] Every backlink has exactly one return caption (from its link record or the node's `returnCaptions[]`) and every link resolves to an authored id; the build fails otherwise.
- [ ] A `proof-edge` prerequisite to a planned id fails the build, while a `cross-link` prerequisite to a planned id renders "available later" and is reported to the prerequisite audit.
- [ ] Drawer open and close restores the exact reading state on desktop and at 320 px.
- [ ] "Explain from the beginning" lands on bridge records.
- [ ] A construction whose instrument is unregistered renders its static worked example with the status line.
- [ ] Print and JavaScript-disabled renderings are complete, and every drawer link has a real `staticHref` target.
- [ ] Every authored `Foundation` and bridge carries a five-part `WorkedExample`; a record missing any part fails compilation with the part named and the foundation id.
- [ ] An empty `limitation` fails; an empty `plausibleFirstThought` fails.
- [ ] The five parts render in order on `/foundations/[concept]` and in the drawer, at every Detail, in print, and with JavaScript disabled.
- [ ] `decisiveStep` is open by default at "Show every step" and closed at the other two Detail levels, opens in one action, and nothing about opening it is stored or logged as reader behavior.
- [ ] Voice lint fails a seeded `plausibleFirstThought` containing "of course", "many people wrongly" and "the naive answer", and passes the Brownian entrance's version.
- [ ] Every `support.transferCase` in a compiled journey changes a structural condition; a fixture that changes only numbers is reported as `transfer-not-structural`.
- [ ] Every transfer case's feedback names what remains valid and which new condition changes the answer; a fixture stating only the new answer fails with `transfer-feedback-incomplete`.
- [ ] The three named transfer cases resolve to `bm-01`, `sr-03` and `me-03` respectively, each naming an action its instrument's action contract offers.

## Test Plan

### Unit and integration tests
- `foundationRegistry.test.ts`, registry validation with fixtures:
  - a duplicate id fails;
  - an id with two owners fails;
  - a record missing from the registry fails;
  - an `authored` entry without a record fails;
  - a kind mismatch fails;
  - the real registry has exactly 36 nodes and 10 bridges, and every `ownerBead` is a bead id that exists;
  - a registry whose entry count differs from the canonical id table of `am-ep-foundations-z1e` fails naming both counts, and `foundation:two-measurements-two-unknowns` resolves to `am-found-statistics-inference-pzqv` with `kind: node`.
- `foundationRender.test.tsx`: rendering with fixture records: all parts present; optional construction absent renders cleanly; unregistered instrument renders the static example and status; a bridge renders obstacle, bridge, and readiness.
- `foundationKind.test.ts`: the clarification-kind registration: the kind registry contains `foundation` after the feature module loads; `parseId("foundation:mean-variance-rms")` resolves for an authored id; `parseId` returns nothing for an unknown slug, a `planned` id, an uppercase or dotted slug, and an over-long value; `staticHref` returns `/foundations/mean-variance-rms`; `title` returns the node's learning objective; a second `registerClarificationKind("foundation", ...)` throws.
- `foundationBacklinks.test.ts`, compiler projection tests: backlinks computed from fixture link records; a link whose caption comes from the node's `returnCaptions[]` passes; a link with no caption in either place fails with a message naming the calling anchor; a link caption and a node caption for the same anchor that differ fail; a stale node caption is flagged; a calling link or `proof-edge` prerequisite to a planned id fails, while a `cross-link` prerequisite to a planned id renders as available later and appears in the audit input; a prerequisite without `kind` is rejected by the schema; a bridge lacking a required field fails.
- `foundationProofRoutes.test.ts`: a fixture route with a cross-link cycle renders, while a cycle inside a selected proof route is rejected by the compiler check.
- `workedExample.schema.test.ts` (real schema, real fixture foundations):
  - all five parts required, each absence failing with the part named;
  - an empty `limitation` and an empty `plausibleFirstThought` fail;
  - the Brownian entrance's example validates, and its `decisiveStep` arithmetic is checked against `src/reader/entrances/signedDisplacements.ts`: signed sum 0, mean absolute 2, mean square 5, doubled 4 and 20, RMS $\sqrt5 = 2.2360680$ and $\sqrt{20} = 4.4721360$, compared through `withinTolerance` from `src/units/tolerance.ts`;
  - the `foundation:ratios-scaling` example's `decisiveStep` asserts $1/\sqrt{2} = 0.7071068$ and not $0.5$.
- `workedExample.render.test.tsx`: part order; disclosure open at Detail 2 and closed at 0 and 1; one action opens it; no storage write and no log event on open; native disclosure without JavaScript.
- `voiceLint.integration.test.ts` (addition): the `plausibleFirstThought` rule set, one passing and one failing fixture per banned phrase.
- `transferCase.test.ts` (against real compiled journeys):
  - a case that changes only a numeric input is reported as `transfer-not-structural`;
  - feedback missing either half fails with `transfer-feedback-incomplete`;
  - the three named cases resolve to `bm-01`, `sr-03` and `me-03` and each names an action present in that instrument's action contract;
  - both findings validate against the coverage ledger's input schema.

### End-to-end tests
- From a reading-face paragraph in the Brownian reference slice:
  - Open a foundation in the drawer, operate its construction, follow a prerequisite, and use the compass to return.
  - Assert sentence focus, selected expression, laboratory snapshot id, and scroll offset are restored, and the caption shown is the one the precedence rule selects.
  - Open the same node from a `?open=foundation:<slug>` deep link and assert the drawer opens at that id with its compass; request `?open=foundation:not-a-node` and assert the value is ignored and the passage still renders.
  - Repeat at 320 px (bottom sheet), keyboard-only, with reduced motion, and with JavaScript disabled (the drawer link degrades to the `staticHref` page).
- Print a foundation page and assert expanded content, including the decisive step and the limitation; request a planned id and assert not-found.
- In `e2e/foundations/worked-example.spec.ts`, through `am-test-e2e-harness-bqmh`:
  1. Open a foundation from a Brownian §4 passage in the drawer, read the five parts in order, and reveal the decisive step in one action.
  2. Switch Detail to "Show every step" and assert the decisive step is already open.
  3. Assert the network log records no request and the storage layer records no write from opening it.
  4. Follow a transfer case from a journey stage, read the feedback, and assert it names both halves.
  5. Repeat with JavaScript disabled using the native disclosure, at 320 px, keyboard only, and in print.

### Structured logging
- JSONL to `artifacts/test-logs/foundations-infra/<log-run-id>.jsonl` with `timestamp`, `suite: "foundations-infra"`, `logRunId`, `testId`, `beadId`, `foundationId`, `callingAnchor`, `returnAnchor`, `captionSource` (`link` or `node`), `prerequisiteKind`, restored state fields (`snapshotVersion`, scroll offset, expression id), `outcome`, `viewport`, `jsEnabled`, `reducedMotion`, `message`; failure evidence (screenshot, trace, DOM snapshot, console log) retained under `artifacts/test-logs/foundations-infra/<log-run-id>/evidence/`.
- Worked-example and transfer lines add `kind` (`node` or `bridge`), `examplePartsPresent`, `limitationLength`, `firstThoughtLength`, `decisiveStepOpenByDefault`, `detail`, `transferCaseId`, `transferChangesCondition`, `feedbackHalvesPresent`, `instrumentId`, `rule`, `expected`, `actual`, `tolerance`, and `comparisonKind`.
- Logs never record whether a reader opened the decisive step; `decisiveStepOpenByDefault` records the authored default, not a reader action.

## Considerations and Pitfalls

- Never let a foundation become an infinite cascade of definitions; the stopping point is part of the record.
- Do not duplicate foundation text inside readings; R2 embeds foundations by reference.
- Do not let a later bead edit another bead's foundation record to add a caption; a later caller's caption belongs on its own link record.
- Do not widen the clarification-kind registry: it is closed, and `foundation` is the only kind registered here.
- `plausibleFirstThought` is not a misconception entry. A misconception is a belief a reader carries in; a first thought is a move a reader makes here, and most first thoughts are partly right.
- Do not use the first thought to set up a reveal. It is stated, it is respected, and the decisive step shows what it does and does not settle.
- `limitation` is where the example stops, not where the physics stops. "Four entries are not a distribution" is a limitation of the example; "the diffusive law needs intervals long compared with the relaxation time" is a limitation of the model and belongs to the argument node.
- Never gate the decisive step behind an attempt. The site's own rule is that guessing is never a condition for continuing, and an example that hides its answer until the reader tries is a quiz.
- The transfer feedback's "what remains valid" half is the one authors drop. It is also the half that produces transfer: a reader who is told only the new answer learns a second fact, not a method.
- Nine beads author examples. Landing the shape after they start means nine revisits, so it belongs here, with the registry, before the cluster beads author content.

## Dependencies

Blocked by:
- `am-read-shell-routes-3ua`: App Router structure and reader shell.
- `am-read-return-stack-oxa`: return stack, compass, the `?open=` parser, and the `registerClarificationKind` API this bead calls.
- `am-cm-schemas-argument-llm`: the `Foundation` schema, the structured five-part `WorkedExample`, the `FoundationLink` shape with its return-caption precedence, and prerequisites typed `{foundationId, kind}`.
- `am-edit-voice-lint-trmf`: the `plausibleFirstThought` rule set is registered there rather than kept here, the same arrangement `am-read-passage-actions-vbe` has for its banned phrasings.

Unblocks:
- `am-bm-slice-foundations-f5z9`, `am-found-quantities-magnitudes-igxe`, `am-found-calculus-6agg`, `am-found-statistics-inference-pzqv`, `am-found-transport-thermo-smv3`, `am-found-linear-geometry-7w15`, `am-found-fields-light-cv3o`, `am-found-reading-german-u8oc`, `am-found-zero-algebra-rest-oipl`: the cluster beads author records against this registry, these rules, and the five-part example shape.
- `am-eq-derivation-renderer-9gd7`: derivation-step tool links open foundations through this drawer.
- `am-disc-journey-framework-umbg`: journey stages link foundations with return captions, and their `support.transferCase` entries are validated against the contract above.
- `am-tours-infra-g518`: tour anchors may address a foundation page.
- `am-rel-candidate-checks-kc7y`: candidate checks load representative foundation pages on the deployed assets.

title: Author foundations: vectors, matrices and linear maps, dot and cross products, hyperbolic functions and rapidity, conservation and symmetry
description:
# Author foundations: vectors, matrices and linear maps, dot and cross products, hyperbolic functions and rapidity, conservation and symmetry

**Epic:** `am-ep-foundations-z1e` · **Batch:** batch-e · **Priority:** P1 · **Plan sections:** §5.3 (later aids), §4.7 (the $\beta$ collision), §7.5, §8.3 (constructed map, boost matrix, rapidity), §12.6 (observer change), §13.3 (boost fixtures) (traceability only)

## Background

The relativity paper and its instruments ask readers to:
- describe one event or one arrow in two frames;
- read a transformation as a rule that combines inputs;
- follow field components parallel and perpendicular to a boost;
- recognize what stays unchanged when the description changes.

These nodes supply those tools for the programmer who thinks in matrices and for the reader meeting them for the first time. Rapidity and spacetime geometry are later aids and are labeled as such; they never become premises of the 1905 route.

One notation hazard runs through this cluster. The usual modern shorthand $\beta = v/c$ collides with the site's most dangerous collision: Einstein's $\beta$ is the modern $\gamma$ in papers 3 and 4, and Wien's constant in paper 1. These nodes therefore write $v/c$ and never use $\beta$ for it.

## Scope

Nodes owned here (canonical ids from `am-ep-foundations-z1e`):

| Id | Concrete entry point | What the reader can do afterward |
|---|---|---|
| `foundation:vectors-components` | Describe one arrow in two coordinate systems | Change components without confusing that with changing the object |
| `foundation:matrices-linear-maps` | Transform a grid and an event table together; determinants, eigenvectors | Read a matrix as a rule for combining inputs |
| `foundation:dot-cross-products` | Projection and oriented area | Follow field transformations and magnetic-force directions |
| `foundation:hyperbolic-functions-rapidity` | $\cosh$, $\sinh$, $\tanh$ and why boosts add like angles | Follow the composition of velocities (labeled as a later aid) |
| `foundation:conservation-symmetry` | Relabel an experiment or change frame | Identify a quantity or relation that should remain unchanged |

Owned elsewhere: frames and events (`foundation:frames-events`, `am-found-fields-light-cv3o`); exponentials and logarithms (`am-found-calculus-6agg`); the binomial series used for low-speed expansions (the Taylor extension authored by `am-found-calculus-6agg`).

## Requirements

**Worked examples (modern golden values, verified by test).**
- **Vectors and components.** One velocity of $0.6c$ along $x$ described in rotated axes. The same field vector split into components parallel and perpendicular to a boost. Changing the description is an observer change, not a change of the world.
- **Matrices and linear maps.**
  - The boost at $v = 0.6c$ acting on $(x, t)$ is $\begin{pmatrix}1.25 & -0.75c\\ -0.75/c & 1.25\end{pmatrix}$, with determinant 1.
  - Its eigenvectors lie on the light lines $x = \pm ct$, with eigenvalues 0.5 and 2.
  - Two events 10 light-seconds apart and simultaneous map to $\Delta t' = -7.5$ s and $\Delta x' = 12.5$ light-seconds.
  - Contrast the Galilean map $\begin{pmatrix}1 & -v\\ 0 & 1\end{pmatrix}$, also of determinant 1, which does not keep light lines fixed.
  - The matrix view is a pedagogical aid, not the paper's §3 presentation. The diagonal entry is written $\gamma = 1.25$, with the note that the relativity paper prints this quantity as $\beta$.
- **Dot and cross products.** $\mathbf{E}_\parallel$ as a projection on the boost direction; the direction of $q\,\mathbf{v}\times\mathbf{B}$; $\mathbf{E}\cdot\mathbf{B}$ as a modern invariant check.
- **Hyperbolic functions and rapidity (later aid).**
  - $\gamma = \cosh\phi$, $\gamma\,v/c = \sinh\phi$, $v/c = \tanh\phi$.
  - $v/c = 0.6$ gives $\phi = \ln 2$. Two collinear boosts of $0.6c$ add rapidities to $\ln 4$, so $v/c = \tanh(\ln 4) = 15/17 \approx 0.8824$.
  - The eigenvalues $e^{\mp\phi}$ are the Doppler factors 1/2 and 2.
  - The node does not write $\beta$ for $v/c$, and its first-use note warns that Einstein's $\beta$ is the modern $\gamma$ (papers 3 and 4) and Wien's constant (paper 1).
- **Conservation and symmetry.** The light-speed postulate as a relation kept in both frames. In the two-pulse argument, energies differ between frames while each frame's balance holds. Interval preservation serves as a modern verification oracle, never a premise of the historical route.

**Constructions.** An arrow with draggable axes and a component table; a grid-and-event-table transformer with determinant and eigenvector readouts; a projection and oriented-area view; a rapidity adder; a "change the description, keep the world" comparison using the command-class vocabulary. Each has a textual equivalent and keyboard operation. Where a construction would embed an SR instrument preset (for example SR-04's matrix view) that is not yet registered, the node shows its static worked example with the library's status line.

**Prerequisites.** Every prerequisite is typed `{foundationId, kind}` (`am-cm-schemas-argument-llm`), each a link record with a caption: `foundation:quantities-units` and `foundation:functions-graphs` are `proof-edge` prerequisites (authored in Batch C); vectors is a `proof-edge` prerequisite of matrices and of the products node; `foundation:exponentials` and `foundation:logarithms` are `proof-edge` prerequisites of the rapidity node; `foundation:frames-events` is a `cross-link` from the conservation node, so the Batch D cluster's node may render "available later" without weakening any proof route.

**Calling passages and return captions.** Captions follow the rule in `am-found-library-infra-002t`: this bead records captions for callers that already exist in the node's `returnCaptions[]`, and later callers put theirs on their own link records. This bead authors captions only for callers that exist when it lands. It records relativity §§3, 5, 6, and 7, SR-04, SR-06, SR-08, and mass–energy's two ledgers as `plannedCallers`; those beads author their captions when they link.

**Stopping points.**
- Vector: "an arrow with a length and a direction."
- Matrix: "a table of multipliers applied to inputs."
- Dot product: "how much of one arrow lies along another."
- Hyperbolic functions: "combinations of $e^x$ and $e^{-x}$."
- Symmetry: "a change that leaves the measured outcome unchanged."

## Technical Approach

- Records under `content/foundations/`. Numeric examples are pulled from `am-ref-kinematics-tjq` fixtures at build time where constructions embed live values, and every comparison runs through `src/units/tolerance.ts` (`am-ver-tolerance-module-ho90`). Later-aid labels are carried as historical-status metadata so `am-cm-anachronism-lint-dl2` can check them. Registry entries are flipped to `authored` in the same change.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Five complete records with all parts and stopping points, registered under their canonical ids with this bead as owner.
- [ ] Rapidity and the matrix view carry later-aid labels; nothing presents interval preservation as a 1904 premise.
- [ ] No node uses $\beta$ for $v/c$; the collision note appears at first use of $\gamma$ and $v/c$.
- [ ] Quoted values match tests; constructions have textual equivalents; captions exist for every existing caller (in the node's `returnCaptions[]` or on the caller's link record); planned callers are recorded; every prerequisite carries its `kind`.

## Test Plan

### Unit and integration tests
- `foundLinearGeometry.numbers.test.ts`, through `src/units/tolerance.ts`: $\gamma = 1.25$ and $\gamma\,v/c = 0.75$ at $0.6c$; determinant $1.25^2 - 0.75^2 = 1$; eigenvalues 0.5 and 2; $\Delta t' = -7.5$ s and $\Delta x' = 12.5$ light-seconds for two simultaneous events 10 light-seconds apart; $\operatorname{artanh}(0.6) = \ln 2 = 0.6931471806$; $\tanh(\ln 4) = 15/17 = 0.8823529412$; the Galilean map's determinant is also 1 while its eigenvectors are not the light lines.
- `foundLinearGeometry.glyph.test.ts`: a check fails if any of these records binds $\beta$ to `speedRatio` or writes "β = v/c", and asserts the collision note is present at first use of $\gamma$.
- `foundLinearGeometry.records.test.ts`: anachronism lint over the records (later-aid labels present and dated); compiler checks for registry entries, link-record captions, and typed prerequisites.
- Failure evidence (the failing value or record id, expected and actual) is written beside the log and retained.

### End-to-end tests
- Open `foundation:matrices-linear-maps` in the drawer from a fixture calling passage in the compiled test corpus, transform the event table by keyboard, read the determinant, and return to the fixture anchor with scroll restored.
- Open `foundation:hyperbolic-functions-rapidity` standalone and assert the later-aid label and the $\beta$ collision note; repeat with JavaScript disabled.
- The relativity routes (from SR-04 and §§3–7) are exercised by the relativity content lanes.

### Structured logging
- JSONL to `artifacts/test-logs/found-linear-geometry/<log-run-id>.jsonl` with `timestamp`, `suite`, `logRunId`, `testId`, `beadId`, `foundationId`, `callingAnchor`, `expected`, `actual`, `tolerance`, `outcome`, `viewport`, `jsEnabled`, `message`; failure evidence retained.

## Considerations and Pitfalls

- Passive frame changes and active physical changes must never blur; say which one each example is.
- Non-collinear boost composition includes a rotation; the rapidity node restricts its adding rule to collinear boosts and says so.

## Dependencies

Blocked by:
- `am-found-library-infra-002t`: rendering, the registry, and link-record captions.
- `am-ref-kinematics-tjq`: the boost fixtures quoted here.

Unblocks:
- `am-found-prereq-audit-71ot`: the audit covers these nodes.
- `am-srk-readings-s3-odqp`, `am-srk-readings-s4-s5-njsh`, `am-sre-readings-s6-c5i4`: these readings link these nodes.
- `am-disc-desk-1904-9hgd`: the 1904 desk's shelf explanations link the vector and symmetry nodes.

title: Audit the prerequisite graph for dead ends, stopping points, and complete backlinks
description:
# Audit the prerequisite graph for dead ends, stopping points, and complete backlinks

**Epic:** `am-ep-foundations-z1e` · **Batch:** batch-h · **Priority:** P1 · **Plan sections:** §1.5 item 2, §6.4, §7.5, §19.3 H exit, §21 ("the arguments are reconstructible") (traceability only)

## Background

Batch H's exit evidence includes a prerequisite graph with no dead ends, and the launch definition requires that a reader can follow each main result without a missing prerequisite. Once the four papers have passed their definitions of done, this audit proves the foundation library actually closes every gap the papers open, and that every explanation ends at a stated stopping point instead of an infinite cascade.

The library's structure makes most of this mechanically checkable:
- the registry of 45 canonical ids with exactly one owner each (`am-ep-foundations-z1e`, `am-found-library-infra-002t`);
- link records that carry their own return captions;
