- typed prerequisites, `{foundationId, kind: "proof-edge" | "cross-link"}` (`am-cm-schemas-argument-llm`), where a cross-link to a node still `planned` renders "available later" and is reported here until the node is authored;
- `plannedCallers` recorded by each owning bead for passages authored later.

## Scope

In scope: an automated audit across all four papers plus an editorial spot-check; a written report; issues filed against owning beads.

Out of scope: writing or fixing content (owning beads); the proof-route acyclicity check itself (`am-cm-checks-epistemic-o7n`), whose results the audit consumes; the readings-ownership audit (`audit-readings.ts`), whose `owner-unassigned` and `owner-conflict` results the papers' definition-of-done beads consume.

## Requirements

**Automated checks (`scripts/audit-prerequisites.ts`, run by `verify-content`).**
- **Registry.** All 35 foundation nodes and 10 bridges in `content/foundations/registry.yaml` are `authored`, each with exactly one owning bead; no entry is `planned`. Extension section records (for example the binomial-series section of `foundation:taylor-expansion` and the inference sections of the statistics nodes) name their owning bead and attach to an authored node.
- **Records.** Every foundation has a compact explanation, worked example, textual equivalent, prerequisites, stopping point, and at least one calling passage. A node with no calling passage is flagged for editorial review.
- **Planned callers.** Every `plannedCallers` entry either appears as an actual link record from that anchor, or is removed from the registry with a written reason.
- **Prerequisites.** Every prerequisite id resolves and carries its `kind`. Following `proof-edge` prerequisites from any node terminates at stopping points or bridges (no dangling chains). Cross-links are typed as cross-links and are excluded from the proof-route acyclicity check. **At audit time no cross-link prerequisite may still render "available later":** a cross-link whose target is still `planned` is a finding against the target's owning bead, because by Batch H every registry entry is `authored`.
- **Links and captions.** Every link record resolves to an authored id and carries a return caption that names a quantity or an operation. Every computed backlink therefore has a caption. No calling link points at a `planned` id.
- **Drawer addressing.** The `foundation` clarification kind is registered exactly once (by `am-found-library-infra-002t`), and every `?open=foundation:<slug>` appearing in compiled content parses to an authored registry id.
- **Entry to bridges.** Every "Explain from the beginning" action in the four papers lands on a bridge.
- **Tracked operations.** Every occurrence of a tracked mathematical operation in R1 and R2 readings, equation readings, and instrument captions either links a foundation or carries an authored inline explanation. The vocabulary is: derivative, partial derivative, integral, limit, series expansion, binomial series, logarithm (including the printed "lg" for the natural logarithm), exponential, Fourier series, variation with a Lagrange multiplier, vector, matrix, determinant, eigenvector, dot product, cross product, probability, variance, Gaussian, chi-square, hyperbolic function, and a unit-system conversion (abvolt, statvolt, gram-equivalent).
- **Proof routes and labels.** Selected proof routes are acyclic to their entry assumptions (consumed from the compiler), and later aids are labeled.
- **Glyph hygiene.** No foundation text uses $\beta$ for $v/c$ or otherwise binds a scoped paper glyph to a different meaning without its collision note.

**Editorial spot-check.** A reviewer samples at least two hard passages per paper at R2, follows every foundation link to its stopping point, and records whether the return lands on the exact argument with the caption naming the right quantity.

**Report.** `docs/acceptance/foundations-prerequisite-audit.md` with per-paper counts, the registry summary, the flagged items, and links to comments or reopened beads.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The automated audit passes with zero dead ends, zero missing captions, zero `planned` registry entries, zero cross-link prerequisites still rendering "available later", and zero unresolved planned callers.
- [ ] Every flagged orphan node is either linked from a calling passage or removed from the launch set with a written reason (no deletion of files without permission).
- [ ] The spot-check is recorded and its findings resolved.
- [ ] The report is published in the repository.

## Test Plan

### Unit and integration tests
- `auditPrerequisites.fixtures.test.ts`: the audit script's own tests with fixture graphs and registries. Each of the following fails with an actionable message naming the id and its owning bead:
  - a dangling prerequisite;
  - a prerequisite without `kind`;
  - a cross-link prerequisite whose target is still `planned` at audit time;
  - a link record without a caption;
  - a calling link to a planned id;
  - a registry entry with two owners;
  - an unresolved planned caller;
  - an untracked operation without a link;
  - an "Explain from the beginning" action landing on a non-bridge;
  - a `?open=foundation:<slug>` value that does not parse to an authored id;
  - an extension section attached to a missing node;
  - a proof-route cycle.
- A passing fixture proves a cross-link cycle is allowed while every registry entry is `authored`.
- Failure evidence (the finding list with ids, owning beads, and the check that produced each) is written beside the log and retained.

### End-to-end tests
- A browser run that, for each paper, follows one tracked-operation link from R2 to its stopping point and back, asserting exact return and the caption text.

### Structured logging
- JSONL to `artifacts/test-logs/found-prereq-audit/<log-run-id>.jsonl` with `timestamp`, `suite`, `logRunId`, `testId`, `beadId`, `check`, `foundationId` or `anchor`, `prerequisiteKind`, `ownerBead`, `status`, `outcome`, and `message` for each finding; failure evidence retained.

## Considerations and Pitfalls

- The operation vocabulary is a heuristic; the editorial spot-check catches what it misses.
- Fix gaps by improving explanations first; adding a node must be justified by a calling passage.
- A finding is filed against the owning bead, never resolved by editing another bead's record.

## Dependencies

Blocked by:
- `am-found-quantities-magnitudes-igxe`, `am-found-calculus-6agg`, `am-found-statistics-inference-pzqv`, `am-found-transport-thermo-smv3`, `am-found-linear-geometry-7w15`, `am-found-fields-light-cv3o`, `am-found-zero-algebra-rest-oipl`, `am-found-reading-german-u8oc`, `am-bm-slice-foundations-f5z9`: the nodes under audit.
- `am-dod-brownian-2k4y`, `am-dod-mass-energy-oxh2`, `am-dod-relativity-105y`, `am-dod-light-quanta-7as8`: the papers' readings and chains must be complete.

Unblocks:
- `am-tour-evening-and-course-5kcb`: the full course's syllabus lists prerequisites from the audited graph.
- `am-launch-readiness-audit-sc9b`.
- `am-disc-batch-h-exit-audit-r8xq`: the Batch H exit evidence cites this report.

title: Author foundations: quantities and units, ratios and scaling, orders of magnitude, and the 1905 unit system
description:
# Author foundations: quantities and units, ratios and scaling, orders of magnitude, and the 1905 unit system

**Epic:** `am-ep-foundations-z1e` · **Batch:** batch-c · **Priority:** P1 · **Plan sections:** §7.5, §8 intro (constant sets), §13.4 (traceability only)

## Background

Every paper mixes quantities across scales and unit systems: Einstein's printed viscosity in poise, Planck's constants in CGS, the light paper's photoelectric check in electromagnetic CGS units, Gaussian fields in the relativity paper, micrometers and seconds in Brownian motion. These four nodes let any reader place a number on a scale, check whether an equation's dimensions agree, and convert the printed historical values.

Light-paper review r2 found, through a comparison translation and a reviewer's recollection, that paper 1's 4.3 V check appears to use a gram-equivalent charge $E = 9.6\cdot10^{3}$ in **electromagnetic** units, with $\Pi\cdot10^{-8}$ read as volts. An esu elementary charge with a statvolt factor is the documented alternative, and the facsimile decides. The 1905 unit system node therefore covers both CGS electrical systems.

## Scope

Nodes owned here (canonical ids from `am-ep-foundations-z1e`; each with compact explanation, one worked example, construction where useful, textual equivalent, prerequisites, stopping point):

| Id | Concrete entry point | What the reader can do afterward |
|---|---|---|
| `foundation:quantities-units` | Is a number in meters comparable with one in seconds? | Distinguish a quantity from its number; check an equation's dimensions |
| `foundation:ratios-scaling` | Double a length; compare area, volume, and a plotted effect | Predict proportional, inverse, and squared dependence |
| `foundation:orders-of-magnitude` | A water molecule versus a 1 μm grain; $v/c$ for a bullet, a jet, the Earth's orbit, Kaufmann's electrons; $h\nu$ for red, green, ultraviolet; molecular kicks per second on a grain | Place every number in the papers on a scale |
| `foundation:unit-system-1905` | Gaussian and CGS to SI, with Einstein's own numbers | Convert his printed values |

Owned elsewhere: scientific notation and units as a zero-algebra bridge (`foundation:bridge-scientific-notation-units`, `am-bm-slice-foundations-f5z9`); functions and graphs (`am-found-calculus-6agg`).

## Requirements

**Worked examples (numbers verified by test against the reference evaluators and constant sets).**
- **Quantities and units.** $D = k_BT/(6\pi\eta a)$ has units m²/s. The light paper's $\rho_\nu$ is energy per volume per frequency (J s m⁻³), not per wavelength. The same letter can name different quantities in different sections (the light paper's $L$ is the speed of light in §§1–2 and absorbed light energy in §9), so a unit check starts from the quantity, not the glyph.
- **Ratios and scaling.** Doubling a sphere's radius halves $D$ and multiplies the RMS displacement at fixed time by $1/\sqrt{2}$, not by $1/2$. The classical energy with resonators up to a frequency $\nu_c$ grows as $\nu_c^3$, so a tenfold widening gives a thousandfold energy.
- **Orders of magnitude.**
  - A water molecule (about 0.3 nm) against a 1 μm grain (roughly 3 000 times larger).
  - $v/c \approx 3.3\times10^{-6}$ for a 1 000 m/s bullet, $8.3\times10^{-7}$ for a 250 m/s jet, $9.9\times10^{-5}$ for the Earth's 29.8 km/s orbit, and a large fraction of $c$ for Kaufmann's electrons (value taken from the cited dataset).
  - $h\nu \approx 1.91$ eV at 650 nm, 2.34 eV at 530 nm, 4.96 eV at 250 nm.
  - The light paper's printed hydrogen-atom mass: $1/N$ gram $= 1.62\times10^{-24}$ g.
  - Molecular kicks on a micrometer grain, an order-of-magnitude estimate shown with its assumptions. An ideal-flux estimate $\tfrac14 n\bar v A$ with liquid water's number density ($3.343\times10^{28}$ m⁻³ from 1 000 kg m⁻³ and 18.015 g mol⁻¹) and a mean molecular speed near 600 m/s gives about $1.6\times10^{19}$ per second on a 1 μm-diameter sphere and about $6\times10^{19}$ for a 1 μm radius, so the text says "$10^{19}$ to $10^{20}$ per second" rather than a single figure.
- **The 1905 unit system.**
  - Mechanical and thermal: Einstein's viscosity $1.35\times10^{-2}$ poise equals $1.35\times10^{-3}$ Pa·s; $R = 8.31\times10^{7}$ erg/(mol K) equals 8.31 J/(mol K); Planck's $\alpha$ (computational value $6.10\times10^{-57}$ erg s⁴ cm⁻³; the printed exponent is verified in the light-paper beads) is $6.10\times10^{-58}$ J s⁴ m⁻³, close to the modern $8\pi h/c^3 = 6.18\times10^{-58}$.
  - **Electromagnetic CGS (the representation the witness indicates for the light paper's §8 and §9 checks).** The correspondences are **conventional, not exact**: since the 2019 SI revision the vacuum magnetic permeability is a measured quantity, so the constant sets mark every CGS-to-SI electrical correspondence `conventional` and never `exact`. By that conventional correspondence 1 abvolt is $10^{-8}$ V and 1 abcoulomb is 10 C.
    - The printed $E = 9.6\cdot10^{3}$ abcoulomb per gram-equivalent is $9.6\times10^{4}$ C, beside the modern Faraday constant $96\,485$ C/mol (labeled modern), which it falls 0.50 percent short of.
    - $\Pi = R\beta\nu/E$ in abvolts, times $10^{-8}$, gives volts: $4.34\times10^{8}$ abvolt is 4.34 V, printed as about 4.3 V.
    - An energy per gram-equivalent divided by $E$ is a potential: $6.38\times10^{12}$ erg per gram-equivalent corresponds to 6.65 V, while 10 V corresponds to $9.6\times10^{12}$ erg per gram-equivalent.
  - **Gaussian (electrostatic) CGS (the relativity paper),** with the same conventional status: 1 statvolt is about 300 V (299.792458 V by the conventional correspondence); 1 statvolt per cm $\approx 3.0\times10^{4}$ V/m; 1 gauss $= 10^{-4}$ T. A contemporary per-electron charge of about $4.7\times10^{-10}$ esu is $1.568\times10^{-19}$ C; it belongs to the documented alternative representation of the light paper's check (4.306–4.309 V).
  - The distinction between "per gram-equivalent" (Einstein's $R$, $E$, $J$) and "per molecule" ($R/N$, $\varepsilon$) is shown explicitly.
  - The node converts units only. It never converts a historical constant's value into a modern constant's value, and it never calls a declared editorial input (the light paper's $R$ and $L$) a printed value.

**Constructions.** A unit-cancellation table (quantities); a scaling table with a slider for a length and its area, volume, and a $\sqrt{t}$ spread (ratios); a zoomable log scale placing the listed numbers (orders of magnitude, with a table equivalent); a conversion calculator restricted to documented conversions (mechanical, electromagnetic CGS, Gaussian CGS), which never converts between historical and modern constant values and which labels every electrical correspondence conventional.

**Prerequisites** (link records with captions, each typed `{foundationId, kind}`): `foundation:bridge-scientific-notation-units` and `foundation:bridge-fractions-ratios`, both `proof-edge` prerequisites to authored slice bridges.

**Calling passages and return captions.** Captions follow the rule in `am-found-library-infra-002t`: this bead records captions for callers that already exist in the node's `returnCaptions[]`, and later callers put theirs on their own link records.
- This bead authors captions for callers that exist when it lands: Brownian §3 and §5 in the reference slice and the complete Brownian readings.
- It records these as `plannedCallers` in the registry: light §1, §2, §8, and §9; relativity §6 and §10 (Gaussian units); mass–energy (energy and $L/V^2$ units).

**Stopping points.**
- Quantities: "a unit is a chosen amount of a kind of quantity."
- Ratios: "scaling as repeated multiplication."
- Magnitudes: "powers of ten as repeated multiplication by ten."
- Units: "a conversion factor as a ratio equal to one."

## Technical Approach

- Records under `content/foundations/` with instrument ids for the constructions; constant values referenced from the constant sets of `am-ref-constants-xik` rather than retyped where the build allows; registry entries flipped to `authored` in the same change.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Four complete records with all parts and stopping points, registered under their canonical ids with this bead as owner.
- [ ] Every number matches the constant sets or evaluator fixtures; historical and modern constants are never mixed silently; the light paper's check is described in the representation the facsimile prints, with the other named a documented alternative.
- [ ] Every CGS-to-SI electrical correspondence is presented as conventional, never as exact, in prose, in the calculator, and in the tests.
- [ ] Captions exist for every existing caller (in the node's `returnCaptions[]` or on the caller's link record); planned callers are recorded in the registry; every prerequisite carries its `kind`.
- [ ] Constructions have textual equivalents and keyboard operation.

## Test Plan

### Unit and integration tests
- `foundQuantities.numbers.test.ts`, numeric consistency for every quoted number, compared through `src/units/tolerance.ts` (`am-ver-tolerance-module-ho90`):
  - speed ratios: $1000/c = 3.3356\times10^{-6}$, $250/c = 8.3391\times10^{-7}$, $29\,800/c = 9.9402\times10^{-5}$;
  - photon energies: $h\nu$ = 1.9074, 2.3393, and 4.9594 eV at 650, 530, and 250 nm;
  - kicks per second: $1.575\times10^{19}$ and $6.301\times10^{19}$ from $\tfrac14 n\bar v A$ with $n = 3.343\times10^{28}$ m⁻³ and $\bar v = 600$ m/s, asserted to one significant figure and reported as an estimate;
  - the $\alpha$ conversion ($6.10\times10^{-58}$ J s⁴ m⁻³; modern $6.180645\times10^{-58}$);
  - electromagnetic conversions (4.3385 V; 6.6507 V; $9.6\times10^{12}$ erg; $9.6\times10^{4}$ C against the modern Faraday constant, 0.50 percent low);
  - Gaussian conversions ($2.997925\times10^{4}$ V/m; $1.5678\times10^{-19}$ C);
  - the hydrogen-atom mass $1.6206\times10^{-24}$ g.
- `foundQuantities.calculator.test.ts`: a request to convert a historical constant value into a modern constant value is refused with an explanation; every electrical conversion row carries the `conventional` marker read from the constant set, and a fixture row marked `exact` fails.
- Compiler checks for registry entries, link-record captions, typed prerequisites, and voice lint.
- Failure evidence (the failing row, its expected and actual values, and the constant-set entry consulted) is written beside the log and retained.

### End-to-end tests
- From Brownian §5 (reference slice), open `foundation:unit-system-1905`, convert Einstein's viscosity from poise to Pa·s, and return to the exact sentence; operate the electromagnetic tab, convert $4.34\times10^{8}$ abvolt to volts, and assert the conventional-correspondence note. Open `foundation:orders-of-magnitude` at 320 px and operate the table equivalent by keyboard. Repeat one route with JavaScript disabled. The light-paper routes into these nodes are exercised by the light-paper content lanes (`am-lq-e2e-x7z0`), not here.

### Structured logging
- JSONL to `artifacts/test-logs/found-quantities-magnitudes/<log-run-id>.jsonl` with `timestamp`, `suite`, `logRunId`, `testId`, `beadId`, `foundationId`, `callingAnchor`, check name, `constantSet`, `expected`, `actual`, `tolerance`, `outcome`, `viewport`, `jsEnabled`, `message`; failure evidence retained.

## Considerations and Pitfalls

- A conversion calculator never converts between historical and modern constant values; it converts units only.
- Label order-of-magnitude estimates as estimates and state their assumptions.
- Describe the light paper's 4.3 V check in the representation the facsimile prints; the calculator supports both CGS electrical systems, so either representation converts correctly.
- Do not write "exactly" for an electrical CGS correspondence; the registry marks these conventional.

## Dependencies

Blocked by:
- `am-found-library-infra-002t`: rendering, the registry, and link-record captions.
- `am-ref-constants-xik`: the historical and modern constant sets, including the conventional CGS correspondences.
- `am-bm-slice-foundations-f5z9`: the prerequisite bridges for scientific notation and fractions must be authored for prerequisite links to resolve.

Unblocks:
- `am-found-prereq-audit-71ot`: the audit covers these nodes.
- `am-found-fields-light-cv3o`: its `foundation:quantities-units` prerequisite is a proof edge, so that cluster waits for this one.
- `am-lq-equations-s1-s4-9gl5`: its chain tool links and equation readings link these nodes.
- `am-lq-readings-intro-s2-n0bq`, `am-lq-readings-s3-s4-k923`, `am-lq-readings-s5-s6-deq6`, `am-lq-readings-s7-s9-yorj`: these readings link these nodes.

title: Author the foundation on reading a German physics sentence
description:
# Author the foundation on reading a German physics sentence

**Epic:** `am-ep-foundations-z1e` · **Batch:** batch-h · **Priority:** P1 · **Plan sections:** §4.5, §6.9 (`gloss` face), §7.5, §7.11 (traceability only)

## Background

The German text is the source face. The interlinear gloss serves three audiences at once:
- readers who want to read Einstein in his own language with support;
- German learners, for whom a three-page physics paper is a fine first text;
- readers whose first language is neither German nor English.

This node gives all three the handful of grammatical and typographic patterns that unlock the papers' sentences.

The node lands in Batch H, after every paper's gloss face and German edition exist. Its callers are therefore older than the node itself, which is the one situation where the library's convention (the calling bead authors the link and its return caption) cannot apply directly; see Calling passages below.

The obvious shape for this node is the wrong one. A reader who opens "reading a German physics sentence" and is given vocabulary has been given the gloss face again. The gloss face already exists (`am-read-gloss-face-lp2`, and the per-paper gloss beads), and it works word by word. This node's job is the layer above it: taking a long German scientific sentence apart into its claim, its condition, and its qualification, before any word-by-word gloss.

## Scope

Node owned here (canonical id from `am-ep-foundations-z1e`):

| Id | Concrete entry point | What the reader can do afterward |
|---|---|---|
| `foundation:reading-german-physics-sentence` | Word order, the Konjunktiv in hypotheses, *sei*, *es gilt*, *man erhält* | Read the source face with support |

Out of scope: term annotations and glosses themselves (`am-edn-gloss-mass-energy-g0y`, `am-edn-gloss-light-quanta-ggj1`, and the other gloss beads); translation policy; the gloss face component (`am-read-gloss-face-lp2`).

## Requirements

**Patterns, each illustrated with an exact sentence from the editions** (quoted from a reviewed German edition by source-block and sentence id, never from memory or from a translation witness):
- Verb-second main clauses and verb-final subordinate clauses; how to find the finite verb and the clause-final verb group.
- Separable prefixes and long compound nouns (*Energieinhalt*, *Lichtkomplex*, *Elementarquantum*, *molekularkinetische Theorie*), read from the last element backward.
- *Es sei …* ("let … be"), *es gilt …* ("… holds"), *man erhält …* ("one obtains …") in derivations.
- The subjunctive in hypotheses and comparisons, and why the translation must keep that modality. The light paper's §6 conclusion is the key example: radiation behaves "as though" it consisted of independent energy quanta. Transcribe its exact wording and verb form (expected *so, wie wenn sie aus … bestünde*; *bestände* is the other possible Konjunktiv II form) from the reviewed edition.
- Letter-spaced emphasis in the 1905 typesetting as a signal of emphasis.
- Period spellings and abbreviations as printed (for example *daß*, *Hrn.*, *l. c.* in the light paper's footnotes citing Lenard), kept on the source face.
- Printed numbers: decimal commas and the raised multiplication dot (for example the light paper's $6{,}17\cdot10^{23}$ and "4,3 Volt"), kept on the source face and rendered with decimal points on the English face.

### Structure before vocabulary: assertion, condition, qualification

The node teaches a reader to take a long German scientific sentence apart into three roles **before** any word-by-word gloss:

1. **The main assertion.** What is being claimed.
2. **Its condition.** Under what circumstances the claim is made (*unter der Voraussetzung, daß…*, *wenn…*, *für…*, *im Falle…*).
3. **Its qualification.** How strongly it is claimed, and what the author is not claiming (*es ist möglich, daß…*, *scheint*, *dürfte*, *müssen*, *so ergibt sich*, *heuristisch*).

Why this and not vocabulary: the site's translation contract turns on exactly this distinction. A close translation **preserves modality and qualification**, and "suggests," "must," "under these assumptions," and "to this approximation" are not interchangeable. A reader who cannot see which clause carries the qualification cannot check the English face against the German, which is the one thing the bilingual edition invites them to do.

- **The worked example is a real sentence from a reviewed ledger**, chosen by this bead's author from `public/papers/transcripts/<key>-reviewed.txt`, never typed from memory and never taken from a witness translation. The strongest candidate is the Brownian introduction's statement that the information available to Einstein about the reported observations was too imprecise for him to form a judgment: it is the paper's most misread sentence, it is a qualification rather than an assertion, and misreading it produces exactly the claim that `am-cm-anachronism-lint-dl2` flags as `observations-studied`. Verify its exact wording and extent on the pinned facsimile and the ledger before authoring, and record the source block and sentence id the example quotes.
- **The three roles are recorded as spans over that sentence**, so the marking can be rendered and checked rather than described in prose. The spans cover the sentence without overlapping.
- **Grammatical signals get their own short section.** An assumed quantity, an observed fact and a proposed conclusion carry different signals in German scientific prose, and the node names the signals it uses with an example of each from the corpus: a subjunctive or a modal for a proposed conclusion, a stated condition clause for an assumption, a plain past or present for a reported observation. It names the signals it teaches and stops; it does not attempt German grammar.
- **It does not require German.** The capsule supports reading the source face with the English face beside it. Its readiness sign is that a reader can point at which clause carries the qualification in a sentence they have not seen, with the translation available. That is a reading skill, not a language skill, and it is stated as an explanation the reader gives, never as a test: no score, timer or correctness mark appears.

**Construction.** An interlinear excerpt from the gloss face with word-order markers and a toggle between the literal gloss and the idiomatic translation, with a textual equivalent. The three role spans are distinguished by a channel other than color.

**Calling passages and return captions.**
- The gloss faces of all four papers, and the term annotation for the subjunctive at the light paper's §6 conclusion, exist before this node does.
- This bead therefore adds the two link references itself in one change: a face-level entry link in the gloss-face configuration, and a link on the §6 subjunctive annotation. Their return captions are recorded in this node's own `returnCaptions[]` ("Back to the gloss face at the same sentence"; "Back to light quanta §6: the conclusion in the subjunctive of comparison"), so the callers' records change only by the added link.
- It records each such edit with a comment on the owning bead (`am-read-gloss-face-lp2`, `am-edn-gloss-light-quanta-ggj1`), and never changes anything else in those records.
- The node also links forward to `am-read-gloss-face-lp2` as the next step for a reader who now wants the words, so the two directions are complete: the gloss face opens this node for a reader who has the words and not the shape, and this node opens the gloss face for a reader who has the shape and not the words.
- Callers created after this node lands author their own links as usual.

**Stopping point.** "A clause frame: subject, finite verb in second position, the rest of the verb at the end," and, for a long sentence, "one claim, its condition, and how strongly it is made." The node never opens a second cascade into German syntax, and it says so.

## Technical Approach

- Record under `content/foundations/`; example sentences referenced by source-block and sentence ids so edits to the edition propagate; the three role spans stored on the record as offsets into the quoted sentence; registry entry flipped to `authored` in the same change as the record and the caller links.
- The node renders on its own route in the foundation library and in the drawer, both owned by `am-found-library-infra-002t`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The record has all parts, each pattern with at least one exact sentence reference, and the stopping point, registered under its canonical id with this bead as owner.
- [ ] The record carries the three roles as named parts, a grammatical-signals section, one worked example quoting a reviewed ledger sentence by its source block and sentence id, a textual equivalent, prerequisites, and the stopping point.
- [ ] Every example resolves to a reviewed German sentence id; none is retyped.
- [ ] The worked example's quoted German is byte-identical to the ledger text at that sentence id, checked by test, and the record names the ledger file and the id rather than embedding an unsourced string.
- [ ] The example sentence's three roles are marked in the record as spans over that sentence, so the marking can be rendered and checked rather than described in prose.
- [ ] The grammatical-signals section names each signal it teaches with one corpus example, and teaches no signal it does not exemplify.
- [ ] The node states its stopping point and opens no prerequisite into German grammar; the prerequisite audit of `am-found-prereq-audit-71ot` reports no dead end from it.
- [ ] The readiness sign is stated as an explanation the reader gives, never as a test, and no score, timer or correctness mark appears.
- [ ] The gloss-face entry links and the §6 annotation link exist with return captions, each cross-bead edit is recorded on the owning bead, and the node's own forward link to the gloss face exists.
- [ ] The construction has a textual equivalent and works with keyboard and screen readers (language metadata marks German spans).
- [ ] The node renders on its foundation route and in the drawer, in print, without JavaScript, at 320 px, and by keyboard, with German diacritics and `ß` rendering correctly in all three themes (the glyph coverage `am-design-themes-typography-288q` owns).

## Test Plan

### Unit and integration tests
- Reference checks that every example id exists and its text equals the edition; a check that the §6 example's verb form equals the reviewed edition's text.
- Language-attribute checks on German spans; voice lint for English prose.
- Compiler checks for the registry entry and the caller link records with captions.
- `foundReadingGerman.example.test.ts`:
  - the quoted German equals the reviewed ledger text at the named sentence id, byte for byte, with original spelling preserved (for example `daß`), compared as an exact string;
  - the three role spans cover the sentence without overlapping and without gaps beyond punctuation;
  - the record names a ledger file that exists and a sentence id that parses under the id grammar of `am-cm-id-scheme-8bn`.
- `foundReadingGerman.signals.test.ts`: every signal named in the grammatical-signals section has at least one corpus example attached, and every attached example resolves to a source block id.
- `foundReadingGerman.records.test.ts`: registry entry flipped to `authored` with this bead as owner; stopping point present; textual equivalent present; no banned abstract vocabulary; voice lint passes.
- `foundReadingGerman.glyphs.test.ts`: the rendered example's German characters are covered by the subset fonts in all three themes, reusing the glyph coverage assertions of `am-design-themes-typography-288q` rather than a second check.

### End-to-end tests

In `e2e/foundations/reading-german.spec.ts`, through `am-test-e2e-harness-bqmh`:

1. From the mass–energy gloss face, open the node, toggle literal and idiomatic readings by keyboard, and return to the exact sentence.
2. From the light paper's §6 conclusion annotation, open the node and return.
3. From the Brownian German face at the introduction, open the node in the drawer, read the three roles marked over the example sentence, and return to the exact sentence through the return stack.
4. Follow the node's forward link to the gloss face, then follow the gloss face's entry link back to this node.
5. Assert the three roles are visibly distinguished by a channel other than color, under forced-colors emulation and in monochrome print.
6. Verify screen-reader language switching on German examples.
7. Repeat keyboard only, at 320 px, at 200 percent zoom, and with JavaScript disabled using the node's standalone route (real links).

Failures retain a screenshot, DOM snapshot and console log under `artifacts/test-logs/foundations/<log-run-id>/evidence/`.

### Structured logging
- Bead-specific fields: `foundationId` (`foundation:reading-german-physics-sentence`), `ledgerFile`, `sentenceId`, `roleSpans`, `signalCount`, `signalsWithExamples`, `callingAnchor`, `returnCaptionSource`, example sentence ids, `rule`.
- Standard fields: `timestamp`, `suite` (`foundations`), `logRunId`, `testId`, `beadId` (`am-found-reading-german-u8oc`), `browser`, `viewport`, `jsEnabled`, `durationMs`, `expected`, `actual`, `comparisonKind` (`bitwise` for the ledger comparison), `outcome`, `message`.
- Path: `artifacts/test-logs/foundations/<log-run-id>.jsonl`; failure evidence retained.

## Considerations and Pitfalls

- Keep grammar explanations minimal and tied to real sentences; this is not a German course and must never grow into one. The reader has the English face open; the skill is seeing the shape of the claim, and the stopping point is written to stop exactly that growth.
- Preserve printed spellings, abbreviations, and number formats on the source face even when modern usage differs.
- The cross-bead link edits are the only exception to caller-owned links and must stay limited to adding link records.
- Choose the example from the ledger, not from a translation. A sentence taken from a witness translation and rendered back into German would be a fabricated source, which is the one thing the source layers exist to prevent.
- The Brownian introduction candidate is valuable because misreading it produces a documented anachronism the lint already flags. If the pinned facsimile's wording turns out to be less clear than expected, pick another sentence and record why.
- Do not mark the roles with color alone. A reader who cannot distinguish the three spans learns nothing, and the semantic-color rule applies here as everywhere.
- *müssen* in a physics paper is often logical necessity within a model, not a claim about the world. The qualification section should say so, because that is the exact modality the translation contract protects.

## Dependencies

Blocked by:
- `am-found-library-infra-002t`: rendering, the registry, the route and drawer, and link-record captions.
- `am-read-bilingual-faces-pao`: German spans, alignment, and gloss rendering used by the examples.
- `am-read-gloss-face-lp2`: the gloss face whose configuration receives the entry link and whose route the end-to-end test starts from.

Unblocks:
- `am-found-prereq-audit-71ot`: the audit covers this node.
- `am-disc-batch-h-exit-audit-r8xq`: the Batch H exit evidence includes the foundation library's completion.

title: Author the error-and-inference foundation and extend the statistics nodes for inference
description:
# Author the error-and-inference foundation and extend the statistics nodes for inference

**Epic:** `am-ep-foundations-z1e` · **Batch:** batch-c · **Priority:** P1 · **Plan sections:** §7.5, §7.9, §8.2 (specified inference model, identifiability, observation noise), §13.4 (traceability only)

## Background

The Brownian paper ends by proposing to determine the molecular number from visible displacements. Doing that honestly requires ideas the slice's statistics nodes do not yet carry:
- several noisy estimates of one parameter;
- an interval explained through repeated hypothetical experiments before chi-square is named;
- bias when an estimate is inverted;
- parameters that the data cannot separate;
- measurement noise that changes statistical dependence.

The plan is explicit that the interval is never described as a posterior probability for a fixed unknown without a Bayesian model.

## Scope

Nodes owned here (canonical ids from `am-ep-foundations-z1e`):

| Id | Concrete entry point | What the reader can do afterward |
|---|---|---|
| `foundation:error-inference` | Several noisy estimates of the same parameter | Separate sampling, measurement, model, and numerical uncertainty |
| `foundation:two-measurements-two-unknowns` | One relation, two unknowns, and a second relation that crosses it | Say why one measurement leaves a curve, and what a crossing does and does not establish |

Plus inference **extension sections** attached to the slice's statistics nodes: `foundation:distributions`, `foundation:mean-variance-rms`, and `foundation:gaussian-distributions`, whose node records belong to `am-bm-slice-foundations-f5z9`. The sections cover estimators, interval coverage, bias under a nonlinear transformation, identifiability, and observation noise. Each extension is a separate section record owned here and rendered inside the slice node's page, so this bead never edits the slice bead's records and ownership of the slice nodes does not change.

### The registry ripple of the second node, applied in the same change

`foundation:two-measurements-two-unknowns` is a new canonical id, and three beads state counts that must move together:

- `am-ep-foundations-z1e`'s partition check currently reads "There are 35 foundation nodes, 9 in the slice and 26 in this epic's cluster beads (4 + 5 + 1 + 6 + 5 + 4 + 1)" and "Each of the 45 ids has exactly one owner". With this node it reads **36 nodes**, 9 in the slice and **27** in the cluster beads (4 + 5 + **2** + 6 + 5 + 4 + 1), and **46 ids**. The statistics cluster, the third term, moves from 1 to 2. The bridge counts are unchanged at 10, 6 in the slice and 4 in the epic.
- `am-found-library-infra-002t` requires `content/foundations/registry.yaml` to list "all 45 canonical ids from `am-ep-foundations-z1e` (35 nodes, 10 bridges)", creates the registry with all 45 entries `planned`, and asserts in an acceptance criterion and in `foundationRegistry.test.ts` that "the real registry has exactly 35 nodes and 10 bridges". Those four readings become 46 and 36.
- This bead adds the registry entry and the record.

All three edits land together. If they do not, the epic's partition check and the registry test contradict each other, and one of them fails on every build. Neither of the other two beads is revised by this bead; the change is requested of their owners and is recorded as a proposal in this review round.

## Requirements

**Content of `foundation:error-inference`.**
- Four kinds of uncertainty kept separate: sampling, measurement, model, and numerical.
- An interval explained through repeated hypothetical experiments: many imagined repetitions produce many intervals, and a stated fraction of them cover the fixed true value; only then is chi-square named.
- Worked interval (modern golden, synthetic): $M = 50$ independent displacement vectors in $d = 2$ coordinates give $q = dM = 100$. With $\widehat D = 0.43\ \mu\text{m}^2/\text{s}$, the 95 % interval is $[q\widehat D/\chi^2_{100,0.975},\ q\widehat D/\chi^2_{100,0.025}] = [43/129.5612,\ 43/74.2219] = [0.3319,\ 0.5793]\ \mu\text{m}^2/\text{s}$ (quantiles pinned by test).
- Inversion bias: for $q > 2$ the expectation of $C/\widehat D$ is $N_A\,q/(q-2)$, a factor of 1.020408 when $q = 100$; transformed intervals reverse their endpoints.
- Identifiability: at fixed $R$, $T$, $\eta$, doubling the radius and halving $N_A$ leaves the predicted diffusivity unchanged, so displacements alone cannot determine both; an independent radius measurement narrows the family. The lesson behind that statement is the second node below.
- Observation noise: measured increments gain $2\sigma^2$ per coordinate and neighboring increments share a noise covariance of $-\sigma^2$; overlapping windows do not create independent samples.
- Synthetic versus real data: a synthetic inverse exercise checks the inference machinery, not the existence of molecules.
- A confidence interval is not an interval-arithmetic enclosure, and a numerical error bar is not a measurement uncertainty.

### Why `foundation:two-measurements-two-unknowns` is needed

Two beads already state the fact and one instrument already explores it, and there is nowhere for a reader to descend to:

- `am-bm-readings-s4-s5-uqbb` tells the reader that "radius and molecular number are not separately identifiable from displacements alone, since doubling $a$ and halving $N$ leave $D$ unchanged at fixed $R$, $T$, $\eta$ (the typed `underdetermined` state)".
- `am-reason-what-can-you-infer-pqwb` builds its workbench "first on radius and molecular-number identifiability".
- `am-companion-dissertation-record-nbvv` is entirely about combining two measurements to get both quantities, and `am-disc-avogadro-lab-pfi7` runs three routes into one readout.

A reader who meets "not separately identifiable" in a §5 reading has met an unfamiliar idea with no lesson behind it. That is the prerequisite dead end the second non-negotiable outcome forbids, and it is in the reference slice.

### Content of `foundation:two-measurements-two-unknowns`

- **Concrete entry point.** One relation with two unknowns, from the paper itself. Einstein's §5 relation is $D = \dfrac{RT}{N}\dfrac{1}{6\pi\eta a}$. At fixed $R$, $T$ and $\eta$, a measured $D$ fixes only the **product** $N a$. Doubling $a$ and halving $N$ leaves $D$ unchanged exactly, which is the statement the §5 reading makes. The reader sees one curve in the $(a, N)$ plane, every point of which is compatible with the measurement.
- **The second measurement.** The dissertation's suspension-viscosity relation gives a second, differently shaped curve in the same plane, and the two intersect. Writing $\eta^*$ for the suspension's viscosity, $\eta$ for the solvent's, $\varphi$ for the volume fraction and $n$ for the **molar concentration of the solute** (moles per unit volume), the volume fraction is $\varphi = \tfrac{4}{3}\pi a^3 N n$, so the viscosity relation gives $a^3 N = \dfrac{3(\eta^*/\eta - 1)}{4\pi c\, n}$, where $c$ is the coefficient of $\varphi$ in the viscosity law: 1 as printed in 1906 and 5/2 after the 1911 correction. Dividing by $aN = \dfrac{RT}{6\pi\eta D}$ from the diffusion relation gives
  $$a^2 = \frac{3(\eta^*/\eta - 1)}{4\pi c\, n}\cdot\frac{6\pi\eta D}{RT},$$
  whose two factors have dimensions m³ mol⁻¹ and mol m⁻¹, so $a^2$ is an area. The node states the combination and links to the companion record, which owns the derivation and the 1911 correction history; the node never re-derives it. The modern symbol $[\eta]$ for the coefficient of $\varphi$ appears only in a modern-notation layer, marked as modern, and the coefficient is never called $k$, because Einstein prints $k$ for the viscosity itself.
- **The intersection is not proof of uniqueness**, and this is the node's real lesson:
  - two curves that cross at a shallow angle determine their intersection poorly, so a small error in either measurement moves the answer a long way;
  - the honest output is a **region**, not a point, and it comes from the measurements' uncertainties through `am-ref-inference-2w9`;
  - two measurements that are not independent can cross and still determine nothing new, which is the case when both rest on the same calibration; the declared shared inputs of `am-dataset-independence-registry-3dfb` are where that claim is recorded;
  - the admitted domain of each relation bounds where the crossing means anything at all.
- **Construction** (optional, by instrument id and preset, following the action contract): the two curves in the $(a, N)$ plane with the measurement uncertainties shown as bands, the intersection shown as the region where the bands overlap, and a control that changes the angle between the curves so the reader watches the region grow. Its nonvisual equivalent is a table of compatible pairs for each measurement and the pairs the two lists share, with the same control as a choice between named cases. Where the instrument or preset is not registered, the static worked example renders with the library's visible "interactive version not yet available" status, never a broken embed.
- **Worked example.** One `workedExample` field, as the `Foundation` shape of `am-cm-schemas-argument-llm` requires, authored in five labelled parts: the question is whether a measured spreading rate can tell you how big the particle is; the given is $D$, $T$, $\eta$ and the relation; the plausible first thought is "solve for $a$", stated respectfully, because it is what the algebra looks like it offers; the decisive step shows that solving gives $a$ **in terms of $N$**, so the answer is a curve, and that doubling $a$ with $N$ halved returns the same $D$ exactly; the limitation says that a second relation is needed, that its usefulness depends on the angle between the curves and on the two measurements being independent, and that the result is a region.
- **Prerequisites**, typed `{foundationId, kind}`: `foundation:ratios-scaling` and `foundation:error-inference`, both `proof-edge`; `foundation:functions-graphs` as a `cross-link`.
- **Stopping point:** "one measurement of one combination of two quantities leaves a curve, not a point."
- **The remaining record parts** required of every foundation by `am-cm-schemas-argument-llm`: `learningObjective`, `compactExplanation`, `fullExplanation`, `textualEquivalent`, and `returnCaptions[]`.

**Construction for `foundation:error-inference`.** A repeated-experiment view draws many seeded synthetic datasets, shows each interval against the known generator value, and reports the covering fraction, with a table equivalent. Seeds are canonical decimal strings. The view reuses the synthetic mode of `am-bm-07-infer-molecular-number-frf9` by instrument id and preset. Until that preset is registered, the node shows the static worked example with the library's "interactive version not yet available" status, never a broken embed.

**Prerequisites of `foundation:error-inference`.** Every prerequisite is typed `{foundationId, kind}` (`am-cm-schemas-argument-llm`), each a link record with a caption: `foundation:distributions`, `foundation:mean-variance-rms`, and `foundation:gaussian-distributions` as `proof-edge` prerequisites (all authored in the slice); `foundation:bridge-squaring-square-roots` and `foundation:bridge-probability-notation` as `proof-edge` prerequisites to authored bridges (the second lands with `am-found-zero-algebra-rest-oipl` in the same batch, so the build order is a graph edge, not a batch label).

**Calling passages and return captions.** Captions follow the rule in `am-found-library-infra-002t`: this bead records captions for callers that already exist in the node's `returnCaptions[]`, and later callers put theirs on their own link records. This bead authors captions only for callers that exist when it lands, which are the Brownian §5 passages of the reference slice, for example "Back to Brownian motion §5: the radius and the molecular number, at fixed temperature and viscosity". It records BM-07, BM-08, the kitchen mode, the Avogadro lab (`am-disc-avogadro-lab-pfi7`), the companion record (`am-companion-dissertation-record-nbvv`), and the what-can-you-infer workbench (`am-reason-what-can-you-infer-pqwb`) as `plannedCallers` in the registry; those beads author their own captions when they link.

**Stopping point of `foundation:error-inference`.** "An interval is a procedure's output that covers the true value in a stated fraction of repetitions."

## Technical Approach

- The two node records and the three extension section records live under `content/foundations/`. Numbers are pulled from `am-ref-inference-2w9` scenario fixtures at build time when a construction is embedded, and every comparison runs through `src/units/tolerance.ts` (`am-ver-tolerance-module-ho90`). The registry entries are flipped to `authored` in the same change.
- The identifiability invariance and the two-measurement region are computed through `am-ref-diffusion-lr3` and `am-ref-inference-2w9`; no number is typed into content.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Both node records have all parts, their stopping points, and their canonical ids with this bead as owner; the three extension sections render inside the slice nodes without editing their records.
- [ ] No text describes the interval as a probability that the fixed unknown lies inside.
- [ ] Quoted quantiles, interval endpoints, and the bias factor match tested values.
- [ ] Captions exist for every existing caller (in the node's `returnCaptions[]` or on the caller's link record); planned callers are recorded; every prerequisite carries its `kind`.
- [ ] `foundation:two-measurements-two-unknowns` exists in `content/foundations/registry.yaml` with `kind: node`, this bead as owner, and status `authored` in the same change as its record.
- [ ] `am-ep-foundations-z1e`'s partition check reads 36 nodes and 46 ids, with the statistics cluster at 2, and `am-found-library-infra-002t`'s registry requirement, acceptance criterion, and `foundationRegistry.test.ts` read 46 ids and 36 nodes. The registry test passes with the new counts and fails with the old ones. The three changes land together.
- [ ] The invariance is asserted numerically, not only stated: for fixed $R$, $T$, $\eta$, doubling $a$ and halving $N$ reproduces the same $D$ to within $10^{-12}$ relative, computed through `am-ref-diffusion-lr3` and compared with `withinTolerance` from `src/units/tolerance.ts`.
- [ ] The node's output for a single measurement is a curve and never a point, and a request for a unique $a$ returns the typed `underdetermined` status of `am-rt-typed-results-mqb`; the two-measurement case reports a region with its uncertainties, computed by `am-ref-inference-2w9` and never typed into content.
- [ ] The near-parallel case is exercised: reducing the angle between the curves widens the reported region, and the node's text says why.
- [ ] The Brownian §5 reading's identifiability statement links to `foundation:two-measurements-two-unknowns` and the link resolves; the prerequisite audit of `am-found-prereq-audit-71ot` reports no dead end from that statement.
- [ ] Both nodes render in the drawer and standalone, in print, without JavaScript, at 320 px and by keyboard; each construction's nonvisual equivalent exposes the same comparison.

## Test Plan

### Unit and integration tests
- `foundInference.numbers.test.ts`: $\chi^2_{100,0.025} = 74.2219$ and $\chi^2_{100,0.975} = 129.5612$ to $10^{-3}$; endpoints $43/129.5612 = 0.3319$ and $43/74.2219 = 0.5793$ μm²/s; bias factor $100/98 = 1.020408$; the identifiability invariance (doubling $a$ and halving $N_A$ leaves $D$ unchanged) to $10^{-12}$ relative; the observation-noise variance inflation $2\sigma^2$ and the neighbouring covariance $-\sigma^2$ from the fixtures.
- `foundInference.coverage.test.ts`: a coverage check with a fixed decimal-string seed under `am-ver-statistical-policy-grj`: over a prespecified number of synthetic repetitions the covering fraction lies within its prespecified binomial tolerance of 0.95. The test is never rerun to pass, and a failure keeps its seed and per-repetition table as evidence.
- `foundInference.wording.test.ts`: a wording check fails on phrases equating a confidence interval with a posterior probability, and on any text calling the synthetic exercise evidence for molecules. It also fails on text that calls the coefficient of $\varphi$ "k" outside a quoted notation warning.
- `foundInference.records.test.ts`: compiler checks for the registry entries, extension-section attachment to authored nodes, link-record captions, and typed prerequisites.
- `foundTwoMeasurements.numbers.test.ts` (against the real evaluators, never literals):
  - with $T = 290.15$ K, $\eta = 1.35\times10^{-3}$ Pa·s and the Brownian constant set, $D$ computed for $(a, N)$ and for $(2a, N/2)$ agree to within $10^{-12}$ relative through `src/units/tolerance.ts`;
  - the single-measurement solution is returned as a parameterized curve, and a request for a unique $a$ returns the typed `underdetermined` status of `am-rt-typed-results-mqb` rather than a number;
  - the two-measurement inversion returns a region whose width grows as the angle between the curves decreases, asserted monotonically over three seeded angles;
  - two measurements sharing one calibration input are reported as not independent and the region is not narrowed.
- `foundTwoMeasurements.records.test.ts`: registry entry, owner, kind, `authored` status, the five labelled parts inside `workedExample`, typed prerequisites with `kind`, the stopping point, no authored backlinks for planned callers, voice lint, and the banned abstract vocabulary check.
- `foundationsRegistry.count.test.ts` (owned by `am-found-library-infra-002t`, updated in the same change): the registry holds 46 ids, 36 of kind `node` and 10 of kind `bridge`, each with exactly one owner; a fixture registry at 45 fails.
- Failure evidence (the failing statistic, its seed, the expected band, and the observed value) is written beside the log and retained.

### End-to-end tests
- From a Brownian §5 passage in the reference slice, open `foundation:error-inference` in the drawer, run the repeated-experiment view with a fixed seed (or read the static worked example while the BM-07 preset is unregistered, asserting the status line), read the covering fraction from the table, and return to the exact sentence. Repeat with JavaScript disabled. The routes from BM-07, BM-08, and the kitchen mode are exercised by those beads' own lanes.
- In `e2e/foundations/two-measurements.spec.ts`, through `am-test-e2e-harness-bqmh`:
  1. From the Brownian §5 reading's identifiability statement, open the node in the drawer, read the worked example, reveal the decisive step in one action, and return to the exact sentence with the reader's place restored.
  2. Operate the construction: read the compatible-pairs table, change the angle, and assert the reported region widens in both the visual and the table route with identical values. Where the construction is not registered, assert the static worked example and its status line instead.
  3. Follow the link to the companion record's inversion and return.
  4. Repeat keyboard only, at 320 px, with JavaScript disabled on the standalone route, and in print.
- Failures retain a screenshot, DOM snapshot and console log under `artifacts/test-logs/found-statistics-inference/<log-run-id>/evidence/`.

### Structured logging
- JSONL to `artifacts/test-logs/found-statistics-inference/<log-run-id>.jsonl` with `timestamp`, `suite`, `logRunId`, `testId`, `beadId`, `foundationId`, `callingAnchor`, `seed` as a decimal string, covering fraction, `expected`, `actual`, `tolerance`, `outcome`, `jsEnabled`, `message`; failure evidence retained.
- The two-measurement cases add `constantSetId`, `a`, `N`, `D`, `invarianceRelError`, `resultStatus`, `regionWidth`, `curveAngle`, `independent`, `interface` (`pointer`, `keyboard`, `table`, `no-js`), `comparisonKind`, `browser`, `viewport`, `durationMs`, and `rule` to the same line shape.

## Considerations and Pitfalls

- The inversion bias explanation is optional for readers and never a prerequisite for using BM-07.
- A synthetic success says nothing about molecules; the text says so.
- The chi-square interval belongs to the specified model of `am-ref-inference-2w9`; do not restate it for a different estimator without that bead's fixtures.
- Adding a canonical id changes three beads. Land the registry entry, the epic's partition counts, and the library infra's "45" together, or two tests will disagree about how many foundations exist.
- The lesson of the second node is the region, not the intersection. A crossing drawn as a point, in any theme, teaches the opposite of what the node is for.
- Do not let the node re-derive the dissertation's inversion. It links to the companion record, which owns that derivation and its 1911 correction history.
- Keep $n$ in the inversion explicit as a molar concentration. Written with a number density instead, the same formula needs a factor of $N$ and quietly stops being dimensionally right.
- "Not identifiable" is a statement about the data and the model together, not about the measurement's quality. A perfect measurement of $D$ still leaves a curve.
- Two measurements that share a calibration look independent and are not. That case belongs in the node because it is the honest reason the Avogadro lab keeps its three routes' assumptions visible.
- The construction is optional. If no instrument is registered when the node lands, the static worked example with its status line is the correct state, and the node is complete without it.

## Dependencies

Blocked by:
- `am-found-library-infra-002t`: rendering, the registry, extension-section rendering, and link-record captions. Its registry count and its count test move from 45 to 46 in the same change as this bead's second node.
- `am-bm-slice-foundations-f5z9`: the statistics nodes these extensions attach to, and `foundation:mean-variance-rms`, `foundation:distributions`, and `foundation:gaussian-distributions` as prerequisites.
- `am-ref-inference-2w9`: the inference fixtures quoted here, the identifiability report, and the interval and region the second node displays. The nodes cite its outputs and type no numbers into content.

Unblocks:
- `am-found-prereq-audit-71ot`: the audit covers both nodes and the extension sections.
- `am-bm-07-infer-molecular-number-frf9`: its readings and its synthetic mode link `foundation:error-inference`, and its preset backs the repeated-experiment view.

Consumers without a dependency edge, recorded as `plannedCallers` and each authoring its own link record and caption: `am-reason-what-can-you-infer-pqwb` (its identifiability workbench links to `foundation:two-measurements-two-unknowns` as the lesson behind the workbench), `am-disc-avogadro-lab-pfi7`, and `am-companion-dissertation-record-nbvv`.

title: Author foundations: viscosity and Stokes drag, free energy and osmotic pressure, work and energy, temperature, entropy
description:
# Author foundations: viscosity and Stokes drag, free energy and osmotic pressure, work and energy, temperature, entropy

**Epic:** `am-ep-foundations-z1e` · **Batch:** batch-c · **Priority:** P1 · **Plan sections:** §3.3 (§§1, 3, 5), §3.4, §7.5, §8.1, §8.2 Route A, §10.3 (gas card caveat) (traceability only)

## Background

The Brownian paper builds its first route to the diffusion coefficient from osmotic pressure and Stokes drag, and the light paper builds its central calculation on the relation between entropy and temperature. These six nodes carry that physics for readers who have never taken thermodynamics, with the physician's familiarity with osmosis as a welcome side door.

Light-paper review r2 (through a comparison translation, verified in the light-paper beads against the facsimile) found three printed passages that call these nodes:
- §1's statement that a bound oscillating charge in equilibrium has mean energy $(R/N)T$ per linear oscillation, two-thirds of a free molecule's kinetic energy;
- §3's entropy–temperature argument, which Einstein attributes to Wien;
- §5's footnote deriving the gas law and the osmotic-pressure law from the entropy volume law.

## Scope

Nodes owned here (canonical ids from `am-ep-foundations-z1e`):

| Id | Concrete entry point | What the reader can do afterward |
|---|---|---|
| `foundation:viscosity-stokes-drag` | Slow motion of a sphere through a liquid | Understand mobility and why geometry and regime qualifications matter |
| `foundation:free-energy-osmotic-pressure` | Move a selective partition | Connect a volume-dependent free energy to a mechanical force |
| `foundation:work-energy` | Force through distance; accounting before and after | Distinguish force, work, power, and reference choices |
| `foundation:temperature-thermal-energy` | A distribution of microscopic motion | Use absolute temperature without equating it to one particle's energy |
| `foundation:entropy-multiplicity` | More accessible configurations at fixed constraints | Understand a relative entropy change without the slogan "disorder" |
| `foundation:entropy-temperature` | Why $dS = dQ/T$ and $\partial S/\partial E = 1/T$ | See why a spectrum can yield an entropy (paper 1 §3) |

Owned elsewhere: flux and continuity, diffusion equation (`am-bm-slice-foundations-f5z9`); partial derivatives and logarithms (`am-found-calculus-6agg`).

## Requirements

**Worked examples (modern constants, verified by test).**
- **Viscosity and Stokes drag.** Drag $F = 6\pi\eta a v$ and mobility $\mu = 1/(6\pi\eta a)$; for $\eta = 1.000$ mPa·s and $a = 0.500$ μm, $\mu = 1.061\times10^{8}$ m N⁻¹ s⁻¹. Regime qualifications: slow motion (low Reynolds number) in a Newtonian liquid far from walls. In a gas, when the mean free path is comparable to the radius, Stokes drag without the Cunningham slip correction is invalid.
- **Free energy and osmotic pressure.**
  - Dilute osmotic pressure is $\Pi = nk_BT$; for 0.1 mol/L at 293.15 K, $\Pi = 2.44\times10^{5}$ Pa (about 2.4 atm).
  - A free-energy term $-N_pk_BT\ln V$ gives the pressure $N_pk_BT/V$ by differentiation.
  - The light paper's §5 footnote takes the same step: from $S - S_0 = R\frac{n}{N}\ln\frac{v}{v_0}$, $p\,dv = T\,dS$ gives $pv = R\frac{n}{N}T$. This is the gas law and the identical osmotic law, obtained without any assumption about how the molecules move.
- **Work and energy.** An electron moved through 1 V gains $1.602\times10^{-19}$ J (1 eV). Energy ledgers compare differences, so the zero of energy is a reference choice (the mass–energy paper's additive constant). The light paper's §8 escape work $P$ is a work done against the body, per electron or per gram-equivalent ($P'$).
- **Temperature and thermal energy.**
  - The mean translational kinetic energy is $\tfrac32k_BT = 6.07\times10^{-21}$ J at 293.15 K, for a molecule and a suspended grain alike, while their speeds differ enormously.
  - A bound oscillating charge in equilibrium has mean energy $k_BT$ per linear oscillation (half kinetic, half potential), which is two-thirds of a free molecule's $\tfrac32k_BT$ (light §1).
  - The mean energy of the quanta over a Wien spectrum is $3k_BT$ (light §6, modern lens), a comparison of energies, not a temperature assigned to one particle.
- **Entropy and multiplicity.** $S = k_B\ln W$; doubling the accessible volume for $n$ independent particles multiplies $W$ by $2^n$ and adds $nk_B\ln 2$.
- **Entropy and temperature.** Reversible heat $dQ$ into a body at temperature $T$ changes its entropy by $dQ/T$. For radiation at fixed volume and frequency, $\partial s_\nu/\partial\rho_\nu = 1/T$. The light paper derives this from the maximum of entropy at fixed energy and attributes the argument to Wien.

**Constructions.**
- A sinking-sphere drag table.
- A selective-partition construction with number density and pressure, reusing `am-bm-02-osmotic-partition-n13x` presets when registered.
- A before-and-after energy ledger.
- A speed-distribution picture with the shared $\tfrac32k_BT$.
- A configuration counter.
- An entropy–temperature check that embeds `am-lq-04-entropy-workbench-senj` at its preset `lq-04-derived-temperature`. Until that instrument lands in Batch F, the check shows a static worked example (600 THz, 3 000 K, $1/T = 3.333\times10^{-4}$ K⁻¹) with the library's "interactive version not yet available" status.

Each construction has a textual equivalent. Embedded instruments are referenced by id and preset, never reimplemented here.

**Prerequisites.** Every prerequisite is typed `{foundationId, kind}` (`am-cm-schemas-argument-llm`): `foundation:partial-derivatives` and `foundation:logarithms` are `proof-edge` prerequisites of `foundation:entropy-temperature` and `foundation:entropy-multiplicity`; `foundation:quantities-units` is a `proof-edge` prerequisite of the drag and pressure nodes; `foundation:flux-continuity` is a `cross-link` from the drag node.

**Calling passages and return captions.** Captions follow the rule in `am-found-library-infra-002t`: this bead records captions for callers that already exist in the node's `returnCaptions[]`, and later callers put theirs on their own link records.
- This bead authors captions for callers that exist when it lands: Brownian §§1–3, BM-02 to BM-04 where registered, and the Brownian slice.
- It records as `plannedCallers` in the registry: the kitchen mode, light §1 and §§3–6, LQ-04, mass–energy's two ledgers, and relativity §10's work integral.

**Stopping points.**
- Drag: "resistance proportional to speed for slow motion."
- Osmotic pressure: "pressure as force per area from particle collisions with a wall."
- Work: "force times distance along the force."
- Temperature: "what two bodies share when heat stops flowing between them."
- Multiplicity: "counting arrangements."
- Entropy and temperature: "the ratio of reversible heat to temperature."

## Technical Approach

- Records under `content/foundations/`; constants referenced from `am-ref-constants-xik`; numeric comparisons run through `src/units/tolerance.ts` (`am-ver-tolerance-module-ho90`); constructions follow the instrument platform's action contracts; registry entries flipped to `authored` in the same change.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Six complete records with all parts and stopping points, registered under their canonical ids with this bead as owner.
- [ ] Regime qualifications for Stokes drag and dilute osmotic pressure appear in every relevant reading level.
- [ ] No text equates temperature with one particle's energy or entropy with "disorder."
- [ ] The embedded LQ-04 check renders its static worked example with the status line until the preset is registered.
- [ ] Quoted numbers match tests; captions exist for every existing caller (in the node's `returnCaptions[]` or on the caller's link record); planned callers are recorded; every prerequisite carries its `kind`.

## Test Plan

### Unit and integration tests
- `foundTransport.numbers.test.ts`, through `src/units/tolerance.ts`: mobility $1.061033\times10^{8}$ m N⁻¹ s⁻¹; osmotic pressure $2.437385\times10^{5}$ Pa (2.406 atm) at 0.1 mol/L and 293.15 K; $\tfrac32k_BT = 6.071059\times10^{-21}$ J; 1 eV $= 1.602177\times10^{-19}$ J; $k_BT = 4.047373\times10^{-21}$ J at 293.15 K, with the ratio of $k_BT$ to $\tfrac32k_BT$ exactly $2/3$; the §5 footnote identity $pv = R\frac{n}{N}T$ derived symbolically from the entropy volume law; $S$ gains $nk_B\ln 2$ when the volume doubles.
- `foundTransport.wording.test.ts`: checks for "disorder" and for temperature-as-one-particle phrasing; voice lint.
- `foundTransport.records.test.ts`: compiler checks for registry entries, link-record captions, typed prerequisites, and instrument references (an unregistered preset yields the status line, not a failure).
- Failure evidence (the failing example, expected and actual values, and the preset status) is written beside the log and retained.

### End-to-end tests
- From Brownian §1 (or its nearest existing passage in the reference slice), open `foundation:free-energy-osmotic-pressure` at 320 px with keyboard only and return to the exact sentence.
- Open `foundation:entropy-temperature` standalone with JavaScript enabled and disabled, and assert the static worked example and the status line.
- The light-paper routes (from §3 and from LQ-04) are exercised by `am-lq-e2e-x7z0`.

### Structured logging
- JSONL to `artifacts/test-logs/found-transport-thermo/<log-run-id>.jsonl` with `timestamp`, `suite`, `logRunId`, `testId`, `beadId`, `foundationId`, `callingAnchor`, `instrumentId` and preset id where embedded, `expected`, `actual`, `tolerance`, `outcome`, `viewport`, `jsEnabled`, `message`; failure evidence retained.

## Considerations and Pitfalls

- A gas card refuses Stokes drag without slip correction; do not let a foundation example contradict the instrument's refusal.
- Keep the physician's osmosis door as an optional route, not a stereotype.
- The light paper's §1 mean energy is per linear oscillation of a bound charge, not per molecule; keep the two-thirds comparison attached to it.

## Dependencies

Blocked by:
- `am-found-library-infra-002t`: rendering, the registry, and link-record captions.
- `am-bm-slice-foundations-f5z9`: flux, continuity, and diffusion nodes these link to.
- `am-ref-constants-xik`: the constant sets.

Unblocks:
- `am-found-prereq-audit-71ot`: the audit covers these nodes.
- `am-lq-equations-s1-s4-9gl5`: its §§3–4 chain tool links resolve to the entropy nodes.
- `am-lq-readings-intro-s2-n0bq`, `am-lq-readings-s3-s4-k923`, `am-lq-readings-s5-s6-deq6`, `am-lq-readings-s7-s9-yorj`, `am-me-readings-69bo`, `am-bm-readings-intro-s1-s3-l3tp`: these readings link these nodes.
- `am-disc-desk-1904-9hgd`: the 1904 desk's shelf objects link the drag, osmotic-pressure, and entropy nodes.

title: Author the remaining zero-assumed-algebra bridges
description:
# Author the remaining zero-assumed-algebra bridges

**Epic:** `am-ep-foundations-z1e` · **Batch:** batch-c · **Priority:** P1 · **Plan sections:** §1.8, §6.4, §7.2, §7.5 (zero-assumed-algebra layer) (traceability only)

## Background

The zero-assumed-algebra layer sits beneath the foundation table. Its lessons are generated by actual obstacles in the papers, not a semester course that delays entry, and "Explain from the beginning" lands on one of these concrete operations. Readiness is shown by what the reader can explain, never by a test. Six bridges are authored for the Brownian slice; this bead authors the other four, which every first encounter and many R2 readings rely on.

## Scope

Bridges owned here (canonical ids from `am-ep-foundations-z1e`):

| Id | Small obstacle | Concrete bridge | Readiness shown without a test |
|---|---|---|---|
| `foundation:bridge-letter-for-quantity` | A letter stands for a quantity | Replace a labeled blank in a measurement sentence with several numbers | Explain what changes and what the letter continues to mean |
| `foundation:bridge-equals-sign-relationship` | An equals sign describes a relationship | Balance two explicit counts or measurements | Distinguish a statement of equality from an instruction to calculate |
| `foundation:bridge-mathematical-punctuation` | Mathematical punctuation | Compare a finite change $\Delta x$, a derivative, a primed frame label, and an exponent | Recognize that similar marks have different jobs |
| `foundation:bridge-probability-notation` | Probability notation | Count a selected outcome within a finite set | Distinguish a single outcome, a frequency, and a model probability |

Owned by `am-bm-slice-foundations-f5z9`: `foundation:bridge-negative-numbers-direction`; `foundation:bridge-fractions-ratios`; `foundation:bridge-squaring-square-roots`; `foundation:bridge-scientific-notation-units`; `foundation:bridge-a-graph`; `foundation:bridge-sum-average`.

## Requirements

**Concrete bridges with examples from the papers.**
- **A letter stands for a quantity.** "After ___ seconds the particle had wandered about ___ micrometers," filled with 1 and 0.8, then 60 and 6 (the Brownian paper's printed estimates, "about 0.8" and "about 6"). The letter $t$ keeps meaning "elapsed time in seconds" while its value changes. The same letter can mean different things in different papers or sections: the light paper's $L$ is the speed of light in §§1–2 and absorbed light energy in §9. A letter's meaning is always stated where it is used.
  - The bridge shows the rounded printed values, and the underlying scenario supplies the exact ones with its constant set named: with the printed $R$ and $N$ of `einstein-1905-brownian-printed`, $\lambda_x = 0.7948$ μm at 1 s and $6.1564$ μm at 60 s; with the mixed scenario `diffusion-einstein-1905-modern-kb`, which names the modern entry it uses, $0.7935$ μm and $6.1467$ μm (all for $a = 0.5$ μm, $\eta = 1.35\times10^{-3}$ Pa·s, $T = 290.15$ K). The bridge never prints a bare "6.1 μm", and never quotes a displacement without the constant set that produced it.
- **An equals sign describes a relationship.** An accounting sheet where energy before equals energy after plus energy sent out (100 = 70 + 30 in made-up units, labeled as made up), then the paper's $E_0 - E_1 = L$ read as a statement about the sheets, not an instruction.
- **Mathematical punctuation.** Similar marks do different jobs:
  - $\Delta$ as a finite displacement in the Brownian paper;
  - a derivative as a rate;
  - a prime marking another frame's quantity (for example $\nu'$ and $\varphi'$ in the relativity paper's §7);
  - an exponent as repeated multiplication in $W = (V/V_0)^n$;
  - the printed "lg", which in the 1905 papers means the natural logarithm and not a base-10 logarithm.
- **Probability notation.** Two tokens in two halves give four outcomes, so the model probability of "both left" is 1/4. In 100 trials the frequency might be 23/100. A single trial either shows both left or does not.

**Each bridge** has a compact explanation, the concrete operation, a textual equivalent, and a stopping point.

**Calling passages and return captions.** Captions follow the rule in `am-found-library-infra-002t`: this bead records captions for callers that already exist in the node's `returnCaptions[]`, and later callers put theirs on their own link records. This bead authors captions only for callers that exist when it lands: the Brownian first encounter (`am-bm-first-encounter-fjvh`) and the Brownian slice readings, wherever they use these bridges. It records the first encounters of the other three papers, their R2 readings, and their "Explain from the beginning" actions as `plannedCallers`. Those beads author their own links and captions, for example `am-lq-first-encounter-hhr8` for the light paper.

**Accessibility.** Every manipulation (filling blanks, balancing counts, comparing marks, counting outcomes) works by keyboard and screen reader with identical totals; no timing, no marks for wrong answers.

## Technical Approach

- Bridge records under `content/foundations/` with `kind: bridge`, rendered by `am-found-library-infra-002t`; registry entries flipped to `authored` in the same change.
- Examples that quote printed numbers reference scenario fixtures by id so they cannot drift, and every numeric comparison in the tests runs through `src/units/tolerance.ts` (`am-ver-tolerance-module-ho90`).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Four complete bridge records with stopping points, registered under their canonical ids with this bead as owner.
- [ ] "Explain from the beginning" in the Brownian first encounter reaches the appropriate bridge wherever it targets these bridges. Later papers' first-encounter beads verify their own routes, and the prerequisite audit checks all four papers.
- [ ] No bridge uses vocabulary such as *linear*, *differential*, *distribution*, or *invariant* in its explanation.
- [ ] Every displacement figure names its constant set; no bridge text contains a bare "6.1 μm".
- [ ] Captions exist for every existing caller (in the node's `returnCaptions[]` or on the caller's link record); planned callers are recorded.

## Test Plan

### Unit and integration tests
- `foundZeroAlgebra.vocabulary.test.ts`: vocabulary lint for the banned abstract words, plus voice lint.
- `foundZeroAlgebra.numbers.test.ts`: numeric consistency against the Brownian scenario fixtures: `einstein-1905-brownian-printed` gives $\lambda_x = 0.7948$ μm at 1 s and $6.1564$ μm at 60 s, and `diffusion-einstein-1905-modern-kb` gives $0.7935$ μm and $6.1467$ μm; the bridge text shows only the printed roundings "about 0.8" and "about 6"; a planted bare "6.1 μm" fails; the probability 1/4 and the frequency 23/100 are distinguished in the record's fields.
- `foundZeroAlgebra.records.test.ts`: compiler checks for registry entries, link-record captions, and bridge `kind`.
- Failure evidence (the offending bridge id, the phrase or value, and the scenario consulted) is written beside the log and retained.

### End-to-end tests
- From the Brownian first encounter, choose "Explain from the beginning" where it targets one of these bridges, complete it by keyboard, and return to the exact step.
- Open each of the four bridges in the drawer from a fixture calling passage and standalone, and repeat with JavaScript disabled using real links.
- The light, mass–energy, and relativity first-encounter routes are exercised by those papers' content lanes (for light, `am-lq-e2e-x7z0`).

### Structured logging
- JSONL to `artifacts/test-logs/found-zero-algebra-rest/<log-run-id>.jsonl` with `timestamp`, `suite`, `logRunId`, `testId`, `beadId`, `foundationId`, `callingAnchor`, `constantSet`, `expected`, `actual`, `outcome`, `viewport`, `jsEnabled`, `message`; failure evidence retained.

## Considerations and Pitfalls

- A bridge ends at its stopping point; it never opens another cascade of definitions.
- The made-up accounting numbers are labeled as made up.
- The displacement example is the paper's own estimate, not a measurement; say so in one short sentence without introducing new vocabulary.

## Dependencies

Blocked by:
- `am-found-library-infra-002t`: bridge rendering, the registry, and link-record captions.
- `am-bm-slice-foundations-f5z9`: the six slice bridges these link to.
- `am-bm-first-encounter-fjvh`: the existing caller whose route the end-to-end test starts from.

Unblocks:
- `am-found-prereq-audit-71ot`: the audit covers these bridges.
- `am-lq-first-encounter-hhr8`: its "Explain from the beginning" lands on the probability-notation bridge.

title: Build the narrow versioned composition adapter only after the slice shows it is needed
description:
# Build the narrow versioned composition adapter only after the slice shows it is needed

**Epic:** `am-ep-frankensim-9kg` · **Batch:** C · **Priority:** P2 · **Labels:** frankensim, upstream-frankensim, wasm · **Plan sections:** §12.4 (narrow adapter), §12.7, §19.2 ("do not generalize the framework until this slice exposes which abstractions help") (traceability only)

## Background

The plan allows a composition and transport boundary, for example `fs-annus-wasm`, that exposes versioned experiment operations and serializes results and refusals for the browser. It also sets two hard limits: the boundary **must not contain a second copy of the laws** owned by generic crates, and nothing should be generalized before the Brownian reference slice shows which abstractions help. This bead is therefore gated on `am-bm-slice-retrospective-pp09` and may legitimately close as "not needed" with a recorded reason.

FrankenSim already hosts per-application browser crates (for example `fs-demo-physics-wasm`, the CMA-ES explainer's browser surface, and `fs-flyer-wasm`, whose pattern it follows: typed refusal envelopes, a `KERNEL_VERSION` baked into envelopes, pure deterministic entries, and explicit no-claims), so an Annus Mirabilis boundary crate upstream would follow existing practice.

By the time this bead can run, three exports exist and are routed through the generic diffusion owner (`am-fs-diffusion-owner-sey`): `brownian_frames`, `philox_normals`, and `diffusion1d_frames`. The question this bead answers is narrow: does the browser boundary want operations composed upstream, or does the worker keep calling the three exports directly?

## Scope
