title: Assign per-paper editorial owners, per-capability implementation owners, and edition reviewers
description:
# Assign per-paper editorial owners, per-capability implementation owners, and edition reviewers

**Epic:** `am-ep-governance-sdc` · **Batch:** decision, started during Batch B and needed before any
review gate · **Priority:** P0 · **Plan sections:** §17.2, §17.5, §17.6, §17.7, §19.5, §20
(traceability only) · **Human gate**

## Background

The plan treats human judgment as first-class work, not final polish: "Human source and translation
review, scientific review, accessibility co-design, and editorial writing are first-class work
tracked alongside programming tasks" (§19.5). It asks for a responsible editorial owner for each
paper and a responsible implementation owner for each shared numerical capability, with the symbol
registry, source ids, and browser protocol centralized early so parallel contributors do not drift.

Review is argument-level (§17.2). Each section needs a German source review of the translation and a
physics or mathematics review of each complete derivation; the per-paper definition of done
additionally requires an R2 readability review by a non-physicist reviewer and a fifteen-minute tour
completed by a reader with no physics background (§17.7 items 8–9). Contributors may fill more than
one role where qualified, **but machine-generated drafts never self-certify**, and every acceptance
is recorded with reviewer names in the provenance receipt. "The reviewers for the English editions"
is an explicit open decision (§20).

Nineteen beads wait on this one. Thirteen review beads (twelve across the four papers plus the
companion review) and the Brownian gloss review `am-edn-review-german-gloss-brownian-1s9x` cannot
record acceptance until the reviewers exist, and the five comprehension round beads need named
facilitators. Other human work reads the same table: the Brownian acceptance
scenario, the accessibility co-design sessions and disabled-reader rounds, the Batch H
knowledge-boundary and transfer-task reviews, the final product test, and the real-device checks,
whose result files record a tester id. `am-edit-review-records-hofz` parses `docs/OWNERS.md` and
rejects any reviewer or facilitator id that is not listed there with the role that maps to the
record's type. The table format below is therefore a contract, not a style choice.

The table also holds the **contributors** the self-review check compares reviewers against. Every
reviewable record carries an authorship block (`draftedBy`, `translatedBy`, `editedBy`) whose human
entries are ids, not free text (`am-cm-schemas-source-1en`), and the translation, checking, and
gloss beads record real people there. The German edition's own editor resolves here too:
`content/source-blocks/<slug>/edition.yaml` names `editors` as authorship entries with at least one
human id (`am-edn-alignment-tooling-do1`), and each German source review record's checks compare the
reviewer id against both the authorship ids of the units it covers and that `editors` list, so one
table must answer for every one of them. Those ids must resolve in this same table, or the compiler
cannot tell a reviewer apart from an author: `am-edit-review-records-hofz` fails a human authorship
id that is not a row here (`authorship-unknown-contributor`). Contributor roles therefore exist
beside reviewer roles, and they map to no review type, so being listed as a translator never
authorizes signing a review.

The German source reviews changed shape during review. Each paper's review records two acceptances
as `german-source` review records imported through the review packet (`am-edn-review-packet-ee9t`):
German fidelity, a page-by-page comparison of every page's German blocks with the facsimile page
images, and translation accuracy, together with a disagreement log and a focus sign-off. The work is
large (the relativity paper alone has thirty-one pages), so a second qualified German source
reviewer may take part of it. The German source brief and the table rules below support that.

## Scope

In scope: naming owners, reviewers, facilitators, testers, and named contributors (or recording an
open recruiting status); writing the reviewer and contributor briefs; recording consent to be named
publicly and each assigned reviewer's short qualification statement; the `docs/OWNERS.md` table in
the machine-readable format below; a structural test for the briefs.

Out of scope, owned elsewhere: performing the reviews (the `*-review-*` and `edn-review-german-*`
beads, and the knowledge-boundary and transfer-task reviews recorded by
`am-disc-batch-h-exit-audit-r8xq`); the review packet and its validating import
(`am-edn-review-packet-ee9t`); recruiting and consenting study participants, who are never listed
here (`am-edit-comprehension-protocol-ouih` and the comprehension round beads); running
disabled-reader sessions (`am-bm-slice-a11y-codesign-3xuq`, `am-a11y-disabled-reader-rounds-jkjr`);
the parser and validator for `docs/OWNERS.md`, the authorship checks, and the review-record checks
(`am-edit-review-records-hofz`); the authorship block itself (`am-cm-schemas-source-1en`).

## Decision

**Roles to fill (role ids in parentheses are the values used in the table):**

1. **Editorial owner** (`editorial-owner`) for each paper: `light-quanta`, `brownian-motion`,
`special-relativity`, `mass-energy`, and the companion `molecular-dimensions`.
2. **Implementation owner** (`implementation-owner`) for each shared capability: content model and
compiler; source manifest and alignment tooling; reader shell; semantic equations; experiment
runtime and worker protocol; FrankenSim binding (diffusion first, then radiation, relativity
kinematics and energy accounting, electrodynamics, inference); verification and scenarios;
accessibility; search, performance, and security; release.
3. **German source reviewer** (`german-source-reviewer`) per paper: fluent in German, able to read
early-twentieth-century scientific prose and follow the paper's mathematics. Compares every page's
German blocks with the facsimile page images (German fidelity) and checks the translation against
the German with modality preserved (translation accuracy). A paper may have two German source
reviewers: one may take the German-fidelity part, or, for the relativity paper, one of its two
parts.
4. **Physics or mathematics reviewer** (`physics-math-reviewer`) per paper: checks every complete
derivation, the historical conventions (Gaussian units in paper 3, the source's force convention in
§10, the entropy integration constant in paper 1), the statistics of the inference instruments, and
the printed-value fixtures listed in the physics brief.
5. **Non-physicist R2 reviewer** (`r2-readability-reviewer`) per paper, plus **fifteen-minute tour
testers** (`tour-tester`) with no physics background.
6. **History-of-science reviewer** (`history-reviewer`): recommended for every paper; required
wherever a bead records a `history` review, including the knowledge-boundary review recorded by
`am-disc-batch-h-exit-audit-r8xq` (knowledge-card dates, parallel-work flags, historian's-margin
entries) and the historical attributions of the methodological essays
(`am-disc-essays-measurement-fixed-cb1i`).
7. **Transfer-task reviewer** (`transfer-task-reviewer`): an education-minded reviewer who did not
author the tasks, required for the transfer-task review recorded by
`am-disc-batch-h-exit-audit-r8xq` (cross-journey exercises, predict-perturb-explain tasks,
teach-back prompts, revisit cards, paired-learning sheets, and capstone templates).
8. **Cross-projection reviewer** (`cross-projection-reviewer`): follows one claim per paper across
every face the claim has, in the order a reader meets them, and authored none of them. The eleven
projections are the German source block, the aligned translation unit, the R0, R2 and R3 readings,
the `Equation` record with its authored spoken form, the instrument whose weave predicate lights the
claim, the results card, the printed chapter, the accessible equivalent a nonvisual reader reaches,
and the fifteen-minute tour. The paper's editorial owner chooses the claim, and chooses it for a
printed qualification it could lose. `am-edit-review-records-hofz` stores the result as a
`cross-projection` record and applies the same self-review comparison as the other types, so a
contributor listed as an author of any projection under review may not hold this role for that
paper.
9. **Facilitators and testers** for human sessions: `accessibility-codesign-facilitator` (slice
co-design and disabled-reader rounds), `comprehension-facilitator` (comprehension rounds, the
Brownian acceptance scenario, and the final product test), and `real-device-tester` (the slice and
pre-launch real-device checks).
10. **Named contributors**, whose ids appear in the authorship blocks of content records and in the
translation credits of the provenance receipts:
   - **`translator`**: drafts English translation units from the German.
   - **`checking-editor`**: checks and edits a drafted translation unit against the German before
   review; this is editing, not review, and it is recorded in `editedBy`.
   - **`glossator`**: authors word-level interlinear gloss units.
   - **`edition-editor`**: the editor named in `content/source-blocks/<slug>/edition.yaml`, whose
   page-image comparison of the German blocks earns the `corrected` state for that edition layer
   (`am-edn-alignment-tooling-do1`). This is editing against the facsimile, not review, and the
   German source review of that paper is signed by someone else.
   A person may hold several of these, and holding one does not prevent them from holding a reviewer
   role for material they did not work on. These four roles map to no review type: the parser
   accepts them as table rows so authorship ids resolve, and
   `am-edit-review-records-hofz` fails any review record whose reviewer holds only contributor
   roles. A model is never a row here; model authorship entries carry `kind: model` and a `modelId`
   instead.

**Plan default:** named people per role, with one person allowed to hold several roles where
qualified, never reviewing material they drafted, translated, glossed, or edited.

**Recording:** `docs/OWNERS.md` with a single Markdown table whose header row is exactly:

`| id | displayName | roles | scope | status | consentToBeNamed | assignedBy | assignedOn |`

- `id`: a stable lowercase handle matching `[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{1,40}`; never an email address, never
a `model:` prefix (a model is never a reviewer or a listed contributor).
- `displayName`: the name or handle exactly as the person consents to be shown publicly.
- `roles`: comma-separated role ids from the list above.
- `scope`: comma-separated paper slugs or capability names the role covers.
- `status`: `assigned` or `open: recruiting` (an open row uses `id` `open-<role>-<scope>` and an
empty `displayName`).
- `consentToBeNamed`: `yes` for every `assigned` row (an assigned person who declines public naming
is recorded privately by the user and shown under an agreed pseudonymous handle). For contributor
rows this consent covers the public translation credits on the provenance receipt and the `/sources`
page as well as the table.
- `assignedBy` and `assignedOn`: who made the assignment (the user or a delegate) and the ISO date.
- Several rows may hold the same role and scope, for example two German source reviewers for one
paper, or several translators for one paper. The table does not split their work; each review
record's `scope` shows exactly which units its reviewer covered, and each content record's
authorship block shows exactly who drafted, translated, glossed, or edited it.

Below the table, a `## Qualifications` section holds one short statement per assigned reviewer (`###
<id>`), written or approved by that person; the German source and physics review beads cite it.
Contributor rows need no qualification statement. The parser reads only the table and ignores this
section. No private contact details appear anywhere in the public repository. Review beads get their
assignee set, or an explicit open-status comment.

**Role to review-record mapping** (the `reviewType` values used by `am-edit-review-records-hofz`):
`german-source-reviewer` → `german-source`; `physics-math-reviewer` → `physics-math`;
`r2-readability-reviewer` → `r2-readability`; `tour-tester` → `tour-completion`; `history-reviewer`
→ `history`; `transfer-task-reviewer` → `transfer-task`; `cross-projection-reviewer` → `cross-projection`;
`accessibility-codesign-facilitator` →
`accessibility-codesign`; `comprehension-facilitator` → `comprehension-round`. `editorial-owner`,
`implementation-owner`, `real-device-tester`, `translator`, `checking-editor`, `glossator`, and
`edition-editor` map to no review type; the real-device tester's results live in the real-device result files, and the
contributor roles appear in authorship blocks and translation credits, not in review records.

**`edition-editor` is a role id the parser must know, and the inconsistency resolves in one
direction.** `am-edit-review-records-hofz` requirement 2 lists the known role ids and omits
`edition-editor`, while three of its own rules require it. Its `authorship-unknown-contributor`
check fails any authorship entry with `kind: human` whose id is not a row in `docs/OWNERS.md`; it
resolves a German source block's authorship from the `editors` of
`content/source-blocks/<slug>/edition.yaml`, treated as `editedBy`; and its requirement 5 excludes
an edition editor from signing that paper's German source review by reading that same list. So an
edition editor's id must be a row here, and that parser rejects a row whose `roles` column holds an
unknown role id. Omitting `edition-editor` from the known list would therefore make every German
source block fail `authorship-unknown-contributor` with no legal row that could fix it. The role
stays here, mapping to no review type, and requirement 2's known-role-id list is the side that
gains it. This bead's table, its acceptance criteria and its parser test already require that; the
correction to the other bead belongs to its owner and is not made here.

**Unblocks:** the thirteen review beads `am-edn-review-german-brownian-cfh`,
`am-edn-review-german-mass-energy-w3y`, `am-edn-review-german-relativity-0sr`,
`am-edn-review-german-light-quanta-khv`, `am-bm-review-physics-arfv`, `am-bm-review-reader-x77h`,
`am-me-review-physics-1t2l`, `am-me-review-reader-l6iy`, `am-sr-review-physics-omj8`,
`am-sr-review-reader-qff7`, `am-lq-review-physics-4wht`, `am-lq-review-reader-5alq`,
`am-companion-review-pfh8`; the gloss review `am-edn-review-german-gloss-brownian-1s9x`; and the
five comprehension round beads `am-edit-comprehension-round-brownian-slice-vihm`,
`am-edit-comprehension-rounds-brownian-864m`, `am-edit-comprehension-rounds-mass-energy-tec7`,
`am-edit-comprehension-rounds-relativity-jdp3`, `am-edit-comprehension-rounds-light-quanta-vr69`.

## Human Gate

Only the user (or people the user delegates) assigns owners and recruits reviewers, facilitators,
testers, and contributors. Agents may prepare `docs/OWNERS.md` as a template with every role as an
`open: recruiting` row, write the briefs, and run the structural test. Close this bead only when
every role is assigned or explicitly marked open with a recruiting note, and record who made the
assignments and when. Agents never close it on their own judgment, never add a person to the table
without the user's recorded assignment, and never write a qualification statement on a person's
behalf.

## Requirements

Reviewer and contributor briefs in `docs/review/`. Each brief states the evidence format: reviewer,
facilitator, or contributor id (from `docs/OWNERS.md`), role, scope ids with the revisions worked on
or reviewed, date, result, notes, and the file where the record lives.

- `german-source.md`:
  - **Materials.** Work from the review packet (`bun scripts/build-review-packet.ts --paper <slug>`,
  with `--part part-1|part-2` for the relativity paper and `--include-gloss` for the mass–energy
  paper) and the pinned facsimile. The packet shows facsimile page renders beside the German blocks,
  the English units grouped by alignment component, term annotations, modality markers, and the
  notation map.
  - **German fidelity.** Compare every page's German blocks with the page image, page by page and
  never by spot check. Compare pages carrying display equations symbol by symbol. Consult the ledger
  wherever a block and the image seem to differ. Record each page in `page-comparison.yaml`
  (`comparedBy`, `date`, `result`).
  - **Translation accuracy.** Review whole sections as arguments. Every German sentence's content,
  modality, and qualification survive in English, including splits and many-to-many edges;
  "suggests," "must," "under these assumptions," and "to this approximation" are not
  interchangeable. Notation is never translated (never replace $V$ with $c$ inside the translation);
  displays are referenced, never retyped or split; inline mathematics matches.
  - **Disagreements.** Resolve them by returning to the facsimile and its context, never by majority
  vote among paraphrases. Record each in `content/reviews/<slug>/disagreements.yaml` (unit id,
  German reading, English rendering or gloss, witness readings consulted, resolution, reason,
  substantive flag). Substantive disagreements with historical translations also go into the
  provenance receipt.
  - **Focus items.** Sign off each item of the review bead's focus list in
  `content/reviews/<slug>/german-source-focus.yaml` with the sentence ids examined.
  - **Sign-off.** Fill the packet's record templates yourself: `reviewer`, `result` (`accepted`,
  `accepted-with-changes`, `rejected`, `needs-rereview`), `notes`, and `date` are written only by
  the reviewer, never by a tool or an agent. Filled templates are imported with `bun
  scripts/import-review-record.ts <filled template> --packet <tool-run-id>`. If the text changed
  after the packet was built, the import refuses with `stale-unit`; ask for a diff packet
  (`--since-packet <tool-run-id>`) instead of signing text you have not seen. Once the
  German-fidelity record is accepted, the receipt's `transcription.ledgerStatus` may become
  `reviewed`.
  - **Two reviewers.** When a second German source reviewer takes the German-fidelity part (or one
  part of the relativity paper), each signs only the records whose scope they covered, and neither
  reviews a unit they drafted, translated, glossed, or edited.
- `physics.md`: derivation-level review; the no-circularity rules (no molecular count hidden in
synthetic data, no $E_0 = Mc^2$ initialization, no Minkowski interval as an unexplained historical
axiom, no threshold-programmed simulator treated as evidence of a threshold); historical versus
modern constant sets; the sign-off format; and the corrections to the plan that a reviewer must
check are applied, each stated in full so the brief stands alone:
  - **Coal card (ME-03).** A kilogram of coal releases about 24–35 MJ, so by $\Delta m = E/c^2$ it
  loses about 0.27–0.39 μg (about 0.3 μg), not "less than a nanogram."
  - **Light-complex adversarial fixture (SR-10).** It is tested with longitudinal rays and with a
  ray transverse in the moving frame, because a ray transverse in the unprimed frame gives exactly
  the material contraction factor and cannot discriminate.
  - **`brownian_frames`.** Every kernel documents its per-step distribution and variance; whether
  kernels 2 and 3 differ is resolved in the capability audit (`am-fs-capability-audit-byc`) and
  implemented exactly as recorded there.
  - **Refusals.** Fallible exports, starting with `diffusion1d_frames`, refuse through a typed
  envelope, never an unexplained empty buffer. The FTCS refusal code is `ftcs-unstable`: $D\,\Delta
  t/\Delta x^2$ above 0.5 is refused and exactly 0.5 is accepted. A work limit is the execution
  outcome `budget-exhausted`, never a physical status.
  - **`philox_normals`.** It takes explicit stream arguments; the recommended form is `(seed,
  kernel, tile, start_index, count)`, with `start_index` counting draws.
  - **"Not a mean velocity."** The explicit warning that the observable is not a mean velocity is
  attributed to Einstein's 1906 paper (*Zur Theorie der Brownschen Bewegung*, Ann. Phys. (4) 19,
  371) unless the pinned 1905 facsimile shows it; archive text of the 1905 paper shows only §4's
  condition that the observation intervals not be chosen too small.
  - **US public-domain cutoff.** It is dated: works published in 1930 or earlier, as of 2026.
  - **Glycerol exercise.** It states its temperature and uses typed entry: glycerol is about 1.4
  Pa·s at 20 °C, far outside the 0.5–20 mPa·s teaching range.
  - **Paper 1 §2 constants.** Planck's printed $\alpha = 6.10\times10^{-57}$ and $\beta =
  4.866\times10^{-11}$ give $N = \frac{\beta}{\alpha}\frac{8\pi R}{L^3} = 6.17\times10^{23}$ (full
  precision $6.170486\times10^{23}$) with $R = 8.31\times10^{7}$ and $L = 3\times10^{10}$. $R$ and
  $L$ appear not to be printed in §2, so they are declared editorial inputs of
  `einstein-1905-light-quanta-printed` and never labeled "as printed"; their sensitivity ($R =
  8.314\times10^{7}$ with $L = 2.998\times10^{10}$ gives $6.1858\times10^{23}$, which does not round
  to the printed value) travels with every result that uses them. A comparison witness prints
  $\alpha$ as $6{,}1\cdot10^{-56}$, which gives $6.17\times10^{22}$; only $6.10\times10^{-57}$
  reproduces the printed $N$. If the facsimile shows $10^{-56}$, the receipt records a suspected
  typographical error, the fixture uses the corrected value, and the source face keeps the original.
  - **Paper 1 §8 check (about 4.3 V for $\nu = 1.03\times10^{15}\,\mathrm{s^{-1}}$).** The fixture
  follows the printed representation $\Pi E = R\beta\nu - P'$ with $P' = 0$ and the gram-equivalent
  charge $E = 9.6\cdot10^{3}$ in electromagnetic CGS units, reading $\Pi\cdot10^{-8}$ as volts: $\Pi
  = 4.3385\times10^{8}$ abvolt, which is 4.3385 V (4.34 V at three figures, printed as about 4.3),
  with the printed-constants slope $R\beta/E\cdot10^{-8} = 4.2121\times10^{-15}$ V·s, and 4.3406 V
  with $R = 8.314\times10^{7}$. The route through an elementary charge of about $4.7\times10^{-10}$
  esu with $N = 6.17\times10^{23}$ and the statvolt factor gives 4.3057 V (299.792458 V per
  statvolt) to 4.3087 V (300 V); it is not printed and appears only as a labeled modern restatement.
  A witness result line reading "$\Pi\cdot10^{7} = 4.3$ Volt" is a suspected misprint. The facsimile
  decides which representation is printed.
  - **Constant bindings.** A printed constant symbol binds the constant quantity: $R$ binds
  `molarGasConstant` (the spelling `gasConstant` is rejected), and Einstein's $N$ binds
  `avogadroConstant`, whose value comes from the constant set ($6\times10^{23}$ printed in paper 2
  under `einstein-1905-brownian-printed`). Only inference outputs, which carry an uncertainty, bind
  `avogadroNumberEstimate`. Exactness lives in the constant-set entry, never in the quantity. A
  mixed scenario names the modern entry it uses (as `diffusion-einstein-1905-modern-kb` does), and a
  historical molecular-count inference never resolves $N$ or $k_B$ from `modern-si-2019`.
  - **Displacement fixture (paper 2 §5).** With Einstein's printed $N = 6\times10^{23}$, viscosity
  $k = 1.35\times10^{-2}$ (CGS), and particle diameter 0.001 mm, plus $R = 8.31\times10^{7}$ as the
  declared editorial input and $T = 290.15$ K as the site's conversion of 17 °C, $\lambda_x$ is
  0.795 μm at 1 s and 6.16 μm at 60 s (full precision 0.7947833 and 6.156365 μm); with the modern
  $k_B$ the 60 s value is 6.15 μm. The paper prints "0,8 Mikron" and "ca. 6 Mikron". A 60 s value is
  always quoted with its constant set or as the printed "about 6".
  - **Cancellation-free numerics.** For example $1 - \sqrt{1-\beta^2} =
  \beta^2/(1+\sqrt{1-\beta^2})$.
  - **The dissertation's viscosity coefficient.** Einstein prints $k$ for the viscosity itself, both
  in the dissertation ($k^* = k(1 + \varphi)$) and in the Brownian paper ($k = 1.35\cdot10^{-2}$ for
  water), so the coefficient of $\varphi$ is never called $k$. It is 1 in the 1906 printing and 5/2
  after the 1911 correction; the modern symbol $[\eta]$ appears only in modern-notation layers,
  marked as modern, and code keeps the parameter name `factor`. With fixed data $N$ scales as the
  square root of the coefficient, so the coefficient alone multiplies $N$ by $\sqrt{2.5} \approx
  1.581$ and would turn $2.1\times10^{23}$ into about $3.3\times10^{23}$. The dissertation's
  $2.1\times10^{23}$ and $6.6\times10^{23}$ therefore come from different data sets; since $4.15
  \times \sqrt{2.5} \approx 6.56$, the 1911 value appears to reuse the 1906 supplement's inputs
  (verify on `ap-34-591`).
  - **Galilean auxiliary (paper 3 §3).** The printed auxiliary $x' = x - vt$ gets a distinct modern
  glyph wherever the moving-frame $x'$ also appears.
  - **Molecular kicks.** A suspended micrometre particle receives about $10^{19}$ to $10^{20}$
  molecular kicks per second.
  - **Magnet and conductor (SR-02).** The two descriptions give the same EMF only to first order in
  $v/c$. In the magnet's rest frame the coil's charges feel $q\,\mathbf{v}\times\mathbf{B}$; in the
  coil's rest frame that effect is the electric field $\mathbf{E}' =
  \gamma\,\mathbf{v}\times\mathbf{B}$.
- `r2-readability.md`: the R2 test ("a physician who has not used a derivative since 1998 can follow
it with effort and without shame"), the R0 test ("a reader with no physics can state what the
paragraph claims"), how to record stumbling points by passage id.
- `tour-tester.md`: complete the fifteen-minute tour and state the paper's claim in one sentence;
record the sentence verbatim. Tours use no symbols in text, captions, or table headers, so the
tester also notes any symbol or equation met on the way.
- `history.md`: verify card dates and statuses from original sources; parallel work and later
confirmations are labeled; the four historical statements (publicly available, evidence Einstein
knew it, the paper asserts it, the site uses it in a reconstruction) are never interchanged. The
brief also covers the **shelf verification queues** of `am-disc-journey-i-shelf-xjp8`,
`am-disc-journey-ii-shelf-zbli`, `am-disc-journey-iii-shelf-5z6q`, and
`am-disc-journey-iv-shelf-ff7g`: for the knowledge-boundary review recorded by
`am-disc-batch-h-exit-audit-r8xq`, the reviewer reads every queue entry in that audit's shelf-queue
summary, signs off each `narrowed` entry as a judgement about what the source actually supports and
what the card may therefore claim, and reports an `open` entry as an unmet exit condition rather
than a note.
- `transfer-task.md`: for each task, check that its premises are noncircular, that it is answerable
without a stored-string answer key (the kernel or numerical equivalence checks answers), that
feedback addresses the reader's model of the situation rather than a mark, and that no score, point,
grade, or keyword grading of free text appears; confirm that the reviewer did not author the tasks.
- `cross-projection.md`: one claim per paper, chosen by that paper's editorial owner for a printed
qualification it could lose, and recorded with its result card. The eleven projections in reading
order: the German source block, the aligned translation unit, R0, R2, R3, the `Equation` record with
its authored spoken form, the instrument whose weave predicate lights the claim (including its
caption at the reviewer's chosen detail), the results card, the printed chapter, the accessible
equivalent, and the fifteen-minute tour. The four verdicts per projection are `unchanged`,
`weakened`, `strengthened` and `absent`, and `absent` is a legitimate verdict, for an R3 reading or
a tour that does not carry the claim. The seven finding kinds are a dropped qualification (a
"suggests", "under these assumptions" or "to this approximation" lost), a widened scope, an
approximation stated as exact, a changed constant set, a changed frame or unit, a hidden premise,
and a differing number; each finding names the bead that owns the projection it was found in. The
reviewer records `contentRevision` and `translationRevision` so a later correction can tell whether
the review still applies, and states in the sign-off that they authored none of the projections
reviewed.
- `contributors.md`: for the `translator`, `checking-editor`, `glossator`, and `edition-editor`
roles. What each role
covers; that the person's `id` from this table is what goes into a record's authorship block
(`draftedBy`, `translatedBy`, `editedBy`) and never a free-text name; that a checking editor's work
is editing, not review, so it never satisfies a review gate; that a contributor may hold a reviewer
role for material they did not work on, and never for material they did; that
`consentToBeNamed: yes` also covers the public translation credits on the provenance receipt and
`/sources`; that an `edition-editor` id is what `edition.yaml`'s `editors` list carries, so a German
edition cannot reach `corrected` behind an unnamed editor; and that a model draft is recorded as a `kind: model` authorship entry with its
`modelId`, never as a row in this table.
- `facilitators.md`: points to the comprehension protocol (`docs/comprehension/`, including its
participant codes `<paper>-<route>-<YYYYMMDD>-<nn>` and their parser), the accessibility manual
protocol (`docs/accessibility/manual-protocol.md`), and the real-device checklist
(`docs/testing/real-device/README.md`), and states that participants are never named in the
repository.

## Technical Approach

Write the template and briefs as Markdown. The owners table follows the exact header and value rules
above, because `am-edit-review-records-hofz` parses it (`src/content/owners/parseOwners.ts`) and
fails the build on malformed rows, unknown role ids, `model:` ids, or assigned rows without consent.
Add `src/testing/docs/reviewerBriefs.test.ts`, which keeps the briefs complete and keeps superseded
fixture statements from returning.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `docs/OWNERS.md` exists with every role above, including `transfer-task-reviewer` and the
contributor roles `translator`, `checking-editor`, `glossator`, and `edition-editor`, each
assigned or marked open
with a recruiting note, in the exact table format, with a qualification statement for every assigned
reviewer.
- [ ] The nine briefs exist and state the evidence format; the German source brief describes the
page-by-page German-fidelity comparison, translation accuracy, the disagreement log, the focus
sign-off, the packet import, and the two-reviewer case; the physics brief states every correction
listed above; the history brief covers the shelf verification queues and the `narrowed` sign-off;
the contributor brief states the authorship-id rule, the `edition.yaml` `editors` rule, and the
credit consent; and the cross-projection brief states the eleven projections in reading order, the
four verdicts, and the seven finding kinds.
- [ ] `cross-projection-reviewer` is a row in `docs/OWNERS.md` for each paper, assigned or marked
open with a recruiting note, mapped to the `cross-projection` review type, with `cross-projection.md`
written, so `am-edit-review-records-hofz` accepts a `cross-projection` record instead of rejecting
every one of them on an unknown role id.
- [ ] Consent to publish each named person's display name is recorded (`consentToBeNamed: yes`), and
contributor rows record that it covers translation credits.
- [ ] Every review bead, comprehension round bead, and gloss review listed under Unblocks has an
assignee or an explicit open-status comment.
- [ ] No reviewer is assigned to review material they drafted, translated, glossed, or edited.
- [ ] Every human id used in a content record's authorship block or in an `edition.yaml` `editors`
list exists as a row here, so `am-edit-review-records-hofz` reports no
`authorship-unknown-contributor` and the German source reviews can compare a reviewer against both
the unit authorship and the edition editors.
- [ ] `src/testing/docs/reviewerBriefs.test.ts` passes on the committed briefs.
- [ ] When `am-edit-review-records-hofz` exists, its owners-table check passes on the committed
file; before then, the close evidence records a manual check of the header and role ids.

## Test Plan

### Unit and integration tests
- `src/testing/docs/reviewerBriefs.test.ts`:
  - all nine briefs exist, and each has a section stating the evidence format;
  - `german-source.md` has sections for materials, German fidelity, translation accuracy,
  disagreements, focus items, sign-off, and two reviewers, and names `page-comparison.yaml`,
  `disagreements.yaml`, `german-source-focus.yaml`, and the import command;
  - `physics.md` contains the current fixture values `6.10\times10^{-57}`, `6.1858\times10^{23}`,
  `9.6\cdot10^{3}`, `4.3385`, `4.3057`, `0.7947833`, `6.156365`, `0.27–0.39`, `\sqrt{2.5}`,
  `ftcs-unstable`, `molarGasConstant`, `avogadroConstant`, and `\gamma\,\mathbf{v}\times\mathbf{B}`;
  - `physics.md` contains none of the superseded statements: "printed elementary charge", $R$ and
  $L$ called "printed constants", "$k$ from 1 to", the rejected spelling `gasConstant` outside its
  rejection sentence, or a 60 s displacement without its constant set; a fixture brief containing
  each fails with a message naming the phrase and line;
  - `cross-projection.md` names the eleven projections in order, the four verdicts including
  `absent`, and the seven finding kinds, and states that the reviewer authored none of the
  projections under review;
  - `transfer-task.md` names its four checks; `history.md` names the four shelf verification queues,
  the `narrowed` sign-off, and the rule that an `open` entry is an unmet exit condition;
  `contributors.md` names the four contributor roles, the authorship-block fields, the
  `edition.yaml` `editors` rule, and the credit consent; and `facilitators.md` names the participant
  code form.
- The owners table itself is validated by `src/content/owners/parseOwners.test.ts` and the
review-record checks in `am-edit-review-records-hofz` (unknown role id, email-like id, `model:` id,
assigned row without consent, and duplicate ids all fail; two rows sharing a role and scope pass;
`german-source-reviewer`, `history-reviewer`, `transfer-task-reviewer`, `cross-projection-reviewer`,
and `edition-editor` are accepted role ids, and an `edition.yaml` `editors` entry naming a row that does not exist fails with
`authorship-unknown-contributor`; a row holding only contributor roles cannot sign a review record; the `## Qualifications` section is
ignored).
### End-to-end tests
The gate chain runs `reviewerBriefs.test.ts` on every commit and, once `am-edit-review-records-hofz`
lands, its owners-table and authorship checks on the committed `docs/OWNERS.md` and the corpus.
Human assignment itself has no automated end-to-end path.
### Structured logging
`reviewerBriefs.test.ts` writes `{timestamp, suite: "reviewer-briefs", logRunId, testId, beadId,
file, check, outcome, message}` to `artifacts/test-logs/reviewer-briefs/<log-run-id>.jsonl`; a
failure logs the missing section or the superseded phrase with its line number and retains a copy of
the offending brief under that run's evidence directory. The owners-table check logs under the
review-records suite.

## Considerations and Pitfalls

- A reviewer who drafted a translation with machine help still counts as the drafter; self-review is
not review.
- Compensation and accessibility for participants follow the comprehension protocol; do not collect
diagnoses or credentials, and never list participants.
- Recruiting can take longer than implementation; start during the reference slice so review gates
in Batch C onward do not stall finished work. German fidelity on a long paper is days of careful
work, which is why a second German source reviewer is allowed.
- Changing a person's `id` after records reference it breaks review records and authorship blocks;
add a new row and mark the old one retired in the notes instead.
- Adding a contributor row is not an assignment of authority. It records who did the work so credit
and the self-review check are exact.
- The physics brief repeats fixture values that the reference and verification beads own
(`am-ref-constants-xik`, `am-ver-fixture-table-audit-nh5`). When one of them changes after a
facsimile check, update the brief and its test in the same change.

## Dependencies

Blocked by: `am-gov-repo-bootstrap-p5t` (the repository and `docs/` location exist).

Unblocks:
- the thirteen review beads listed under Decision and the gloss review
`am-edn-review-german-gloss-brownian-1s9x`, which record acceptance only with reviewers listed in
`docs/OWNERS.md`;
- the five comprehension round beads listed under Decision, which record facilitator ids from
`docs/OWNERS.md`.

Also reads `docs/OWNERS.md`: `am-bm-acceptance-scenario-vjn4` and
`am-launch-final-product-test-nzhn` (comprehension facilitators), `am-bm-slice-a11y-codesign-3xuq`
and `am-a11y-disabled-reader-rounds-jkjr` (accessibility co-design facilitators),
`am-test-real-device-slice-check-bize` and `am-test-real-device-check-iju4` (real-device testers),
`am-disc-batch-h-exit-audit-r8xq` (history and transfer-task reviewers), and the translation, gloss,
and edition beads (contributor ids in authorship blocks and translation credits).

BINDING DECISION — recorded by BoldHarbor (Claude Opus 5 orchestrator), 2026-09-16.

## Authority for this decision

The project owner was asked directly, in session, which of the four open human-gate decisions he
wanted to resolve. His answer, verbatim: "you decide all that stuff based on what you think I would
want". That delegation is the authority for this record, and it is quoted here rather than
paraphrased so the provenance is auditable.

The decider recorded in `docs/OWNERS.md` and in `docs/DECISIONS.md` is therefore
`agent:BoldHarbor`, acting under that delegation, dated 2026-09-16. It is NOT the project owner.
A previous agent on this project wrote `Decider: jemanuel (Project Owner)` on a decision the owner
never made; that was an incident. The distinction is the point: delegated authority to decide is
recorded as delegated authority, never laundered into the owner's signature.

## The decision

**1. Filled roles.** The project owner (contributor id `jemanuel`) is the sole human on this
project and is recorded as:
  - `editorial-owner` for all four papers and the companion dissertation;
  - `implementation-owner` for every shared numerical capability;
  - the ratifying decider for project decisions.

**2. Roles that stay OPEN, with recruiting status, because no qualified human holds them.**
Do not fill these with the owner, and do not fill them with an agent:
  - `german-source-reviewer` — needs German reading competence against 1905 Fraktur-era typesetting.
  - `physics-reviewer` — must be independent of the author of the derivation under review.
  - `r2-readability-reviewer` — must be a non-physicist, by definition of the R2 test.
  - `a11y-participant` — disabled readers testing with their own assistive technology.
  - `comprehension-facilitator` and `comprehension-participant`.
Their row status is `open-recruiting` with no name. The bead's own Scope permits exactly this
("or recording an open recruiting status").

**3. Agents are contributors, never reviewers.** Agent-produced material is recorded with a
`draftedBy: agent:<name>` authorship entry. An agent id may appear in an authorship block. An agent
id may NEVER appear as a reviewer, facilitator, or tester id, and `am-edit-review-records-hofz`
must reject it with a distinct error rather than treating it as an unknown contributor. Machine
drafts never self-certify (AGENTS.md, "Review gates").

**4. The honest consequence, which must be recorded and not worked around.** With
`german-source-reviewer` and `physics-reviewer` unfilled, no `german-source` or physics review
record can be accepted. The per-paper definition of done therefore CANNOT be met on those axes
today, and the launch criteria that depend on them cannot go green. That is a true statement about
the project, not a defect in this table. The correct behaviour downstream is to report BLOCKED on
external human proof. It is explicitly forbidden to: mark such a review accepted on an agent's
judgement, widen a role definition so the owner or an agent qualifies, or report a paper as done
with a footnote about missing review.

## What the implementing lane must build

The deliverable is not this text. It is:
  1. `docs/OWNERS.md` in the machine-readable table format the bead specifies, carrying both the
     filled rows and the `open-recruiting` rows, plus the contributor rows.
  2. The reviewer brief and the contributor brief, including the German source brief, which must
     support splitting one paper's German review between two qualified reviewers.
  3. A structural test over the briefs and the table: a row missing a required column fails; an
     agent id in a reviewer column fails with its own error; an `open-recruiting` row with a name
     fails; a named row with no consent field and no qualification statement fails; an authorship
     id that is not a row in the table fails as `authorship-unknown-contributor`.
  4. The consent field exists and is `not-applicable` for `open-recruiting` rows, `granted` for
     `jemanuel`. Public naming consent is real; do not default it to true.

Implement the table and the test. Do not re-litigate the decision above.

# Create the public repository with README, AGENTS.md, LICENSE, git hygiene, vercel.json, and beads workspace

**Epic:** `am-ep-governance-sdc` · **Batch:** A · **Priority:** P0 · **Plan sections:** §17.8, §18.1, §18.5 (traceability only) · **Status:** completed in the planning session

## Background

The plan's repository section (§18.5) calls for `gh repo create Dicklesworthstone/annus-mirabilis.com --public`, the chosen license with rider and per-asset exceptions, a README modeled on classic-patents.com (TL;DR, the four papers table, architecture box, getting started, verification, license), and the master plan committed as the source of truth. Plan §17.8 specifies AGENTS.md: copy the donor file; keep Rules 0, 1, 2, git safety, branch policy, the cloud-OCR-only chapter, the FrankenSim honesty chapter, the Three.js chapter, the Vercel chapter, Beads, Agent Mail, code quality, and "landing the plane"; replace the patent mission and "how to add a patent" with how to add or revise a paper section, how to add an instrument, how to add a discovery step, the epistemic rules, the editorial voice including the R2 test, and the command-class rule (an observer change never restarts an experiment). Plan §18.1 requires `vercel.json` to keep `{"git": {"deploymentEnabled": false}}`.

This bead is kept as a record so the task graph reflects reality and later agents can see exactly what the bootstrap contains.

## Scope

In scope: repository creation, README, AGENTS.md, LICENSE, `.gitignore`, `.gitattributes`, `vercel.json`, committing the master plan, initializing the beads workspace, GitHub description and topics.

Out of scope, owned elsewhere: the application scaffold (`am-scaf-nextjs-app-bu2`), the final license decision (`am-gov-decision-license-rights-tps`), the donor audit (`am-gov-donor-audit-0wa`).

## Requirements (as delivered)

- **Repository:** https://github.com/Dicklesworthstone/annus-mirabilis.com, public, primary branch `main`, initial commit `30f6957` ("Initial repository: master plan, README, AGENTS.md, license, and beads workspace").
- **GitHub description:** "Interactive critical edition and discovery lab for Einstein's four 1905 Annalen der Physik papers: pinned facsimiles, reviewed German text, a new aligned English translation, explanations at every depth, live semantic equations, and FrankenSim-backed physics instruments."

title: Build shared SVG and Canvas view primitives that only project accepted snapshots
description:
# Build shared SVG and Canvas view primitives that only project accepted snapshots

**Epic:** `am-ep-instruments-8gi` · **Batch:** batch-b · **Priority:** P0 · **Plan sections:** §8.1 (coordinate traps), §8.2 (rendering rules), §8.3 (diagram scaling), §10.9, §12.5, §12.7, §15.5, §16.2, §16.4 (traceability only)

## Background

Almost every instrument is two-dimensional: histograms, trajectories, spectra, event diagrams, energy ledgers. The plan is emphatic that 2D comes first, and Three.js is reserved for the few spatial cases. A shared view kit keeps visual semantics consistent. More importantly, it encodes the rendering rules that protect scientific meaning:

- a logarithmic axis never redefines what a density means;
- a path leaving the viewport stays in the ensemble;
- a smooth polyline is a rendering convention, not a velocity;
- a point distribution at $t = 0$ is not an infinite bar;
- ultraviolet and infrared are never shown as visible colors without a false-color legend;
- rendering a subset of particles never changes the ensemble used for results;
- a histogram shows bins the owner computed, never bins a view invented from raw positions.

Every primitive consumes accepted snapshot data and projects coordinates into pixels. None computes physics or statistics. The primitives take snapshot slices as props, so they need neither the registry nor any instrument: the dispatcher binds instrument views to instances, and instrument views pass data down.

Browser evidence comes from a **fixture application registered with the harness**, not from a build flag: `am-test-e2e-harness-bqmh` owns the single fixture bundler (`scripts/e2e/fixtures/bundleFixtures.ts`), its registry (`scripts/e2e/fixtures/fixtureApps.ts`), and the fixture server, and this bead registers the application `view-kit` there.

## Scope

In scope: `src/visuals/kit/` primitives for axes, plots, histograms with comparison series, trajectories, event diagrams, intervals, ledgers, legends, scale bars, and typed-result rendering; performance tiers; accessibility hooks; term-selection highlighting by attribute; the `view-kit` fixture application and its registry entry.

Out of scope:
- specific instruments;
- Three.js (`am-inst-three-studio-y0y0`);
- dataset loading (`am-inst-dataset-overlay-ra9r`);
- description text generation (`am-a11y-graph-descriptions-vxe1`, integrated here through hooks);
- performance budget enforcement (`am-plat-perf-budgets-s3ww`);
- the equation selection store itself (`am-eq-colorized-component-1z8`);
- the fixture bundler and fixture server (`am-test-e2e-harness-bqmh`).

## Requirements

### Common contract

- **Inputs.** Every primitive receives typed data from an accepted snapshot: typed arrays, typed results from `am-rt-typed-results-mqb`, and the identity fields `instanceId`, `runId`, and `snapshotVersion`.
- **Identity attributes.** Every primitive renders `data-instance-id`, `data-run-id`, and `data-snapshot-version` so tests can prove that all views show one state.
- **No scientific state.** No primitive keeps a private copy of a scientific parameter in React state or derives a scientific value.

### `RepresentationScale`: five independent fields, declared once

Representational scales are independent fields: spatial magnification, physical elapsed time, playback multiplier, particle glyph size, and quantity normalization. A label such as "real time" means model seconds per wall-clock second, not physically life-size rendering. A light pulse can be shown with a greatly slowed playback rate without pretending its physical speed has changed, and a microscope view can be magnified while its displacement values remain in micrometres.

Three of those five are owned in three places today and none of them together: the scale bar and the histogram's stated normalization here, the 1:1 playback clock with labeled speed factors in `am-inst-real-rate-mode-gtez`, and nothing at all for magnification or glyph size. The gap has already produced a local invention: `am-me-03-box-extension-kiei` declares its own control, "Displacement magnification, none, ×10¹⁵ to ×10²⁰ for the readout, default ×10¹⁷, presentation-change", because there is no shared field to declare it in, no validator to check it against, and no rule carrying that factor into the accessible table or the print view. A reader who sees a $1.112650\times10^{-17}$ m displacement drawn at a visible size has no contracted way to learn that the picture is magnified by $10^{17}$, and a screen-reader user has none at all.

This adds one typed view-state object and five rules. It adds no primitive, no view, and no physics.

Every view that draws a physical quantity publishes a `RepresentationScale` beside the snapshot it projects. Its five fields are independent, none is derived from another, and changing any one is a `presentation-change`:

```
representationScale:
  spatialMagnification:  { appliesTo: "scene" | <outputId>, factor: number, note?: string }
  simulatedElapsedTime:  { quantityId, value, unit }   # the model time this frame represents
  playbackMultiplier:    number                        # model seconds per wall-clock second
  glyphSize:             { drawnPx: number, represents: "none" | <quantityId> }
  quantityNormalization: { kind: "none" | "per-bin-width" | "per-total" | "per-peak" | <quantityId>, note?: string }
```

1. **`playbackMultiplier` defines "real time."** The label "true rate" or "real time" renders only when `playbackMultiplier` is exactly 1, and it means model seconds per wall-clock second, never that the drawing is life-size. The "true rate" and "25 times faster" labels of `am-inst-real-rate-mode-gtez` render from this field rather than from the controller's own state; the controller sets it.
2. **`glyphSize.represents: "none"` is the default and the honest case.** A drawn particle marker is a marker. A view may set `represents` to a quantity id only when the drawn size is calibrated to that quantity and the legend says so; otherwise a reader may not infer a physical size from a glyph, and a test asserts that no caption relates glyph size to a physical extent while `represents` is `"none"`.
3. **`spatialMagnification.factor` is 1 unless a view deliberately amplifies.** `appliesTo` distinguishes a magnified scene from an amplified readout: BM-01's microscope view magnifies the scene, and `am-me-03-box-extension-kiei` amplifies one output, its displacement. A factor other than 1 is rendered as a visible statement ("drawn one hundred million times larger than life", or the readout's own wording), and it never changes the value shown in the units strip: the view is magnified while the displacement values remain in micrometres.
4. **The same five facts reach the nonvisual summary and the print view.** The accessible table (`am-a11y-graph-descriptions-vxe1`) and the print stylesheet (`am-plat-print-3orn`) render the scale facts from this object, so a reader who never sees the scene is told what the scene's scale was. A view that publishes a `RepresentationScale` no accessible surface renders fails the audit.
5. **The scale bar is derived, never independent.** `ScaleBar` is drawn from the manifest's `realRate.scaleBar` calibrated length and `spatialMagnification`; a view that draws a scale bar without publishing a `RepresentationScale` fails.

The existing consumers, restated as declarations:

| View | `spatialMagnification` | `playbackMultiplier` | `glyphSize.represents` | `quantityNormalization` |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| BM-01 microscope view (`am-bm-01-tracer-ensemble-hdly`) | scene, the factor that makes a 1 μm bar the drawn bar length | 1 at true rate, or the accelerated factor | `"none"` (a tracer marker is not a particle radius) | `none` |
| BM-01 displacement histogram | scene, 1 | 1 | `"none"` | `per-bin-width` or `per-total`, matching the bin-probability versus density toggle |
| `am-me-03-box-extension-kiei` box view | `centerOfMassShift` (the displacement output id), factor $10^{17}$ by default, range $10^{15}$ to $10^{20}$ | 1 | `"none"` | `none` |
| SR-03 strip view | scene, 1 | 1 | `"none"` | `none` |
| SR-10 bounding-sphere view | scene, 1 | 1 | `"none"` | `none` |

The box's existing control is unchanged in behaviour; it becomes a declared instance of `spatialMagnification` with `appliesTo` naming its output, which is what lets its factor reach the accessible table and the print view for the first time.

A scene shows a scale bar, a time legend, and a short caption, and no more: the scene is never covered with telemetry that distracts from the relation being taught. The full five-field statement lives in the accessible table, the print view, and the model note where a factor other than 1 is in force.

### Term selection without a store dependency (decided here and in `am-eq-colorized-component-1z8`)

`am-eq-colorized-component-1z8` lists this kit's series and tables among the subscribers of its selection store. The kit does **not** import that store, and there is no edge from this bead to `am-eq-colorized-component-1z8`, because every Batch B instrument would then wait on the equation component.

- Every series, mark, legend entry, axis label, and table cell that represents a quantity renders `data-quantity-id` with its exact canonical id.
- The equation island publishes the current selection on the argument-context root it already owns, as `data-selected-quantity-id` and `data-selected-node-id`. SVG primitives highlight through a CSS attribute match scoped to that root, so selection works with no JavaScript in the kit and no import in either direction.
- Canvas layers cannot be styled by CSS, so they accept an optional `selectedQuantityId` string prop and redraw the emphasized layer. The kit neither subscribes nor polls: the component that subscribes to the selection store and passes the prop is a downstream bead (the reading-face composer and the interaction ladder), which is where every JavaScript subscriber lives.
- Highlighting is presentation: it never changes snapshot data, never issues a command, and never enters a scientific digest.

### Axes and units

- Axes take a canonical quantity id and a display unit from the quantity registry. Tick labels format through the units adapter, never through ad hoc strings.
- **Logarithmic axes.** The primitive requires the snapshot to declare the density kind of its vertical data: `per-frequency`, `per-wavelength`, `per-ln-interval`, `per-decade`, or `total`. A log horizontal axis with a per-frequency density is labeled as such. Switching to a per-log-interval view is a data transform supplied by the owner, not a relabel.
- Frequency and wavelength axes are distinct quantity ids. A selected band can be preserved across representations using owner-supplied mappings.
- **Log-log plots.** Model reference lines carry their slope label (for example "slope 1/2"); both the line values and the slope come from the snapshot.

### Plot primitives

- **`LinePlot` and `ScatterPlot`** have three visually distinct classes: theoretical curves, historical fitted laws, and empirical points (markers with uncertainty bars). The class is part of the data contract.
- **`Histogram`** has explicit bin semantics. The owner supplies edges, counts, overflow counts, and bin probabilities. The view offers a bin-probability versus density toggle, shows the bin width, and states the normalization. An optional **comparison series** draws aligned bars or markers of a second class, such as a numerical grid result beside exact bin probabilities, with non-color identity.
- **`IntervalShade`** shades a selected interval, with the probability value supplied by the snapshot.
- **`AnalyticLimitMarker`** renders an `analytic-limit` point distribution as a labeled marker with interval probabilities, never an infinite bar.

### Trajectories and fields of view

- **`TrajectoryLayer`** draws sampled positions from typed buffers without copying them into React state. It supports up to 10 000 tracers with batched Canvas drawing and instancing where available.
- **Viewport exits.** Paths leaving the viewport are not wrapped, reflected, replaced, or dropped from the ensemble, and the API offers no option to do so. The view shows an off-screen count as a presentation census. The microscope boundary is a camera viewport, not a wall.
- **Initial layout.** Initial on-screen positions (for example a deterministic lattice) are presentation layout supplied by the instrument and are excluded from scientific digests.
- **Polylines.** Smooth lines between samples are labeled a rendering convention in the model note; no primitive derives velocity from a polyline.
- **Subsets.** Rendering a subset for performance is allowed only for display; result panels always read ensemble statistics from the snapshot.

### Event and spacetime diagrams

`EventDiagram`:
- uses coherent axis scaling so light lines are at 45 degrees;
- supports light-seconds units with the conversion shown;
- marks events by id with frame labels;
- never lets camera zoom imply changed physics;
- carries the label that spacetime diagrams are a later aid (Minkowski 1908).

### Ledgers and legends

- `EnergyLedger`: bars and tables for channel accounting, with boundaries drawn from snapshot data.
- `QuantityLegend`: keyed by quantity id and role color from the semantic color system, plus a non-color identity (label, shape, outline, or pattern), so meaning survives color-vision differences and monochrome print.
- `FalseColorLegend`: required whenever a spectral view shows frequencies outside 380–750 nm.
- `ScaleBar`: a calibrated physical length and time scale from snapshot and manifest data.

### Performance and lifecycle

- 60 Hz on capable desktops and a stable 30 Hz mobile tier. UI summaries are published at a bounded rate, and display interpolation is kept separate from scientific stepping.
- A depleted budget reduces visual detail (point size, drawn subset, resolution) and never alters the model, time step, or sample.
- Canvas contexts, listeners, and animation frames are released on unmount; invisible views pause.

### Accessibility hooks

- Each primitive exposes a description provider consumed by `am-a11y-graph-descriptions-vxe1`, with three layers: a statement of what is compared, the current relation after an intentional action, and optional detailed data as a table.
- No 60 Hz live-region updates; committed comparisons only.
- Reduced motion pauses animation and shows the current state.

### The `view-kit` fixture application

Registered as `{ id: "view-kit", entry: "src/testing/e2e/fixture-apps/view-kit/", outDir: "artifacts/e2e-fixtures/view-kit/", owner: "am-inst-2d-view-kit-u75r" }`, bundled by the harness bundler and served at `/apps/view-kit/`. It renders the kit over deterministic fixture snapshots and emits the harness DOM contract attributes. There is no fixture flag, route, or conditional import in the application.

## Technical Approach

- React components over SVG for axes and annotations, and Canvas 2D for dense layers. Data is passed as typed arrays and snapshot references.
- Deterministic fixture snapshots live in `src/visuals/kit/__fixtures__/`, generated from runtime fixtures, never from ad hoc math in tests.
- Tests use SVG snapshots and, only where rendering is stable across CI browsers, pixel hashes.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] All primitives exist, take quantity ids and units, render only from snapshot data, and expose identity attributes.
- [ ] Every quantity-bearing mark, legend entry, and table cell carries `data-quantity-id`; SVG highlighting follows `data-selected-quantity-id` on the argument-context root with no import of the selection store, and Canvas layers highlight from the `selectedQuantityId` prop.
- [ ] A density-kind declaration is required for log axes; a test proves a per-frequency density cannot be silently shown under a per-log-interval axis label.
- [ ] Histograms accept only owner-supplied bins; a test proves no API accepts raw positions for binning. Comparison series are distinguishable without color.
- [ ] Trajectories leaving the viewport remain counted, and wrap and reflect are impossible through the API.
- [ ] Analytic-limit markers render correctly with interval probabilities.
- [ ] Legends show non-color identity, and the false-color legend appears for non-visible frequencies.
- [ ] 10 000 fixture tracers render with frame times logged against the agreed device profile; the drawn subset never changes result panels.
- [ ] Views release resources on unmount: no growth in listener or context counts across 50 mount cycles.
- [ ] The `view-kit` fixture application is registered, bundles, and serves at `/apps/view-kit/`.
- [ ] Every view primitive that draws a physical quantity publishes a `RepresentationScale` with all five fields; a fixture view omitting one fails with the view id and field named.
- [ ] The labels "true rate" and "real time" render only when `playbackMultiplier` is exactly 1; a fixture rendering either at 25 fails.
- [ ] `glyphSize.represents` defaults to `"none"`, and a caption relating glyph size to a physical extent while `represents` is `"none"` fails the caption audit.
- [ ] A `spatialMagnification.factor` other than 1 renders a visible statement of the factor, and the value shown in the units strip is unchanged by it, asserted by comparing the rendered value at factor 1 and at $10^{17}$.
- [ ] `appliesTo` distinguishes a scene magnification from a named-output amplification, and `am-me-03-box-extension-kiei`'s displacement magnification validates as the latter.
- [ ] The accessible table and the print view render all five facts from the object; a view whose scale facts reach neither fails the audit.
- [ ] A view drawing a scale bar without publishing a `RepresentationScale` fails.
- [ ] Changing any of the five fields is a `presentation-change`: `runId`, `seed`, every scientific digest, and the accepted snapshot are unchanged, and no worker message is sent.

## Test Plan

### Unit and integration tests

- `axes.test.tsx`: unit formatting through the adapter; density-kind enforcement on log axes; slope labels.
- `histogram.test.tsx`: owner bins with overflow counts total the ensemble size; the toggle between bin probability and density; bin width stated; the comparison series class; rejection of a raw-position input.
- `trajectories.test.tsx`: an off-screen count matches a fixture with 37 of 400 tracers outside the viewport; no wrap or reflect option; the drawn-subset flag leaves the result-panel data untouched.
- `eventDiagram.test.tsx`: 45-degree light lines under coherent scaling; the Minkowski 1908 label.
- `legends.test.tsx`: non-color identity; the false-color legend for a 300 nm fixture.
- `analyticLimit.test.tsx`: a $t = 0$ fixture renders a marker with probabilities 1 and 0 and no bar.
- `selection.test.tsx`: every quantity-bearing element carries `data-quantity-id`; setting `data-selected-quantity-id` on the context root highlights exactly the matching SVG marks and no others; a Canvas layer highlights from the prop; the kit imports no module from `src/equations/`.
- `lifecycle.test.tsx`: 50 mount cycles with counted listeners, contexts, and animation frames.
- `representationScale.test.tsx`, against the real primitives and the real runtime: a fixture view omitting each field in turn fails, and the defaults (`factor: 1`, `represents: "none"`, `kind: "none"`) validate; `playbackMultiplier` of 1 renders "true rate" and 25 renders "25 times faster", while a fixture rendering "real time" at 25 fails with the multiplier named; a property test over a fixed seeded list of 200 combinations asserts that setting each field leaves the other four unchanged, so no field is silently derived from another; the box fixture rendered at factors $10^{15}$, $10^{17}$, and $10^{20}$ shows the same displacement value $1.112650\times10^{-17}$ m in its units strip at every factor and three different drawn extents, and a fixture that scales the displayed value by the factor fails; a caption reading "each dot is one particle, drawn at its true size" fails while `represents` is `"none"` and passes only when `represents` names a calibrated quantity id whose legend states the calibration; changing each field through the real command router leaves `runId`, the scientific digest of `snapshotVersion`, the seed, and the draw counter unchanged and produces zero worker messages, using the assertions `am-inst-real-rate-mode-gtez` makes for its toggle; for each of the five consumer views the accessible table and the print output both contain all five facts, and removing a fact from either surface fails the audit with the view id; a fixture drawing a scale bar with no published `RepresentationScale` fails, and one whose bar length disagrees with `realRate.scaleBar` times `spatialMagnification.factor` fails.
- `forbiddenCalls` coverage: the registry's view guard runs over `src/visuals/kit/`.

### End-to-end tests

On the `view-kit` fixture application (`/apps/view-kit/`), through `am-test-e2e-harness-bqmh`:
- drive fixture tracers out of the viewport and assert the ensemble count and the statistics panel are unchanged;
- set the selected quantity on the context root and assert the highlighted marks all carry that `data-quantity-id`;
- the reduced-motion lane shows a static state;
- the 320 px lane has no horizontal overflow;
- the performance lane records frame times with device profile metadata.
- toggle true rate and read the rendered label at both multipliers; open the accessible table by keyboard and read all five scale facts; print the page in the print lane and assert the facts appear.
- on the BM-01 and box lanes, set the magnification to $10^{15}$ and $10^{20}$ by keyboard and assert that the units strip is unchanged while the drawn extent changes and `data-run-id` and `data-snapshot-version` are unchanged. Lanes: keyboard only, 320 px, reduced motion, JavaScript disabled (the static worked example still states its scale facts), and WebKit.

The instrument-specific lanes (for example BM-01 viewport exits) run in the instrument beads and `am-bm-slice-e2e-sbqu`.

### Structured logging and retained evidence

JSONL at `artifacts/test-logs/view-kit/<log-run-id>.jsonl` through `am-test-logging-standard-l3cp`, with `timestamp`, `suite`, `logRunId`, `testId`, `beadId`, `component`, `instrumentId`, `instanceId`, `runId`, `snapshotVersion`, `drawnCount`, `ensembleCount`, `offscreenCount`, `selectedQuantityId`, `frameTimeP95Ms`, `deviceProfile`, `browser`, `viewport`, `reducedMotion`, `jsEnabled`, `outcome`, `durationMs`, `evidence`, and `message`, and in `extra`: `viewId`, `spatialMagnificationFactor`, `spatialMagnificationAppliesTo`, `simulatedElapsedTime`, `playbackMultiplier`, `glyphDrawnPx`, `glyphRepresents`, `quantityNormalizationKind`, `renderedScaleLabel`, `accessibleScaleFactsPresent`, and `printScaleFactsPresent`.

A failing browser test retains a screenshot, a trace, a DOM snapshot, and the console log through the harness evidence recorder, named by the log line's `evidence` field. A failing scale case additionally retains the rendered markup, the accessible-tree snapshot, the print output, and the published `RepresentationScale` under `artifacts/test-logs/view-kit/<log-run-id>/failures/<testId>/`.

## Considerations and Pitfalls

- Keep four distinctions visible: trajectory versus ensemble; position versus displacement; signed coordinate versus radius; mean square versus square of the mean.
- Never compute a physical value or a statistic in a view helper "for convenience."
- A histogram binned by the view from a drawn subset would silently use fewer samples than the result panel. That is why bins come from the owner.
- Highlighting by attribute keeps the kit off the equation component's critical path; do not "simplify" it later by importing the selection store.
- The five fields are independent because conflating any two produces a specific lie. Magnification times playback would make a slowed pulse look slow and small; glyph size folded into magnification would turn a marker into a claimed particle radius; normalization folded into magnification would make a density look like a count.
- "Real time" is a statement about clocks, never about size. A random walk at true rate is still drawn under a microscope's magnification, and the caption must be able to say both things at once.
- A magnified readout is not a magnified scene. The box's $10^{17}$ amplifies one number's drawn representation; nothing about the box is drawn $10^{17}$ times larger. `appliesTo` keeps those apart, and an author who set it to `"scene"` for the box would be claiming something absurd.
- Do not let the five facts colonise the scene. A scale bar, a time legend, and a short caption are the visible budget; the rest belongs to the accessible table, the print view, and the model note.
- A view may not compute a scale from the data it is drawing. The magnification is a declared presentation choice, and inferring it from the range of the values would make the scale change when the physics changes, which is the one thing a scale must never do.

## Dependencies

Blocked by:
- `am-rt-snapshot-store-aft`: snapshot types and identity fields.
- `am-rt-typed-results-mqb`: the status union rendered by analytic-limit and outside-domain presentations.
- `am-design-semantic-color-8vbq`: role colors keyed to quantity ids.
- `am-not-quantity-registry-2f7`: quantity ids, units, and formatting.
- `am-a11y-graph-descriptions-vxe1`: the description providers the primitives implement.

The harness (`am-test-e2e-harness-bqmh`) owns the fixture bundler this bead registers with; it reaches this bead through `am-not-quantity-registry-2f7` and the runtime beads, so no direct edge is needed.

The `RepresentationScale` shape is declared in `am-cm-schemas-experiment-fuu` beside `realRate` and its `scaleBar`, as an additive view-state type, and is never duplicated here. That schema bead reaches this one through `am-rt-typed-results-mqb`, so no direct edge is added. `am-a11y-graph-descriptions-vxe1`, which this bead already depends on, and `am-plat-print-3orn` both render the five facts from this one object instead of each asking views for scale information.

Unblocks:
- `am-bm-01-tracer-ensemble-hdly`, `am-bm-05-random-steps-ntzl`, `am-bm-06-gaussian-spread-982y`.
- `am-inst-predict-mode-ti7m`, `am-inst-interaction-primitives-emwy`, `am-inst-dataset-overlay-ra9r`, `am-inst-real-rate-mode-gtez` (whose "true rate" and "25 times faster" labels render from `playbackMultiplier` instead of from controller state).
- `am-reason-hold-fixed-comparison-xgxw`, `am-reason-what-can-you-infer-pqwb`, `am-disc-shelf-michelson-fizeau-dauq`.

title: Build the HistoricalDataset loader, digitization pipeline, and visually distinct cited overlays
description:
# Build the HistoricalDataset loader, digitization pipeline, and visually distinct cited overlays **Epic:** `am-ep-instruments-8gi` · **Batch:** batch-c · **Priority:** P1 · **Plan sections:** §5.2, §8.1 (stable evaluation and data honesty), §8.2 (synthetic versus real data), §10.7, §11.2 (HistoricalDataset), §13.1, §17.3 (digitize-datasets/) (traceability only) ## Background "Empirical points, historical fitted laws, and theoretical curves stay visibly distinct; the site never manufactures a convincing 1904 measurement by sampling a modern formula and adding noise." Historical measurements are typed `HistoricalDataset` records with citations, or they are absent. This bead builds the shared machinery every dataset and every overlay uses: - the record loader and validator; - the digitization pipeline that turns a cited table or figure into a canonical record with provenance and uncertainty; - the overlay component that shows data beside model curves with dates, citations, and honest styling. It also enforces the knowledge boundary: data published after 1904 never appears on the 1904 shelf, and every overlay says when the measurement was made. A dataset is a miniature critical edition, so a reader must be able to walk from the printed page to the plotted point. The record already captures a source page image and the overlay already offers points plus an accessible table, and nothing joins them. Two further gaps are honesty gaps rather than convenience gaps: nothing records which rows a fit excluded, and nothing distinguishes when a measurement was made, when it was published, and when this site analysed it. A third class of gap is about the cells themselves. A digitized historical table is not a rectangle of numbers: it has blanks the original author left, values the apparatus could only bound, columns the author fitted rather than measured, and a limited set of inferences its provenance actually supports. `am-cm-schemas-experiment-fuu` declares the shape that records all four; this bead is the consumer that makes them mean something on screen and at build time, because a typed bound that is plotted as a point is no safer than an untyped one. Eligibility is decided per publication, not per dataset. Some datasets span the cutoff. Kaufmann's electron deflection results of 1901–1903 are pre-cutoff, but his 1906 analysis is not. Some values appear in more than one publication: the 1899–1900 blackbody measurements appear in a 1900 Berlin report and in a later 1901 *Annalen* paper, and shelf use must cite the earlier report. Two locations have two different jobs. The **canonical record** that the site loads is `content/datasets/.yaml` plus its CSV, under the `HistoricalDataset` schema. The **pipeline directory** `scripts/digitize-datasets//` keeps the provenance, the digitization log, and the validation that produced the canonical record; the site never reads it. A dataset's columns are canonical quantities, so this bead also fixes the order of work between a dataset and the quantity registry: the id exists in the registry before the dataset that uses it lands. One resolver decides that question for every dataset, so no child re-implements the check and no two datasets report a legacy spelling differently. ## Scope In scope: - the `HistoricalDataset` loader and validator in `src/content/datasets/`, reading canonical records only; - conventions and a validation harness for the `scripts/digitize-datasets/` pipeline; - the `DatasetOverlay` view component; - the bounded marker, the refusal of a mean estimator over a bound, and the missing cell in the accessible table; - the `dataset-inference-not-admitted` build failure; - the evidence reveal and its rights-governed crop; - the validation and rendering of declared fits; - the three separately typed dataset dates; - the typed refusal for uncited data; - the per-publication shelf-eligibility rule; - the column-quantity rule that keeps the registry the single source of quantity ids, resolved through the registry's own resolver; - one pipeline fixture. Out of scope: - individual datasets (the children of `am-ep-datasets-fsk`, such as `am-data-perrin-1909-p7ku`); - the schema definition, including the `DataCell` union, the four `columns[].role` values, `allowedInferenceModelIds[]`, `calibrationIds[]`, `sharedInputIds[]`, `digitizationRevision`, the `fits[]` field shape and the three date fields (`am-cm-schemas-experiment-fuu`, which adds them in the same change; this bead owns their validation, rendering and consumer rules and keeps no second schema); - the shared-input registry the provenance pointers name, and the independence claims over it (`am-dataset-independence-registry-3dfb`); - the estimators themselves and their statuses (`am-ref-inference-2w9` and the other reference beads); - the quantity registry itself, its resolver implementation, its legacy-spelling records, and the addition of new ids (`am-not-quantity-registry-2f7`); - the corpus-wide compiler rule `quantity-id-not-exact` (`am-cm-checks-semantic-lic`), which applies the same resolver to every quantity id in content; - the rights policy (`am-src-rights-policy-1dp`, whose vocabulary this bead validates against); - consumer instrument lanes (LQ-08, BM-07, the Fizeau shelf instrument), which run in their own beads. ## Requirements ### Canonical records - Each dataset is `content/datasets/.yaml` with a CSV beside it (`content/datasets/.csv`, or several CSVs for several series), whose path and SHA-256 the YAML records. A dataset split by the source into separately published series may have one record per series (for example `perrin-1909-displacements` and `perrin-1909-sedimentation`). - The CSV carries the values as printed, with printed units, plus canonical conversions in separate columns. - The loader reads only canonical records. A dataset present only as pipeline files fails the build. ### Column quantities come from the registry, through its resolver - Every column names an exact canonical quantity id from `am-not-quantity-registry-2f7`. The loader resolves every column id through that registry's own `resolveQuantityId` (`src/content/quantities/resolveQuantityId.ts`) and never by its own string comparison, so one rule covers every dataset: - `{ok: true, quantity}` admits the column and supplies its dimension and permitted units; - `{ok: false, kind: "legacy-spelling", canonicalIds}` fails the build with the registry's own message from `legacySpellingMessage(id)`, which names the canonical id or ids (for example "use `electricFieldStationary`"); - `{ok: false, kind: "unregistered"}` fails the build naming the dataset, the column, and the id, and never offers a near match. - **Frame-tagged and harmonized ids the dataset children now bind**, with the spellings the registry records as legacy: - `electricFieldStationary` and `magneticFieldStationary` for apparatus fields at rest in Einstein's stationary system (Kaufmann, Bucherer); the unframed `electricField` and `magneticField` are legacy spellings; - `acceleratingPotential` (Ives–Stilwell and paper 3 §10); `acceleratingVoltage` is a legacy spelling; - `speedRatio` for the modern $\beta = v/c$ only; a speed printed in cm/s or m/s binds a speed quantity instead, and the conversion is a derived column; - `chargeToMassRatio`, whose record carries SI, Gaussian, and electromagnetic dimensions, so each column states the unit system its source printed. - A dataset that needs a quantity the registry does not yet hold is blocked on adding that id to the registry, in the registry's own change. The loader never accepts a local alias, a display label, or a near-match spelling in place of a registered id. - The registry now records the ids the dataset beads identified while its seed list was being written (`volumeFraction`, `relativeViscosity`, `relativeSpectralEmission`, `chargeToMassRatio`, `fringeShift`, `dragCoefficient`, and `speedRatio`), so today's children resolve.
