title: Build the searchable /notation page
description:
# Build the searchable /notation page

**Epic:** `am-ep-notation-vrg` · **Batch:** H · **Priority:** P1 · **Plan sections:** §4.7, §15.1, §16.1, §16.2, §16.3 (traceability only)

## Background

Readers who meet $\beta$, $k$, or $L$ in a passage get a scoped callout at that anchor, but many also want the whole map in one place: every symbol Einstein prints, in every paper and section where it holds, beside its modern form and the kind of change that modern form involves. `/notation` is that reference. It must be fully readable without JavaScript, and it must make collisions obvious rather than hiding them behind a single dictionary entry per letter.

Collisions come in three kinds, and the page shows all of them:
- **Cross-paper collisions:** $\beta$ is Wien's constant in paper 1 and the modern $\gamma$ in paper 3.
- **Within-paper collisions:** paper 3's $\varphi$ is an unknown function in §3 and an angle in §§7–8.
- **Cross-toggle collisions:** a modern glyph coincides with a glyph the same paper prints with another meaning.

Renames can also cover a printed group ($R/N \to k_B$) or turn a symbol into an expression ($\beta \to h/k_B$ in paper 1). The page displays those as what they are.

## Scope

In scope: the `/notation` route; static rendering of all concordance entries; filters; search integration; collision views; first-use links; print styles; tests.

Out of scope: the entries themselves (the `not-entries-*` beads); the resolver and validation (`am-not-concordance-model-uag`); the site-wide search index (`am-plat-search-index-snx1`); per-passage callouts (`am-read-perspective-toggle-abd` and the reader faces); static KaTeX rendering (`am-eq-static-katex-7da`).

## Requirements

1. **Static page.** Generated at build time, the page lists every entry grouped by paper and section. Each entry shows:
   - the glyph as printed (static KaTeX), or, for a group rename, the printed group;
   - the meaning, and the modern form (symbol or expression);
   - the dimension and display units, and the frame or reference condition;
   - the operation kind (rename, unit conversion, modernization) with its rule;
   - the collision flags with their kind;
   - a link to the first use in the edition.

   Only glyphs the edition prints are listed as entries. Expected glyphs recorded as not printed in an entries bead's verification log never appear as entries.
   - **Modern-layer glyphs** are listed in a separate, clearly labeled section per paper, built from each file's `modernOnlySymbols[]` (`am-not-concordance-model-uag`): the glyph, the quantity it binds, the records that introduce it, and the note that the paper never prints it. A reader who meets the rapidity glyph in SR-04, or the modern mobility in a Brownian explanation, finds it here without it ever being presented as Einstein's notation.
2. **Collision view.** Selecting a glyph (for example $\beta$ or $\varphi$) shows every entry for that glyph across and within papers side by side, including cross-toggle collisions. Danger collisions are marked in red and also by an icon and a text label, never by color alone. Without JavaScript the same view exists as a static per-glyph section reachable from the glyph index.
3. **Filters.** Paper, section, glyph, modern symbol, operation kind, and collision severity and kind. Filters enhance the page. Without JavaScript the full grouped list and a glyph index of in-page anchors remain usable.
4. **Search.** `am-plat-search-index-snx1` indexes the entries under several keys, so `β`, `beta`, `k viscosity`, `speed of light`, and `R/N` all find the right entries:
   - the glyph, its LaTeX, and its spelled name;
   - the modern symbol and any printed group;
   - the plain-language meaning.
5. **Links.** Each first-use link opens the paper at the anchor in the reading face with the notation callout visible. Each entry has its own stable anchor, using the entry id grammar of `am-cm-id-scheme-8bn` (for example `/notation#lq.beta.wien`); glyph segments are case-sensitive, so `sr.L.…` and `sr.l.…` are distinct anchors.
6. **Accessibility.**
   - Glyphs have authored spoken names ("beta, Wien's constant, light-quanta paper, section 2"), and the page never relies on generated speech of LaTeX.
   - The table is navigable by keyboard and screen reader.
   - There is no page-level horizontal overflow at 320 px; long rows reflow into cards.
7. **Print.** A print stylesheet produces a clean concordance grouped by paper, with collision labels in text.

## Technical Approach

- The App Router page `src/app/notation/page.tsx` is statically generated from compiled concordance records and quantity metadata.
- Client-side filters are progressive enhancement over the static list; search runs through the shared palette and index.
- Static KaTeX rendering is used for glyphs, groups, and modern forms.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The page lists every concordance entry with all required fields and a working first-use link, and lists no unprinted glyph.
- [ ] The collision view shows cross-paper, within-paper, and cross-toggle collisions for a glyph, with danger collisions marked by color and by text.
- [ ] Group and expression renames display the printed group or symbol and the modern form.
- [ ] Filters and search work, and the page remains fully usable with JavaScript disabled.
- [ ] Keyboard, screen-reader, 320 px, and print checks pass.

## Test Plan

### Unit and integration tests
`src/app/notation/notationPage.test.ts`:
- the page data includes every compiled entry;
- every first-use link resolves to an existing anchor;
- every entry anchor is unique, including case-distinct anchors;
- a fixture entry marked as not printed is excluded;
- the collision view data for $\varphi$ includes a within-paper pair from paper 3;
- the search records for the $R/N$ group include the keys `R/N` and `k_B`.

### End-to-end tests
The `scripts/e2e-paper-vertical-slices.ts` notation scenario runs in these lanes: desktop, 320 px touch, keyboard-only, JavaScript disabled, print, and the WebKit lane.
- Search `β` and see Wien's constant (light quanta) and the Lorentz factor (relativity), with the danger marking in text and color.
- Search `k` and see viscosity in the Brownian paper.
- Open the $\varphi$ collision view and see paper 3's §3 function and §§7–8 angle as separate entries.
- Follow a first-use link and land on the anchor with the callout visible.
- With JavaScript disabled, reach the $L$ entries through the glyph index.
- Confirm no page-level horizontal overflow at 320 px, and that print output groups entries by paper with collision labels in text.

### Structured logging
JSON lines per the browser harness to `artifacts/test-logs/notation-page/<log-run-id>.jsonl` with `timestamp`, `suite: "notation-page"`, `logRunId` (this execution of the suite, never an experiment `runId`), `testId`, `beadId` (`am-not-notation-page-2us`), `browser`, `viewport`, `jsEnabled`, `reducedMotion`, `query`, `expectedEntryIds`, `actualEntryIds`, `outcome`, `durationMs`, and `message`. Failures retain a screenshot, trace, DOM snapshot, and console log.

## Considerations and Pitfalls

- Do not collapse entries for the same glyph into one row; the collision is the lesson.
- Keep the page static-first; filtering must never be the only way to find an entry.
- A case-insensitive anchor or search key would merge paper 3's $L$ and $l$; test case distinctness explicitly.

## Dependencies

Blocked by:
- `am-not-entries-brownian-1rq`, `am-not-entries-mass-energy-wq2`, `am-not-entries-relativity-f6e`, `am-not-entries-light-quanta-9cb`: the entries the page lists.
- `am-read-shell-routes-3ua`: App Router shell and anchor conventions.
- `am-plat-search-index-snx1`: the build-time search index.
- `am-test-e2e-harness-bqmh`: the lanes, JSONL logging, and retained failure evidence the end-to-end scenario runs in.

Added as an edge in round 3: `am-eq-static-katex-7da` (static rendering of glyphs, groups, and modern forms).

Unblocks:
- `am-disc-batch-h-exit-audit-r8xq`: the Batch H exit audit checks that no prerequisite dead ends remain, including notation.

title: Build the canonical quantity registry and unit display adapters
description:
# Build the canonical quantity registry and unit display adapters

**Epic:** `am-ep-notation-vrg` · **Batch:** A · **Priority:** P0 · **Plan sections:** §2.2 (equation seams), §4.7, §8, §11.2 (`Quantity`), §11.4, §11.5, §13.4, §22.5 (traceability only)

## Background

The donor's colorized equations looked telemetry up by human label and matched tokens permissively (`variableId.startsWith("var_" + id)`). That is tolerable in a patent museum and wrong in a bilingual scientific edition where one symbol means different things in different sections. Here every live term, control, readout, dataset column, color role, and unit adapter binds to an **exact canonical quantity id**.

The registry also carries the distinctions dimensions cannot settle:
- cyclic versus angular frequency;
- a spectral density versus a total;
- coordinate time versus a proper interval;
- laboratory versus comoving force;
- mean square versus variance;
- measured versus latent position.

Frame and observation identities belong on quantities, not only in captions.

Many beads already name quantities in their text, and every one of them says the final ids come from this registry. Their spellings disagree in places (`speedOfLight` versus `lightSpeed`, `gasConstant` versus `molarGasConstant`, an unframed `electricField` versus `electricFieldStationary`). This bead makes one decision per quantity, records the rejected spellings so nobody reintroduces them, and gives the rest of the graph a stable vocabulary before equation authoring starts. The decisions below settle each family, including the frame rule (the `frame` field is always present, and the frame is also part of the id only for paired quantities), `molarGasConstant` for $R$ (`gasConstant` is a rejected spelling), and the role rule for Avogadro's number: Einstein's printed $N$ is a constant symbol and binds `avogadroConstant`, whose value comes from a printed-historical constant set, while only an inference output that carries an uncertainty binds `avogadroNumberEstimate`.

Electromagnetic quantities need two dimension records. Paper 3 is printed in Gaussian units, where an electric and a magnetic field component share a dimension. In SI they do not, and one cannot be derived from the other by exponent arithmetic alone. The light-quanta paper's §8 numerical check is printed in electromagnetic CGS units, so the quantities it uses carry a third record.

## Scope

In scope:
- `content/quantities/*.yaml`: one record per quantity, grouped by domain files. Constant-set records live in `content/quantities/constant-sets/` and are not loaded as quantities.
- `content/quantities/legacy-spellings.yaml`: spellings that must not become ids, each mapped to its canonical id for use in error messages only.
- `src/content/quantities/registry.ts`: loader, validation, exact lookup.
- `src/content/quantities/resolveQuantityId.ts`: the one exact lookup and legacy-spelling resolution that every quantity-id check uses.
  - `resolveQuantityId(id)` returns `{ok: true, quantity}` for a registry id, `{ok: false, kind: "legacy-spelling", canonicalIds}` for a recorded legacy spelling, or `{ok: false, kind: "unregistered"}`. `legacySpellingMessage(id)` builds the message that names the canonical id or ids (for example "use molarGasConstant").
  - Neither function ever resolves a binding for the author: a legacy spelling is reported, never silently mapped.
  - The compiler rule that applies this lookup to every quantity id referenced anywhere in content (equation terms and numerical bindings, experiment parameters and outputs, dataset columns, constant-set entries, concordance entries, and sonification mappings) is `quantity-id-not-exact`, registered by `am-cm-checks-semantic-lic`, which already depends on this bead and on the compiler core. The registry therefore never waits for the compiler, and one rule reports each bad id once.
- `src/units/adapters.ts`: display adapters and conversion factors.
- `docs/QUANTITY_IDS.md`: the published id list, generated from the records by `scripts/generate-quantity-ids.ts` (id, name, dimension, frame, kind, and every legacy spelling that maps to it), with a freshness test, so the list other beads cite never drifts from the registry. `bun scripts/generate-quantity-ids.ts --check` validates every record and fails on a stale list without writing; it is the registry's quality-gate step.
- The seed registry for all four papers, the companion's needs, and the core instruments.

Out of scope, owned elsewhere:
- constant values and constant sets (`am-ref-constants-xik`);
- dimension arithmetic (`am-cm-dimension-validator-aoz`, which validates every record here);
- the compiler rule `quantity-id-not-exact`, which applies `resolveQuantityId` to every quantity id referenced in content (`am-cm-checks-semantic-lic`);
- the `Quantity` schema and its enums (`am-cm-schemas-argument-llm`);
- notation entries (`am-not-concordance-model-uag` and the entries beads);
- significant-figure policy, sensitivity conversion, and uncertainty display (`am-ver-precision-display-5e5`, which uses this bead's conversion factors), and tolerance comparison (`src/units/tolerance.ts`, owned by `am-ver-tolerance-module-ho90`);
- color values (`am-design-semantic-color-8vbq`);
- the runtime integer-exponent helper `src/units/qty.ts` (extracted later by `am-scaf-extract-runtime-utilities-99y`). Nothing here waits for it and no dependency edge exists in either direction: this bead's records and validators use the exact rational dimensions of `am-cm-dimension-validator-aoz`, and the runtime helper is adopted later where a snapshot needs integer exponents at speed.

## Requirements

### Record fields

Every record uses exactly the `Quantity` field set of `am-cm-schemas-argument-llm`:
- `id`, `name`, `description`;
- `dimension` over the six-dimension basis (length, mass, time, temperature, current, amount), `gaussianDimension` for electromagnetic quantities used in Gaussian-context equations, `emuDimension` for those used in electromagnetic-CGS equations, and `dimensionStatus` with `dimensionNote` for the four state-dependent symbols of paper 2 §2;
- `mathematicalKind`, `densityKind` and `densityPer`, `spectralBasis`, `frequencyKind`, `timeKind`, `frame`, `observation`, `modelArtifact` with `artifactNote`, `statistic`, and `dimensionlessKind`;
- `referenceConditions`, `permittedUnits`, `formatting`, `colorRole` (`energy`, `time-rate`, `space-geometry`, `material`, `statistical`, `field`, `quanta`), and `isConstant`.

Enum values are kebab-case, as that schema defines them.

### Naming rules
- **Frame is a field on every record, and part of the id only for pairs.** Every record carries the `frame` field. Quantities also get distinct, frame-tagged ids in two cases: when conflating them is a known error, or when they appear on opposite sides of a transformation law.
  - The suffixes are `Stationary` (Einstein's system $K$, or $(x, y, z)$ in paper 4), `Moving` ($k$, or $(\xi, \eta, \zeta)$), `RestFrame` or `Rest` (the body's own rest frame), `Comoving` (a particle's instantaneous rest frame), and `Laboratory`.
  - Each suffix must agree with the record's `frame` field, and a test enforces the agreement.
- **Components.** Selecting a vector component ($x$, $y$, $z$) is a term-binding field on the equation, never a separate quantity id.
- **Model variants.** Model-specific evaluations (a Wien, Planck, or classical spectral density) are experiment output ids bound to one quantity (`frequencyEnergyDensity`), never separate quantities.
- **Constants and estimates.** A constant symbol binds a constant quantity, and its values come from constant sets (`molarGasConstant`, `boltzmannConstant`, `avogadroConstant`, `speedOfLight`). Exactness and evidential status belong to each constant-set entry, never to the quantity. Einstein's printed $N$ in papers 1 and 2 therefore binds `avogadroConstant`, and its printed values live in the historical constant sets as `printed-historical` entries ($6.17\times10^{23}$ from Planck's constants in paper 1, $6\times10^{23}$ in paper 2 §5); only `modern-si-2019` holds the exact modern value. An inference output with an uncertainty, such as BM-07's $\widehat N$, is a different quantity and binds `avogadroNumberEstimate`. A historical fixture never borrows modern exactness silently: its values come from its declared constant set, a mixed scenario names the modern entry it uses (as `diffusion-einstein-1905-modern-kb` does), and `am-cm-checks-epistemic-o7n` rejects a historical molecular-count inference that resolves `avogadroConstant` or `boltzmannConstant` from `modern-si-2019`.

### Unit display adapters (`src/units/adapters.ts`)
- **Canonical transport is SI.** Conversion factors are exact rationals where the definition is exact, and each factor records `exactness: exact | conventional`.
- **Exact factors:**
  - m to μm, nm, and cm;
  - the light-second (1 ls = 299 792 458 m);
  - Pa·s to mPa·s, and the poise (1 P = 0.1 Pa·s, so Einstein's printed $1.35\times10^{-2}$ P is $1.35\times10^{-3}$ Pa·s);
  - J to eV (1 eV = 1.602176634×10⁻¹⁹ J, exact in the 2019 SI) and the erg (10⁻⁷ J);
  - Hz to THz; g to kg.
- **Conventional factors** follow the Gaussian–SI and electromagnetic–SI correspondences with $\mu_0 = 4\pi\times10^{-7}$ H/m:
  - statcoulomb: 1 statC ↔ $1/(10c)$ C ≈ 3.3356409520×10⁻¹⁰ C;
  - statvolt: 1 statV ↔ 299.792458 V;
  - statvolt per centimeter: 1 statV/cm ↔ 29 979.2458 V/m;
  - gauss: 1 G ↔ 10⁻⁴ T;
  - abvolt: 1 abV ↔ 10⁻⁸ V; abcoulomb: 1 abC ↔ 10 C; abampere: 1 abA ↔ 10 A. These serve paper 1 §8's check as printed, where $E = 9.6\cdot10^{3}$ abC per gram-equivalent is $9.6\times10^{4}$ C/mol, 0.50 percent below the modern Faraday constant $96\,485.33$ C/mol.

  Since the 2019 SI, $\mu_0$ is measured, so these factors deviate from the exact SI relation by less than one part in 10⁹ (the relative deviation is $\sqrt{\mu_0/(4\pi\times10^{-7}\,\mathrm{H/m})} - 1$). They are recorded as `conventional`, never as exact. Historical calculations often used 300 V per statvolt, and a historical fixture records which factor reproduces a printed number.
- **Temperature display.** Kelvin, and degrees Celsius with the exact affine offset 273.15. The offset applies to temperatures, never to temperature differences or sensitivities.
- **Historical labels.** "Per gram-molecule" is shown as a historical label for mol⁻¹, with a note; the value does not change. "Per gram-equivalent" is shown the same way for the charge of a monovalent ion's gram-equivalent (one gram-equivalent is $1/z$ mole for valence $z$), and "Mikron", as paper 2 prints it, is a historical label for μm.
- **Sensitivities.** The adapters expose exact factors and their inverses. `am-ver-precision-display-5e5` implements sensitivity conversion with them (a derivative per meter becomes a derivative per micrometer by the inverse factor).
- **Locale.** Display uses the locale number primitives of `am-cm-i18n-readiness-b2g`. Display language never changes a stored value.

- BM-02 and BM-04: `partitionForce` (M L T⁻², the osmotic force $\Pi A$ on a partition of area $A$), `hydrostaticHead` (L, $\Pi/(\rho g)$), and `kickDiffusivity` (L² T⁻¹, the diffusivity of BM-04's random kicks, a separate id so the Einstein relation $D = \mu k_BT$ is a result the instrument tests, never an identity of the registry);
- dataset columns: `relativeViscosity` (ratio $\eta^*/\eta$, Bancelin 1911), `relativeSpectralEmission` (ratio on a relative scale whose reference the dataset states, the 1899–1900 spectra), `chargeToMassRatio` (SI T I M⁻¹; Gaussian M^{-1/2} L^{3/2} T⁻¹; electromagnetic M^{-1/2} L^{1/2}; Kaufmann and Bucherer), `fringeShift` (count, real-valued, Fizeau 1851), and `dragCoefficient` (ratio, the measured counterpart of Fresnel's $1 - 1/n^2$, Fizeau 1851); `speedRatio` (ratio $v/c$, the modern $\beta$ of the Kaufmann, Bucherer, and Ives–Stilwell columns and of modern-lens formulas).

**Kinematics:**
- `frameSpeed` (L T⁻¹, signed), `lorentzFactor` (ratio), `rapidity` (hyperbolic angle), `scaleFactorUnknown` (ratio, Einstein's §3 $\varphi(v)$);
- paper 3 §§3 and 5 as printed: `transformationCoefficientA` (ratio, Einstein's §3 $a$, the undetermined function of $v$ before it is fixed), `velocityDirectionAngle` (angle, §5's $\alpha$ between $w$ and the direction of motion), and `speedDeficitFromLight` (L T⁻¹, §5's $\kappa$ and $\lambda$ in $v = V - \kappa$, $w = V - \lambda$). $\kappa$ and $\lambda$ are **speeds, not ratios**: they are the amounts by which each speed falls short of the light speed, so one record with a speed dimension serves both, and the printed inequality $U = V(2V - \kappa - \lambda)/(2V - \kappa - \lambda + \kappa\lambda/V) < V$ dimension-checks. `am-srk-equations-30cq` and `am-not-entries-relativity-f6e` bind this id, and the reviewer confirms the printed form on the facsimile before authoring;
- the modern side-door ansatz of `am-srk-equations-30cq` (labeled modern-layer symbols, never printed notation): `ansatzSpatialScale` (ratio, $a(v)$ in $\xi = a(v)(x - vt)$), `ansatzTimeScale` (ratio, $b(v)$), `ansatzTimeSpaceCoefficient` (T L⁻¹, $d(v)$, so that $d(v)\,x$ is a time), and `ansatzTransverseScale` (ratio, the transverse coefficient). The transverse coefficient is never written $k$ in any layer, because $k$ is Einstein's moving system from §3 on;
- `coordinateTimeStationary`, `coordinateTimeMoving` (T, coordinate); `coordinatePositionStationary`, `coordinatePositionMoving` (L, vector); `auxiliaryGalileanCoordinate` (L, Einstein's §3 $x' = x - vt$); `properTimeElapsed` (T, proper);
- `eventSeparationSpatial` (L), `eventSeparationTemporal` (T), `lengthProper` (L), `lengthMeasuredStationary` (L), `sphereRadius` (L), `lightSphereRadius` (L), `clockOffset` (T);
- `spacetimeIntervalSquared` (L², `frame: not-applicable`, signed): the squared interval between two events, $s^2 = \Delta x^2 - c^2\Delta t^2$, positive for a spacelike separation. **The sign convention is part of the record**, because the opposite convention flips the sign of every classification that reads it. It carries `frame: not-applicable` rather than a frame-tagged pair because every inertial frame computes the same value from its own separations, which is exactly why `am-sr-03-rod-simultaneity-0l5i` displays it beside the frame-relative `simultaneityClassification`: the contrast is the lesson. That bead requested the id as `intervalSquared` and binds the assigned `spacetimeIntervalSquared`; `am-ref-events-yvl` owns the classification computed from it, and the boundary band near zero is the tolerance module's, never this registry's;
- `velocityInMovingFrame` (L T⁻¹, vector, moving system), `velocityComposed` (L T⁻¹, stationary system), `particleVelocity` (L T⁻¹, vector, laboratory).

**Electrodynamics (paper 3):**
- fields: `electricFieldStationary`, `electricFieldMoving` (SI M L T⁻³ I⁻¹; Gaussian M^{1/2} L^{-1/2} T⁻¹); `magneticFieldStationary`, `magneticFieldMoving` (SI M T⁻² I⁻¹; Gaussian M^{1/2} L^{-1/2} T⁻¹); `fieldInvariantE2MinusC2B2` (SI M² L² T⁻⁶ I⁻²; Gaussian $E^2 - B^2$ in M L⁻¹ T⁻²); `fieldInvariantEDotB` (SI M² L T⁻⁵ I⁻²; Gaussian M L⁻¹ T⁻²); `fieldScaleFactorUnknown` (ratio, §6's $\psi(v)$, the common undetermined factor of the transformed fields, a distinct record from §3's `scaleFactorUnknown` because the two are established by different arguments and only later both shown to equal 1);
- sources: `chargeDensityStationary`, `chargeDensityMoving` (SI L⁻³ T I; Gaussian M^{1/2} L^{-3/2} T⁻¹); `currentDensityStationary`, `currentDensityMoving` (SI L⁻² I; Gaussian M^{1/2} L^{-1/2} T⁻²); `chargeVelocityMoving` (L T⁻¹, §9's $u_\xi, u_\eta, u_\zeta$) and `chargeVelocityStationary` (L T⁻¹, the same velocity's components in $K$; both exist because §9 transforms one into the other);
- waves: `waveFrequencyStationary`, `waveFrequencyMoving` (cyclic); `waveAngularFrequencyStationary`, `waveAngularFrequencyMoving` (angular); `directionCosineStationary`, `directionCosineMoving` (ratio, vector); `propagationAngleStationary`, `propagationAngleMoving` (angle); `lightAmplitudeStationary`, `lightAmplitudeMoving` (field dimensions); `lightComplexVolumeStationary`, `lightComplexVolumeMoving` (L³); `lightComplexEnergyStationary`, `lightComplexEnergyMoving` (M L² T⁻²);
- `wavePhase` (dimensionless, `dimensionlessKind: angle`, radians, `frame: not-applicable`): the phase of a plane wave at a named event, $\varphi = \mathbf{k}\cdot\mathbf{x} - \omega t$ in $K$ and $\varphi' = \mathbf{k}'\cdot\mathbf{x}' - \omega' t'$ in $k$. It is **one record, not a frame-tagged pair**: the phase is a scalar with the same value in both frames, and that invariance is the single fact paper 3 §7 derives the Doppler principle and aberration from. `am-sr-09-doppler-aberration-rabd` requested it and binds it for both frames of its `phaseAtEvent` output, so their agreement stays a result its adversarial fixture can break rather than an identity this registry asserts. Its `formatting` records that a phase is compared as printed and never reduced modulo $2\pi$ first, because that would hide a genuine $2\pi$ disagreement, and never compared through its cosine;
- mirror: `dopplerFactor`, `reflectedFrequencyRatio` (ratio); `mirrorSpeed` (L T⁻¹); `interceptedPower` (M L² T⁻³); `radiationPressureMirror` (M L⁻¹ T⁻²); `radiationForce` (M L T⁻²);
- the electron: `electronCharge` (T I; Gaussian M^{1/2} L^{3/2} T⁻¹), `electronMass` (M), `longitudinalMass`, `transverseMassComoving`, `transverseMassLaboratory` (M); `transverseForceComoving`, `transverseForceLaboratory`, `longitudinalForce` (M L T⁻²); `electronWork` and `kineticEnergy` (M L² T⁻²); `acceleratingPotential` (potential dimensions); `radiusCurvatureMagnetic`, `radiusCurvatureElectric` (L). The two §10 deflectability symbols that `am-sre-equations-2g3h` expects (`magneticDeflectability` and `electricDeflectability`, Kaufmann's $A_m$ and $A_e$) are **reserved spellings, not records**: their dimensions follow the definition the paper prints, so `am-sre-equations-2g3h` adds both records here under the extension rule after the printed-glyph check of `am-edn-inventory-relativity-0u9`, each citing the printed definition. If §10 prints no such symbols, neither record is created and the printed deflection ratio stays an expression over `radiusCurvatureMagnetic`, `radiusCurvatureElectric`, and the field components. Nothing is registered from memory.

**Mass–energy:**
- `emittedEnergyRestFrame` (M L² T⁻², object rest frame);
- `bodyEnergyRestBefore`, `bodyEnergyRestAfter` (stationary system, where the body rests); `bodyEnergyMovingBefore`, `bodyEnergyMovingAfter` (moving system);
- `kineticEnergyBefore`, `kineticEnergyAfter`, `kineticEnergyDifference` (moving system); `additiveEnergyConstant` (M L² T⁻², always `symbolic` on the historical route);
- `emissionAngle` (angle);
- `finiteSpeedMassProxy`, `inertialMassDecrease` (the paper's $L/V^2$, the limit of the proxy at $v \to 0$), `massChangeSigned`, `invariantMassSystem` (M);
- the 1906 box: `boxMass` (M), `boxLength` (L), `pulseFlightTime` (T), `pulseMomentum` (M L T⁻¹, the momentum $E/c$ the pulse carries), `recoilSpeed` (L T⁻¹), `centerOfMassShift` (L), `lightMassAssigned` (M).

### Extension by later beads
Later beads add records as ordinary content changes, validated by the same schema and tests with no code change. An entries or equation bead that needs a missing quantity adds it here first. A new spelling that turns out to duplicate an existing quantity goes into `legacy-spellings.yaml`.

## Technical Approach

- YAML records are parsed with `parseStrictYaml` from `am-cm-schemas-source-1en` (reached through `am-cm-schemas-argument-llm`; duplicate keys, custom tags, merge keys, anchors, and non-NFC text are rejected) and validated by the zod schema from `am-cm-schemas-argument-llm`; dimension objects use its rational-exponent shape and are checked by `am-cm-dimension-validator-aoz`. The content compiler later ingests the same files through the same schema, so there is one record format and one parse rule.
- `getQuantity(id)` throws a typed `UnknownQuantityError` for unknown ids; no label, prefix, or case-insensitive lookup exists.
- Unit adapters are pure functions over exact rational factors, with a `convertValue(value, fromUnit, toUnit)` for doubles and `convertExact(decimalString, fromUnit, toUnit)` for exact rational results.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Every seed quantity exists with complete fields, and ids are unique lower camel case.
- [ ] Frame-tag suffixes agree with `frame` fields, and paired quantities are distinct records.
- [ ] Every electromagnetic quantity used by paper 3 or paper 1 §8 has a `gaussianDimension`, and every quantity in paper 1 §8's printed check has an `emuDimension`.
- [ ] The round 2 additions (paper 2 §§1–3, paper 1 §§1 and 5–9, BM-02, BM-04, and the dataset columns) exist with complete fields, and the four state-dependent quantities are `symbolic` only.
- [ ] The round 3 additions exist with complete fields: `pulseMomentum`, `fourierAmplitude`, `fourierPhase`, `longAveragingInterval`, `lagrangeMultiplier`, `speedRatio`, `timeStep`, `gridSpacing`, and `suspensionViscosityCoefficient`; `acceleratingVoltage` and `viscosityRatio` are recorded legacy spellings.
- [ ] The second round 3 pass's additions exist with complete fields: `meanResonatorEnergy`, `meanResonatorEnergyAtFrequency`, `meanQuantumEnergyWien`, `speedOfLightSquared`, `stepInterval`, `stepRms`, `intervalProbability`, `meanDisplacement1d`, `kolmogorovDistance`, `maxProbabilityDifference`, `molesPerVolume`, `transformationCoefficientA`, `velocityDirectionAngle`, `speedDeficitFromLight`, `ansatzSpatialScale`, `ansatzTimeScale`, `ansatzTimeSpaceCoefficient`, `ansatzTransverseScale`, `fieldScaleFactorUnknown`, and `chargeVelocityStationary`; `logFrequencyEnergyDensity` is declared as a representation field and is neither an id nor a legacy spelling; `magneticDeflectability` and `electricDeflectability` are documented as reserved spellings with no record yet.
- [ ] The closing sweep's additions exist with complete fields: `absorbedQuantumRate`, `emittedQuantumRate`, and `ionizationRate`, each recording its counted object beside the dimension, and `entropyVolumeCoefficient`; `entropyCoefficient` is a recorded legacy spelling whose message names both candidates.
- [ ] `wavePhase` exists as one record with complete fields, `dimensionlessKind: angle`, `frame: not-applicable`, and formatting that forbids reduction modulo $2\pi$ before comparison; no frame-tagged pair of phase ids exists.
- [ ] `spacetimeIntervalSquared` exists with complete fields, dimension L² and its stated sign convention, and `intervalSquared` is a recorded legacy spelling whose message names it.
- [ ] `docs/QUANTITY_IDS.md` is generated from the records and fresh, and lists the reserved spellings and the declared representation field names in their own sections so no author invents a second name for either.
- [ ] Unknown ids throw, and no label or prefix lookup exists.
- [ ] No legacy spelling is a registry id; `resolveQuantityId` returns the canonical id or ids for every recorded legacy spelling, and `legacySpellingMessage` names them (the corpus-wide rule that reports them is `quantity-id-not-exact` in `am-cm-checks-semantic-lic`).
- [ ] Every listed unit conversion exists with its exactness, and exact conversions are exact.
- [ ] The records load through the `Quantity` schema and `resolveQuantityId`; the content compiler (`am-cm-compiler-core-oa7`) ingests the same files through its path routing table when it lands, and they are consumable by equations, controls, datasets, constant sets, and colors.
- [ ] `bun scripts/generate-quantity-ids.ts --check` passes on the real records and fails, with a JSONL finding naming the record, on each fixture defect listed under the end-to-end tests.

## Test Plan

### Unit and integration tests
`src/content/quantities/registry.test.ts`:
- **Records:** schema validation for every record; unique ids; lower camel case; frame suffix agreement (`electricFieldMoving` has `frame: moving-system`).
- **Dimensions:**
  - `diffusionCoefficient` is L² T⁻¹, `rmsDisplacement1d` is L, and `diffusionCoefficient` × `elapsedTime` raised to 1/2 is L (rational exponent arithmetic);
  - `frequencyEnergyDensity` (M L⁻¹ T⁻¹), `wavelengthEnergyDensity` (M L⁻² T⁻²), and `logIntervalEnergyDensity` (M L⁻¹ T⁻²) are pairwise distinct;
  - `molarGasConstant` equals `avogadroConstant` × `boltzmannConstant` dimensionally (and equally `avogadroNumberEstimate` × `boltzmannConstant`), and both Avogadro quantities are N⁻¹;
  - `wienConstantBeta` × `frequency` divided by `temperature` is dimensionless;
  - `electricFieldStationary` and `magneticFieldStationary` share a Gaussian dimension and differ in SI dimension;
  - `elementaryCharge` has Gaussian dimension M^{1/2} L^{3/2} T⁻¹;
  - in electromagnetic dimensions, `gramEquivalentCharge` × `stoppingPotentialMagnitude` is an energy per amount (M L² T⁻² N⁻¹), the dimension of `molarGasConstant` × `wienConstantBeta` × `frequency`, and in Gaussian dimensions `elementaryCharge` × `stoppingPotentialMagnitude` is an energy;
  - `osmoticDecayLength` and `kineticDecayLength` are both L and remain distinct records;
  - a state-dependent quantity has no `dimension`, and a fixture binding `configurationIntegral` as an experiment parameter is rejected;
  - `lagrangeMultiplier` × `radiationEnergy` has the dimension of `radiationEntropy` (Θ⁻¹ times M L² T⁻² is M L² T⁻² Θ⁻¹), `fourierAmplitude` shares the SI and Gaussian dimensions of `radiationElectricField`, and `pulseMomentum` × `speedOfLight` is an energy;
  - `diffusionCoefficient` × `timeStep` ÷ (`gridSpacing` × `gridSpacing`) has the dimension of `stabilityRatio`;
  - `stepRms` squared ÷ `stepInterval` has the dimension of `diffusionCoefficient` (the walk's $D = \langle s^2\rangle/(2\tau)$ up to the numerical factor, which the registry never asserts);
  - `speedOfLightSquared` has the dimension of `speedOfLight` squared, and `emittedEnergyRestFrame` ÷ `speedOfLightSquared` has the dimension of `inertialMassDecrease`;
  - `molesPerVolume` × `molarGasConstant` × `temperature` has the dimension of `osmoticPressure`;
  - `entropyVolumeCoefficient` has the dimension of `entropy` (a logarithm is dimensionless) and `entropyVolumeCoefficient` ÷ `universalEntropyConstant` is dimensionless, so a fixture binding a J/K readout to `effectiveIndependentCount` fails the dimension check and a fixture binding the dimensionless count to `entropyVolumeCoefficient` fails likewise;
  - each of the five rate records is T⁻¹, and `absorbedLightEnergy` ÷ (`molarGasConstant` × `wienConstantBeta` × `frequency`) has the dimension of `ionizedGramMolecules` (amount), so §9's printed $j = L/(R\beta\nu)$ cannot be bound to a rate;
  - `ansatzTimeSpaceCoefficient` × `frameSpeed` is dimensionless, and `speedDeficitFromLight` has the dimension of `speedOfLight`, so both sides of §5's printed inequality are speeds;
  - `spacetimeIntervalSquared` has the dimension of `eventSeparationSpatial` squared and of (`speedOfLight` × `eventSeparationTemporal`) squared, so both terms of $s^2 = \Delta x^2 - c^2\Delta t^2$ dimension-check against the record itself, and a fixture binding it to a time or to `observationInterval` fails;
  - `wavePhase` is dimensionless, and `waveAngularFrequencyStationary` × `coordinateTimeStationary` has its dimension, as does `waveAngularFrequencyMoving` × `coordinateTimeMoving`, so a phase term dimension-checks in either frame against one record.
- **Distinctness:** `transverseForceComoving` versus `transverseForceLaboratory`; `properTimeElapsed` versus `coordinateTimeStationary`; `frequency` versus `angularFrequency`; `meanSquareDisplacement1d` versus `displacementVariance1d`; `latentPosition1d` versus `measuredPosition1d`; `avogadroConstant` versus `avogadroNumberEstimate`; `kickDiffusivity` versus `diffusionCoefficient`; `driftFluxComponent` versus `diffusionFluxComponent`; `systemEnergy` versus `microstateEnergy`; `speedRatio` versus `lorentzFactor`; `apparentSpeedRatio` versus both `apparentSpeed` and `speedRatio` (a dimensionless model artifact, a model artifact with a speed dimension, and the physical $v/c$); `timeStep` versus `observationInterval`; `longAveragingInterval` versus `temperature`; `relativeViscosity` versus `suspensionViscosityCoefficient`; `meanResonatorEnergy` versus `meanResonatorEnergyAtFrequency` versus `meanQuantumEnergyWien` versus `quantumEnergy` (all four are energies and none is a spelling of another); `speedOfLightSquared` versus `speedOfLight`; `stepInterval` versus both `timeStep` and `observationInterval`; `intervalProbability` versus `probabilityDensity`; `meanDisplacement1d` versus `rmsDisplacement1d`; `entropyVolumeCoefficient` versus `effectiveIndependentCount` versus `entropy` versus `universalEntropyConstant`; `quantumRate` versus `absorbedQuantumRate` versus `emittedQuantumRate` versus `emissionRate` versus `ionizationRate` (five T⁻¹ records whose descriptions name different counted objects, and `emissionRate` counts electrons); `ionizationRate` versus `ionizedGramMolecules`; `kolmogorovDistance` versus `maxProbabilityDifference`; `scaleFactorUnknown` versus `fieldScaleFactorUnknown`; `chargeVelocityStationary` versus `chargeVelocityMoving`; `molesPerVolume` versus `numberDensity`; `spacetimeIntervalSquared` versus `observationInterval`, `stepInterval`, `longAveragingInterval`, `intervalProbability` and `logIntervalEnergyDensity` (a squared spacetime separation, three times, a probability and a spectral density, and none of them a spelling of another); `wavePhase` versus `fourierPhase` versus `propagationAngleStationary` (three angles that differ in what they are the angle of, and only the first is an invariant).
- **Model artifacts:** `apparentSpeed` and `apparentSpeedRatio` have `modelArtifact: true` and a note.
- **Legacy spellings:** every entry in `legacy-spellings.yaml` is absent from the ids and maps to an existing id; `resolveQuantityId("gasConstant")` returns `legacy-spelling` with `molarGasConstant`, and its message reads "use molarGasConstant"; `avogadroNumber` returns both `avogadroNumberEstimate` and `avogadroConstant`, and its message says which to choose; `decayLength` names both decay lengths; `acceleratingVoltage` names `acceleratingPotential`; the typo `electricFieldStationry` returns `unregistered`, never a near match; `logFrequencyEnergyDensity` returns `unregistered` and is never reported as a legacy spelling of `logIntervalEnergyDensity`, a fixture record that declares it in `representationFields[]` validates, and a fixture declaring a representation field named `frequency` fails `representation-field-shadows-id`; `magneticDeflectability` returns `unregistered` with a message naming `am-sre-equations-2g3h` as the bead that adds the record after the facsimile check; `intervalSquared` returns `legacy-spelling` with `spacetimeIntervalSquared`, and its message reads "use spacetimeIntervalSquared".
- **Unknown ids:** lookup throws the typed error.

`src/content/quantities/quantityIdsDoc.test.ts`: regenerating `docs/QUANTITY_IDS.md` from the records reproduces the committed file byte for byte, and every legacy spelling appears beside its canonical id.

`src/units/adapters.test.ts`:
- exact conversions: `convertExact("1.35e-2", "P", "Pa*s")` is exactly `1.35e-3`; 1 ls is exactly 299 792 458 m; 1 eV is exactly 1.602176634×10⁻¹⁹ J; 1 erg is exactly 10⁻⁷ J;
- conventional conversions: 1 statV is 299.792458 V, 1 G is 10⁻⁴ T, 1 abV is 10⁻⁸ V, and 1 abC is 10 C, all marked `conventional`, never `exact`; the printed 9.6×10³ abC converts to 9.6×10⁴ C;
- `convertValue` returns the double nearest the exact rational product, or its neighbor within one unit in the last place, verified with exact rational arithmetic (no tolerance constant);
- Celsius: the offset applies to 17 °C → 290.15 K but not to a 1 °C difference, which stays 1 K;
- the inverse factor for m to μm is exactly 10⁻⁶.

### End-to-end tests
No browser surface. `scripts/generateQuantityIds.e2e.test.ts` runs `bun scripts/generate-quantity-ids.ts --check` through `Bun.spawn`:
- over the real records, it exits zero and leaves `docs/QUANTITY_IDS.md` byte-identical;
- over committed fixture directories under `src/content/quantities/__fixtures__/`, it exits non-zero with one JSONL finding per defect: a record whose id is a legacy spelling (the finding names the canonical id), a frame suffix that disagrees with `frame`, a dimension with a non-reduced exponent, a duplicate id, and a stale copy of `docs/QUANTITY_IDS.md`;
- the same `--check` step runs in the quality gate chain. Once `am-cm-checks-semantic-lic` lands, its fixture compile proves the corpus-wide rule end to end with a dataset column, a constant-set entry, and an equation term that each use a legacy spelling.

### Structured logging
- Test suites write JSON lines through the shared logger (`am-test-logging-standard-l3cp`) to `artifacts/test-logs/quantities/<log-run-id>.jsonl` with `timestamp`, `suite: "quantities"`, `logRunId`, `testId`, `beadId` (`am-not-quantity-registry-2f7`), `expected`, `actual`, `comparisonKind` (`bitwise` for ids, dimensions, and exact rationals), `outcome`, `durationMs`, `message`, and in `extra`: `quantityId`, `check`, `exactness`, `legacySpelling`, `canonicalIds`.
- `generate-quantity-ids.ts` follows the logger's mapping for scripts: `suite: "generate-quantity-ids"` in `artifacts/test-logs/generate-quantity-ids/<log-run-id>.jsonl`, `testId` naming the record or the freshness step, and the same `extra` fields.
- A failure retains the offending record path and the full zod issue list and, for a stale list, the regenerated text under `artifacts/test-logs/<suite>/<log-run-id>/evidence/<testId>/`.

## Considerations and Pitfalls

- A missing $2\pi$ is invisible to dimensional analysis; the frequency kind is the guard.
- Do not store constant values here; keep values in `am-ref-constants-xik` with era, provenance, and exactness per entry.
- `apparentSpeed` exists only to label the velocity trap as a model artifact; it must never feed a physical claim. `apparentSpeedRatio` is its dimensionless companion and carries the same prohibition: it measures a method, not a motion.
- A Celsius offset applied to a difference or a sensitivity is a silent error; the adapter refuses it.
- "Exactly 299.792458 V" is a convention, not a 2019 SI identity; display it as conventional.
- Renaming ids after equations bind them is expensive; settle names here, before equation authoring.
- Einstein's printed $N$ is not the modern exact value. It binds `avogadroConstant` with its value from a printed-historical constant set; exactness is a property of the `modern-si-2019` entry, never of the quantity, so a historical record cannot inherit it by binding.
- One decay length named for two mechanisms would turn BM-04's central comparison into an identity.
- Five quantities share the dimension T⁻¹ and differ only in what they count. A record that says "rate" without naming the counted object invites LQ-07's emitted quanta and LQ-08's emitted electrons to be bound to one id, which would make a fluorescence yield look like a quantum efficiency.
- A coefficient in entropy units and the dimensionless count it contains are two quantities that differ by $k_B$. Displaying both from one id would let a J/K value and a pure number share a binding, and LQ-06's match would compare a quantity with a count.
- Two compiler rules for one bad id (one here, one in the semantic checks) would report every legacy spelling twice; this bead owns the lookup and the message, and `am-cm-checks-semantic-lic` owns the one rule.
- `speedRatio` is the modern $v/c$ only; binding Einstein's printed $\beta$ to it would reproduce the paper 3 collision inside the data.
- A log-space representation is not a new quantity. `logFrequencyEnergyDensity` carries $\ln u_\nu$ of `frequencyEnergyDensity`; `logIntervalEnergyDensity` is $\nu u_\nu$, a different physical density. Mapping one to the other as a spelling would silently exchange a plotting representation for a spectral quantity, so representation field names are declared data and exempt from the legacy-spelling check.
- Paper 3 §5's $\kappa$ and $\lambda$ are **speeds**, defined by $v = V - \kappa$ and $w = V - \lambda$, not ratios. Registering them as dimensionless would make the printed inequality fail its dimension check and would invite a $v/c$ reading of a quantity measured in cm/s.
- Paper 4 prints the factor $9\cdot10^{20}$ cm² s⁻², not $V$, so `speedOfLightSquared` is a record of its own. Deriving it from the set's `speedOfLight` would replace a printed historical value with a modern one and hide the paper's 0.14 percent rounding.
- A reserved spelling is not a record: it exists so two beads cannot invent two names for one quantity, and `resolveQuantityId` still reports it `unregistered` until the owning bead adds the record with its printed definition.
- "Interval" already names three times, a probability and a spectral density here. A bare `intervalSquared` would drop a squared spacetime separation among them and make the message "use the interval id" useless; the assigned id says which interval it squares, and the sign convention travels with it, since the opposite convention would silently exchange every spacelike classification for a timelike one.
- Phase invariance is a result, not a naming convention. A `wavePhaseStationary` and `wavePhaseMoving` pair would assert that the phase transforms, which is precisely the raised-and-lowered-index confusion SR-09's modern-layer note exists to prevent, and it would turn the equality that instrument tests into a comparison between two different quantities, which no adversarial fixture could then fail.

## Dependencies

Blocked by:
- `am-cm-schemas-argument-llm`: the `Quantity` entity schema, enums, and dimension basis.
- `am-cm-dimension-validator-aoz`: rational dimension arithmetic and Gaussian contexts.

Unblocks: `am-not-concordance-model-uag`, `am-eq-expression-tree-8kl`, `am-cm-checks-semantic-lic`, `am-ref-constants-xik`, `am-ver-precision-display-5e5`, `am-inst-2d-view-kit-u75r`, `am-inst-parameter-controls-cmj9`, `am-design-semantic-color-8vbq`, `am-disc-exercise-checker-i4h2`, `am-inst-registry-dispatcher-66l0`, `am-linked-experiment-groups-5t5s`, `am-sr-03-rod-simultaneity-0l5i`, `am-sr-09-doppler-aberration-rabd`, and `am-bm-08-measurement-bias-h1ye`: the fourteen beads that depend on this one in `br dep list`. All of them bind to exact quantity ids, and `am-cm-checks-semantic-lic` also registers `quantity-id-not-exact` over `resolveQuantityId`.

title: Build the cookieless clarity signal and the weekly About-page summary
description:
# Build the cookieless clarity signal and the weekly About-page summary

**Epic:** `am-ep-platform-8ci` · **Batch:** batch-i · **Priority:** P1 · **Plan sections:** §6.2, §16.6, §17.5, §20 (traceability only)

## Background

The site keeps exactly one analytic: **the clarity signal**. Under every paragraph a one-click "this was clear / this was not" control records **the detail level and anchor**, **aggregated without cookies, identifiers, or IP retention**, because it tells editors exactly where an explanation fails; **its weekly summary is published on the About page**. Free-text answers are never sent anywhere, and there are no third-party scripts, fingerprinting, advertising, or accounts. With small traffic, results are descriptive observations, never claims of statistical power.

A bare boolean does not quite deliver that promise. An editor learns that paragraph `s4-p3` was unclear to eleven readers at Detail 1 and cannot tell whether they were stopped by an undefined symbol, an algebraic move, or too much at once, and those have different fixes. The site already asks the right question in the right place: beside every hard passage, "What is getting in the way?" offers six typed choices, defined once by `am-cm-schemas-argument-llm` and rendered by `am-read-passage-actions-vbe`, and that choice stays on the device. So when a reader has already chosen a category and then votes "not clear", the vote carries that category and nothing else.

A statically generated site needs a small first-party write path and aggregate storage for this, and abuse control must work without retaining anything that identifies a person. Two further constraints shape the design:

- **Publishing a summary never requires a build or a deployment.** Every deployment needs the user's explicit authorization, so an unattended weekly rebuild is not an option. The summary is computed from stored counters of closed weeks and rendered on request or through revalidation.
- **Hosting platforms log requests by default.** For example, function logs can record client addresses. The privacy record states what the platform logs, for how long, and what was configured, and `/about` publishes that disclosure (`am-design-sources-about-zumd` renders it).

`am-launch-readiness-audit-sc9b` lists this bead among the publication-finish deliverables that must exist at launch in their first concrete form.

## Scope

In scope:

- the paragraph control and its repeat-vote record;
- the first-party vote endpoint and the summary endpoint;
- the aggregate storage schema, and the store adapter behind a narrow interface;
- abuse control without retention;
- the closed-week summary, its obstacle breakdown, and its rendering on `/about`;
- the editor view;
- the build-emitted manifest of readable anchors;
- the privacy design record;
- tests proving the privacy properties.

Out of scope, owned elsewhere:

- the About page and its placeholder for this summary (`am-design-sources-about-zumd`);
- the six obstacle kinds themselves, their ids, and the menu that offers them (`am-cm-schemas-argument-llm` owns the enum, `am-read-passage-actions-vbe` renders it); this bead imports the enum and keeps no list of its own;
- comprehension testing (`am-edit-comprehension-rounds-tcgi`);
- the storage layer (`am-plat-local-storage-km8f`);
- the site-wide Content-Security-Policy, headers, and cookie scan (`am-plat-security-f644`);
- the print stylesheet (`am-plat-print-3orn`);
- the reading-only setting (`am-a11y-reading-only-6wwd`);
- the embed route (`am-inst-embed-route-rnyg`).

## Requirements

### The control

- **Buttons.** Two buttons under each readable unit, "This was clear" and "This was not clear", with accessible names that name the paragraph.
- **Feedback.** A short thank-you confirmation is announced once. There are no counts shown to readers, no badges, and no prompts for text.
- **Readable units.** These are the paragraph containers of `am-read-detail-axis-sfc`. The control records the Detail level the reader is viewing (0, 1, or 2). Under a historian's margin record it records that record's anchor.
- **Where it does not appear.**
  - Hidden in print: it is chrome under the policy of `am-plat-print-3orn`.
  - Shown in reading-only mode as one compact text link that expands to the two choices, never as a prominent pair of buttons.
  - Absent from `/embed/*`, as `am-inst-embed-route-rnyg` requires.
  - Absent without JavaScript. Nothing else depends on it.
- **Repeat votes.** The client records voted anchors through `am-plat-local-storage-km8f` under `am:clarity:v1`, as `{ contentRevision, votedAnchors[] }`.
  - The record clears when `contentRevision` changes and is listed in the "Your data on this device" panel.
  - When storage is blocked, an in-memory set covers the page session.
  - This record never leaves the device.

### Payload and endpoint

- **Payload.** Exactly `{ anchor, paper, detail, vote, contentRevision, obstacle? }`, where `detail` is 0, 1, or 2 and `vote` is `"clear"` or `"unclear"`. The body is at most 512 bytes, sent as `Content-Type: application/json`.
- **The obstacle field.**
  - It is one of the six obstacle kinds of "What is getting in the way?", imported from the frozen `OBSTACLE_KIND_IDS` that `am-cm-schemas-argument-llm` exports. This bead declares no second list and no spelling of its own, so a rename in the schema reaches the payload validator and the menu together. (Both owners now spell the ids in lower camel case, and `OBSTACLE_KIND_IDS` excludes the seventh key `exampleFirst`, which is a worked-example reference rather than a menu choice.)
  - **Where the value comes from.** `obstacle` is present only when, in this page session, the reader has already selected a category in the "What is getting in the way?" menu for this anchor, and then votes "This was not clear". The clarity control reads that in-memory selection from the passage-actions component; it never prompts for a category, never adds a step, and never adds a second control. A "This was clear" vote never carries an obstacle. When no category was chosen the field is absent, which is the common case.
  - **Still no free text.** The field is a closed enum. Free-text answers are never sent anywhere; there is no comment box, no preview-and-send flow, and no prompt for text. The category carries the editorial value without the privacy cost a comment would carry, and the rule in AGENTS.md stands unchanged.
- **Endpoint.** `src/app/api/clarity/route.ts`, the site's single App Router root, accepting `POST` only.
  - It validates the anchor and revision against the build-emitted manifest of readable anchors for the deployed `contentRevision`. A vote carrying another revision is rejected as stale.
  - It increments one aggregate counter, keyed by ISO week (UTC), `contentRevision`, `paper`, `anchor`, `detail`, `vote`, and `obstacle` (nullable, after `vote`), and stores nothing else.
  - It never logs or persists client addresses, user agents, request identifiers, or any time finer than the ISO week.
  - It sets no cookies.
- **Responses.**

| Case | Response |
|---|---|
| Accepted vote | `204`, no body |
| Wrong method | `405` |
| Malformed body or wrong content type | `400` |
| Unknown `obstacle`, or `obstacle` sent with `vote: "clear"` | `400`, nothing stored |
| Oversized body | `413` |
| Unknown anchor or stale revision | `422` |
| Rate-limited | `429`, nothing stored |

### Abuse control without retention

- **Rate limit.** An in-memory sliding window, keyed by a salted hash of the client address. The salt is generated at process start, rotated at least daily, held only in memory, and never persisted or logged.
- **Provisional limits.** 60 votes per key per 10 minutes, and one vote per anchor per key per hour. Both values are recorded in the privacy record.
- **Soft limit.** Serverless instances are ephemeral and do not share memory, so this limit is soft. The privacy record says so and explains why that is acceptable: votes are pointers for editors, never decisions, and the summary suppresses small counts.
- **Privacy record.** `docs/decisions/clarity-signal-privacy.md` records:
  - the design and its privacy review;
  - the storage provider;
  - what the hosting platform logs by default, and the configured retention;
  - the suppression minimum for anchor totals and for breakdown cells;
  - the disclosure text that `/about` publishes.

### Storage

- **Provider.** A first-party aggregate store, chosen at implementation with the privacy review.
- **Interface.** `aggregateStore.ts` exposes only `increment(key)` and `readWeek(week)`. The key is the tuple above, and the stored schema holds only aggregate keys and counts.
- **Local implementation.** A local implementation of the same interface serves tests and local development, and passes the same contract tests as the production adapter.
- **Retention.** Retention of old counters is decided and recorded in the privacy record. Nothing is removed without that recorded decision.

### Weekly summary

- **Computation.** A pure function, `src/platform/clarity/weeklySummary.ts`, computes the summary of the most recent closed ISO week from stored counters.
  - For each section and anchor, it counts votes by detail level and vote.
  - It suppresses anchors whose total is below a minimum (provisionally 5, recorded in the privacy record) and reports how many were suppressed.
  - For each anchor that clears the minimum, it reports the obstacle breakdown of its unclear votes. **The same suppression rule applies to the breakdown**, because splitting into six categories makes small cells likely: a breakdown cell below the minimum is reported as "fewer than the minimum" rather than as a count, and the summary says how many cells were suppressed. An anchor whose unclear total clears the minimum while every breakdown cell does not still reports its total.
- **Stability.** New votes land in the current week, so a closed week's counters no longer change. The same counters always give byte-identical output.
- **On `/about`.** A server-rendered or revalidated segment (revalidated at most daily) renders the latest closed-week summary.
  - The text is plain language that emphasizes where explanations were found unclear, with counts and no inferential claims.
  - Publishing needs no build or deployment, and the summary is in the HTML without JavaScript.
  - Before the first closed week with data, `/about` shows an honest empty state.
  - The published disclosure states what the hosting platform logs by default and the configured retention. It must not claim perfect anonymity or unqualified non-retention: the site's own store keeps no identifier, and that is the sentence the page may make.
- **Summary endpoint.** `GET /api/clarity/summary?week=<ISO week>` returns a closed week's summary JSON. The response is cacheable and sets no cookies.
- **Editor view.** `scripts/clarity/editorView.ts` reads the summary endpoint and prints the same summary sorted by the share of "unclear" votes, with counts and anchor links, and adds the top obstacle category per anchor where one survives suppression. It adds no route.
- **What this does not become.** The obstacle category is a pointer for editors, not a measurement. It never ranks readers, never appears to readers as a count, never feeds a score, and never enters the comprehension-round evidence, which remains the only source of statements about understanding. With small traffic the summary stays descriptive.

### No cookies, no third parties

- No page or endpoint sets a cookie.
- The control makes only same-origin requests, within `connect-src 'self'` under `am-plat-security-f644`.

## Technical Approach

- Client and payload: `src/platform/clarity/ClarityControl.tsx` (an island) and `payload.ts` (the schema, importing the obstacle enum rather than redeclaring it).
- Routes: `src/app/api/clarity/route.ts` and `src/app/api/clarity/summary/route.ts`.
- Server modules: `rateLimit.ts`, `aggregateStore.ts` (provider adapter and local implementation), and `weeklySummary.ts`.
- Scripts: `scripts/build-clarity-manifest.ts` (readable anchors per `contentRevision`, run by `bun run build`) and `scripts/clarity/editorView.ts`.
- A summary section component consumed by `/about`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Each vote from the control increments exactly one aggregate counter in the local store, and nothing else is stored, as a schema assertion over every write shows.
- [ ] Unknown anchors, stale revisions, oversized or malformed bodies, and wrong methods are rejected with their status codes; rate limiting works without persisting or logging identifiers.
- [ ] No cookies are set and no third-party requests occur. The control is absent in print, in embeds, and without JavaScript, and compact in reading-only mode.
- [ ] The closed-week summary suppresses low counts, is byte-identical for identical counters, and renders on `/about` without JavaScript and without a new deployment.
- [ ] The privacy design record exists, with its review and the hosting-log disclosure used by `/about`.
- [ ] The payload accepts an optional `obstacle` from the six obstacle kinds, imported from `am-cm-schemas-argument-llm`, with no second list in this bead, proven by a static test.
- [ ] An unknown `obstacle`, or an `obstacle` with `vote: "clear"`, returns `400` and stores nothing.
- [ ] The field is populated only from a category the reader already selected for that anchor in the session; no new prompt, control, or step appears, and a reader who selects nothing sends nothing.
- [ ] The aggregate key carries `obstacle` as a nullable dimension and nothing else is added to storage.
- [ ] The weekly summary reports the obstacle breakdown under the same suppression minimum as anchor totals, and states how many cells were suppressed.
- [ ] The `/about` disclosure names the platform's default logging and configured retention and contains no unqualified anonymity claim, proven by a copy test.
- [ ] Nothing in the reader-facing interface displays obstacle counts.

## Test Plan

### Unit and integration tests

- `src/app/api/clarity/route.test.ts`:
  - validation, plus method, size, and content-type limits;
  - manifest and stale-revision checks;
  - exactly one counter increment per accepted vote;
  - `204` with no body and no `Set-Cookie`.
- `src/platform/clarity/payload.test.ts`: a valid `obstacle` is accepted and each of the six keys round-trips; an invented key returns `400`; `obstacle` with `vote: "clear"` returns `400`; a payload at 512 bytes with `obstacle` present is accepted and one byte over returns `413`; a static test asserts the enum is imported from the schema module and not redeclared here.
- `src/platform/clarity/aggregateStore.contract.test.ts`: the store contract (`increment`, `readWeek`, schema-only keys) runs against the local implementation, with `obstacle` in the key so that two votes differing only in `obstacle` occupy different cells. The same suite runs against the production adapter in a preview environment when its credentials are present, and records `not-available` otherwise.
- `src/platform/clarity/rateLimit.test.ts`:
  - limits within a window, and salt rotation;
  - every argument passed to the store and to the logger contains no client address, user agent, or salt.
- `src/platform/clarity/weeklySummary.test.ts`: aggregation, the suppression threshold, closed-week stability, and deterministic bytes; a fixture week with 12 unclear votes at one anchor split 7 / 3 / 2 across three categories reports the 7 and suppresses the 3 and the 2, naming two suppressed cells; an anchor below the anchor minimum is suppressed entirely.
- `src/platform/clarity/ClarityControl.test.tsx`:
  - accessible names and a single announcement;
  - repeat-vote prevention with working, blocked, and throwing storage;
  - the compact reading-only form;
  - absence under the embed layout;
  - with no category selected the submitted body has no `obstacle` key; with a category selected for this anchor an unclear vote carries it and a clear vote does not; a category selected for a different anchor does not leak into this one; no additional button or prompt is rendered.
- `src/platform/clarity/aboutDisclosure.test.ts`: the published text names the platform's logging and the configured retention; a fixture text containing "we never store any information about you" fails.
- `scripts/build-clarity-manifest.test.ts`: every readable anchor of the fixture corpus appears exactly once per revision.

### End-to-end tests

Through `am-test-e2e-harness-bqmh`, against a local production server with the local store. A preview deployment is used only with the user's explicit authorization.

1. Vote on a fixture paragraph at Detail 1 and at Detail 2, then read the counters.
2. Vote again on the same paragraph, and assert no second request is sent.
3. Assert no `Set-Cookie` in any response, no third-party request, and no request body beyond the payload fields.
4. Open a hard passage, choose "the algebraic move" in the obstacle menu, vote "This was not clear", and assert the network body equals `{anchor, paper, detail, vote, contentRevision, obstacle}` with no other keys and no cookie set; repeat without choosing a category and assert the field is absent; vote "This was clear" after choosing a category and assert no `obstacle` is sent.
5. Assert where the control appears: hidden under print emulation, compact in reading-only mode, absent on the embed route, and absent with JavaScript disabled.
6. Render `/about` with JavaScript disabled, once with a fixture closed-week summary including a suppressed breakdown, and once with the empty state.

Failures retain a screenshot, trace, DOM snapshot, console log, and network log.

### Structured logging

Through the shared logger of `am-test-logging-standard-l3cp`, suite `platform-clarity`, file `artifacts/test-logs/platform-clarity/<log-run-id>.jsonl`.

- Standard fields: `timestamp`, `suite`, `logRunId`, `testId`, `beadId`, `paper`, `anchor`, `outcome`, `durationMs`, `browser`, `viewport`, `jsEnabled`, and `message`.
- In `extra`: `detail`, `vote`, `obstacle`, `obstaclePresent`, `obstacleSuppressed`, `breakdownCellsSuppressed`, `status`, `rejectedReason`, `rateLimited`, `cookiesSet`, `thirdPartyRequests`, `summaryWeek`, `suppressedAnchors`, and `storeImplementation`.
- Logs never include client addresses, user agents, or salts, and a test asserts it.

## Considerations and Pitfalls

- A vote is a pointer for editors, not a measure of learning. Satisfaction and confidence are not understanding.
- Hosting platforms may log requests by default. Configure or document that behavior in the privacy record, and publish the disclosure.
- An automatic weekly rebuild would be an unattended deployment. The summary is computed from stored counters instead.
- Small weekly counts invite over-reading. Suppression and plain descriptive wording are the guard.
- Six categories multiply the cells by six. Without suppression on the breakdown, a rarely read paragraph could produce a cell of one, which is a step toward identifying a person from a public summary. Suppress the breakdown, not just the total.
- Do not add a prompt. The moment the site asks "why was it unclear?" it has added a step to a one-click control, and the control's value is that it costs nothing.
- The category says what the reader thought was in the way, which is not always what was in the way. Treat it as a pointer to a passage worth rereading, never as a diagnosis.
- Keep the enum in one place. A second copy here would drift the first time a category is renamed, and the payload validator and the passage-actions menu would then disagree silently.

## Dependencies

Blocked by:

- `am-read-detail-axis-sfc`: readable units and the Detail level recorded with each vote.
- `am-design-sources-about-zumd`: the page and placeholder that publish the summary and the hosting-log disclosure.
- `am-test-e2e-harness-bqmh`: browser lanes and network assertions.
- `am-plat-local-storage-km8f`: the `am:clarity:v1` namespace for the repeat-vote record, and the data panel that lists it.
- `am-plat-security-f644`: the Content-Security-Policy, the cookie scan, and request bounds.
- `am-a11y-reading-only-6wwd`: the compact reading-only form.
- `am-plat-print-3orn`: hidden as chrome in print.

Unblocks:

- `am-launch-readiness-audit-sc9b`: the clarity signal is a publication-finish deliverable that must exist at launch.

title: Build the later installable offline edition

# Build the later installable offline edition

**Epic:** `am-ep-later-gap` · **Batch:** later · **Priority:** P3 · **Plan sections:** §12.8, §16.3, §18.3, §19.7 (traceability only)

## Background

Readers on unreliable connections, in classrooms without network access, or traveling benefit from an edition that works offline. The plan sequences this carefully.

1. First comes an explicit "save this chapter for offline reading" path: a self-contained HTML chapter with its size stated, "before a service worker exists" (`am-plat-offline-chapter-un8i`).
2. Then "a later installable mode caches a coherent edition manifest, its required assets, and optionally the selected laboratory packages, claiming offline numerical operation only when the exact bundle and initialization path have been tested without a network; prior cached editions stay readable during an update; storage eviction never corrupts the online reader; private notes are never cached into shareable URLs or exports by default."

This edition builds on the release path:

- **Release manifest.** `am-rel-release-manifest-3gna` writes `public/release-manifest.json`, served at `/release-manifest.json`. It holds `releaseId`, `createdAt`, `profile`, source-asset and WASM entries with SHA-256 digests, and a `determinismDigest`.
- **Cache policy.** `am-rel-smoke-rollback-cache-phre` sets the caching rules:
  - HTML, the release manifest, the search index manifest, and route JSON fragments: `Cache-Control: public, max-age=0, must-revalidate`;
  - content-addressed paths, including the search index's hashed shards: immutable;
  - service-worker caching is named as this bead's concern.
- **CSP.** `am-plat-security-f644` owns the Content-Security-Policy that the service worker script runs under.

**Why later:** a service worker can pin readers to stale or broken content and interferes with rollback if done carelessly. The site is static-first, so the online reader must stay excellent without one. The innovation sequence allows offline work to expand only after "the access need is tested and the publication and revision path is reliable."

**Start only when all three hold:**

1. the offline-chapter path has shipped and been used;
2. the release manifest and rollback have proven reliable in real public releases;
3. a tested access need for installable offline reading is recorded in this bead.

The first two are dependencies, and each is a real edge in the Dependencies section below (`am-plat-offline-chapter-un8i` for the first; `am-rel-release-manifest-3gna`, `am-rel-smoke-rollback-cache-phre`, and `am-launch-public-release-5nkq` for the second). The third is a human decision recorded before work begins.

Two failure modes are specific to an installed edition and are covered by requirements 11 to 14. An installed edition is pinned to one `releaseId`, so a shared `?tape=` link made against a different release names identities the installed edition may never have held; requirement 5 covers an instrument with no verified offline bundle, not a link that asks for assets the edition never had. And an offline suite that installs and then calls `context.setOffline(true)` in the same browser context proves very little, because fonts, the worker bundle, the WASM artifact and the route payloads are already resident in that page: the acceptance evidence has to come from a cold start.

## Scope

In scope:

- the service worker;
- the per-release offline edition manifest;
- edition caches keyed by release;
- explicit install and update flows;
- optional laboratory packages;
- eviction handling;
- rollback compatibility;
- offline routing of shared-preset compatibility refusals;
- the kill switch;
- range responses for cached facsimiles;
- tests, including the cold-start lane.

Out of scope, owned elsewhere:

- the offline chapter export (`am-plat-offline-chapter-un8i`);
- the release manifest (`am-rel-release-manifest-3gna`);
- cache headers (`am-rel-smoke-rollback-cache-phre`);
- the Content-Security-Policy (`am-plat-security-f644`);
- the search index format (`am-plat-search-index-snx1`);
- the tape compatibility codes, their reader text, and the new-run repair (`am-inst-permalink-tape-s677` and `am-rt-control-tapes-0gc`);
- background sync and push features, which are not planned.

## Requirements

1. **Explicit install.**
   - The reader chooses "Install this edition for offline reading" in the reader settings.
   - Before downloading, the reader sees the size, computed from the offline edition manifest's byte counts, beside the storage estimate where the browser provides one.
   - The reader selects papers and, optionally, laboratory packages.
   - Nothing installs silently, and no install prompt appears on a first visit.
2. **Per-release edition manifest.** `scripts/build-offline-edition-manifest.ts` writes `public/offline/edition-<releaseId>.json` at build. It lists every cacheable file for each paper with its SHA-256 and byte size, and records the release manifest's `releaseId` and `determinismDigest`, so a service worker can verify every byte it caches.
3. **Coherent edition cache.** Caches are keyed by `releaseId`. An edition holds:
   - the HTML for the chosen paper and section routes and their static Detail fallback pages;
   - route payloads and JSON fragments;
   - fonts and KaTeX assets, and permitted figures;
   - the search index manifest and its shards;
   - a copy of the release manifest.

   An install record `{ releaseId, routes, assets, verifiedAt }` is written only after every entry is fetched and hash-verified. The edition is complete or it is not used: a partial download never serves.
4. **Updates and rollback.**
   - When online, the worker fetches `/release-manifest.json` network-first, at most once per hour during navigation.
   - When the server's `releaseId` differs from the installed one (including an older release after a rollback), the worker downloads that edition completely, verifies every hash, then switches atomically by replacing the install record.
   - The previous edition stays readable until the switch.
   - The worker follows the server's current release even when it is older, so rollback reaches offline readers.
5. **Laboratory packages.**
   - Content-addressed WASM and worker bundles for selected instruments may be cached.
   - An instrument is labeled as working offline only when the edition manifest marks its exact bundle digest `offlineVerified`. That mark requires the bundle and its initialization path to have passed the offline initialization test for this build.
   - Otherwise the instrument shows "This experiment is unavailable on this device" offline, and its static worked example remains.
6. **Eviction safety.**
   - Missing cache entries are detected. Online, the worker falls back to the network; offline, it shows an honest state ("This page was not saved for offline reading") with links to the saved content, without corrupting the reader.
   - Persistent storage is requested only after the reader asks, with an explanation, never by default.
7. **Privacy.**
   - Notes, predictions, and tours stay in local storage and are never written into caches, shareable URLs, or exports by default.
   - Cache keys for navigations use the path only; query strings such as `?tape=` are stripped, so reader state never lands in Cache Storage.
8. **Safety valves.**
   - The worker validates each manifest's schema and refuses an invalid edition.
   - `/offline/control.json`, always fetched network-first, carries `{ minWorkerVersion, disabled }`. When `disabled` is true or the worker is older than `minWorkerVersion`, the worker removes its edition caches and unregisters itself.
   - `/release-manifest.json` is never served stale from the cache while online.
9. **Headers, CSP, and scope.**
   - The worker respects the cache policy of `am-rel-smoke-rollback-cache-phre`: it never serves a must-revalidate resource from cache while online without revalidation. That policy classifies the two search-index files differently, and the worker follows it: `search/index-manifest.json` is revalidated like HTML, while the hashed shards it names are immutable and may be served from cache.
   - It runs under the CSP of `am-plat-security-f644`. The worker script is served with `Cache-Control: no-cache`, and its scope never widens beyond `/`.
   - It does not handle requests under `/embed/*` or `/api/*`. It never intercepts or queues the clarity signal endpoint.
10. **Facsimiles.** pdf.js fetches facsimile PDFs with HTTP range requests. A cached facsimile must answer a range request with a correct `206` response sliced from the cached bytes. Otherwise facsimiles are excluded from the offline edition, and the facsimile face says so when offline.
11. **Offline preset compatibility.** `am-inst-permalink-tape-s677` already defines the behaviour for a mismatch, with seven registered compatibility codes (`tape-version-unsupported`, `tape-model-mismatch`, `tape-artifact-mismatch`, `tape-constant-set-mismatch`, `tape-stream-version-mismatch`, `tape-allocation-mismatch`, `tape-grid-mismatch`) and the rule that a changed artifact or constant set produces different science, so the link is refused and any replay is a new, labeled run. Offline routes into it rather than inventing a second behaviour.
    - When a `?tape=` payload decodes and its identities are compatible with the installed edition, it restores exactly as online.
    - When its `modelVersion`, `artifactDigest`, `constantSetId`, `streamVersion`, `allocationId` or grid identity is absent from or differs from the installed edition, the page shows that bead's registered refusal with both identities in the model note, and offers the two repairs that are honest offline:
      - the permalink bead's registered "Start a new run with the current model", which offline means the installed edition's model: the offline copy names the installed `releaseId` beside it so the reader can see which model that is, and it replays the shared control events as a new identified run under the installed identities, labeled as such, exactly as the permalink bead specifies;
      - "Connect to load the assets this link needs", shown only when the release manifest the worker last fetched lists them, and never presented as a guaranteed fix.
    - The refusal names the installed `releaseId` and the one the link was made against, so the reader can see that the difference is an edition difference and not an error in the link.
    - Nothing is silently migrated, and no number from the installed model is ever displayed under the shared link's identities.
12. **The same rule binds an update.** A reader who declines an update keeps an older edition (requirement 4's atomic switch runs only on acceptance). A link made against the newer release therefore hits requirement 11 rather than triggering an unrequested download.
13. **The cold-start lane.** The "Install and read offline" test is two lanes, and the warm lane alone never satisfies the acceptance criteria.
    - **Warm lane:** install, go offline in the same context, read. It proves the install record and the cache contents.
    - **Cold lane:** install in context A and close it. Open a **new browser context** with network blocked at the transport level for every request, not only `setOffline`, and with a cold HTTP cache and no in-memory module graph. Then, with all requests blocked, exercise in one run:
      - a deep link to a section anchor, not the home page;
      - the German, English and reading faces, and one static Detail fallback page;
      - one prerequisite page reached from a passage action;
      - subset font loading, asserted by computed font family rather than by a request that cannot happen;
      - worker startup and one **accepted** numerical result from an `offlineVerified` bundle, with its `data-execution-label` and `data-snapshot-version`;
      - the show-the-code disclosure for that result, which reads generated source;
      - the search palette, loading its index manifest and at least one hashed shard from cache and answering a query.
    - The lane asserts **zero** network requests over its whole duration, from the network log, and fails on any request rather than on a timeout.
