# Run candidate checks against the deployed, unpromoted assets

**Epic:** `am-ep-release-as1` · **Batch:** batch-c · **Priority:** P1 · **Plan sections:** §12.9,
§16.5, §16.6, §17.4, §18.3 (traceability only)

## Background

A green local build proves that the code compiled; it does not prove that the bytes Vercel serves
are the reviewed texts and pinned kernels the release claims. The plan therefore requires candidate
checks that run **against the deployed, unpromoted deployment**, not the build directory: "Candidate
checks load all four complete paper texts, representative foundation pages, and every instrument
bundle, and include one no-JavaScript source-text check, one real accepted WASM result per numerical
capability, and one deliberate typed refusal." Only after they pass may
`am-rel-verified-deploy-qndt` move any public alias. The donor ran its full source-reader sweep
after promotion; this project moves the full sweep before promotion. The same catalogue runs again,
against the already-deployed candidate, when `--promote` promotes an audited candidate without
rebuilding it.

## Scope

In scope: `scripts/candidate-checks.ts`, its profile-aware check catalogue and registration
interface, its browser and HTTP drivers, logs, and evidence retention.
Out of scope: the release orchestration (`am-rel-verified-deploy-qndt`); the manifest itself
(`am-rel-release-manifest-3gna`), including the kernel-source entries check 16 reads; the
post-promotion smoke test, rollback, and the cache-header check it registers
(`am-rel-smoke-rollback-cache-phre`); the preview leak audit and the in-preparation states it
asserts (`am-rel-preview-policy-cf6g`); the route registry and its canonical, indexing, sitemap and
alternate invariants (`am-route-canonical-registry-57b6`), which check 18 imports rather than
restates; kernel-source extraction and source hashing (`am-inst-show-the-code-4brv`); the general
browser harness (`am-test-e2e-harness-bqmh`), which this bead reuses; the production
Content-Security-Policy (`am-plat-security-f644`); the behavior of the surfaces these checks touch,
which belongs to the paper lanes and to `am-rt-browser-conformance-09i5`.

## Requirements

Invocation: `bun scripts/candidate-checks.ts --deployment <candidate-url> --profile
<scaffold|preview|launch> --manifest-digest <sha256> [--release-record <path>] [--tool-run
<tool-run-id>]`. The release script calls it after the unpromoted deploy, and again in `--promote`
mode, passing the release's `toolRunId` so both evidence sets belong to one release. Exit non-zero
on any failed check.

**Access to protected previews.** HTTP checks go through the protected-preview adapter from
`am-rel-verified-deploy-qndt` (`protectedFetch`: `vercel curl --deployment <url>` where the locked
CLI provides it, otherwise the Deployment Protection bypass header). Browser checks use Vercel's
automation bypass header, with the secret supplied through an environment variable set up by the
user. Never commit or log the secret. Without a bypass, browser checks refuse rather than silently
skipping.

**Check catalogue** (each check has an id, profile applicability, an owner, and JSONL records; other
beads may register checks through `registerCandidateCheck`):
1. **Manifest identity.** Fetch the deployed `/release-manifest.json`; its SHA-256 must equal
`--manifest-digest` (the digest in the candidate's release record), and its `determinismDigest` must
recompute. For every `sourceAssets` and `wasm` entry with a path, fetch the deployed bytes and
compare SHA-256. All entries, not a sample.
2. **Complete paper texts.** For each paper in `publishedPapers` (all four at launch): load
`/papers/<slug>?view=german`, `?view=english`, and `?view=reading`. Every source-block id in the
paper's source manifest appears as an anchor on the German and English faces. Closing date-lines and
acknowledgments render as edited (for example the relativity paper's thanks to M. Besso). No
page-marker furniture (`--- REVIEWED TRANSCRIPTION PAGE`) appears on an edition face. No
unreviewed-draft marker appears on a published face.
3. **No-JavaScript source text.** With JavaScript disabled, load one complete German face and its R1
reading (the mass–energy paper is quickest). The full German text and R1 reading are in the HTML,
the other readings are reachable through real links, and nothing depends on hydration.
4. **Representative foundations.** Load at least one foundation page per authored foundation cluster
present in the release. Each shows its compact explanation, worked example, textual equivalent, and
a return caption.
5. **Every instrument bundle.** For every experiment id in the registry (the 33 core ids at launch):
`/lab/<id>` responds 200; every JavaScript and WASM chunk it requests returns 200; the static worked
example is visible before interaction; `data-execution-label` is present; no uncaught page errors or
console errors outside the documented allowlist. Where the manifest marks an instrument embeddable,
`/embed/lab/<id>` responds 200 with attribution. A catalogue id with no manifest renders the
registry's single in-preparation state (`am-inst-registry-dispatcher-66l0`) and no controls or
numbers; an unknown id fails explicitly and never falls back to another instrument.
6. **One accepted WASM result per numerical capability.** For each capability in the manifest's
`wasm` entries (initially the diffusion slice: `brownian_frames`, `philox_normals`,
`diffusion1d_frames`), drive one instrument that uses it to an accepted snapshot. Assert the public
label "Ideal model, computed with FrankenSim" and `data-execution-label="frankensim"`; the
snapshot's `artifactDigest` equals the manifest digest; and the numerical result matches its golden
scenario under the recorded comparison kind (bitwise for Philox integer outputs, tolerance for
floating-point transforms, verdicts from `src/units/tolerance.ts`).
7. **One deliberate typed refusal.** Request a state the model must refuse, for example
`diffusion1d_frames` with $D\,\Delta t/\Delta x^2 > 0.5$ (refusal code `ftcs-unstable`) or a frame
speed with $|v| \ge c$. Assert that a typed refusal renders with a readable reason and repair
(`data-refusal-code` present and equal to the registered code), the previous accepted snapshot is
preserved and marked as not matching the request, and no `NaN`, `Infinity`, or blown-up field
appears.
8. **Forbidden output.** Published pages contain no raw `$...$` LaTeX, no `NaN`, `Infinity`, or
`undefined` in visible text, and no leaked status enum names. The list of status, execution-outcome,
and refusal-code ids is not hand-written here: it is imported as `statusEnumIds` from
`src/experiments/results/ids.ts`, the frozen export of `am-rt-typed-results-mqb` (the same ids the
voice lint of `am-edit-voice-lint-trmf` mirrors in `content/editorial/voice-rules.yaml`), so a code
registered later is covered without editing this script and no second deny list exists.
9. **Headers.** `.wasm` responses carry `Content-Type: application/wasm`; the
Content-Security-Policy header is present and allows the worker and WASM loading path without broad
`unsafe-eval`. Cache-header assertions are registered by `am-rel-smoke-rollback-cache-phre` as check
`cache-headers`.
10. **Top-level routes.** At launch: `/`, `/papers`, `/sources`, `/about`, `/timeline`,
`/foundations`, `/notation`, `/robots.txt`, `/sitemap.xml` respond 200 with non-trivial bodies.
11. **Profile states.** In `preview`, every unpublished paper shows its honest in-preparation state,
and its draft text is absent from HTML, the search index, and machine-readable exports. The
assertions and the leak audit are registered by `am-rel-preview-policy-cf6g` as the checks
`preview-states` and `preview-leak`; this catalogue runs them and fails the release on either. In
`scaffold`, no paper text is served.
12. **Same-origin only.** While loading every page in checks 2 to 5 and 10, the browser makes no
request to any origin other than the deployment's own (no third-party scripts, fonts, analytics, or
images).

### Release-coherence checks (13 to 19): the evidence and the interface ship together

Checks 1 to 12 prove that the deployed bytes are the reviewed texts and pinned kernels, that every
instrument bundle loads, and that one accepted result and one typed refusal work. They do not touch
six surfaces on which the edition's claims actually rest, each of which can ship broken without
failing anything: the Results face, the notation switch, a rendered accessible embed, the
source-inspection disclosure, the offline chapter, and the site's language alternates. A release
that binds the edition to its kernels but not to the disclosure that claims to show the kernel's
source has bound the wrong half.

Like checks 2 to 12, these derive their targets from compiled content, the manifest, and the route
registry, never from hand lists, and they run against the deployed candidate through the
protected-preview adapter.

13. **The Results face is complete.** For each paper in `publishedPapers`, load
`/papers/<slug>?view=results`. Every result id in that paper's compiled results set appears as an
anchor. Each card renders its printed form, its modern form, its one-sentence statement, and its
`limitation` line. The result **as printed** resolves to the edition text at its anchor rather than
to a retyped string, which is the rule that results are read from the edition; the authored
one-sentence statement and the limitation line are asserted for presence and non-emptiness, because
they are authored rather than transcribed. A card whose live probe is declared in content shows a
probe element; a card declaring none shows its static worked value. Owner:
`am-read-results-face-uzh`.
14. **One historical-to-modern notation switch.** On one reading page per paper, take one displayed
equation whose concordance carries a dangerous collision (paper 3's $\beta$ for the modern $\gamma$;
paper 2's $k$ for viscosity; paper 1's $L$ for the light speed) and render it in both notation
states through the toggle's own URL state, `?notation=modern`, as `am-read-perspective-toggle-abd`
defines it. Assert that the two renderings differ in the expected glyphs, that the semantic term ids
are identical in both, that the concordance entry for that symbol is reachable from the equation,
and that the modern rendering is not produced by string substitution (the term ids must survive).
Assert also that changing notation does not change any displayed value. Owner:
`am-read-perspective-toggle-abd`.
15. **One accessible embed, actually driven.** For one embeddable instrument, load
`/embed/lab/<id>` and reach an accepted snapshot **through the nonvisual path only**: keyboard
focus, typed value entry, and the action contract's equivalent action, with pointer input disabled
for the check rather than merely unused. Assert `data-execution-label`, a non-empty `notModeled`
line, the attribution block with its link back to `/lab/<id>` and to the source passage, `noindex`,
a canonical link to the lab page, no `Set-Cookie`, and no request to any origin other than the
deployment's own. Check 5 already proves embeds respond 200; this proves one is operable without
sight or dragging, which is the claim the site makes about every instrument. Owner:
`am-inst-embed-route-rnyg`.
16. **The source-inspection disclosure matches the release.** For one instrument per numerical owner
kind, one whose accepted result carries the FrankenSim label and one whose result is a host
calculation, open show-the-code and assert three things: the disclosed function's recorded source
hash equals the hash the release manifest lists for that kernel record; every live term's canonical
quantity id appears as an identifier binding in the disclosed source; and the disclosed text is the
deployed text, fetched from the deployment rather than read from the build directory. For the WASM
case this closes the loop that check 6 opens by comparing `artifactDigest`; for the host-calculated
case it is the only check of the claim at all. The hashes are the ones `am-inst-show-the-code-4brv`
pins. This check reads the manifest's kernel-source entries, which the manifest does not carry
today: `am-rel-release-manifest-3gna` adds that section, one entry per pinned kernel record with its
module or crate path, export name and source hash, in the same change as this check. Until that
section exists the check reports `not-available` with that reason, never a pass.
17. **One offline chapter.** Request one generated offline chapter of one published paper, which
`am-plat-offline-chapter-un8i` emits per section at `public/offline/<paper>/<section>-<hash>.html`.
Assert the response is a self-contained document; that it carries the identity block that bead
specifies, including its canonical URL, `contentRevision`, `translationRevision` and the release's
`releaseId`, and that the `releaseId` resolves in `/release-manifest.json`; that every asset it
embeds has publication decision `publish` while `pin-local-only` and `reference-only` assets appear
as citations with their locators; and that the document opens and reads in the harness with the
network blocked. Owner: `am-plat-offline-chapter-un8i`.
18. **Language alternates and canonicals resolve on the deployment.** Collect every `hreflang`
alternate and every `rel=canonical` emitted by the deployed pages, including the German and English
fallback pages. Assert each target returns 200 on this deployment, and that the emitted set matches
the declared policy for the active profile in the route registry of
`am-route-canonical-registry-57b6`, which this check imports. The reciprocity invariant, the
canonical-never-points-at-`noindex` invariant and the sitemap invariants are that bead's audit
rules, run against the built output; this check asserts that the deployed bytes agree with them, so
one rule is never defined twice. A page that emits no alternates records "none emitted" as a result
rather than passing silently, so a regression that drops alternates is visible. A proposed companion
or a future language edition may not appear as an alternate merely because a route exists.
19. **A cached older edition stays identifiable.** In `--promote` mode, fetch one reader page twice,
once accepting cached representations and once with cache revalidation forced, and assert that both
responses carry a visible release identity: the page's own metadata names its `releaseId` and that
value resolves in `/release-manifest.json`. The point is that a reader or a bug report can always
say which edition they saw. Cache header values themselves stay with the `cache-headers` check
registered by `am-rel-smoke-rollback-cache-phre`; this check asserts identity, not headers, so the
two never define the same rule twice.

**Profile applicability.** Checks 13, 14, 16 and 18 run in `preview` and `launch`; 15 and 17 run in
`launch` and in `preview` when the corresponding surface exists in that profile; 19 runs only in
`--promote` mode. In `scaffold` none of them runs, because no paper text is served.

**Flakiness policy.** Transport errors (DNS, connection reset, timeout before first byte) may retry
at most twice with backoff, and each retry is logged. Assertion failures never retry. Checks 13 to
19 are assertion checks, so this policy binds them unchanged, and any failure exits non-zero and
refuses promotion.

## Technical Approach

Reuse the Playwright harness, its DOM readiness contract (`data-reader-root`, `data-ready`,
`data-view`, `data-instance-id`, `data-run-id`, `data-snapshot-version`, `data-input-revision`,
`data-accepted-input-revision`, `data-pending`, `data-execution-label`, `data-refusal-code`), and
the JSONL logger from `am-test-e2e-harness-bqmh`. Derive routes, block ids, experiment ids,
capabilities, golden values, result ids, kernel records, and route policy from compiled content, the
manifest, and the route registry, never from hand lists, so new content is checked automatically.
Run instrument checks with bounded concurrency (at most 4 pages). Check 15 runs on a context with
pointer input disabled, so the driver cannot fall back to a pointer when the keyboard path stalls.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Every check in the catalogue is implemented, profile-aware, and logged, and the registration
interface accepts checks from other beads (`cache-headers`, `preview-states`, `preview-leak`) and
rejects a duplicate id.
- [ ] Checks run against the candidate URL and fetched bytes, never the local build directory.
- [ ] A failing check refuses promotion, and the release script proves it with an injected failure.
- [ ] The accepted-WASM and typed-refusal checks assert the manifest digest and the refusal
semantics, not merely that a page loaded.
- [ ] Check 8 imports `statusEnumIds` from the registries and keeps no second deny list.
- [ ] Retries apply only to transport errors and are logged.
- [ ] The catalogue runs in `--promote` mode against an existing deployment without needing a local
build, and its events carry the release's `toolRunId`.
- [ ] Checks 13 to 19 exist in the catalogue with ids, profile applicability, owners and JSONL
records, and their targets are derived from compiled content, the manifest and the route registry
rather than hand lists.
- [ ] Check 13 fails on a fixture deployment whose results face omits one compiled result id, on one
whose printed form does not resolve to the edition text at its anchor, and on one whose `limitation`
line is empty.
- [ ] Check 14 fails on a fixture whose modern rendering changes a term id, and on one where
switching notation changes a displayed value.
- [ ] Check 15 reaches an accepted snapshot in an embed using keyboard and typed entry only with
pointer input disabled, and fails on a fixture embed that sets a cookie, loads a third-party origin,
or omits the link back.
- [ ] Check 16 fails when a disclosed kernel's source hash differs from the manifest entry, and when
a live term's quantity id is absent from the disclosed source; with no kernel-source section in the
manifest it reports `not-available` with that reason rather than passing vacuously.
- [ ] Check 17 fails when the offline document embeds a non-`publish` asset, omits the `releaseId`,
or carries a `releaseId` that does not resolve in the manifest.
- [ ] Check 18 fails when an alternate or canonical target does not return 200 on the deployment,
and when the emitted set disagrees with the route registry's declared policy for the profile; a page
emitting none records "none emitted" rather than passing.
- [ ] Check 19 fails when a served page carries no resolvable release identity.
- [ ] Every new check appears in the candidate-check catalogue for its declared profiles, and a
duplicate registration is rejected.

## Test Plan

### Unit and integration tests
- `scripts/candidate-checks.test.ts`: route and block-id derivation from fixture content; profile
applicability table; transport-versus-assertion retry classification; forbidden-string detection,
including a page that renders a status id registered after this script was written (proves the list
is imported, not copied); header policy parsing; SHA-256 comparison of fetched fixtures; manifest
digest mismatch refusal; registration of an extra check by id with duplicate-id rejection; a
`--tool-run` value appears in every emitted event. One passing and one failing fixture per check 13
to 19, with the failure message naming the check id, the route, and the specific mismatch.
- `checkCatalogue.test.ts`: the catalogue lists checks 1 to 19 plus the externally registered
`cache-headers`, `preview-states` and `preview-leak`, each with a profile set; a check registered
twice is rejected; a check with no owner is rejected.
- `check16Manifest.test.ts`: a fixture manifest whose kernel entry hash differs from the disclosed
source produces a failure naming the kernel, both hashes, and the instrument; a manifest with no
kernel-source section produces `not-available` naming the missing section rather than passing
vacuously.
- `check18Alternates.test.ts`: a fixture page set whose emitted alternates and canonicals match the
fixture route registry passes; a target returning 404 on the deployment fails; an alternate the
registry does not declare for the profile fails; a canonical the registry declares as pointing at a
`noindex` family fails through the imported invariant rather than a local rule; a page emitting none
records "none emitted".
- Check-logic self-tests on the harness's static fixture server: one correct and one deliberately
broken fixture per check (for example a page with a `frankensim` label but a mismatched artifact
digest, a refusal that renders `NaN`, a page loading a third-party font, an instrument page whose
`data-refusal-code` is absent), each broken fixture failing for its intended reason. Fixture
instruments are registered in the harness's single fixture application registry
(`scripts/e2e/fixtures/fixtureApps.ts`); nothing adds a fixture route, flag, or conditional import
to the application.
- An integration run of the full catalogue against a local production build of the current commit
served by `next start` (no test-only content is compiled into the application).

### End-to-end tests
- Run against a real unpromoted deployment during the first authorized preview or launch candidate
(evidence recorded in the release record). Lanes: desktop Chromium for the full catalogue, plus a
WebKit pass for checks 2, 3, and 6.
- Run `bun scripts/candidate-checks.ts --deployment <candidate> --profile launch --manifest-digest
<sha256>` against an authorized unpromoted candidate and confirm checks 13 to 18 execute and report;
then run the same catalogue in `--promote` mode and confirm check 19 executes.

### Structured logging
- `artifacts/test-logs/candidate-checks/<log-run-id>.jsonl` with `timestamp`, `suite:
"candidate-checks"`, `logRunId`, `toolRunId` (the release this run belongs to), `profile`, `mode`,
`deploymentUrl`, `checkId`, `owner`, `paper`, `route`, `anchor`, `instrumentId`, `capability`,
`artifactDigest`, `executionLabel`, `resultStatus`, `resultId`, `equationId`, `notationState`,
`kernelRecordId`, `kernelSourceHashExpected`, `kernelSourceHashActual`, `embedInteractionPath`
(`keyboard-only`), `offlineAssetDecisions`, `alternateFrom`, `alternateTo`, `releaseIdOnPage`,
`expected`, `actual`, `comparisonKind`, `attempt`, `outcome`, `durationMs`, `browser`, `viewport`,
`jsEnabled`, `message`. Failures retain a screenshot, Playwright trace, DOM snapshot, console log,
network log, the fetched response bodies, and the fetched response headers under
`artifacts/test-logs/candidate-checks/<log-run-id>/evidence/<checkId>/`, copied and never deleted.
The run summary goes into the retained release record.

## Considerations and Pitfalls

- Checking the build directory instead of the deployment is exactly the mistake this bead prevents.
- A loaded WASM file does not earn the FrankenSim label; only an accepted result does, so check 6
must read the snapshot, not the network log.
- Keep the allowlist of console messages small and reviewed; a growing allowlist hides regressions.
- A candidate promoted days after its first checks can be affected by expired bypass secrets or
retention; rerunning the catalogue in `--promote` mode is what catches that.
- A check that another bead registers must still fail this run when it fails; never let a missing
registration silently reduce the catalogue. The catalogue asserts that every check id its profile
requires is registered before it starts.
- Check 15 is worth nothing if the driver falls back to a pointer when the keyboard path stalls.
Disable pointer input for that check rather than preferring the keyboard.
- Check 16 must fetch the disclosure from the deployment. Reading the extracted source from the
build directory would prove only that the build is self-consistent, which is exactly the failure
mode candidate checks exist to catch.
- Check 18 is the easiest to make vacuous: if a page emits no alternates, the check must record
"none emitted" as a result rather than passing silently. It is also the easiest place to duplicate
another owner's rule; import the route registry rather than restating reciprocity here.
- Do not let these checks grow into a second browser acceptance suite. They assert the existence and
coherence of deployed surfaces; the behavior of those surfaces belongs to the paper lanes and to
`am-rt-browser-conformance-09i5`.

## Dependencies

Blocked by:
- `am-rel-release-manifest-3gna`: checks compare deployed bytes against the manifest, and check 16
reads its kernel-source entries.
- `am-test-e2e-harness-bqmh`: the browser driver, lanes, DOM contract, fixture application registry,
and JSONL logging are reused.
- `am-inst-lab-route-f8f3`: check 5 loads `/lab/<id>` and its embed route.
- `am-read-shell-routes-3ua`: checks 2, 3 and 13 load the paper faces and their no-JavaScript HTML.
- `am-found-library-infra-002t`: check 4 loads foundation pages.
- `am-inst-execution-labels-5ywv`: checks 5 and 6 read the execution label and the model note.
- `am-plat-security-f644`: check 9 asserts the Content-Security-Policy and the WASM MIME type.
- `am-rt-typed-results-mqb`: check 8 imports `statusEnumIds`, and check 7 asserts registered refusal
semantics.
- `am-route-canonical-registry-57b6`: check 18 imports the declared canonical, indexing and
alternate policy per profile.
- `am-read-results-face-uzh`: check 13's compiled result set and card layers.
- `am-read-perspective-toggle-abd`: check 14's notation URL state and term-id preservation.
- `am-inst-show-the-code-4brv`: check 16's pinned kernel source hashes and identifier bindings.
- `am-plat-offline-chapter-un8i`: check 17's generated chapter, identity block and rights rule.

Unblocks:
- `am-rel-smoke-rollback-cache-phre`: promotion, smoke testing, and rollback follow passing
candidate checks, and it registers the `cache-headers` check here.

title: Configure the Cloudflare zone for Vercel with explicit authorization
description:
# Configure the Cloudflare zone for Vercel with explicit authorization

**Epic:** `am-ep-release-as1` · **Batch:** batch-i · **Priority:** P1 · **Labels:** human-gate ·
**Plan sections:** §18.1, §18.2 (traceability only)

## Background

The domain `annus-mirabilis.com` is registered at Cloudflare, which also serves authoritative DNS.
The site itself is hosted on Vercel; registration at Cloudflare does not imply hosting there. The
plan fixes the zone configuration: apex and `www` records per Vercel's current instructions,
**DNS-only (grey cloud)** at launch so Vercel manages certificates and edge caching without a second
proxy layer; CAA records when the zone has any; DNSSEC once records are stable; a null MX with SPF
and DMARC reject so nobody can send mail as the domain; and `https://annus-mirabilis.com` canonical
with `www` redirecting consistently. Vercel's own guidance warns that putting an extra proxy in
front complicates caching, routing, and request visibility. Changing DNS and attaching a domain are
outward-facing and the plan does not authorize them, so this is a human-gate bead.

Attaching a domain to a Vercel project makes it serve some deployment of that project, and the
deployment it serves is not necessarily the one intended (for example the newest production
deployment could be an unpromoted candidate). The configuration is therefore verified by asking what
the domain actually serves, and corrected through the verified release script if needed.

**Current state (recorded 2026-09-14, at the user's direct request, outside the verified script).**
`annus-mirabilis.com` and `www.annus-mirabilis.com` are already attached to the Vercel project
`annus-mirabilis` and serve the in-preparation placeholder deployment. The records Vercel supplied
for that project were `CNAME @` and `CNAME www` to `37f4f6b91ca01544.vercel-dns-016.com`, DNS only
(the CLI also suggested `A @ 76.76.21.21`), and the user was adding them in the Cloudflare
dashboard. Those values are history, not instructions: re-read the records Vercel displays for this
project at execution time and use those. CAA, the null MX, SPF, DMARC, DNSSEC, the canonical
redirect, and `docs/RELEASE.md` remain to do, which is why this bead stays open.

## Scope

In scope: confirming both hostnames are attached to the correct Vercel project, the Cloudflare
records, CAA, DNSSEC, mail-spoofing protection, the canonical redirect, verification of what the
hostnames serve, and documentation in `docs/RELEASE.md`.
Out of scope: Vercel project creation (`am-rel-vercel-setup-ituk`); what content is promoted
(`am-rel-preview-policy-cf6g`, `am-launch-public-release-5nkq`); moving hosting to Cloudflare
(`am-rel-cloudflare-hosting-experiment-n7re`).

## Requirements

1. **Authorization.** Obtain the user's explicit written authorization in the current conversation
for (a) any change to which domains are attached to the Vercel project, (b) each Cloudflare zone
change, and (c) any alias move needed to make the domains serve the intended page. Record quotes and
timestamps; an alias move also needs an authorization file for the release script. Authorization for
the 2026-09-14 placeholder does not cover any later change.
2. **Timing and holding page.** The custom domains stay on an honest page at every moment: the
in-preparation placeholder (moved onto the custom domains with `bun
scripts/verified-production-deploy.ts --profile scaffold --promote <scaffold deployment>
--include-custom-domains --authorization <file>`), an authorized preview, or the launch release.
Never expose an unreviewed candidate as if it were the site.
3. **Records from Vercel, not from memory.** For each hostname in the Vercel project, read the exact
records Vercel displays for this project (apex `A` or `CNAME` value or values, and the `www` target)
at execution time. **Use the exact records supplied for the project, not addresses copied from a
plan, a blog, or this bead's history paragraph.**
4. **Cloudflare DNS records:**
   - Apex record with the Vercel-supplied values (`A`, or the `CNAME`-flattened form Vercel
   supplies; `AAAA` only if Vercel instructs), **proxy status DNS only**.
   - `www` `CNAME` to the Vercel-supplied target, **DNS only**.
   - **CAA:** if the zone has any CAA records, add records permitting the certificate authority
   Vercel currently uses (confirm from Vercel's documentation at execution time). If the zone has
   none, adding none leaves every CA permitted.
   - **Email (the domain sends no mail):** null MX `MX 0 .` at the apex (RFC 7505); SPF `TXT "v=spf1
   -all"` at the apex; DMARC `TXT "v=DMARC1; p=reject; sp=reject; adkim=s; aspf=s"` at `_dmarc`. Add
   aggregate-report addresses only if the user asks, because reports route mail about the domain to
   a third party. Optionally, if the user approves, an empty DKIM wildcard `*._domainkey TXT
   "v=DKIM1; p="` as additional parked-domain hardening.
   - **DNSSEC:** enable in Cloudflare once the records are stable and Vercel shows a valid
   configuration with issued certificates. With Cloudflare as registrar the DS record is published
   at the registry automatically; verify it.
5. **What the hostnames serve.** After DNS resolves, run `vercel inspect
https://annus-mirabilis.com` and `vercel inspect https://www.annus-mirabilis.com` and confirm they
serve the intended deployment (the holding page, the preview, or the release). If not, move them
with the verified script under authorization; never with a hand-typed alias command.
6. **Canonical host.** In Vercel's domain settings, make the apex the primary domain and redirect
`www` to it with a permanent redirect. The site's canonical links and `metadataBase` use
`https://annus-mirabilis.com`. HTTP redirects to HTTPS. Record the `Strict-Transport-Security`
header actually served; do not add `preload` or submit the domain to the HSTS preload list without
the user's explicit authorization, because it is hard to reverse.
7. **Proxied mode stays off at launch.** Enabling the orange cloud later requires SSL mode Full
(strict), a review of Vercel's documented caveats, and a new authorization.
8. **Documentation.** `docs/RELEASE.md` records every record (type, name, value, proxy status, TTL),
the date and authorization, which deployment each hostname serves, and the verification output. No
secrets or API tokens are recorded.

## Human Gate

- **Who qualifies:** the user authorizes each change; an agent may execute only afterward, or the
user makes the changes and shares the evidence.
- **Evidence to record** (a `br comments add` on this bead plus `docs/RELEASE.md`): authorization
quotes and timestamps; a Cloudflare record export or screenshot summary; the Vercel domain status
("Valid Configuration") for both hostnames; the `vercel inspect` output for both hostnames; the
verification command outputs below.
- **Agents may prepare:** the record plan table with placeholders for Vercel-supplied values, the
verification script, and the documentation skeleton.
- **Agents never close this bead on their own judgment**, never change a DNS record without the
user's authorization in the current conversation, and never treat this bead, the plan, or an earlier
placeholder as authorization.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Both hostnames are attached to the correct Vercel project under recorded authorization and
serve the intended deployment.
- [ ] Apex and `www` records match Vercel's supplied values with DNS-only proxy status.
- [ ] CAA is correct for the zone's state; null MX, SPF `-all`, and DMARC `p=reject` are published.
- [ ] DNSSEC is enabled and validates.
- [ ] `https://annus-mirabilis.com` is canonical, `www` and HTTP redirect permanently, TLS
certificates cover both names, and no HSTS preload was requested without authorization.
- [ ] `docs/RELEASE.md` records every record, the served deployments, and the verification output.

## Test Plan

### Unit and integration tests
- `scripts/verify-dns.test.ts`: parser tests for `dig` output fixtures (A, CNAME, CAA present and
absent, MX `0 .`, SPF, DMARC, DS present or absent), for `curl -sI` redirect fixtures (301 and 308
accepted as permanent, 302 rejected), for HSTS header fixtures (a `preload` directive flagged), and
for `vercel inspect` fixtures naming a deployment id. A fixture whose apex points at a proxied
Cloudflare address fails with the DNS-only rule named.

### End-to-end tests
- `bun scripts/verify-dns.ts` runs and records: `dig +short A annus-mirabilis.com`; `dig +short
CNAME www.annus-mirabilis.com`; `dig CAA annus-mirabilis.com`; `dig MX annus-mirabilis.com`; `dig
TXT annus-mirabilis.com`; `dig TXT _dmarc.annus-mirabilis.com`; `dig DS annus-mirabilis.com
+dnssec`; `delv annus-mirabilis.com` (validation); `curl -sI http://annus-mirabilis.com`; `curl -sI
https://www.annus-mirabilis.com`; the HSTS header on `https://annus-mirabilis.com`; a TLS
certificate subject check for both names; `vercel inspect` for both hostnames. Each result is
compared with the recorded plan. Web requests use the user agent "OpenAI File Downloader,
XaiImageApiFetch/1.0" per AGENTS.md.
- After attachment, the smoke test in `am-rel-smoke-rollback-cache-phre` passes on both hostnames
with the profile of the page they serve.

### Structured logging
- `artifacts/deploy-logs/dns-<log-run-id>.jsonl` with `timestamp`, `suite: "verify-dns"`,
`logRunId`, `toolRunId` (when the verification runs as part of a release), `check`, `command`,
`expected`, `actual`, `outcome`, `message`. A failing check retains the raw command output beside
the log, copied and never deleted; secrets and tokens are never logged.

## Considerations and Pitfalls

- DNS propagation and certificate issuance take time; verification may need a wait. Never "fix" a
pending certificate by switching to proxied mode.
- A stale CAA record pointing at a different CA silently blocks certificate issuance.
- Enabling DNSSEC with records that later change is safe with Cloudflare-managed DNS, but enabling
it during registrar or nameserver moves is not; do it last.
- The domains already point at the project, so a careless alias move changes what the public sees
immediately. Every move goes through the verified script under its own authorization.
- Never modify DNS for `classic-patents.com` as part of this work.

## Dependencies

Blocked by:
- `am-rel-vercel-setup-ituk`: the domains attach to the project created there, and its recorded
project identity, protection, and retention settings are what the release script checks.

Unblocks:
- `am-launch-readiness-audit-sc9b`: DNS, certificates, redirects, and mail protection on the real
hostnames must be verified before launch, because the launch promotion moves those hostnames.

title: Run a bounded Cloudflare-hosting compatibility experiment only for a concrete reason
description:
# Run a bounded Cloudflare-hosting compatibility experiment only for a concrete reason

**Epic:** `am-ep-later-gap` · **Batch:** later · **Priority:** P4 · **Labels:** deploy, later · **Plan sections:** §18.1, §18.4 (traceability only)

## Background

The domain is registered at Cloudflare, but "registration at Cloudflare does not require hosting on Cloudflare." The plan chooses Vercel hosting through the verified prebuilt candidate-then-promote workflow and says a Cloudflare-hosted alternative is "worth testing only with a concrete cost, operational, or product reason, after a bounded compatibility experiment covering the framework version, static generation, source assets, workers, WASM, and preview releases. The release script, its lock, its prebuilt-artifact validation, and the smoke test are Vercel-shaped; re-validating them is not free, and editorial and instrument work never blocks on a hosting comparison."

The current path is already specified and partly built by other beads, and this experiment compares against it rather than replacing any of it:

- `am-rel-verified-deploy-qndt` owns `scripts/verified-production-deploy.ts`, its exclusive local lock, its dirty-worktree refusal, the prebuilt artifact validation, and the `--skip-domain` candidate deploy.
- `am-rel-candidate-checks-kc7y` owns `bun scripts/candidate-checks.ts --deployment <candidate-url> --profile <scaffold|preview|launch> --manifest-digest <sha256>`, run against the unpromoted candidate.
- `am-rel-smoke-rollback-cache-phre` owns the post-promotion smoke test, the coherent rollback, and the cache and MIME policy (immutable content-addressed paths, must-revalidate HTML and manifests, `application/wasm`).
- `am-rel-release-manifest-3gna` owns the release manifest and its digests.
- `am-plat-security-f644` owns the production Content-Security-Policy and headers, and `am-rt-browser-conformance-09i5` owns the WASM and worker loading assertions under a strict reference policy.
- `am-rel-cloudflare-dns-e3tm` owns the Cloudflare zone, which stays DNS-only (grey cloud) at launch. This experiment never touches it.

**Why later:** it solves no reader problem by itself and would re-open a verified release path. **Start only when all of these hold:**

1. someone records a concrete reason (a measured cost, an operational incident Vercel cannot address, or a product capability that needs it);
2. the Vercel path is complete and proven, including a rollback drill with retained evidence;
3. the user approves the time box in the current conversation;
4. no editorial or instrument work is waiting on the outcome.

## Scope

In scope: a time-boxed compatibility experiment on a non-production Cloudflare preview hostname, and a decision memo.

Out of scope: migrating production; changing DNS for `annus-mirabilis.com` or `www.annus-mirabilis.com`; changing the Vercel project, its aliases, or `vercel.json`; changing the release script, the candidate checks, the smoke test, or the cache policy; adding a Cloudflare adapter to the application's build. Any migration needs a separate plan, its own beads, and its own authorization.

## Requirements

1. **Record the reason and the time box** in `docs/hosting/cloudflare-experiment.md` before starting, with the user's authorization text and its date. A planning document is never authorization.
2. **Isolation.**
   - Use a Cloudflare preview hostname (for example a `pages.dev` or `workers.dev` subdomain) under the user's account, with the user's explicit written authorization in the current conversation for creating it.
   - Production DNS, the Vercel project, its aliases, and the verified release script stay unchanged, and this is verified at the end by comparing the zone records and the alias list with the values recorded before the experiment.
   - No new git branches unless the user asks. Any adapter-specific code lives under a clearly separated directory and never enters the production build graph.
3. **Compatibility matrix.** Each item is `pass`, `fail`, or `unsupported`, with evidence (a log line, a response header dump, or a screenshot) and the exact versions used:
   - the framework version in use and the supported Cloudflare adapter for it, both pinned in the memo;
   - static generation of every route, including all four readings rendered into HTML and the inline pre-paint scripts (theme, Detail, view, perspective) with their hashes under the production Content-Security-Policy;
   - source assets (facsimile PDFs with HTTP range requests, figures, fonts) served with correct headers and the cache classes of `am-rel-smoke-rollback-cache-phre`;
   - dedicated Web Workers and WASM streaming instantiation with `application/wasm` under the site's Content-Security-Policy, re-running the loading assertions of `am-rt-browser-conformance-09i5`;
   - an unpromoted preview release equivalent, so candidate checks can run before promotion, and an equivalent of the `--skip-domain` step;
   - release manifest validation, `bun scripts/candidate-checks.ts --deployment <cloudflare-preview-url> --profile launch --manifest-digest <sha256>`, the smoke test, and a rollback drill adapted to the platform;
   - the exclusive deployment lock and dirty-worktree refusal, or the platform's equivalent, since losing them loses a safety property;
   - performance budgets on the agreed device profiles (`am-gov-decision-device-profiles-1zm`), measured, not estimated.
4. **Comparison.** Correctness, performance, cost, and operations (lock, artifact validation, candidate-then-promote, rollback, log access) against the current Vercel path, with numbers and the measurement conditions (hardware, network profile, cache state, date).
5. **Decision memo.** Recommend keep, revisit later, or plan a migration, with reasons and with the risks of each. The user decides; the agent records the decision and its date.
6. **Stop rules.** When the time box is reached, stop and write the memo with whatever evidence exists, marking untested items as untested. A failed item is recorded, not retried indefinitely. If the experiment would require changing the production path to proceed, stop and ask.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The concrete reason, the time box, and the user's authorization are recorded before work starts.
- [ ] Every matrix item has a result and evidence, or is explicitly marked untested with the reason.
- [ ] Candidate checks and the smoke test ran against the Cloudflare preview, with their log paths recorded.
- [ ] Production hosting, DNS, aliases, `vercel.json`, and the release script are unchanged, shown by a before-and-after comparison.
- [ ] The decision memo exists, and the user's decision and its date are recorded in it.
- [ ] No bead outside this one changed as a result of the experiment.

## Test Plan

### Unit and integration tests

- Any adapter-specific code gets unit tests in its separated directory, and the production build's module graph is asserted not to contain it.
- No existing release test is modified. A test run of the unchanged Vercel path before and after the experiment shows the same results, and both runs' `logRunId` values are recorded in the memo.

### End-to-end tests

- `bun scripts/candidate-checks.ts --deployment <cloudflare-preview-url> --profile launch --manifest-digest <sha256>` (or the profile in force), the smoke test, and the performance budget lane against the preview.
- The browser conformance lane for WASM and worker loading under the production Content-Security-Policy, on Chromium, Firefox, and WebKit.
- A rollback drill on the preview: deploy release A, deploy release B, roll back to A, and assert that HTML, manifests, and content-addressed artifacts remain coherent and that no HTML points at a removed artifact.
- A range-request check on a facsimile PDF (a `206` response with the correct slice), because the facsimile face depends on it.

### Structured logging

One JSON line per matrix item and per check at `artifacts/test-logs/hosting-experiment/<log-run-id>.jsonl`, written through `am-test-logging-standard-l3cp`, with `timestamp`, `suite` (`hosting-experiment`), `logRunId`, `testId`, `beadId`, `platform` (`vercel` or `cloudflare`), `matrixItem`, `check`, `url`, `status`, `header`, `expected`, `actual`, `comparisonKind`, `outcome`, `durationMs`, `deviceProfile`, `browser`, and `message`. Larger artifacts (header dumps, manifest copies, budget reports) go under `artifacts/hosting-experiment/<tool-run-id>/`, and the log lines that point at them carry that `toolRunId`. Failures retain the response headers, the body's first 4 KiB, and the browser console log; nothing is deleted.

## Considerations and Pitfalls

- Adapter support for Next.js features changes often; pin versions in the memo and re-measure rather than citing release notes.
- A green experiment is not a migration plan. Release safety must be re-proven end to end before any switch, and the switch itself is a separate authorized change.
- Proxying the zone (orange cloud) to test a Cloudflare feature would change production behavior; the zone stays DNS-only and untouched.
- Do not let the experiment quietly become a second supported deployment path. Two half-maintained release paths are worse than one proven path.
- Changing DNS, connecting a domain, or deploying anything requires the user's explicit written authorization in the current conversation.

## Dependencies

Blocked by:

- `am-rel-smoke-rollback-cache-phre`: the experiment compares against a complete, proven Vercel release path, including the smoke test, the rollback drill, and the cache and MIME policy it re-tests on the other platform.
- `am-launch-public-release-5nkq`: hosting comparisons happen after the edition is public, so no editorial or instrument work waits on them.
- `am-ep-later-gap` (parent): later work that must never displace the core.

Reached transitively, and named above where this bead consumes them: `am-rel-candidate-checks-kc7y`, `am-rel-verified-deploy-qndt`, `am-rel-release-manifest-3gna`, `am-plat-security-f644`, and `am-gov-decision-device-profiles-1zm`.

Unblocks: none.

title: Define and ship the honest public preview with in-preparation states
description:
# Define and ship the honest public preview with in-preparation states

**Epic:** `am-ep-release-as1` · **Batch:** batch-d · **Priority:** P2 · **Plan sections:** §4.6,
§19.3 (batches C and D), §19.6 (traceability only)

## Background

The Brownian motion paper (the reference slice and first full paper) and the mass–energy paper (the
first complete paper, deliberately short) finish long before the light-quanta and relativity papers.
The plan allows a public preview at that point: "A public preview may contain the complete Brownian
and mass–energy papers while the others are clearly marked in preparation; it must not advertise
four complete interactive editions before they exist. The launch is the complete four-paper site. A
preview is a way to learn from a real reading experience, not permission to redefine the project as
four landing pages and four famous equations." A preview is optional. If it happens, it must be
honest in every surface a visitor or a search engine can reach.

A preview is also the first publication of the site's own English translation and explanatory prose,
so it waits for the user's license and rider decision (`am-gov-decision-license-rights-tps`); the
scaffold placeholder deploy was the only earlier publication, and it contained none of that
material.

## Scope

In scope: the preview policy, the `preview` publication profile rules, in-preparation states for
unpublished papers, sitewide copy and metadata rules, the preview candidate checks and the leak
audit this bead registers in the candidate-check catalogue, and (only with authorization) the
preview release itself.
Out of scope: the launch release (`am-launch-public-release-5nkq`); DNS
(`am-rel-cloudflare-dns-e3tm`, needed only if the preview uses the custom domain); the release
orchestration and profiles (`am-rel-verified-deploy-qndt`); the manifest and the profile contract
(`am-rel-release-manifest-3gna`); the candidate-check harness itself
(`am-rel-candidate-checks-kc7y`); the home page, `/papers`, `/sources`, and `/about` themselves
(`am-design-home-page-0s7s`, `am-design-papers-index-afnu`, `am-design-sources-about-zumd`), whose
preview states this bead specifies and tests.

## Requirements

1. **Eligibility.** A paper is publishable in a preview only when its definition-of-done bead is
closed: `am-dod-brownian-2k4y` and `am-dod-mass-energy-oxh2`. The release manifest's
`publishedPapers` must equal the set of closed definitions of done (`am-rel-release-manifest-3gna`),
and every surface reads the profile through `src/content/publicationProfile.ts`, never through its
own environment read. The license decision must be recorded before any preview is deployed.
2. **One in-preparation wording.** The experiment registry (`am-inst-registry-dispatcher-66l0`)
already renders "This experiment is in preparation" for a catalogue id with no manifest. That exact
sentence and its component are the site's single in-preparation state: the paper, journey,
laboratory, embed, and card states below use the same wording and the same component with a
different subject ("This paper is in preparation", "This journey is in preparation"), so a reader
never meets two phrasings for one state. No page invents "coming soon", a date, or a percentage.
3. **In-preparation state** for each unpublished paper at `/papers/<slug>`: the printed German
title, the working English title, the bibliographic identity (journal, volume, pages, received and
published dates), the single in-preparation sentence, and links to the published papers. No draft
German or English text, no unreviewed readings, no discovery journey, and no instruments presented
as belonging to a finished paper. These pages carry `noindex` and are excluded from the sitemap.
4. **Every surface respects the profile:** home-page invitations for unpublished papers lead to
their in-preparation pages; `/papers` shows the correct availability state for each paper and for
the companion (whose state follows `am-gov-decision-companion-at-launch-936`); the search index
(`am-plat-search-index-snx1` indexes only records the profile publishes), machine-readable exports,
notation page, timeline, connections, tours, and Open Graph images never expose unpublished draft
content or imply completeness; `/lab/[experiment]` and `/embed/lab/[experiment]` routes for
instruments of unpublished papers are either absent or carry the same in-preparation state.
5. **Copy rules.** No page, metadata field, README section, or social card claims "four complete
editions" during the preview. The About page states what the preview contains, that the launch is
the complete four-paper site, and the license under which the published translation and prose may be
reused. Visitor-facing text follows the editorial voice rules (no em dashes, no hype words) and
passes the voice lint (`am-edit-voice-lint-trmf`).
6. **Feedback.** If `am-plat-clarity-signal-nlwr` exists, it may run on published papers. Otherwise
the preview collects no analytics. No accounts, no third-party scripts.
7. **Candidate checks.** This bead registers two checks in the catalogue of
`am-rel-candidate-checks-kc7y` through `registerCandidateCheck`: `preview-states` (every unpublished
paper shows the in-preparation state with the exact wording, `noindex`, and no draft text) and
`preview-leak` (no unpublished sentence id or distinctive German string appears in HTML, the search
index, exports, or Open Graph text sources). In the `preview` profile the catalogue runs the full
checks on each published paper and confirms same-origin loading; a failure of either registered
check refuses promotion.
8. **Shipping the preview is outward-facing.** The deploy runs through `bun
scripts/verified-production-deploy.ts --profile preview --authorization <file>` only with the user's
explicit written authorization in the current conversation, quoted in the authorization file. On the
custom domain it also needs `am-rel-cloudflare-dns-e3tm` and `--include-custom-domains` with an
authorization that names the domains; otherwise it lives on `annus-mirabilis-seven.vercel.app`. No
agent writes that file without the user's actual words, and the preview is never self-authorized
from this bead, the plan, or an earlier release.
9. **Exit.** The preview ends at the launch release or on the user's decision; `docs/RELEASE.md`
records its start, contents, license statement, end, and the release `toolRunId` of the preview
release.

## Human Gate (shipping step only)

The policy, states, and checks are agent work. The public preview deploy requires recorded user
authorization (quote and timestamp, in the authorization file and a bead comment). If the user
declines a preview, close this bead with that decision recorded, keeping the implemented profile
rules for future use. Agents never close this bead by deciding a preview is unnecessary.

## Technical Approach

The in-preparation page is a component rendered from the paper's bibliographic record only, so it
has no access to draft content by construction; it composes the registry's in-preparation state
component rather than copying its string. `scripts/preview-leak-audit.ts` searches the static
output, the search index, exports, and Open Graph images' text sources for sentence ids and
distinctive German strings belonging to unpublished papers, and is the implementation behind the
registered `preview-leak` check. Profile state comes from `src/content/publicationProfile.ts`, which
reads the release manifest at build time under `AM_RELEASE_PROFILE=preview`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `docs/RELEASE.md` contains the preview policy.
- [ ] In-preparation pages exist for every unpublished paper and meet requirements 2 and 3, using
the registry's single wording and component.
- [ ] Profile rules are enforced in the manifest validator and candidate checks, with tests, and the
two registered checks appear in the catalogue.
- [ ] The leak audit of the preview build output finds no unpublished draft text.
- [ ] The license decision is recorded before any preview deploy.
- [ ] Either the preview shipped under recorded authorization with passing candidate checks and
smoke test, or the user's decision not to preview is recorded.

## Test Plan

### Unit and integration tests
- Manifest profile tests: `preview` with an open definition of done fails; unpublished paper content
in the search index fixture fails.
- Page tests for the in-preparation component: required identity fields, `noindex`, no instrument or
journey links, a type-level test that the component's props contain only bibliographic fields, and a
string test asserting the wording comes from the shared in-preparation component of
`am-inst-registry-dispatcher-66l0` rather than a local literal.
- `scripts/preview-leak-audit.test.ts`: in-memory fixture output containing an unpublished sentence
id in the search index fails; containing a distinctive German string from an unpublished paper in an
export fails; a clean fixture passes; the audit reports the file and the matched id.
- Registration test: both checks appear in the candidate-check catalogue for the `preview` profile,
and a duplicate registration is rejected.

### End-to-end tests
- The browser harness in `preview` profile against a local production build: visit home, both
published papers, each in-preparation page, `/papers`, and `/about`; search for a term that only
appears in an unpublished paper (no result); open the sitemap (no in-preparation routes); confirm
the About page's license statement matches `NOTICE.md`; confirm every in-preparation surface renders
the same sentence.

### Structured logging
- `artifacts/test-logs/preview/<log-run-id>.jsonl` with `timestamp`, `suite: "preview"`, `logRunId`,
`toolRunId` (when run as part of a release), `profile`, `paper`, `route`, `check`, `expected`,
`actual`, `outcome`, `message`; failures retain screenshots, DOM snapshots, and the matched leak
context under that run's evidence directory.

## Considerations and Pitfalls

- The search index and JSON exports are the easiest places to leak drafts; audit them, not just the
HTML.
- A preview must never become the project's new definition. Launch still requires all four papers.
- Do not publish a scan in an in-preparation page unless its redistribution rights are recorded.
- Two phrasings for one state is the quiet failure here: a reader who sees "in preparation" on one
page and "coming soon" on another cannot tell whether they mean the same thing.

## Dependencies

Blocked by:
- `am-dod-brownian-2k4y`: only a paper that meets its definition of done may appear in a preview.
- `am-dod-mass-energy-oxh2`: the same rule for the second preview paper.
- `am-rel-smoke-rollback-cache-phre`: a public release needs smoke testing and rollback.
- `am-gov-decision-license-rights-tps`: a preview publishes the translation and prose.
- `am-design-home-page-0s7s`, `am-design-papers-index-afnu`, `am-design-sources-about-zumd`: the
surfaces whose preview states this bead requires and tests.

Unblocks: nothing structurally; it informs `am-launch-public-release-5nkq`. A bead of the separate
iPhone app plan (`am-app-testflight-preview-w1if`) waits on this preview; app work never delays a
website batch.

title: Generate and validate the release manifest
description:
# Generate and validate the release manifest

**Epic:** `am-ep-release-as1` · **Batch:** batch-c · **Priority:** P1 · **Plan sections:** §10.4,
§11.3, §12.4, §18.3, §21 "The publication is maintainable" (traceability only)

## Background

A scientific edition is a bundle of separately versioned things: the site code, the content edition,
pinned facsimile scans, reviewed translations, and WASM kernels built from a pinned FrankenSim
revision. The plan requires a **release manifest** that binds "the site source revision, content
edition version, source-asset hashes, WASM artifact hashes, generated schema version, and test
results." Without it, a rollback can point old HTML at incompatible new WASM, a candidate check
cannot prove it tested the bytes that went live, and nobody can reconstruct which reviewed
translation a reader saw. The content model keeps `contentRevision`, `sourceAssetDigest`,
`translationRevision`, `modelVersion`, and `artifactDigest` separate, and the manifest preserves
that separation rather than collapsing it into one version number or one flattering completeness
score.

The manifest also answers a launch question: is the deployment being promoted the same content that
was audited? Test logs and timestamps legitimately differ between two builds of one commit, so the
manifest carries a **determinism digest** over everything that describes content and artifacts, and
excludes only the run-specific fields.

## Scope

In scope: the manifest schema, the generator run as part of the build, the determinism digest, its
validator, the publication-profile contract and its reader module, the retained release record, and
the rules each publication profile imposes.
Out of scope: running candidate checks (`am-rel-candidate-checks-kc7y`); rollback and cache headers
(`am-rel-smoke-rollback-cache-phre`); building the WASM artifact itself (`am-fs-slim-artifact-0yh`);
the content compiler (`am-cm-compiler-core-oa7`); the coverage computation
(`am-cm-coverage-ledger-0ip`); the in-preparation pages and the preview leak audit
(`am-rel-preview-policy-cf6g`).

## Requirements

**Location.** The generator (`scripts/build-release-manifest.ts`, invoked by `bun run build` after
the content compiler and before `next build`) writes `public/release-manifest.json`, which is listed
in `.gitignore` in the same change, so it is served at `/release-manifest.json` with a short,
revalidating cache and never dirties the tree. A retained copy goes to
`artifacts/releases/<commit>-<tool-run-id>.json`, the release record of
`am-rel-verified-deploy-qndt`, which that script later extends with candidate-check results and
promotion events under the same `toolRunId`. The deployed file is immutable once built and never
contains post-deploy results.

**Profile input and its published contract.** The profile comes from the environment variable
`AM_RELEASE_PROFILE` (`scaffold`, `preview`, or `launch`), set by the release script. When it is
absent, the manifest records `profile: "development"`, which the validator refuses to deploy. This
bead owns that contract and implements it once in `src/content/publicationProfile.ts`, a leaf module
that imports nothing from the release script or the generator and exports:
- `getPublicationProfile()`: parses the environment variable, returns `development` when absent, and
throws on an unknown value;
- `getPublishedPapers(profile)`: in `development`, every paper with compiled content; otherwise the
`publishedPapers` array of `public/release-manifest.json`, refusing when the manifest is absent;
- `PUBLICATION_PROFILES`, the ordered enum, for exhaustive switches.

Four Batch B design beads read this contract before this Batch C bead closes:
`am-design-papers-index-afnu`, `am-design-home-page-0s7s`, `am-design-sources-about-zumd`, and
`am-design-og-images-pwok`. That consumption is deliberately non-blocking: putting the Batch B
`/papers` page behind the release script would invert the batches, so those pages state the contract
they read, test their preview states with fixture manifests, and import this module rather than
reading `process.env.AM_RELEASE_PROFILE` in each page. The real states are verified before anything
ships, because `am-rel-preview-policy-cf6g` depends on all three page beads and reaches this bead
through `am-rel-smoke-rollback-cache-phre` and `am-rel-candidate-checks-kc7y`, and no preview or
launch profile can be deployed without a valid manifest.

**Fields** (zod schema `src/content/releaseManifest.ts`, `schemaVersion` starting at 1):
- `releaseId`, `createdAt` (ISO), `profile`.
- `site`: `commit` (full hash), `branch` (`main`), `treeClean: true`, `toolchain` (Bun, Node.js,
Next.js, TypeScript versions).
- `content`: `editionVersion`; per paper (`light-quanta`, `brownian-motion`, `special-relativity`,
`mass-energy`, and the companion `molecular-dimensions` when admitted): `contentRevision`,
`translationRevision`, the published faces, and completeness dimensions reported **separately** from
the coverage ledger (source manifest coverage, translation review state, argument coverage,
instrument availability, accessibility equivalence, numerical validation). `publishedPapers` lists
the papers the profile publishes.
- `sourceAssets`: for every facsimile, ledger, figure crop, and dataset file the site serves or
cites: `key`, `path` (or `null` when not redistributed), `sha256` (lowercase hex), `rightsStatus`,
`redistributable` flag, and the provenance receipt path.
- `wasm`: for every content-addressed artifact listed in `public/wasm/manifest.json`: `path`,
`sha256`, `capabilities`, `exports`, `modelVersion`, the FrankenSim commit, the Rust toolchain (for
example `nightly-2026-07-06`), and the generated glue version.
- `schema`: generated content schema version and compiler version.
- `donors`: the classic-patents.com and FrankenSim commits pinned in `docs/DONOR_AUDIT.md` and
`docs/FRANKENSIM_BINDING.md`.
- `kernels`: for every function `am-inst-show-the-code-4brv` extracts and publishes as a
computation-source record: `recordId`, the module path (or crate and file for Rust), the function
name, the `displayRole`, and `sourceSha256`, the pinned lowercase hash of the extracted source text.
Entries are sorted by `recordId`. Only records whose `displayRole` is `executing-source` or
`reference-implementation` are listed, because a `pseudocode` or `derivation` listing carries no
source hash to bind. For WASM the claim that this is the code that produced your number is already
enforced, because a candidate check compares a snapshot's `artifactDigest` with the `wasm` section.
The audited TypeScript reference evaluators own most closed-form instruments and had nothing binding
their disclosed source to the release, so a stale or mismatched disclosure could ship undetected.
- `tests`: for each pre-deploy suite (the gate steps the profile required): `stepId`, `command`,
`result`, counts, `logRunId`, `logPath`, and the SHA-256 of the JSONL log.
- `determinismDigest`: SHA-256 of the canonical JSON (sorted keys, sorted arrays, no insignificant
whitespace) of the whole manifest except `releaseId`, `createdAt`, `tests`, `site.toolchain`, and
`determinismDigest` itself. `kernels` is inside that digest, so a changed disclosed source changes
the release identity rather than passing as the same release.

**Publication configuration.** `content/papers/publication.yaml` records the companion's status
(`admitted` or `deferred`) with the decision id from `docs/DECISIONS.md`
(`am-gov-decision-companion-at-launch-936`); the generator lists `molecular-dimensions` only when it
is `admitted`.

**Validation** (`scripts/validate-release-manifest.ts`, called by `am-rel-verified-deploy-qndt` on
the fresh artifact and by `--promote` on the deployed file):
- The schema validates; `profile` is not `development`; `commit` equals `HEAD`; the tree was clean.
- `determinismDigest` recomputes to the recorded value.
- Every `sourceAssets` and `wasm` entry with a path exists in the output and its hash matches the
bytes on disk.
- Every WASM file the instrument registry or HTML references is listed, with matching digest; no
listed artifact is unreferenced without a declared reason.
- Every `kernels` entry's module or crate path exists in the output and its `sourceSha256` matches
the extracted source text on disk; every published computation-source record appears exactly once;
and the section is present and non-empty whenever the profile publishes a paper, so it can never
pass vacuously.
- Every test entry is `passed`; any other result refuses the release.
- Profile rules: `scaffold` lists no published papers; `preview` lists exactly the papers whose
definition-of-done beads are closed (read through `br show <id> --json` in the release environment)
and marks the others "in preparation" (`am-rel-preview-policy-cf6g`); `launch` requires all four
papers with every completeness dimension satisfied. `molecular-dimensions` appears only when the
publication configuration says `admitted` and the named decision id exists in `docs/DECISIONS.md`.
- A manifest may never state a completeness dimension that the source manifest or coverage ledger
does not support, and never aggregates dimensions into a single percentage.

## Technical Approach

Hash files with streaming SHA-256; read source and translation revisions from compiled content
records; read coverage dimensions from the coverage ledger's compiled output; read WASM identities
from `public/wasm/manifest.json` and `docs/FRANKENSIM_BINDING.md`; read test results from JSONL logs
written under AGENTS.md "Testing and Logging Standards". Keep generation deterministic: sorted keys
and arrays, no wall-clock values except `createdAt`, so two builds of one commit and profile differ
only in `releaseId`, `createdAt`, `tests`, and `site.toolchain`, and share one `determinismDigest`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The schema and generator exist and produce a manifest during `bun run build`, written to an
ignored path.
- [ ] The validator rejects each tamper case in the Test Plan with a specific message.
- [ ] Profile rules, including the companion rule, are enforced by tests.
- [ ] The retained release record exists for every build the release script runs and is named by the
release's `toolRunId`.
- [ ] Rebuilding the same commit and profile yields the same `determinismDigest`.
- [ ] `src/content/publicationProfile.ts` is the only implementation of the profile contract; a
static test fails if any page or script reads `process.env.AM_RELEASE_PROFILE` directly.
- [ ] The manifest carries a `kernels` section binding every published computation-source record to
its module path, function name, and pinned source hash; that section is inside the
`determinismDigest`; and the validator refuses a release whose `kernels` section is absent or empty
while the profile publishes a paper.

## Test Plan

### Unit and integration tests
- `scripts/build-release-manifest.test.ts` on a fixture output tree (in-memory file listing and
bytes): correct hashes; sorted, deterministic output; separate completeness dimensions; `profile:
"development"` when the environment variable is absent; two generations with different `createdAt`,
`releaseId`, and test logs produce the same `determinismDigest`, while a one-byte change in a
facsimile changes it, as does a one-character change in an extracted kernel source.
- `src/content/publicationProfile.test.ts`: the four profiles parse; an unknown value throws with
the allowed values in the message; `development` resolves published papers from compiled fixture
content; `preview` resolves them from a fixture manifest and refuses when the manifest is absent.
- `scripts/validate-release-manifest.test.ts` tamper cases: one flipped byte in a facsimile, a
missing WASM file, an HTML reference to an unlisted artifact, a failing test entry, a commit
mismatch, a dirty tree flag, a `development` profile, an edited field that no longer matches
`determinismDigest`, `preview` listing a paper whose definition of done is open (fixture `br`
output), `launch` missing a paper, `molecular-dimensions` listed while the publication configuration
says `deferred`, a completeness claim unsupported by the coverage ledger, a single aggregated
percentage field, a `kernels` entry whose `sourceSha256` differs from the extracted source on disk,
a published computation-source record missing from `kernels`, and an absent or empty `kernels`
section while the profile publishes a paper.

### End-to-end tests
- In CI, run `bun run build` on the current commit, then the validator against the Next.js output
with `AM_RELEASE_PROFILE=scaffold`; assert pass and log the manifest digest and determinism digest.
- Build the same commit twice in one CI job with different clocks and test logs; assert both
manifests carry the same `determinismDigest` and different `releaseId` values.

### Structured logging
- The generator and validator append JSONL records (`timestamp`, `suite: "release-manifest"`,
`logRunId`, `toolRunId` when the release script supplies one, `commit`, `profile`, `check`, `path`,
`expected`, `actual`, `outcome`, `message`) to
`artifacts/test-logs/release-manifest/<log-run-id>.jsonl`. A failing validation retains the
offending manifest, the computed digests, and the fetched or read bytes' hashes under
`artifacts/test-logs/release-manifest/<log-run-id>/evidence/<check>/`, copied and never deleted.

## Considerations and Pitfalls

- A checksum proves byte identity, not compatible meaning; compatibility between HTML and WASM comes
from `modelVersion` and schema checks, which the rollback bead also relies on.
- Non-redistributable scans are listed with `path: null`; never publish a scan to satisfy the
manifest.
- Keep the manifest small; do not inline logs.
- A `determinismDigest` that changes between two builds of the same commit is a bug in the generator
(an unsorted list or a timestamp), not a reason to drop the check.
- The profile contract is read at build time by pages that ship before this bead closes. Changing
its shape is therefore a cross-batch change: update `src/content/publicationProfile.ts`, the four
design beads' fixture manifests, and this bead's tests together.

## Dependencies

Blocked by:
- `am-rel-verified-deploy-qndt`: the release script validates the manifest in the artifact and owns
the release record this bead writes into.
- `am-fs-slim-artifact-0yh`: WASM artifacts and pinned digests must exist to be listed.
- `am-cm-compiler-core-oa7`: content revisions and route payloads come from the compiler.
- `am-cm-coverage-ledger-0ip`: the separate, never-aggregated completeness dimensions come from the
coverage ledger.

Unblocks:
- `am-rel-candidate-checks-kc7y`: candidate checks verify deployed bytes against this manifest,
including the deployed-bytes check that compares a disclosed kernel's source hash with this
manifest's `kernels` entry and fails, rather than passing vacuously, when the section is absent.
- `am-plat-installable-offline-oit3`: the offline edition keys its caches on `releaseId` and
`determinismDigest`.
- `am-a11y-reviewed-narration-r28u`: narration audio hashes are listed here, and stale narration is
refused against this manifest.
- Beads of the separate iPhone app plan (`am-app-edition-export-kwpu`, `am-app-edition-parity-bwa5`,
`am-app-verified-release-1jbu`, `am-app-facsimile-downloads-72nz`) also depend on this manifest; app
work never delays a website batch, and this bead makes no commitment to it.

Blocked by, added as an edge in review: `am-inst-show-the-code-4brv` produces the computation-source
records the `kernels` section lists. Without them the section is empty, which only the `scaffold`
profile accepts.
