title: Scaffold the Next.js App Router application with strict TypeScript, Biome, Bun tests, and an empty corpus
description: # Scaffold the Next.js App Router application with strict TypeScript, Biome, Bun tests, and an empty corpus **Epic:** `am-ep-scaffold-5wh` · **Batch:** A · **Priority:** P0 · **Plan sections:** §1.5, §2.4, §15.1, §15.2, §16.4, §16.6, §19.1 (traceability only) ## Background Batch A requires "`typecheck`, `lint`, `build`, and the architecture test green with an empty corpus" (§19.1). This bead creates that application: the single Next.js App Router root under `src/app`, strict TypeScript, Biome for lint and format, Bun for tests and scripts, and the planned directory layout that every later bead writes into. It deliberately contains no content, no physics, and no instruments, so later work lands in a clean, verified structure. The scaffold must already respect the product's non-negotiables: the reading experience works without JavaScript, without a GPU, and without running a simulation (§1.5); the initial reading route has no Three.js, pdf.js, or WASM in its dependency graph and at most 200 KiB of compressed first-route JavaScript (§16.4); no third-party scripts, fonts, or requests (§16.6); and the home page makes no claim that an edition exists before it does. Because three later beads need to prove the initial-route absence (this one, the UI extraction that introduces pdf.js and Three.js, and the performance budgets), this bead creates the single shared check they all use. One more shared mechanism belongs here for the same reason. Several reader and platform beads set a `data-` attribute on `` before first paint with a tiny inline script, and each records its script's hash "in the build's inline-script hash manifest, consumed by `am-plat-security-f644`": the theme script (`am-design-themes-typography-288q`), the Detail script (`am-read-detail-axis-sfc`), the view script and the root-arming script (`am-read-shell-routes-3ua`), the perspective, notation, and units script (`am-read-perspective-toggle-abd`), the storage key constants (`am-plat-local-storage-km8f`), and the generated offline chapter's shared Detail script (`am-plat-offline-chapter-un8i`). Nothing owned generating that manifest, and the security bead (Batch C) only consumes it: its own text records the gap and recommends this bead. The scaffold is the right owner, because it owns the root layout that hosts inline scripts and the build that emits them, and the manifest must exist in Batch A, when the first inline script lands, not in Batch C. With the manifest owned here, a missing entry becomes a build failure instead of a silent Content-Security-Policy relaxation. ## Scope In scope: project initialization with the locked versions, runtime pins, TypeScript and Biome configuration, Bun test configuration, the directory layout, the root layout, a placeholder home page, error and not-found routes, `robots` and `sitemap` routes for an empty corpus, package scripts, the shared initial-route graph check, the inline-script registry and its hash manifest emitter, the local static-output check, and first real unit tests. Out of scope, owned elsewhere: the architecture gate (`am-scaf-architecture-gate-l1p`); donor extractions (`am-scaf-extract-runtime-utilities-99y`, `am-scaf-extract-ui-components-c31`, `am-scaf-extract-scripts-7jm`); themes and fonts, including the first real inline script (`am-design-themes-typography-288q`); the reader routes (`am-read-shell-routes-3ua`); the gate registry and CI (`am-scaf-quality-gates-ci-4xx`); structured test logging (`am-test-logging-standard-l3cp`); the Content-Security-Policy header, its hash directives, and the verification that every emitted inline script is registered (`am-plat-security-f644`, which consumes the manifest this bead emits); byte budgets and transferred-size measurement (`am-plat-perf-budgets-s3ww`, which extends the graph check). ## Requirements 1. **Versions:** exactly those recorded in `docs/DECISIONS.md` by `am-gov-decision-stack-versions-6ax`; exact pins in `package.json`; `bun.lock` committed; `engines.node` set to the recorded Node.js version; `packageManager` set to the recorded Bun version so CI reads the same string. 2. **TypeScript:** `strict: true`, `noEmit`, bundler module resolution, path alias `@/*` to `src/*`. Enable `noUncheckedIndexedAccess` unless the stack decision records a reason not to. 3. **Directory layout** (plan §15.2), documented in `content/README.md`, `src/README.md`, and `public/README.md` rather than placeholder files: - `content/` with `papers/`, `source-blocks/`, `translations/`, `glosses/`, `annotations/`, `arguments/`, `foundations/`, `misconceptions/`, `historical-premises/`, `equations/`, `quantities/`, `experiments/`, `scenarios/`, `datasets/`, `tours/`, `bibliography/`; - `src/` with `app/` (the only App Router root), `content/`, `reader/`, `equations/`, `experiments/`, `workers/`, `physics/reference/`, `visuals/`, `units/`, `search/`, `testing/`; - `public/` with `papers/pdfs/`, `papers/transcripts/`, `wasm/`, `figures/` (only assets admitted for redistribution); - `docs/` with `provenance/`; `scripts/`; - `docs/README.md` and `scripts/README.md` layout notes that also list the source-layer paths other beads create, so nobody invents a second location or mistakes them for stray files: `scripts/sources/facsimile-sources/` (per-key download configuration, `am-src-download-script-15ar`); `scripts/sources/ocr-plans/` and `scripts/sources/ocr-instructions/` (`am-src-ocr-orchestrator-u1e0`); receipts at `docs/provenance/.md` and survey records at `docs/provenance/survey/` (`am-src-receipt-format-npo5`, `am-src-scan-survey-sqnu`); `docs/editorial/RECEIPT_FORMAT.md` (`am-src-receipt-format-npo5`); `docs/rights-vocabulary.yaml` (`am-src-rights-policy-1dp`); and the gitignored root `sources/` directory for local-only pins and parent scans (its `.gitignore` entry is added by `am-src-download-script-15ar`). The scaffold creates none of these paths; it documents them. 4. **Routes:** `src/app/layout.tsx` (``, `metadataBase` `https://annus-mirabilis.com`, minimal chrome, no heavy imports, no remote font loading, system font stack until the typography bead lands); `src/app/page.tsx` (a static placeholder that says the edition is in preparation and links to the repository, with no claim that papers, translations, or instruments are available and no promised dates); `src/app/error.tsx`; `src/app/global-error.tsx`; `src/app/not-found.tsx`; `src/app/robots.ts`; `src/app/sitemap.ts` (lists only `/` for the empty corpus). All routes statically generated. 5. **Package scripts:** `dev`, `build`, `start`, `typecheck` (`tsc --noEmit`), `lint` (`biome check`), `format` (`biome format --write`), `format:check`, `test` (Bun test with the per-file isolation mechanism recorded by the stack decision). Do not add scripts for tools that do not exist yet (`gates` arrives with `am-scaf-quality-gates-ci-4xx`). 6. **Biome:** formatter and linter enabled; generated directories ignored. 7. **Shared initial-route graph check** `scripts/perf/initialRouteGraph.ts`: after a production build, determines the client JavaScript the `/` route loads and fails if it contains Three.js, pdf.js, a WASM file, or a WASM or worker loader. Method: use the bundler's route-level module trace or stats output when the locked Next.js version provides one, and always also scan the route's emitted chunks for signature strings (`WebGLRenderer`, `GlobalWorkerOptions`, `WebAssembly.instantiateStreaming`, `.wasm`). It accepts the route to inspect as an argument so `am-read-shell-routes-3ua` and `am-plat-perf-budgets-s3ww` reuse it for the reading route; the performance bead adds byte budgets on top rather than writing a second graph check. 8. **Static output check** `scripts/scaffold/check-static-output.ts`: starts `next start` on a free port against the production build, fetches `/`, `/robots.txt`, `/sitemap.xml`, and an unknown path over plain HTTP (user agent "OpenAI File Downloader, XaiImageApiFetch/1.0" per AGENTS.md), asserts status codes and content, asserts no `

title: Wire the local and CI quality gate chain
description:
# Wire the local and CI quality gate chain

**Epic:** `am-ep-scaffold-5wh` · **Batch:** A · **Priority:** P0 · **Plan sections:** §17.1, §17.3,
§17.7 item 9, §18.3 (traceability only)

## Background

The per-paper definition of done requires `verify-content`, typecheck, lint, format, build, `ubs
--diff`, the WASM artifact test, and the Playwright vertical slice to be green (§17.7 item 9), and
the release workflow runs the quality gates before deploying anything (§18.3). Those gates must
exist as one ordered, reproducible chain that every agent runs the same way locally, that GitHub
Actions runs on every push and pull request, and that the release script runs for each publication
profile. If the release script kept its own list of gate commands, the two lists would drift; so
this bead builds **one typed gate registry**, and every consumer (local runs, CI, the release
profiles, the nightly job) selects steps from it.

Two principles from AGENTS.md shape the chain. First, **never weaken a gate** to get green: no
skipped lanes, loosened tolerances, deleted evidence, or reruns of flaky statistical tests. Second,
**a command that does not exist yet is never reported as passing**; the chain shows it as
`not-available` until the bead that creates it registers it, and a release profile that requires it
refuses. And CI never deploys: releases go only through the verified prebuilt workflow
(`am-rel-verified-deploy-qndt`).

## Scope

In scope: the gate registry, the runner script, the `gates` package script, release-profile
selection and refusal, the GitHub Actions workflow for the fast chain, the nightly workflow for
steps that are too slow for every push, log retention, and tests.

Out of scope, owned elsewhere: the individual gates' implementations (architecture
`am-scaf-architecture-gate-l1p`, content `am-cm-audit-scripts-d34`, WASM `am-fs-slim-artifact-0yh`,
voice `am-edit-voice-lint-trmf`, license inventory `am-gov-license-inventory-w6yz`, scenarios
`am-ver-scenario-registry-om3`, browser `am-test-e2e-harness-bqmh`, performance
`am-plat-perf-budgets-s3ww`, resource stress `am-plat-resource-stress-9zgu`, receipts
`am-src-receipt-format-npo5`, facsimile configuration `am-src-download-script-15ar`); the
browser-acceptance workflow file (`.github/workflows/browser-acceptance.yml`, owned by
`am-test-e2e-harness-bqmh`); deployment (`am-rel-verified-deploy-qndt`).

## Requirements

1. **Registry** `scripts/quality-gates/registry.ts`: a typed list of `GateStep` entries with `id`,
`title`, `command` (argument array), `family` (`fast`, `browser`, `perf`, or `apple`), `cadence`
(`every-run` or `nightly`), `requiredInCi` (boolean), `requiredInProfiles` (a subset of `scaffold`,
`preview`, `launch`), `availability` (a script path that must exist or a tool that must be on
`PATH`), and `owner` (the bead id that registered the step). Registry validation rejects duplicate
ids, unknown profiles, unknown families, and steps without an owner. The `apple` family exists
because AGENTS.md runs Apple validation locally and never in the website's CI: an `apple` step is
never selected by the CI workflow and is never required in a website release profile.
2. **Initial steps, in order:** `architecture` (`bun scripts/app-router-architecture.ts`),
`typecheck`, `lint` (`biome check`), `format-check`, `unit-tests` (`bun run test`), `ubs-diff` (`ubs
--diff`), `ubs-staged` (`ubs --staged`), `build` (last among the fast steps). All are `fast`,
`every-run`, and required in the `scaffold`, `preview`, and `launch` profiles; all except the two
`ubs` steps are required in CI.
3. **Later registrations** (each by its owning bead, in the same change that creates the command):

   | Step id | Owner | Family | Cadence | Notes |
   |---|---|---|---|---|
   | `publication-contract` | `am-rel-verified-deploy-qndt` | fast | every-run | A `bun test` subset of the edition, dispatcher, architecture, and determinism tests, ordered first so release refusals come early |
   | `verify-content` | `am-cm-audit-scripts-d34` | fast | every-run | |
   | `verify-wasm-artifacts` | `am-fs-slim-artifact-0yh` | fast | every-run | |
   | `voice-lint` | `am-edit-voice-lint-trmf` | fast | every-run | Until `verify-content` absorbs it |
   | `license-inventory` | `am-gov-license-inventory-w6yz` | fast | every-run | |
   | `scenarios` | `am-ver-scenario-registry-om3` | fast | every-run | |
   | `receipts` | `am-src-receipt-format-npo5` | fast | every-run | `bun scripts/check-receipts.ts`, with `--surveys`; no network |
   | `facsimile-config` | `am-src-download-script-15ar` | fast | every-run | `bun scripts/download-facsimiles.ts --check-config`; no network |
   | `perf-budget-change` | `am-plat-perf-budgets-s3ww` | fast | every-run | The diff check that a change to a byte budget carries a committed measurement record and a decision entry |
   | `browser-acceptance` | `am-test-e2e-harness-bqmh` | browser | every-run | Separate CI job |
   | `perf-budgets` | `am-plat-perf-budgets-s3ww` | perf | nightly | Measurement run against recorded profiles |
   | `resource-stress` | `am-plat-resource-stress-9zgu` | perf | nightly | Repeated route changes and mounts; required in `preview` and `launch`, never on every push |

   Each later step is required in CI and in the `preview` and `launch` profiles unless its owner
   records a reason otherwise; a `nightly` step is required in those profiles but excluded from the
   every-push workflow. Two owners (`am-src-receipt-format-npo5` and `am-src-download-script-15ar`)
   have no dependency edge to this bead, so whichever of the two beads lands second adds the entry,
   and the registry test's availability probe proves the command exists.
4. **Runner** `scripts/quality-gates.ts`, with modes:
   - `--fail-fast` (local default): run available steps of the selected families in registry order,
   stopping at the first failure;
   - `--all` (CI): run every step of the selected families and summarize;
   - `--profile <scaffold|preview|launch>` (used by the release script): run exactly the steps
   required in that profile, regardless of cadence, fail-fast; any required step whose availability
   check fails is `refused`, and the run exits with code 2 before running anything;
   - `--cadence <every-run|nightly|all>` (default `every-run` in `--fail-fast` and `--all`, `all` in
   profile mode), and `--family <fast|browser|perf|apple>` and `--only <ids>` filters.
5. **Outcomes:** `passed`, `failed`, `not-available` (the step's script is absent), `skipped` with a
reason (`tool-unavailable` for an absent tool in a mode where the step is not required,
`not-required-in-ci`, or `cadence`), and `refused` (profile mode only). `not-available` and
`skipped` are never counted as passing. Exit codes: 0 when every required step passed, 1 on any
failure, 2 on refusal.
6. **Package script:** `bun run gates` runs `bun scripts/quality-gates.ts --fail-fast --family
fast`.
7. **GitHub Actions** (`.github/workflows/quality-gates.yml`): triggers on push and pull request to
`main` (never `pull_request_target`); `permissions: contents: read`; checkout pinned by commit SHA
with `persist-credentials: false`; the Bun version read from `package.json` `packageManager` and the
Node.js version from `engines.node`; `bun install --frozen-lockfile`; `bun scripts/quality-gates.ts
--all --family fast --cadence every-run`; uploads `artifacts/test-logs/` as a workflow artifact on
failure; all third-party actions pinned by commit SHA; a concurrency group cancels superseded runs
on the same ref; no secrets; **no deployment, alias, or DNS step of any kind**. A second workflow
file `.github/workflows/nightly-gates.yml` runs `--all --family perf --cadence nightly` on a
schedule with the same permissions and artifact upload; it never runs `apple` steps.

## Technical Approach

The runner spawns each command, streams output, measures duration, records an outcome per step, and
exits with the codes above. It writes a summary table to stdout and JSON lines to the logs
directory. Registry entries are plain data plus an availability probe, so the runner's tests can
pass fixture registries whose commands are real processes.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `bun run gates` passes locally on the empty-corpus scaffold.
- [ ] `bun scripts/quality-gates.ts --profile scaffold` passes locally when `ubs` is installed, and
exits with code 2 naming the missing tool when it is not.
- [ ] The workflow passes on `main` and fails the job when any required step fails, with logs
uploaded.
- [ ] Not-yet-available steps are reported as such and never counted as passing.
- [ ] A `nightly` step is excluded from the every-push workflow and still required in the `preview`
and `launch` profiles.
- [ ] No `apple` step runs in either workflow.
- [ ] The workflow contains no deploy, alias, or DNS command and requests only read permission.
- [ ] README.md and AGENTS.md reference `bun run gates` and the profile flag consistently.

## Test Plan

### Unit and integration tests
`scripts/quality-gates.test.ts` runs the real runner with small fixture registries whose commands
are real processes:
- a step running `bun -e "process.exit(0)"` passes; a step running `bun -e "process.exit(3)"` fails
and stops the chain in fail-fast mode;
- in `--all` mode later steps still run and the exit code is 1;
- a step whose script path does not exist reports `not-available` in `--all` mode and is not counted
as passing;
- in `--profile preview` mode, a required step whose script is absent produces `refused`, exit code
2, and no step runs;
- a required tool absent from `PATH` is `skipped: tool-unavailable` in `--all` mode when not
required in CI, and `refused` in profile mode;
- a `nightly` step is `skipped: cadence` under `--cadence every-run` and runs under `--cadence
nightly` and in profile mode;
- an `apple` step is never selected by `--family fast|browser|perf` and never by the CI invocation
used in the workflow;
- registry validation rejects a duplicate id, an unknown profile name, an unknown family, and a step
without an owner;
- the JSONL output contains one line per step with the fields below plus a summary line.

`scripts/quality-gates/workflowScan.test.ts`: reads every file in `.github/workflows/` and fails on
`vercel`, `deploy`, `alias`, `wrangler`, `cloudflare`, `pull_request_target`, or a `permissions`
block granting write access; a fixture workflow containing `vercel deploy` fails; a fixture workflow
invoking `--family apple` fails.

### End-to-end tests
The CI workflow itself on a pull request; a deliberately failing fixture step in the test suite
(never in the real registry) proves failure propagation, and its run directory, stdout, stderr, and
JSONL log are retained under `artifacts/test-logs/quality-gates/<log-run-id>/evidence/`.

### Structured logging
One JSON line per step `{timestamp, suite: "quality-gates", logRunId, mode, profile, cadence,
stepId, owner, family, command, outcome, reason, exitCode, durationMs, message}` to
`artifacts/test-logs/quality-gates/<log-run-id>.jsonl`, plus a summary line with counts per outcome.

## Considerations and Pitfalls

- Browser and performance families are slow; they run in separate workflow jobs owned by their
beads, but they are never dropped from the definition of done or from the `preview` and `launch`
profiles. `cadence: nightly` moves a step off every push without removing it from a profile.
- Keep the build step last among the fast gates so earlier failures surface quickly.
- CI minutes must not become a reason to skip gates; if the chain is slow, profile it.
- A release profile's step list only grows; removing a step from a profile requires a recorded
decision.
- The `apple` family is registered here so there is one registry, but it runs only on the owner's
machine; never add it to a website workflow.

## Dependencies

Blocked by: `am-scaf-architecture-gate-l1p` (the first step of the chain).

Unblocks:
- `am-rel-verified-deploy-qndt`: the release script runs this registry in profile mode before
building a candidate.
- `am-cm-audit-scripts-d34`, `am-edit-voice-lint-trmf`, `am-fs-slim-artifact-0yh`,
`am-ver-scenario-registry-om3`, `am-gov-license-inventory-w6yz`, `am-test-e2e-harness-bqmh`: each
registers its step in the same change that creates its command.
- `am-app-apple-quality-gate-q6gs`: registers the local `apple` family, which this registry types
and which never runs in the website's CI.

title: Emit ScholarlyArticle and translation metadata with a strict attribution separation
description:
# Emit ScholarlyArticle and translation metadata with a strict attribution separation

**Epic:** `am-ep-platform-8ci` · **Batch:** C · **Priority:** P1 · **Labels:** platform, source, search · **Plan sections:** ASTRA_V2 §18.12; AGENTS.md "Sources, Rights, and Provenance" and "Rights layers stay separate" (traceability only)

## Background

The site is a critical edition whose purpose is that people can read, cite and find four 1905 papers. It already holds, as validated records, everything a bibliographic description needs:

- per paper, the bibliographic key, printed German title, author line, typed dates by kind (date-line, receipt, issue publication), the journal record with `name`, `series: 4`, `volume`, `wholeSeriesVolume`, `issue`, `issueSource`, `pages: {first, last}`, `doi` and `doiVerifiedAt`, plus `laterEditionDois[]` (`am-cm-schemas-source-1en`, and the receipts written through `am-src-receipt-format-npo5`);
- the verified DOIs themselves: `10.1002/andp.19053220607`, `10.1002/andp.19053220806`, `10.1002/andp.19053221004`, `10.1002/andp.19053231314`, `10.1002/andp.19063240204`, with the 2005 reissue DOI correction recorded (Crossref records `10.1002/andp.200590007` as the reissue of the light-quanta paper, not of paper 4);
- translator and editor credits with review dates and reviewer names, and the correction graph (`am-edit-review-records-hofz`);
- `contentRevision` and `translationRevision`, kept separate by design;
- distinct language documents: `am-read-shell-routes-3ua` makes the `german` and `english` face pages self-canonical with reciprocal `hreflang="de"` and `hreflang="en"` alternates, which is exactly the precondition ASTRA sets before `hreflang` is meaningful;
- citation formats published on `/about` "for the edition, a paper, a section anchor, an equation or result anchor, and an instrument permalink, each including the content and translation revision identities" (`am-design-sources-about-zumd`).

None of it is emitted in a machine-readable form. A graph-wide search for `ScholarlyArticle`, `schema.org` and `JSON-LD` returns nothing.

The gap matters twice. The first reason is ordinary discoverability: a scholar, a library tool or a reference manager that meets `/papers/special-relativity` learns nothing about what it is looking at. The second reason is the site's own honesty rule, and it is the one that makes this bead more than plumbing. AGENTS.md keeps rights and authorship layers strictly separate: "Original historical text, facsimile scans, the new translation, new explanatory prose, interactive code, numerical libraries, fonts, images, and historical datasets each carry their own recorded rights status." The characteristic failure of a naive metadata block is to collapse them: it emits one record per page with Einstein as `author` and 1905 as `datePublished`, thereby attributing the site's own English translation and explanatory prose to Einstein and backdating them by 120 years. That is precisely what ASTRA warns against: "Do not identify a new commentary as an article published in 1905 or attribute it to Einstein."

ASTRA also states the limit, which this bead must state too: structured metadata improves machine readability; it does not guarantee search ranking or a rich-result display.

## Scope

In scope: the metadata projection and its generator; the two-entity model and the attribution separation; emission on canonical document pages only; the validator and its build gate; the human-readable citation block's shared source; tests.

Out of scope, owned elsewhere:
- receipts, their parser, checker and `receiptToSourceAsset` mapping (`am-src-receipt-format-npo5`);
- the paper, journal and citation record schemas (`am-cm-schemas-source-1en`);
- the rights vocabulary and per-asset rights statements (`am-src-rights-policy-1dp`), and the license decision (`am-gov-decision-license-rights-tps`);
- reviewer names, consent and the correction graph (`am-edit-review-records-hofz`, `am-gov-owners-and-reviewers-hte`);
- `/sources`, `/about` and the how-to-cite prose (`am-design-sources-about-zumd`), which this bead feeds rather than duplicates;
- canonical URLs, `hreflang` and the sitemap (`am-read-shell-routes-3ua`, and the proposed `am-route-canonical-registry-57b6`);
- the search index (`am-plat-search-index-snx1`);
- later reviewed editions in other languages (`am-later-language-editions-sp4e`), which this bead's model must not block.

## Requirements

### Two entities, never one

1. **The historical article.** For each paper, a `ScholarlyArticle` describing the document Einstein published:
   - `name`: the printed German title, exactly as the source face carries it;
   - `author`: Albert Einstein, with no other author;
   - `inLanguage`: `de`;
   - `datePublished`: the issue publication date at its recorded precision; `dateReceived` where the record carries it;
   - `isPartOf`: the journal record as a `PublicationIssue` inside a `PublicationVolume` inside a `Periodical` named *Annalen der Physik*, carrying `volumeNumber`, the whole-series volume as an additional property, `issueNumber`, `pageStart` and `pageEnd`;
   - `identifier`: the verified DOI, and `laterEditionDois[]` emitted as clearly labelled later editions, never as the citation DOI;
   - `sameAs` is emitted only for identifiers the receipt verified, with its `verifiedAt` date recorded in the projection.
2. **The site's edition.** A separate entity for what this site publishes about that paper:
   - a translation entity for the English face, with `translator` naming the site's translator and editor credits, `inLanguage: en`, `translationOfWork` pointing at the historical article, `datePublished` the edition's own date, and `version` the `translationRevision`;
   - a commentary entity for the explanatory prose of that paper's reading face, with its own `author` (the site's named contributors and roles, including editorial agents by model where `am-design-sources-about-zumd` records them), `isBasedOn` the historical article, and `version` the `contentRevision`;
   - `license` from the license-status projection of `am-design-sources-about-zumd`. While the status is `provisional`, the `license` field is **omitted** rather than guessed, and the projection records why.
3. **Disjoint attribution, enforced.** A validator fails the build when:
   - Einstein appears as `author` or `translator` of any entity other than the historical article;
   - any entity other than the historical article carries a `datePublished` in 1905 or 1906;
   - the translation entity lacks `translationOfWork`, or the commentary entity lacks `isBasedOn`;
   - the historical article carries a `translator`, a `version`, or a `license` (the German text is public domain and the site grants nothing over it);
   - a DOI appears on any entity other than the historical article.

### Where it is emitted

4. Metadata is emitted **only on the canonical document** of a content identity, so a `noindex` variant, a face fallback page that canonicalises elsewhere, a tape URL and an embed never carry it. On the German and English face pages, which are self-canonical language documents, the emitted set is the historical article plus the entity for that language face, and nothing else.
5. Emission is server-rendered into the static HTML, so it is present without JavaScript and identical in the offline chapter files where those carry the same identity.
6. Under the `preview` profile, a paper absent from `getPublishedPapers()` emits nothing at all, rather than a partial record, so the preview leak audit of `am-rel-preview-policy-cf6g` has nothing to find.

### One source for the human and machine forms

7. The projection that builds the structured metadata also supplies the fields for the human-readable citation block on `/about` and on each paper page, so the printed citation and the machine record cannot disagree. `am-design-sources-about-zumd` renders the block from this projection instead of composing its own fields, and a test asserts the two forms carry identical values for title, author, journal, volume, issue, pages, DOI, date and revision identities.

### Honest limits

8. `/sources` gains one sentence, passing the voice lint, stating that the site publishes structured bibliographic metadata to make the edition machine-readable, that the historical article and the site's own translation and commentary are described as separate works with separate authorship, and that such metadata does not determine how any search engine ranks or displays the pages.
9. No claim of indexing, ranking or rich-result eligibility appears anywhere in the repository, and a phrase scan enforces it.

## Technical Approach

- `src/content/metadata/scholarlyProjection.ts` builds both entities from the compiled paper record and the parsed receipt, using `parseReceipt` and `receiptToSourceAsset` rather than re-reading the receipt file.
- `src/content/metadata/attributionCheck.ts` implements requirement 3 and runs in the content compiler, so a violation fails `bun run build` rather than a later audit.
- `src/content/metadata/JsonLd.tsx` is a server component emitting one `application/ld+json` script per canonical document; the payload is serialised through a strict encoder that rejects any key not in the declared shape.
- The citation-block fields are exported from the same projection and consumed by `am-design-sources-about-zumd`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Each published paper's canonical document carries exactly two or three entities: the historical article, and the language or commentary entity appropriate to that document.
- [ ] The historical article carries the printed German title, Einstein as sole author, `inLanguage: de`, the typed publication date at its recorded precision, the full journal record including the whole-series volume, the verified DOI, and later-edition DOIs labelled as such.
- [ ] The translation entity carries the site's translator and editor credits, `inLanguage: en`, `translationOfWork`, and the `translationRevision` as its version; the commentary entity carries the site's authors, `isBasedOn`, and the `contentRevision`.
- [ ] Each of the five attribution violations in requirement 3 fails the build with a message naming the entity and the field; a seeded record with Einstein as translator, and one with a 1905 `datePublished` on the commentary, each fail.
- [ ] While the license status is provisional, `license` is omitted and the reason is recorded; with a decided fixture it is emitted from `NOTICE.md`.
- [ ] No `noindex` route, face fallback page canonicalising elsewhere, tape URL or embed carries metadata; the German and English face pages carry the article plus their own language entity only.
- [ ] Metadata is present in the served HTML with JavaScript disabled.
- [ ] Under `preview`, an unpublished paper emits nothing.
- [ ] The human citation block and the structured record carry identical values for title, author, journal, volume, issue, pages, DOI, date and revision identities.
- [ ] `/sources` carries the limits sentence, and the phrase scan finds no ranking or rich-result claim.

## Test Plan

### Unit and integration tests

- `scholarlyProjection.test.ts`, against the real compiled fixture records and fixture receipts: every field above for each of the five keys; the whole-series volume is emitted as an additional property and not as `volumeNumber`; `laterEditionDois[]` are labelled later editions; the paper-4 reissue-DOI correction is respected, so `10.1002/andp.200590007` never appears as paper 4's identifier.
- `attributionCheck.test.ts`: the five violations, each failing with the entity and field named; a correct record passing; a record with no `license` while provisional passing with its recorded reason.
- `jsonLdEmission.test.tsx`: emission on a canonical document; no emission on a `noindex` route, a face fallback page canonicalising elsewhere, a tape URL and an embed; the German and English face pages emit the article plus their own language entity; the strict encoder rejects an undeclared key.
- `citationParity.test.ts`: the human block and the structured record agree field by field for every fixture paper; a seeded divergence fails, naming the field.
- `previewProfile.test.ts`: an unpublished paper emits nothing under `preview`.
- `metadataClaims.test.ts`: the phrase scan over repository prose and page copy rejects seeded claims such as "improves our search ranking" and "guarantees a rich result".

### End-to-end tests

Through `am-test-e2e-harness-bqmh`, against the production build of the fixture site:

1. Load each paper's canonical document with JavaScript disabled, parse the emitted `application/ld+json`, and assert the two-entity shape and the disjoint authorship.
2. Load the German and English face pages and assert the article plus one language entity each, with the reciprocal `hreflang` alternates `am-read-shell-routes-3ua` emits.
3. Load a tape URL, an embed and a Detail fallback page and assert no metadata is present.
4. In a `preview`-profile build, assert an unpublished paper's page carries none.
5. Assert that the visible citation block on the paper page and the parsed record agree on every shared field.

### Structured logging

Through `am-test-logging-standard-l3cp`, suite `am-scholarly-metadata-mjrx`, file `artifacts/test-logs/scholarly-metadata/<log-run-id>.jsonl`: `timestamp`, `suite`, `logRunId`, `testId`, `beadId`, `paper`, `route`, `entityTypes`, `articleAuthor`, `translationTranslator`, `commentaryAuthor`, `doi`, `laterEditionDois`, `datePublished`, `datePrecision`, `contentRevision`, `translationRevision`, `licenseEmitted`, `licenseStatus`, `attributionViolations`, `emittedOnCanonicalOnly`, `profile`, `jsEnabled`, `outcome`, `durationMs`, `message`.

A failing attribution or parity case retains, under `artifacts/test-logs/scholarly-metadata/<log-run-id>/failures/<testId>.json`, the emitted payload, the offending entity and field, the record it was built from, and a one-line reproduction command.

## Considerations and Pitfalls

- One record per page is the tempting shape and the wrong one. The page carries an 1905 article **and** a 2026 translation **and** a 2026 commentary, by different people under different rights, and the whole point of the edition is that those layers stay distinct.
- Never emit a DOI for the site's own work. A DOI on the translation entity would assert an identifier the site does not hold and would invite a citation of Einstein's paper that resolves to this site.
- The whole-series volume is not `volumeNumber`. Annalen's series-4 volume 17 and its whole-series number are different facts, both recorded, and collapsing them produces a wrong citation that looks right.
- Emit nothing while the license is undecided rather than guessing a permissive one. An omitted field is honest; a wrong license statement is a claim about other people's rights.
- Metadata must never become a second source of bibliographic truth. Build it from the receipts and the paper records, and let the citation block read the same projection, or the two will disagree the first time a date precision changes.
- Say the limit out loud. Structured metadata makes the edition machine-readable; it decides nothing about how anyone ranks or displays it.

## Dependencies

Blocked by:
- `am-cm-schemas-source-1en`: the `Paper`, journal and `Citation` record shapes the projection reads.
- `am-src-receipt-format-npo5`: the receipt parser, checker and mapping that supply verified DOIs, typed dates and translation credits.
- `am-read-shell-routes-3ua`: the canonical documents metadata is emitted on, and the self-canonical German and English language pages with their reciprocal alternates.
- `am-design-sources-about-zumd`: the license-status projection, the authorship and translation policy, and the citation block that consumes this projection.
- `am-edit-review-records-hofz`: translator and editor credits and their review states.
- `am-test-e2e-harness-bqmh`: browser lanes and failure evidence.

Related without an edge:
- The proposed `am-route-canonical-registry-57b6` decides which document is canonical for each identity; this bead emits only there. Until it exists, emission follows each route owner's declared canonical.
- `am-later-language-editions-sp4e`: a later reviewed edition adds one more language entity per paper under the same two-entity model, with no change to the historical article.

Unblocks:
- `am-launch-readiness-audit-sc9b`: machine-readable bibliographic identity is launch evidence that the edition can be cited and found.

title: Build SR-01 clock synchronization with the event ledger

# Build SR-01 clock synchronization with the event ledger

**Epic:** `am-ep-relativity-kinematics-q2g` · **Batch:** batch-e · **Priority:** P1 · **Plan sections:** §3.5 §1, §7.2, §8.3, §9.4, §10.1-10.7, §12.6, §13.2 (traceability only)

## Background

The relativity paper opens its kinematics with a question a careful person can actually answer: how will you assign a time to an event that happens elsewhere? SR-01 makes the procedure concrete. Its primary view is an **event ledger** of emissions, reflections, and receptions at named clocks; a spatial scene supports it without implying that what a distant camera sees equals a simultaneous coordinate measurement. The instrument applies Einstein's criterion $t_B - t_A = t'_A - t_B$ explicitly, keeps an event distinct from its reception in every view, runs the same procedure on the ends of a moving rod (§2's chase), and then shows that a pair of clocks synchronized in its own frame and moving at $v$ is judged out of step by $vL/c^2$ (for proper separation $L$) in the platform frame. It is also the destination of the no-algebra first encounter, the "make a measurement procedure" stage of Journey III, and the fifteen-minute tour, so its named presets and its registered predict prompt are part of its contract.

## Scope

In scope: the SR-01 manifest, controls, typed outputs, views, caption readings, named preset scenarios, the registered predict prompt with its stable candidate ids, weave predicate records, action contract, predict mode, show-the-code, tape identity, permalink, embeddable flag, and tests.

Out of scope: the evaluator (`am-ref-events-yvl`); rod measurements (`am-sr-03-rod-simultaneity-0l5i`); the no-algebra entrance (`am-srk-first-encounter-471z`); Journey III narration (`am-disc-journey-iii-chain-hpr7`); the `/embed/lab/[experiment]` route itself (`am-inst-embed-route-rnyg`, Batch H); the tour's plain-words rendering of the prompt (`am-tour-15min-relativity-qcxc`).

## Requirements

**Explanatory question.** How can distant clocks acquire an operational common time, and do moving clocks share it?

**Linked source and argument ids.** §1 (definition of simultaneity, the criterion, $2\overline{AB}/(t'_A - t_A) = V$); §2 (clocks at the ends of a moving rod and the chase); Journey III stage "make a measurement procedure."

### Controls

| Control | Dimension | Display unit | Model domain | Numerical domain | Default | Mapping | Class |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Clock separation (stations A, B) | length | light-seconds (km toggle) | $> 0$ | $10^{-6}$ to $10^{6}$ ls | 10 ls | logarithmic | setup-change |
| Initial clock offsets | time | s | any finite | $\pm10^{6}$ s | 0 | linear, typed entry | setup-change |
| Signal emission time at A | time | s | finite, after run start | $0$ to $10^{6}$ s | 0 | typed | physical-intervention |
| Station motion (§2 mode: A and B as rod ends moving in the stationary frame) | velocity | fraction of $c$ | $\lvert u\rvert < c$ | $\lvert u\rvert \le 0.95c$ | 0 | linear | setup-change |
| Moving clock pair velocity | velocity | fraction of $c$ | $\lvert u\rvert < c$ | $\lvert u\rvert \le 0.95c$ | $0.6c$ | linear | setup-change |
| Moving pair proper separation $L$ | length | ls | $> 0$ | as above | 10 ls | logarithmic | setup-change |
| Frame of description | velocity | fraction of $c$ | $\lvert v\rvert < c$ | $\lvert v\rvert \le 0.95c$ | 0 | linear | observer-change |

Typed entry sits beside every slider; out-of-domain entries explain the problem and offer the admissible boundary; nothing is silently clamped.

### Derived outputs (all from one accepted snapshot)

- Ledger rows: event id, kind (emission, reflection, reception), clock, the clock's own reading at the event (invariant under a change of description), coordinates in the chosen frame, and the reception event linked to each remote event. Receptions are separate rows.
- Criterion check per clock pair: `value` offset $t_B - t_A - (t'_A - t_B)$, or "synchronized by definition" when zero within the declared absolute tolerance.
- Assigned remote time by the equal-travel-time rule, labeled "stated procedure."
- Round-trip speed $2\overline{AB}/(t'_A - t_A)$: `value` equal to $c$ in the frame where the procedure is applied.
- §2 chase legs for moving rod ends: $t_B - t_A = r_{AB}/(c - u)$ and $t'_A - t_B = r_{AB}/(c + u)$ in the stationary frame (from `movingRodLegs`), with the criterion's failure for observers moving with the rod stated.
- Desynchronization of the moving pair as judged in the platform frame: `value` $vL/c^2$ with the trailing clock ahead. This is the output `desynchronizationObserved`, the control the registered predict prompt is attached to.
- One-way light speed: `not-applicable` with the explanation that the model defines it by convention.
- $\lvert v\rvert \ge c$ or $\lvert u\rvert \ge c$: `outside-domain` ("no inertial observer moves at or above light speed"); nonfinite or nonpositive separation: input refusal with the reason and the admissible boundary.

### Model assumptions and admitted domain

Inertial frames; aligned axes; point events; ideal clocks; light speed $c$ in every inertial frame (postulate); separations and speeds within the numerical domain.

### The procedure is a convention, and light is not the only way to compare clocks

SR-01 teaches the paper's synchronization procedure: a signal out, a signal back, and a common time established for two distant clocks. The risk is a claim the paper does not make and the site would be wrong to teach, that **only** light can compare distant clocks. A reader who leaves SR-01 believing that has learned a false uniqueness, and the derivation rests on the stated postulates together with symmetry and coordinate assumptions, not on "two postulates and nothing else".

The paper gives the anchor. §1 does not derive the equality of the two one-way light times; it establishes it by definition, in the source's own words, before anything is derived from it. Verify the exact wording and its extent on the pinned `ap-17-891` facsimile and the reviewed ledger, record the sentence id, and let the instrument show the reader that the paper called it a definition.

- **The manifest declares the procedure as a convention.** Add to the manifest an `assumptions` entry naming, in one line each, that the two one-way transit times are set equal by definition rather than measured, and the source sentence id where the paper says so.
- **At least one alternative procedure is named with its own assumption.** The natural one is **slow clock transport**: synchronize two clocks side by side and carry one to the distant station.
  - What it needs that the light procedure does not: an assumption about how a clock's rate depends on its motion, which is a dynamical assumption about clocks rather than a convention about signals.
  - What it gives: in the limit of vanishingly slow transport, within one inertial frame, it agrees with the light convention; at any finite transport speed the two differ by an amount that goes to zero with the speed. That is stated as the limiting statement it is, with the limit named, and never as an exact equivalence at finite speed.
  - It is presented as a coherent alternative that requires its own analysis, in the register the fair-hearing rule uses for historical alternatives. It is not a fork in Journey III, because that journey's forks are about 1904 alternatives and this is a statement about method; it is an instrument-level note with its own reading.
- **The caption and readings never claim uniqueness.** The banned constructions are registered as a rule set with `am-edit-voice-lint-trmf`, not kept as a local check: "only light can", "light is the only way", "must use light", and "requires light" applied to the comparison of distant clocks. Preferred: "the paper compares distant clocks with light because that makes the assumption it is making visible".
- **The reader can inspect the choice.** One action is added to the action contract, available identically in the visual, keyboard, and table routes: select a synchronization procedure from the named set (the paper's light convention, and slow transport) and read what each one assumes and what each one leaves open, as text beside the same event ledger. No new physics is computed and no second owner is introduced; the alternative is an authored note attached to the same accepted snapshot, and its execution label is unchanged.
- **The historian's margin carries the boundary.** Whatever the site says about the status of the convention beyond what §1 states belongs to R3 under the explicit modern lens, with citations, and is subject to the anachronism lint's `lens` requirement like any other later-development claim. The contemporary-perspective readings say what the paper says: this is established by definition.

### `notModeled`

Signal delays in cables or electronics; gravitational effects; accelerated or rotating clocks; clock mechanisms; optical appearance of distant clocks; detector response times; any measurement of one-way light speed.

### Owner and execution label

`src/physics/reference/events.ts` (`synchronizationRound`, `synchronizationTransitivity`, `movingRodLegs`, `receptionTime`, `classifySimultaneity`, `desynchronizationObserved`, `redescribe`), with transforms from `kinematics.ts`. Public label "Ideal model, host calculation" until `am-fs-owner-relativity-feh` is adopted and an accepted FrankenSim result produced the snapshot.

### Views and caption readings

Primary: the ledger table. Secondary: an SVG track scene with stations and signal paths, where a received flash is visibly a later event than its emission. Optional: an event diagram labeled "later geometric aid (Minkowski 1908)" with light lines at 45 degrees and coherent axis scaling. Canvas and WebGL are not needed. Every view caption carries authored R0-R3 texts in the manifest's caption records (audited by `audit-readings.ts`), consistent with the §1 readings.

### Named preset scenarios (`content/scenarios/`, referenced by the first encounter, results cards, Journey III, and the tour)

- `sr-01-sync-0-10`: emission at 0, reception at 10, reflection assigned 5.
- `sr-01-second-flash-20-30`: emission at 20, reception at 30, reflection assigned 25.
- `sr-01-round-trip-10ls`: a round trip over 10 ls gives speed $c$.
- `sr-01-rod-chase-0.6c`: rod ends 10 ls apart moving at $0.6c$; legs 25 s and 6.25 s.
- `sr-01-moving-pair-0.6c`: $L = 10$ ls at $0.6c$; 6 s desynchronization, trailing clock ahead. This is the preset the fifteen-minute tour's step 3 cites beside the predict prompt, and it commands the moving-pair velocity, so its reveal settles that prompt.
- `sr-01-three-stations`: transitivity of synchronization across A, B, C.

### Action contract (clock and event geometry family)

Choose named events from the ledger with the shared `EventSelector` (from `am-inst-interaction-families-m2ps`: events addressed by ledger ids; selecting two events and a frame issues the `estimator-change` query "Which frame regards these as simultaneous?"; changing the frame issues an `observer-change` that keeps event and run identities; near-equal times are classified through `classifyWithTolerance` and may return an indeterminate boundary result); set separations, offsets, and speeds by typed entry validated against the owner's domain without clamping; emit a signal with a button at a typed model time. Screen readers receive committed comparisons ("In the platform frame the trailing clock of the moving pair reads 6 s ahead"), never per-frame streams. The visual and equivalent paths produce identical runtime commands (`am-a11y-action-contracts-k75g`).

### Predict mode, code, tape, permalink, embed

- **Registered predict prompt.** Predict mode is on by default for first visits: before revealing the moving pair, the reader chooses among three candidates. The prompt is registered in the manifest as `sr-01-predict-moving-pair`, under the `<instrumentId>-predict-<slug>` grammar of `am-cm-id-scheme-8bn`, on the control whose reveal answers it (the output `desynchronizationObserved`, reached by the moving-pair velocity control and by the preset `sr-01-moving-pair-0.6c`). Its question is "A pair of clocks rides past at a steady speed, and the riders set their clocks with the same light-signal rule. Judged by our clocks, what do theirs show?" It carries **three stable candidate ids**, which other beads cite instead of retyping the words:
  - `they-agree`: they agree with ours;
  - `leading-clock-ahead`: the leading clock is ahead;
  - `trailing-clock-ahead`: the trailing clock is ahead.

  The answer is `trailing-clock-ahead`, read from the accepted snapshot's `desynchronizationObserved` output and its sign, never from authored text, so the question and the reveal cannot drift. The question, the candidate labels, and the candidate descriptions contain no symbols, so a fifteen-minute tour may render them directly. `am-tour-15min-relativity-qcxc` step 3 cites this prompt id together with the preset `sr-01-moving-pair-0.6c` and supplies its own plain-words `tourPrediction` whose three `candidateId`s are exactly these three, each used once; citing the preset alone does not satisfy the `tour-instrument-step-missing-prompt` rule of `am-tours-infra-g518`. Journey III cites the same id rather than re-authoring the wording. The prediction is a tape `prediction` event; the explanation is available regardless, and nothing is scored.
- Show the code: the pinned source of `synchronizationRound` and `desynchronizationObserved`, identifiers colored like their equation terms, with identifier bindings for every live term.
- Tape model identity `sr-01@<modelVersion>`; commands classified as listed above; permalink `?tape=` with bounded size.
- Manifest sets `embeddable: true`; the rendered embed at `/embed/lab/sr-01` is exercised by `am-inst-embed-route-rnyg` and recorded at `am-dod-relativity-105y`.

### Result weave (predicate records owned here, targets from the §1-2 readings)

`threshold` and `agreement` predicates with hysteresis light the §1 criterion sentence when a pair satisfies it, the §1 constant sentence when the round-trip speed is shown, and the §2 sentence about observers moving with the rod when the chase legs or the moving pair's desynchronization are shown. Targets are sentence ids from the frozen inventory.

### Misconceptions addressed

"Time dilation is symmetric, so it cannot be real" (groundwork: simultaneity is procedure-relative); the network-latency confusion (the analogy stops because the effect is not a delay artifact).

## Technical Approach

- Manifest `content/experiments/sr-01.yaml` per `am-cm-schemas-experiment-fuu`; explicit dispatcher case; owner binding in `src/experiments/owners.ts`; instance-scoped owner from the runtime; views (planned `src/visuals/relativity/sr-01/`, location as frozen by the retrospective) consume only the accepted snapshot.
- The predict prompt lives in the manifest's `predictMode.prompts[]` entry with its `id`, its bound control, its question, and its three `{ candidateId, label, description }` candidates, so `am-tours-infra-g518`'s prompt binding resolves it from the compiled manifest and never from this bead's prose.
- The ledger is the canonical scientific state; the scene and diagram are projections. A change of the frame of description calls `redescribe` and never creates events.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The ledger implements the stated procedure; reception and remote-event times are distinct in every view; each clock's own reading at an event is unchanged by an observer change.
- [ ] Fixtures pass: emission 0 and reception 10 assign 5; emission 20 and reception 30 assign 25; a round trip over 10 ls gives speed $c$; §2 rod ends with $r_{AB} = 10$ ls and $u = 0.6c$ give legs of 25 s and 6.25 s; a pair with $L = 10$ ls at $0.6c$ is desynchronized by 6 s in the platform frame, trailing clock ahead; at $v = 0$ there is no desynchronization.
- [ ] An observer change leaves event ids, clock histories, and run identity unchanged.
- [ ] $\lvert v\rvert \ge c$ returns `outside-domain`; one-way speed returns `not-applicable`; malformed separations are refused with a reason.
- [ ] The exported `clock-event` parity cases of `am-inst-interaction-families-m2ps` (`src/experiments/interactions/parity.suite.ts`) run green in this bead's suite **against the real `events.ts`**, not against that bead's runtime-fixture evaluator, and the execution is cited by its `logRunId`. SR-01 does not close on fixture-only parity.
- [ ] Every view caption has R0-R3; every named preset exists and reproduces its stated values.
- [ ] The predict prompt `sr-01-predict-moving-pair` is registered in the manifest with the three stable candidate ids `they-agree`, `leading-clock-ahead`, and `trailing-clock-ahead`, is bound to the `desynchronizationObserved` control, resolves from the tour and from Journey III, reveals its answer from the accepted snapshot rather than authored text, and carries no symbols in its question, labels, or descriptions.
- [ ] Contract items present: `notModeled`, predict mode, show-the-code with bindings, tape identity, permalink, `embeddable: true`, action contract, 320 px, keyboard, reduced motion, honest label (`audit-instruments.ts` shows every column satisfied).
- [ ] The manifest declares the by-definition assumption with the source sentence id where §1 states it, verified against the pinned `ap-17-891` facsimile and the reviewed ledger.
- [ ] At least one alternative procedure is named in the manifest with its own stated assumption, and the slow-transport entry states the agreement as a limit of vanishing transport speed within one inertial frame, never as an exact equivalence at finite speed.
- [ ] The procedure-selection action exists in the visual, keyboard, and table routes and exposes identical text and the same event ledger in all three; it computes nothing and changes no execution label.
- [ ] No visitor-facing string on SR-01, its captions, its readings, or Journey III's synchronization stage asserts that only light can compare distant clocks. The voice lint fails each seeded phrase and passes the preferred phrasing.
- [ ] Claims about the status of the convention beyond §1's own statement appear only at R3 under the modern lens, inside a `lens` annotation with a date and an attribution, and the anachronism lint passes.

## Test Plan

### Unit and integration tests

- `sr-01.test.ts` (beside the instrument binding) against the real `events.ts`, never a mock, with `expectClose` (relative $10^{-12}$, absolute $10^{-12}$ s for zero offsets): every fixture above; offsets; transitivity of synchronization for three stations through `synchronizationTransitivity`, including its `not-applicable` result for stations in relative motion; sign of the desynchronization for $\pm v$; the chase legs from `movingRodLegs`; observer-change invariance of event ids, clock readings at events, and run id; each typed refusal and its reader-facing explanation.
- **Exported `clock-event` parity suite, run against the real owner.** `am-inst-interaction-families-m2ps` builds `EventSelector` in Batch D and can only prove it against a runtime-fixture event evaluator, because `am-ref-events-yvl` lands in Batch E. This bead is one of the two first consumers that re-run that bead's exported family parity suite, `src/experiments/interactions/parity.suite.ts`, parameterized with the real `events.ts`:
  - selecting the same two events by pointer and from the ledger table gives the same command hash, the same classification, and the same accepted snapshot id;
  - a frame change is an `observer-change` that keeps event ids, `runId`, `eventSetDigest`, and draw counters unchanged;
  - a near-equal pair inside `classifyWithTolerance`'s band reports `indeterminate`;
  - the exported case shared with SR-03: two events 10 light-seconds apart and simultaneous in K, described at $v = 0.6c$, give $\Delta t' = -7.5$ s and $\Delta x' = 12.5$ ls from `events.ts`, with the identities above unchanged.
  Every parity assertion logs `parityCaseId` and `ownerSource: events.ts`, so a run that silently fell back to the runtime fixture (`ownerSource: runtime-fixture`) is visible in the log and fails the suite.
- Property test over a fixed seeded list of 200 admissible configurations: the midpoint rule assigns $(t_A + t'_A)/2$; the criterion offset is zero after synchronization; the round-trip speed equals $c$ in the procedure's frame; redescribing to $v$ and back to 0 returns coordinates within tolerance.
- Adversarial: "changing observer starts a new experiment" must fail (identities compared before and after); "a camera image of the distant clock shows its coordinate time" must fail (reception time differs from the event time by the light travel time).
- Preset tests: each named preset scenario loads through the scenario runner and reproduces its values.
- **Predict-prompt test** (`sr-01.predictPrompt.test.ts`, against the compiled manifest): `sr-01-predict-moving-pair` resolves; its candidate ids are exactly `they-agree`, `leading-clock-ahead`, and `trailing-clock-ahead`, in that order and each declared once; a fixture manifest with two candidates, with a duplicated candidate id, or with an id outside the set fails validation; the prompt is bound to the `desynchronizationObserved` control, and a fixture binding it to a control the preset never commands fails the tour rule `tour-tape-does-not-reveal-prompt` when `sr-01-moving-pair-0.6c` is cited; the reveal is read from the accepted snapshot's `desynchronizationObserved` output (asserted by changing the sign of $v$ and seeing the settled candidate change from `trailing-clock-ahead` to `leading-clock-ahead`) rather than from a stored string; and `symbolScan` over the question, the three labels, and the three descriptions returns no tokens, so the tour may render them unchanged.
- Weave predicate tests on scripted snapshots: enter and exit with hysteresis; targets resolve to sentence ids.
- Caption audit: `audit-readings.ts` finds R0-R3 for every caption; manifest validation through `audit-instruments.ts`.
- `sr01.assumptions.test.ts`, against the real manifest and the real compiled source blocks: the by-definition assumption names a sentence id that resolves in `ap-17-891` §1; at least one alternative procedure is declared with a non-empty assumption line; the slow-transport entry's text contains the limit statement and does not assert equality at finite speed, with a seeded "is identical to" failing; a manifest with no alternative declared fails with `sr01-no-alternative-procedure`.
- `sr01.procedureAction.test.tsx`: the action appears in all three routes; selecting a procedure changes only the displayed note; `data-run-id`, `data-snapshot-version`, and `data-execution-label` are unchanged across every selection, and no worker message is sent.
- `voiceLint.integration.test.ts` (addition): the uniqueness rule set, with a failing fixture for each of "only light can", "light is the only way", "must use light", and "requires light" in this context, and a passing fixture for the preferred phrasing.
- `sr01.lens.test.ts`: a contemporary-perspective reading asserting a modern claim about the convention fails the anachronism lint, and the same claim inside an R3 `lens` with a date and an attribution passes.

### End-to-end tests

- Keyboard-only: set separation, emit a signal, select the reflection and reception rows, ask the simultaneity question in two frames; screen-reader announcements occur once per committed comparison.
- Answer `sr-01-predict-moving-pair` from the `sr-01-moving-pair-0.6c` preset, commit, and confirm the reveal shows the trailing clock 6 s ahead and that the tape's newest event is the `prediction` event carrying this `promptId` and the chosen `candidateId`.
- JavaScript disabled: the static worked ledger for the 0-5-10 case renders with its caption.
- In `e2e/instruments/sr-01.spec.ts`, through `am-test-e2e-harness-bqmh`: mount SR-01, read the assumption note, follow its link to the §1 sentence on the source face, and return through the return stack; use the procedure-selection action in the pointer route, then keyboard only, then through the table route, asserting identical text and identical event-ledger contents in all three; assert that `data-run-id` is unchanged across every selection, so choosing a procedure never restarts an experiment; scan the rendered page for the banned uniqueness phrases; repeat at 320 px, with reduced motion, and with JavaScript disabled, where the note is static and the procedure comparison is a real table.
- 320 px (no page overflow), WebKit, reduced motion; permalink restore reproduces the accepted snapshot id; two SR-01 instances on one page keep independent run ids; rapid typed changes never show an older result under newer labels.

### Structured logging

- Unit suite `instrument-sr-01` to `artifacts/test-logs/instrument-sr-01/<log-run-id>.jsonl` through the logging library: `timestamp`, `suite`, `logRunId`, `testId`, `beadId` (`am-sr-01-clock-sync-jbfn`), `paper`, `anchor`, `instrumentId`, `instanceId`, `runId` (the experiment run), `inputRevision`, `acceptedInputRevision`, `snapshotVersion`, `modelVersion`, `artifactDigest` (or the host evaluator's pinned source hash), `executionLabel`, `resultStatus`, `expected`, `actual`, `tolerance`, `comparisonKind`, `outcome`, `durationMs`, `message`, and `extra: {commandClass, scenarioId, eventIds, frameSpeed, parityCaseId, ownerSource, promptId, candidateId, procedureSelected, assumptionShown, sourceSentenceId, interface (pointer, keyboard, table, or no-js), bannedPhraseHits, rule}`. `seed` and `streamVersion` are omitted (closed-form, no random stream).
- Browser steps (through the harness) add `browser`, `viewport`, `reducedMotion`, `jsEnabled`, and `evidence`; a failing step retains screenshot, Playwright trace, DOM snapshot, console log, network log, and the accepted snapshot JSON. Evidence is kept under `artifacts/test-logs/instrument-sr-01/<log-run-id>/evidence/`.

## Considerations and Pitfalls

- A camera image of a distant clock shows an earlier reading than the coordinate time; never present the picture as the measurement.
- Moving the pair (physical) and changing the frame of description (observer) are different command classes and different labels.
- Near-equal times in a criterion check use an absolute tolerance, never a relative one.
- The parity suite proves the control, not the physics. A green parity run against the runtime fixture says nothing about `events.ts`; only the run recorded with `ownerSource: events.ts` counts toward closing.
- A candidate id is the stable thing other beads cite; the label is not. Rewording a label is an editorial change, but renaming a candidate id breaks every tour and journey that cites it and must be treated as a contract change.
- Keep the convention note bounded. The point is one sentence of honesty about why the paper chose light, plus one named alternative with its own assumption. A full treatment of synchronization conventions is a later-lens deep dive and does not belong in the instrument that teaches §1.
- The slow-transport statement is a limit, and the limit is the interesting part. Writing it as an exact equivalence at finite speed would be wrong, and writing it without the limit would make the alternative look like a free lunch.
- Do not turn this into a Journey III fork. That journey's forks are about what a reader in 1904 could have believed; this is about what a procedure assumes, and mixing them would put a methodological choice on the 1904 shelf.
- The paper's own word is the strongest evidence available, and it is in §1. Verify it on the facsimile before quoting it, and if the ledger's wording turns out weaker than expected, say what the paper does say and stop there.
- Nothing in the procedure note computes. The alternative is an authored note on the same accepted snapshot, and an implementation that added a second owner for slow transport would break the ownership rule for no reader benefit.

## Dependencies

Blocked by:
- `am-ref-events-yvl`: ledger, synchronization, chase, and desynchronization functions.
- `am-bm-slice-retrospective-pp09`: frozen instrument platform and runtime contracts.
- `am-inst-show-the-code-4brv`: the instrument contract requires a show-the-code disclosure pinned to the kernel source.
- `am-inst-predict-mode-ti7m`: predict mode, the prompt and candidate id shape this manifest fills in, and the verbal-candidate form.
- `am-inst-permalink-tape-s677`: the instrument contract requires bounded `?tape=` permalinks.
- `am-inst-interaction-families-m2ps`: the `EventSelector` primitive for choosing events and asking the simultaneity query, and its exported family parity suite `src/experiments/interactions/parity.suite.ts`, which this bead re-runs against the real `events.ts`.

Unblocks: `am-srk-e2e-4qkd`; `am-srk-first-encounter-471z` (the entrance opens SR-01 presets); `am-sr-results-cards-k9ck` (card probes); `am-disc-journey-iii-chain-hpr7` (the measurement-procedure stage, which cites `sr-01-predict-moving-pair` by id); `am-disc-essays-measurement-fixed-cb1i` (the essay anchors here); `am-tour-15min-relativity-qcxc` (step 3 cites `sr-01-predict-moving-pair` with the preset `sr-01-moving-pair-0.6c` and renders its three candidate ids in plain words).
