title: Run bounded cloud OCR drafts for ap-17-891, never locally
description:
# Run bounded cloud OCR drafts for ap-17-891, never locally

**Epic:** `am-ep-sources-zbs` · **Batch:** A · **Priority:** P1 · **Plan sections:** §4.4, §17.3;
AGENTS.md "Cloud OCR Only" (traceability only)

## Background

The reviewed German ledger for the relativity paper (introduction, part headings, and ten sections)
starts from machine drafts of the pinned page images. Drafts save editor time, but they are
**research evidence only**: every line that reaches the ledger is corrected by hand against the
facsimile, and every equation is retyped by the editor and compared directly with the page image.
Parsed PDF text layers, including any OCR layer a host embedded in the scan, are frequently
unreliable for these scans and are never accepted for an equation. At 31 pages this is the largest
run of the four papers, so budget and resumability matter most here.

An OCR run is a tool run: its artifact directory is `artifacts/ocr-runs/<key>/<tool-run-id>/`, the
receipt records the run as `transcription.ocrRuns[].toolRunId`, and a resumed run keeps that id
while each process writes its own `logRunId` in the log lines.

## Hard resource policy (binding, no exceptions)

- **Never run OCR on this machine.** Do not install, invoke, benchmark, resume, or monitor a local
OCR engine or daemon (`focr`, Tesseract, OCRmyPDF, vision transcription loops, a locally run
multimodal model, or anything that recognizes text from page pixels). Do not use local CPU, GPU,
NPU, or memory for OCR.
- Delegate every job to a cloud **GPT-5.6 Luna worker** through `am-src-ocr-orchestrator-u1e0` and
the cloud adapter (`am-src-ocr-cloud-adapter-7wa1`).
- If the worker or the cloud path is unavailable, **pause and report the blocker** (`br comments
add` on this bead with the error code and time, no secrets). There is no local fallback of any size.
- Bounded, checkpointed page ranges; preserve partial results after every chunk; limited concurrency
so results stay reviewable.
- Rendering page images locally for upload is allowed; recognizing text locally is not.

## Scope

In scope: confirming dispatch preconditions; planning, dispatching, checkpointing, and summarizing
cloud OCR for all 31 journal pages (891–921) of `ap-17-891`; a draft coverage report; updating the
provenance receipt's transcription method section and `transcription.ocrRuns`.

Out of scope: correcting the drafts (`am-src-ledger-relativity-sby`), inventorying blocks
(`am-edn-inventory-relativity-0u9`), and any change to the pinned facsimile.

## Requirements

1. **Preconditions** (checked and recorded before any submission): `docs/provenance/ap-17-891.md`
records `cloudProcessing: permitted` with its basis (`forbidden` blocks this bead and is reported;
`unknown` goes to the user and waits); `docs/OCR_DISPATCH.md` records the user's authorization for
paper runs and a spending cap that covers the estimated cost of 16 two-page chunks (the estimate is
recorded before dispatch); the adapter's smoke test record exists; the orchestrator and adapter test
suites pass on the current tree.
2. **Job plan** `scripts/sources/ocr-plans/ap-17-891.yaml`: `facsimileSha256` and `facsimilePath`
copied from the receipt (the orchestrator refuses a mismatch); `pdfPageRange` from the receipt's
page map (PDF page indices, not journal pages); `chunkSize` 2 (maximum 4); `maxConcurrency` 1, or 2
only if `docs/OCR_DISPATCH.md` allows it (never more); `cloudProcessing: permitted` with
`cloudProcessingBasisRef`; `render` at 300 dpi PNG; `instructionsVersion: v1`;
`expectedWorkerIdentity` from `docs/OCR_DISPATCH.md`; `expectedCounts` per PDF page from the
receipt's page map.
3. **Diplomatic draft instructions** (fixed in the orchestrator as
`scripts/sources/ocr-instructions/v1.md`, confirmed here, never edited per paper): keep original
spelling (for example `daß`) and punctuation; keep paragraph order; mark letter-spaced emphasis
`[[SPERR]]…[[/SPERR]]`, footnote marks `[[FN-MARK <label>]]`, footnote text `[[FN <label>]]`,
running heads `[[RUNNING-HEAD …]]`, and printed page numbers `[[PAGE-NUMBER …]]`; never modernize;
mark every mathematical region with `[[MATH-REGION page=n]]` plus a best-effort LaTeX draft flagged
`unverified`; write `[[ILLEGIBLE]]` instead of guessing.
4. **Mathematics in this paper** needs particular care: primes and the Greek coordinates $\xi, \eta,
\zeta, \tau$; the §3 auxiliary $x' = x - vt$, which is not the moving-frame coordinate; $\beta$ as
defined in §3; the Gaussian field components $X, Y, Z, L, M, N$ in §6; many fractions with $V$; the
§5 addition formulas; the §7 Doppler and aberration formulas and the §8 energy relations, which are
printed with explicit radicals $\sqrt{1-(v/V)^2}$; and the §10 electron equations and mass
expressions, where the electron's mass is $\mu$. These drafts are never trusted; the ledger editor
retypes them.
5. **Run order.** First `--dry-run` (plan validation, digest and rights checks, rendering, no
submission). Then submit the first chunk alone and inspect the returned draft for format only (every
page returned, markers used as instructed, nothing modernized, no text invented in blank regions);
if the format is wrong, stop and report rather than tuning instructions per paper. Then run the
remaining chunks. Any interruption is resumed with `--resume <tool-run-id>` and recorded; a
completed chunk is never resubmitted without a logged reason.
6. **Checkpoints** in `artifacts/ocr-runs/ap-17-891/<tool-run-id>/` (gitignored): one Markdown file
per PDF page under `pages/` and `run.jsonl`. Resume after interruption without resubmitting
completed chunks.
7. **Draft coverage report** `artifacts/ocr-runs/ap-17-891/<tool-run-id>/coverage.json`: every PDF
page in range has a draft; per-page counts of `[[MATH-REGION`, `[[FN-MARK`, and `[[ILLEGIBLE]]` are
compared with `expectedCounts`, and mismatches are listed for the ledger editor, never
auto-corrected.
8. **Receipt update** (`docs/provenance/ap-17-891.md`): add the run to `transcription.ocrRuns`
(`toolRunId`, adapter, reported worker identity and model, job ids, page range, start and finish
times, summary path) and replace the pending transcription-method text with the orchestrator's
`receipt-block.md`, including image digests, instructions version, renderer version, failures,
retries, cost units where reported, and the statement that drafts are research evidence only. The
receipt checker must still pass.

## Technical Approach

`bun scripts/ocr-ledgers.ts --plan scripts/sources/ocr-plans/ap-17-891.yaml --dry-run`, then the
first chunk, then the full run with `OCR_ADAPTER` set to the documented adapter, `--resume
<tool-run-id>` after any interruption, and `--summarize <tool-run-id>` for `summary.json`,
`coverage.json`, and `receipt-block.md`. If the adapter configuration is missing, authorization is
absent, the budget cap would be exceeded, or the service reports an outage, stop, record the blocker
on this bead, and wait; do not substitute anything local.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The preconditions are recorded in the close reason: `cloudProcessing: permitted` with basis,
recorded authorization, the cost estimate within the cap, and passing test suites.
- [ ] Every PDF page of `ap-17-891` in the mapped range has a cloud draft checkpoint from the
reported Luna worker identity.
- [ ] The first-chunk format check is recorded; any interruption was resumed into the same
`<tool-run-id>` directory with zero unlogged resubmissions.
- [ ] The coverage report exists, and every math-region, footnote, and illegible-count mismatch
against the page map is listed.
- [ ] The receipt records the run in `transcription.ocrRuns` with its `toolRunId` and the method
section, and `bun scripts/check-receipts.ts --key ap-17-891` reports no errors.
- [ ] The orchestrator's OCR guard test passes on the tree at the time of the run.
- [ ] No local OCR process was started at any point, and no draft text was copied into the ledger,
edition, or translation by this bead.

## Test Plan

### Unit and integration tests
- Before dispatch, run `bun test scripts/ocr-ledgers.test.ts scripts/ocr-guard.test.ts
scripts/ocr-adapters/` and record the result in the close reason.
- `bun scripts/ocr-ledgers.ts --plan scripts/sources/ocr-plans/ap-17-891.yaml --dry-run` confirms
the digest match, the rights determination, the chunk limits, and the rendering of all 31 pages
before any submission.
- After the run, `bun scripts/check-receipts.ts --key ap-17-891` passes.

### End-to-end tests
- The full run is the pipeline test on real data: dry run, first-chunk format check, dispatch,
checkpoint, resume if interrupted, summarize, coverage. The close reason lists the `toolRunId`, the
chunk count (16 at chunk size 2), submission counts per chunk, cumulative cost units, and the
evidence paths.

### Structured logging
- `run.jsonl` fields: `timestamp`, `suite`, `logRunId`, `toolRunId`, `beadId`, `key`, `planPath`,
`facsimileSha256`, `chunkIndex`, `pdfPages`, `renderer`, `rendererVersion`, `dpi`, `imageSha256`,
`textSha256`, `instructionsVersion`, `adapter`, `workerIdentity`, `jobId`, `status`, `retry`,
`costUnits`, `errorCode`, `exitCode`, `message`, `durationMs`. No credentials. The coverage report,
summary, and log path are cited in the receipt.

## Considerations and Pitfalls

- OCR confidence is not correctness; a clean-looking draft still gets line-by-line correction.
- Letter-spaced emphasis and ligatures in 1905 roman type confuse recognition; mark them rather than
guess.
- Running heads and page numbers belong to the ledger's page anchors, never inside paragraphs.
- Keep drafts out of git; the receipt records their existence and digests.
- A draft may silently "modernize" $V$ to $c$, $\mu$ to $m$, or radicals to $\beta$ or $\gamma$; the
coverage report cannot detect that, so the ledger editor retypes every region from the image.
- Never tune the fixed instructions to this paper.

## Dependencies

Blocked by:
- `am-src-facsimile-relativity-kav`: the pinned bytes, SHA-256, page map, and `cloudProcessing`
determination.
- `am-src-ocr-orchestrator-u1e0`: bounded, checkpointed orchestration that cannot run OCR locally.
- `am-src-ocr-cloud-adapter-7wa1`: the working, authorized adapter.

Unblocks:
- `am-src-ledger-relativity-sby`: the hand-corrected diplomatic ledger starts from these drafts.

title: Define the provenance receipt format, its machine-readable front matter, and the receipt checker
description:
# Define the provenance receipt format, its machine-readable front matter, and the receipt checker

**Epic:** `am-ep-sources-zbs` · **Batch:** A · **Priority:** P0 · **Plan sections:** §3.1, §3.2,
§4.3, §11.2, §17.2, §17.3 (traceability only)

## Background

A provenance receipt, `docs/provenance/<key>.md`, is written before any editorial copy and then
extended by many beads: the facsimile beads write identity, scan, rights, page map, witnesses, and
the transcription watch list; the inventory beads refine the page map; the OCR beads add the
transcription method; the ledger beads add correction editors, the typographical-error register, and
the ledger status; the translation beads add credits; the review beads add acceptance through
`am-edit-review-records-hofz`, which renders the "editorial acceptance" section from review records;
`am-design-sources-about-zumd` compiles receipts into `/sources` and checks digests at build time;
`am-cm-audit-scripts-d34` checks that every referenced asset is present; and
`am-rel-release-manifest-3gna` records source-asset hashes.

Without one format every writer invents structure, parsers break, and fields drift. Before this
bead, each facsimile bead planned its own interim `docs/provenance/receiptShape.test.ts` (several
beads owning one deliverable) and cited a receipt check that `am-cm-source-manifest-6qa` does not
provide. This bead owns the single format, the checker, the survey-record check, and a safe writer
for generated sections.

The receipt is also read by the product, not only by auditors. `am-read-facsimile-face-er0` opens
the pinned PDF at the page a reader asks for, and it resolves that page from this file's `pageMap`;
`am-design-sources-about-zumd` renders the terms, witnesses, and typographical-error register on
`/sources`. A page map that cannot answer "which PDF page prints equation (1) of §4" is therefore a
reader-facing defect, not only a bookkeeping one, which is why the page map records section ids,
printed equation labels, and (after the inventory beads refine it) the ids of unnumbered display
equations.

## Scope

In scope:
- `docs/editorial/RECEIPT_FORMAT.md`: the normative format with a complete example receipt for the
fictional key `ap-99-001`.
- `src/content/provenance/receiptSchema.ts` (zod), `parseReceipt.ts`, `checkReceipt.ts`,
`receiptToSourceAsset.ts`, `writeGeneratedSection.ts`, and `surveySchema.ts`.
- The CLI `scripts/check-receipts.ts`.
- Fixtures, tests, and JSONL logging.

Out of scope: writing real receipts (the beads above); the `SourceAsset` and `Paper` schemas
(`am-cm-schemas-source-1en`, whose field names this format uses); rendering `/sources`
(`am-design-sources-about-zumd`); review records (`am-edit-review-records-hofz`); wiring the CLI
into CI (`am-scaf-quality-gates-ci-4xx`).

## Requirements

1. **Location and kinds.** Facsimile receipts live at `docs/provenance/<key>.md` with `key` matching
`ap-<volume>-<first page>`. Front matter declares `receiptKind`. This bead implements
`facsimile-scan` and an extension point; other kinds (for example the observation-sequence receipts
of `am-later-real-brownian-sequence-o6l3`) register their own schemas through it. Survey records
live at `docs/provenance/survey/<key>.md` and are validated by `surveySchema.ts`.
2. **Front matter** (YAML between `---` lines) for `facsimile-scan`:
   - `receiptFormatVersion: 1`, `receiptKind`, `key`, `slug`.
   - `paper`: `titleGerman`, `titleEnglishWorking`, `authorLine`, and `dates[]`, each `{ type,
   text?, iso, precision: day | month | year, source, verifiedAt, confirmedFromScan }`, where `type`
   uses the `Paper` date types specified in `am-cm-schemas-source-1en`: `date-line`, `received`,
   `issue-publication`, `submitted`, `later-edition`. `journal`: `{ name, series: 4, volume,
   wholeSeriesVolume, issue, issueSource, pages: { first, last }, doi, doiVerifiedAt,
   laterEditionDois: [{ doi, description, verifiedAt }] }`. `collectedPapers`: `{ volume, document
   }`.
   - `scan`: the download script's receipt-stub fields (`originUrl`, `finalUrl`, `institution`,
   `hostItemId`, `hostFileName`, `hostFileSource`, `hostChecksumsVerified`, `termsStatementUrls`,
   `acquisitionDate`, `sha256`, `mimeType`, `pageCount`, `parent?` with `sha256`, `pageCount`,
   `path`, `parentPageIndices`, `embeddedTextLayer`, `rightsStatus`, `publicationDecision`,
   `publicationReason?`, `cloudProcessing`, `cloudProcessingBasis`, `reuseTerms`, `credit?`, `path`,
   `downloadLog`) plus `termsStatements: [{ url, retrievedAt, text }]` with the terms quoted verbatim. `downloadLog` is
   the pinning run's tool log, `artifacts/facsimile-logs/<key>/<tool-run-id>.jsonl`, so the receipt
   names the exact run that produced the digest. `reuseTerms` and `credit` are the two fields
   `am-src-rights-policy-1dp` adds to the rights vocabulary, written in the receipt's flat spelling of
   the `rights.` block exactly as `rightsStatus` carries `rights.status`: `reuseTerms` is one of
   `pending-decision`, `named-license`, `source-terms`, or `no-reuse-offered`, and `credit` names the
   archive, the photographer where known, and the date. The receipt and the schema use identical field
   names, so a vocabulary field the receipt omitted would leave `receiptToSourceAsset` unable to
   produce a complete `publish` asset.
   - `pageMap[]`: `{ pdfPageIndex, printedPage, contents[], sectionIds[], displayEquations: {
   numbered: [labels], unnumbered: count, unnumberedIds?: [ids] }, footnoteMarks: [labels],
   refinedBy? }`, one entry per PDF page of the pinned file, with `pdfPageIndex` 1-based to match
   the viewer. `contents[]` uses a closed set so five facsimile beads cannot invent five
   vocabularies: `front-matter`, `usage-notice`, `masthead`, `article-text`, `other-article`,
   `plate`, `back-matter`. Pages that belong to other articles in an issue extract use `contents:
   [other-article]` and carry no `sectionIds`. At pinning time `displayEquations.unnumbered` is a
   count, because ids are allocated later; when an inventory bead refines an entry it sets
   `refinedBy` to its bead id and replaces the count with `unnumberedIds` (`eq-s<n>-d<j>` ids in
   printed order), so the facsimile face can resolve an unnumbered-equation anchor to a page.
   - `witnesses[]`: `{ kind: collected-papers | augsburg | wikisource | historical-translation |
   other, identity, url?, revisionId?, availability: available | not-found, checkedAt, rightsStatus,
   notes }`.
   - `transcription`: `{ ocrRuns: [{ toolRunId, adapter, workerIdentity, model, jobIds,
   pdfPageRange, startedAt, finishedAt, summaryPath }], ledgerPath?, ledgerSha256?,
   ledgerSourcePdfSha256?, ledgerScopePages?, printingProvenance?, ledgerStatus: not-started |
   in-progress | corrected | corrected-second-read | reviewed, editors: [{ name, role, pages, dates
   }] }`. `toolRunId` is the OCR run's `<tool-run-id>` in the timestamp-plus-hex form of AGENTS.md;
   a resumed OCR run keeps its `toolRunId` while each process writes its own `logRunId` log, so one
   receipt entry covers a resumed run. `ledgerScopePages` lists the PDF page indices a scoped ledger
   covers (the dissertation); when absent, the article pages of `pageMap` define the ledger scope.
   `printingProvenance` is `[{ item, kind: passage | numerical-input, printing, pdfPageIndex,
   printedPage, notes }]`, used where several printings of one work supply passages or numbers.
   - `typographicalErrors[]`: `{ id, locator: { pdfPageIndex, printedPage, line? }, originalReading,
   proposedReading, reasoning, evidence, layer: source | translation, recordedBy, recordedAt }`.
   - `watchList[]`: `{ id, item, expectedCheck, result: pending | matches | differs | not-found,
   notes, checkedBy?, checkedAt? }`.
   - `pending[]`: `{ section, owner }` naming the bead that will write each pending section.
3. **Body sections**, as Markdown headings in this order: `## Identity`, `## Scan and rights`, `##
Page map`, `## Comparison witnesses`, `## Transcription method`, `## Translation credits`, `##
Editorial boundaries`, `## Suspected historical typographical errors`, `## Transcription watch
list`, `## Editorial acceptance`. A pending section contains exactly the line `Status: pending
(owner: <bead id>)`. The editorial acceptance content sits between `<!--
generated:editorial-acceptance:start -->` and `<!-- generated:editorial-acceptance:end -->` and is
written only through `writeGeneratedSection`.
4. **Checker errors:**
   - schema: missing or unknown top-level keys for the kind; `key` not matching the filename;
   `journal.pages.first` not equal to the key's first page; `sha256`, `parent.sha256`, or
   `ledgerSourcePdfSha256` not lowercase 64-character hex; an untyped or unparseable date; an
   invalid DOI; a missing `verifiedAt` or `doiVerifiedAt`; an `ocrRuns[].toolRunId` that is not in
   the `<tool-run-id>` timestamp-plus-hex form, or two `ocrRuns` entries sharing one `toolRunId`;
   - chronology, compared at the coarser of the two precisions: `received` before `date-line`, or
   `issue-publication` before `received`;
   - rights: values not in `docs/rights-vocabulary.yaml`, or a violated vocabulary constraint,
   including a `reuseTerms` outside the four values, a `public-domain-image` or `cleared-image`
   without `credit`, a `named-license` without `rights.source`, and a `publicationDecision` other than
   `publish` whose `reuseTerms` is not `no-reuse-offered`; a
   `publish` asset whose `scan.path` is not under `public/papers/pdfs/`; a `pin-local-only` asset
   whose path is not under `sources/pinned/`;
   - consistency: the `scan` block disagreeing with `scripts/sources/facsimile-sources/<key>.yaml`
   `pinned` (`sha256`, `pageCount`, `originUrl`, `acquisitionDate`, rights fields); a receipt
   claiming a pin with no configuration record; a present pinned file whose SHA-256 differs;
   `ledgerSourcePdfSha256` present and not equal to `scan.sha256`;
   - page map: not covering PDF pages 1 to `pageCount` exactly once; a `contents[]` value outside
   the closed set; an `other-article` page carrying `sectionIds`; article pages whose printed pages
   fall outside the paper's range or decrease; a refined entry (`refinedBy` set) that still carries
   `displayEquations.unnumbered` instead of `unnumberedIds`, or an `unnumberedIds` list whose length
   disagrees with the count it replaced;
   - witnesses: no `collected-papers` entry, or no `wikisource` entry (an entry with `availability:
   not-found` satisfies the rule);
   - body: headings missing or out of order; a malformed pending line; generated markers missing,
   duplicated, or unbalanced;
   - status: `ledgerStatus: reviewed` without a German source review record in the editorial
   acceptance section; `ledgerStatus: reviewed` while any `watchList` entry is still `pending`, so a
   ledger cannot be called reviewed while a printed reading it depends on is unchecked; a
   typographical-error entry without `evidence`.
5. **Checker flags** (reported, not failing): pending sections; watch-list items still `pending`
while `ledgerStatus` is below `reviewed`; a `pin-local-only` file or parent absent on this machine
(`not-available`, which becomes an error with `--require-local`, and never passes silently).
6. **SourceAsset mapping.** `receiptToSourceAsset(receipt)` maps front matter to `SourceAsset`
fields (`originUrl`, `acquisitionDate`, `sha256`, `mimeType`, `pageCount`, `pageMapping` from
`pageMap`, `rights.status`, `rights.statement` from `termsStatements`, `rights.source`,
`rights.recordedAt`, `publicationDecision`, `publicationReason`, `cloudProcessing`,
`cloudProcessingBasis`, `rights.reuseTerms` from `reuseTerms`, `rights.credit` from `credit`,
`parentSha256`, `parentPageIndices`), so the compiler and `/sources` derive
records from the receipt instead of retyping them. The mapping is documented in `RECEIPT_FORMAT.md`.
Without those two fields the function cannot produce a complete `publish` asset, because
`rights.reuseTerms` is required on every asset a reader can take away and `rights.credit` on every
published image.
7. **Survey records.** `surveySchema.ts` checks the front matter defined by `am-src-scan-survey-sqnu`:
required keys; each candidate has `termsStatements` or `termsNotFound`; proposed classifications use
vocabulary values and respect constraints; the recommendation names existing candidates; every
`unknown` classification appears in `openQuestionsForUser`.
8. **Generated sections.** `writeGeneratedSection(path, sectionId, content)` replaces only the text
between the named markers, refuses when markers are missing or duplicated, preserves every other
byte, and writes through a temporary file and rename.
9. **CLI.** `bun scripts/check-receipts.ts [--key <key>] [--surveys] [--require-local]` exits
non-zero on errors, prints flags separately, and emits JSONL diagnostics.

## Technical Approach

- Parse YAML front matter with the YAML library locked by `am-gov-decision-stack-versions-6ax`; scan
Markdown headings line by line (no Markdown renderer).
- Build the rights enums and constraints from `docs/rights-vocabulary.yaml` at load time. Define the
date-type enum locally with exactly the names specified for `Paper` in `am-cm-schemas-source-1en`;
when that schema lands, it imports or asserts equality with these types rather than defining
different ones. The same applies to the `contents[]` vocabulary: it is defined here and imported by
the schemas bead, never redefined.
- Keep chronology comparison precision-aware: `1905-05` (month) is not earlier than `1905-05-11`
(day).
- Validate `toolRunId` with the shared helper from the logging standard
(`am-test-logging-standard-l3cp`) once it exists, so the receipt and the logs agree on the id form;
until then, keep one local regular expression with the standard named beside it.
- Fixtures under `src/testing/fixtures/provenance/`, including a miniature
`scripts/sources/facsimile-sources/` tree for consistency checks.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `RECEIPT_FORMAT.md` specifies every field and heading with a complete example that passes the
checker.
- [ ] The schema, parser, checker, mapping function, generated-section writer, survey schema, and
CLI exist.
- [ ] Every error rule in requirement 4 has a failing fixture, and every flag in requirement 5 has a
flagged fixture.
- [ ] `writeGeneratedSection` preserves all bytes outside the markers and refuses malformed markers.
- [ ] `receiptToSourceAsset` output matches a committed golden file.
- [ ] The front matter carries `reuseTerms` and `credit`, and `receiptToSourceAsset` maps them to
`rights.reuseTerms` and `rights.credit`, so a `publish` fixture yields a complete `SourceAsset`.
- [ ] Survey front matter is validated.
- [ ] The `contents[]` vocabulary and the page-map refinement rule are documented, and a refined
fixture resolves an unnumbered-equation id to a PDF page.

## Test Plan

### Unit and integration tests
`src/content/provenance/receipt.test.ts` against real code and committed fixtures:
- the valid example `ap-99-001.md` passes, and `receiptToSourceAsset` equals
`ap-99-001.source-asset.golden.json`;
- a second valid fixture uses the Brownian paper's plan values (date-line "Bern, Mai 1905" with
precision month, received 1905-05-11, issue publication 1905-07-18, pages 549–560, DOI
`10.1002/andp.19053220806`) to prove month-precision chronology passes;
- a third valid fixture is a refined page map: an entry with `refinedBy` and
`unnumberedIds: ["eq-s4-d1", "eq-s4-d2"]`, and a helper case that resolves `eq-s4-d2` to its
`pdfPageIndex`;
- one failing fixture per error: `ap-99-002.md` containing key `ap-99-001`; an uppercase digest; a
63-character digest; an untyped date; received 1905-07-18 with publication 1905-05-11; received
before the date-line; an invalid DOI; a rights status absent from the vocabulary;
`scan-terms-restrict-redistribution` with `publish`; a `publish` path outside `public/papers/pdfs/`;
a scan digest that disagrees with the fixture configuration; a receipt that claims a pin with no
configuration; a page map missing page 3 of 4; a duplicated page; decreasing printed pages; a
`contents` value `frontmatter` outside the closed set; an `other-article` page carrying
`sectionIds`; a refined entry that still carries `unnumbered`; an `unnumberedIds` list shorter than
the count it replaced; no `wikisource` witness entry; headings out of order; a malformed pending
line; unbalanced generated markers; `ledgerStatus: reviewed` without an acceptance record;
`ledgerStatus: reviewed` with a `pending` watch-list entry; `ledgerSourcePdfSha256` differing from
`scan.sha256`; a typographical-error entry without evidence; an `ocrRuns[].toolRunId` of
`run-1` (wrong form); two `ocrRuns` entries with the same `toolRunId`;
- the vocabulary's two added rights fields: a valid fixture carrying `reuseTerms: source-terms` with
its quoted statement, and a `public-domain-image` fixture carrying `credit`, both map through
`receiptToSourceAsset` to `rights.reuseTerms` and `rights.credit`; a fifth `reuseTerms` value, a
`pin-local-only` scan whose `reuseTerms` is `named-license`, and a `public-domain-image` without
`credit` each fail;
- flags: a pending section; a pending watch-list item under `ledgerStatus: in-progress`; an absent
local-only file reported `not-available`, and an error under `--require-local`;
- `writeGeneratedSection`: replaces the section; the SHA-256 of the bytes before and after the
markers is unchanged; missing markers and two start markers are refused;
- survey schema: a valid survey passes; a candidate with neither terms nor `termsNotFound` fails; a
proposed status outside the vocabulary fails; a recommendation naming a missing candidate fails; an
`unknown` classification absent from `openQuestionsForUser` fails.

### End-to-end tests
- `scripts/check-receipts.e2e.test.ts` runs the CLI through Bun's process API over the fixture
directory and asserts exit 1 with the expected set of rule codes in JSONL, exit 0 on the valid
subset, `--require-local` escalation, and `--surveys` coverage. On failure it retains stdout,
stderr, and the JSONL log under `artifacts/test-logs/receipts/<log-run-id>/evidence/`, and a
deliberately failing case in a test-only variant proves that the evidence is written.

### Structured logging
JSON lines (through the `am-test-logging-standard-l3cp` library once it exists) to
`artifacts/test-logs/receipts/<log-run-id>.jsonl`: `timestamp`, `suite: "receipts"`, `logRunId`,
`testId`, `beadId`, `key`, `receiptPath`, `rule`, `severity`, `path` (field path), `expected`,
`actual`, `outcome`, `message`, `repair`.

## Considerations and Pitfalls

- One format, many writers: extend it only by a versioned change to `RECEIPT_FORMAT.md` and the
schema, never with ad hoc headings.
- The generated editorial acceptance section is never edited by hand.
- Date comparisons must respect precision, or month-precision date-lines will fail spuriously.
- The receipt and the download configuration record the same pin; the checker compares them so
neither drifts.
- `toolRunId` names a pipeline run (an OCR job set), `logRunId` names one execution of a test suite,
and `runId` is reserved for an experiment realization. A receipt never carries a `runId`.
- Receipts are compiled into public pages: no secrets, no personal data beyond reviewer names as
they wish to be credited.
- A local-only asset is flagged, not failed, on machines that do not hold it, and it never passes
silently.

## Dependencies

Blocked by:
- `am-scaf-nextjs-app-bu2`: Bun, TypeScript, and the test runner.
- `am-src-rights-policy-1dp`: the rights vocabulary and constraints.

Unblocks:
- `am-src-facsimile-light-quanta-t4n`, `am-src-facsimile-brownian-mox`,
`am-src-facsimile-relativity-kav`, `am-src-facsimile-mass-energy-cat`,
`am-src-facsimile-dissertation-2mp`: receipts are written in this format and must pass the checker.
- `am-edit-review-records-hofz`: writes the generated editorial acceptance section.
- `am-design-sources-about-zumd`: compiles receipts through the parser and mapping.
- `am-cm-schemas-source-1en`: imports the rights vocabulary, the `Paper` date types, and the
`contents[]` vocabulary rather than defining competing enums.
- `am-edn-ledger-validator-edv`: the validator emits `ledgerSha256` and `ledgerSourcePdfSha256`,
which this format records and checks against `scan.sha256`.
- `am-edn-alignment-tooling-do1`: the edition test harness reads `ledgerScopePages` and the page map
to bind segments to printed pages.
- `am-read-facsimile-face-er0`: the facsimile face resolves section and equation anchors to PDF
pages through `pageMap`.
- `am-design-papers-index-afnu`: `/papers` reads typed dates, journal identity, and the companion
flag from the receipts.

title: Write the rights and attribution policy and the SourceAsset rights vocabulary
description:
# Write the rights and attribution policy and the SourceAsset rights vocabulary

**Epic:** `am-ep-sources-zbs` · **Batch:** A (start immediately; only the closed repository
bootstrap precedes it) · **Priority:** P0 · **Plan sections:** §4.1, §4.2, §4.6, §11.2
(`SourceAsset`), §20 (traceability only)

## Background

The site will publish a German source edition, a new English translation, new explanatory prose,
interactive code, fonts, figures, and digitized historical datasets, and it will pin scans made by
third-party institutions. Each of these has a different rights basis. The plan's central rule is
that **rights layers stay separate**: a license for code never grants rights to an embedded scan,
dataset, or translation, and a host's possession of a scan is not itself a rights determination.
Without a written policy and a controlled vocabulary, agents surveying and acquiring facsimiles and
datasets will make inconsistent, undocumented calls, cloud OCR jobs may send page images that a
scan's terms do not allow to be processed, and the `/sources` page will not be able to say honestly
what may be reused.

Real candidate scans show why the vocabulary must be precise. Library and archive copies of *Annalen
der Physik* 1905 exist as Google-digitized whole volumes, whose PDFs typically carry a usage notice
inside the file, and as microfilm-derived items whose host metadata names the journal's present-day
commercial publisher. Host metadata may also carry a copyright-status flag for the underlying work.
None of these is, by itself, a license statement for the scan file, and each must be classified from
the terms actually stated.

The same separation has a reader-facing consequence that nothing else in the graph resolves. A
teacher who wants to reuse one figure or embed one instrument needs to know which assets may be
reused and on what terms, and that answer is per asset, because the rights layers are per asset.
`am-design-sources-about-zumd` publishes the edition-level "how to cite" and the public rights
summary, and `am-inst-embed-route-rnyg` gives an embed its attribution footer and link back, but
attribution is not a grant and an edition-level statement cannot speak for a third-party scan. The
per-asset reuse terms recorded here are what those surfaces read.

This bead produces that policy before any asset is surveyed, pinned, or sent to a cloud service. It
is an editorial and conservative policy, not a legal opinion, and it says so.

## Scope

In scope:
- `docs/RIGHTS.md`: the rights and attribution policy, including the "How to record an asset"
checklist and a dated decision log.
- A controlled vocabulary for four determinations on every `SourceAsset`: `rights.status`,
`publicationDecision`, `cloudProcessing`, and `rights.reuseTerms`, documented in `docs/RIGHTS.md` and
mirrored as the data file `docs/rights-vocabulary.yaml`. The file sits under `docs/` rather than
`content/` because it is not a content record: the content compiler validates every file under
`content/` against a record schema. `am-cm-schemas-source-1en` imports this file for its enums.
- The attribution rules for comparison witnesses, secondary literature, letters, and photographs.
- The per-asset reuse-terms rule for figures and instrument embeds.

Out of scope (owned elsewhere): the final license and rider decision for new code and prose
(`am-gov-decision-license-rights-tps`, a user decision, which supplies the terms for site-original
assets); schema code and the executable vocabulary test (`am-cm-schemas-source-1en`); the receipt
file format (`am-src-receipt-format-npo5`); the public `/sources` and `/about` pages and the
edition-level "how to cite" (`am-design-sources-about-zumd`, which renders the recorded terms and
never invents them); the embed route and its attribution footer (`am-inst-embed-route-rnyg`); dataset
digitization (`am-inst-dataset-overlay-ra9r` and the `data-*` beads); the OCR service's own
data-handling terms (`am-src-ocr-dispatch-interface-m1ur`).

## Requirements

### Policy content (`docs/RIGHTS.md`)

1. **Historical German text.** The four papers (1905), the dissertation (published in *Annalen* in
1906), and Einstein's correction (1911) are public domain: in the United States by publication date
(as of 2026, works published in 1930 or earlier are public domain, because the 95-year term for 1930
expired at the end of 2025; recheck at publication) and in life-plus-70 jurisdictions because
Einstein died in 1955 (the term expired at the end of 2025). The German text may be transcribed,
reproduced, and translated freely.
2. **Scans are not the text.** A scan file may carry the scanning institution's terms. For every
pinned scan record: source URL, every stated terms statement quoted verbatim with its URL (the item
page, the host's general terms, and any notice embedded in the file itself, such as a usage-notice
page at the front of a Google-digitized PDF), retrieval date, and SHA-256. Prefer library or archive
scans with open terms (Internet Archive, HathiTrust full view, a university digital library). Never
pin a publisher PDF served under a subscription license. Host metadata that describes the copyright
status of the underlying work (for example a "not in copyright" flag) is not a license for the scan.
A microfilm-derived item whose metadata names the journal's current commercial publisher is not a
publisher PDF, and that metadata does not establish open terms either: classify it from its stated
terms, and use `scan-terms-unknown` until they are found.
3. **Existing English translations are not reused.**
   - Perrett and Jeffery (Methuen, 1923; Dover reprint; the Fourmilab electronic text derives from
   it and changes notation) and A. D. Cowper's translation of the Brownian papers (Methuen, 1926,
   ed. R. Fürth; Dover 1956) are public domain in the United States by publication date, but their
   status elsewhere depends on the translators' death dates, and the site is served worldwide.
   - The Beck translations (Princeton, 1989) and the Arons–Peppard translation of paper 1 (Am. J.
   Phys., 1965) are in copyright.
   - **Policy:** the site publishes its own translation made from the German and cites historical
   translations only as attributed comparison witnesses in the provenance receipt. This is the
   conservative editorial choice, not a legal opinion, and it produces a better product because a
   sentence-aligned translation must be built from the German anyway.
4. **Comparison witnesses** (the Collected Papers transcriptions and notes, the Augsburg facsimiles,
German Wikisource, historical translations) are consulted and cited, never copied into the ledger,
edition, translation, or notes. Machine-readable witness text may be loaded into a gitignored
working file under `artifacts/` solely to list candidate differences; it is never committed, and
every difference is resolved against the facsimile.
5. **Secondary literature**: short attributed phrases only; everything else paraphrased with
citation.
6. **Letters**: the Habicht letter and other correspondence are paraphrased, never reproduced. The
Collected Papers transcriptions and translations are Princeton's editorial work.
7. **Photographs.** Public-domain photographs of Einstein may be used anywhere on the site,
including the home page, share cards, and the timeline, with an accurate source credit naming the
holding archive, the photographer where known, and the date or approximate date. The placeholder
identified in planning is Lucien Chavan's patent-office portrait of about 1905 (ETH-Bibliothek
Zürich, Bildarchiv, Portr_05937), to be confirmed at use with the archive record and its terms for
the scan file. The credit is a required field, not a courtesy: an image asset without one fails the
vocabulary constraint below.
8. **Name and likeness**: no restriction. The owner decided on 2026-09-14 that this free,
open-source site may use Einstein's name and public-domain likeness freely; the decision is recorded
here and in `am-gov-decision-license-rights-tps`. Do not add caveats about name or likeness
restrictions, and do not reintroduce a no-photograph or year-only-branding rule.
9. **Rights layers**: separate policies for original historical text, facsimile scans, the new
translation, new explanatory prose, interactive code, numerical libraries, fonts, images, and
historical datasets. Preserve inherited notices from Classic Patents and FrankenSim, including their
rider language. The license and rider for new code and prose are decided intentionally before
publication (`am-gov-decision-license-rights-tps`); until then `LICENSE` (MIT with the
OpenAI/Anthropic rider) covers code and new prose only.
10. **Datasets**: a digitized historical dataset records the publication it comes from, the table or
figure number, the digitizer, and the rights status of the published figure or table.
11. **Machine processing of scans.** Sending page images to a cloud OCR service is a use distinct
from publishing. Every pinned scan records a `cloudProcessing` determination with its basis quoted
from the stated terms. Only `permitted` scans are sent; the orchestrator
(`am-src-ocr-orchestrator-u1e0`) refuses anything else, and every `src-ocr-*` bead checks the
receipt before dispatch. `unknown` is escalated to the user (the owner of
`am-gov-decision-license-rights-tps`) and never resolved by an agent's guess. The service's own
retention and training terms are recorded separately in `docs/OCR_DISPATCH.md`; a scan whose terms
forbid third-party processing is never sent, whatever the service promises. OCR itself never runs on
this machine (AGENTS.md, "Cloud OCR Only").
12. **Embedded third-party text layers.** Many library scans embed the host's own OCR as an
invisible text layer. That text is third-party machine output: it is never a transcription source,
never accepted for an equation, never shown to readers as the edition's text, and never extracted by
project scripts. Receipts record whether the pinned file carries one (`embeddedTextLayer: present |
absent | unknown`); the pinned bytes are never altered to remove it.
13. **Per-asset reuse terms.** Publication is not reuse. A visitor may read anything the site serves;
whether a teacher may take a figure into a handout, or place an instrument embed in a course page,
is a separate determination, recorded on the asset and never inferred from a site-wide default.
   - Every asset a reader can take away records `rights.reuseTerms`: the terms actually recorded for
   that asset. A reviewed figure or source crop records the terms of the work it reproduces; a scan
   or a third-party image records its own stated terms, which may be narrower than the site's
   license; a site-original figure or an instrument embed records the terms the license decision
   supplies.
   - **Instrument embeds** are assets of this kind. The embed route gives each embed an attribution
   footer and a link back (`am-inst-embed-route-rnyg`), and attribution is not a grant: the terms
   under which an embed may be placed elsewhere are recorded here, on the instrument's embed asset
   record, and the embed snippet is offered unchanged beside them.
   - **Before the license decision is recorded** (`am-gov-decision-license-rights-tps`), a
   site-original asset's `rights.reuseTerms` is `pending-decision`, and every surface that shows
   reuse terms names the asset as pending and offers none. It never falls back to `LICENSE`, which
   covers code and new prose only.
   - **An asset whose `publicationDecision` is not `publish`** is described with its locator and its
   recorded terms and is never offered for reuse.
   - **Nothing is relicensed by being listed.** This policy records terms; it never creates them,
   and no surface may widen them. `am-design-sources-about-zumd` renders the recorded terms beside
   its edition-level citation rules, and reads this field rather than restating a site-wide answer.

### Controlled vocabulary

The vocabulary uses the `SourceAsset` field names specified in `am-cm-schemas-source-1en`
(`originUrl`, `acquisitionDate`, `sha256`, `mimeType`, `pageCount`, `pageMapping`, `rights.status`,
`rights.statement`, `rights.source`, `rights.recordedAt`, `publicationDecision`) and adds five
fields that the schema must adopt: `publicationReason`, `cloudProcessing`, `cloudProcessingBasis`,
`rights.credit`, and `rights.reuseTerms`. If the schema's enum values differ (its current draft lists
`local-only` and `withheld`), this policy's values govern and the schema changes to match.

`rights.status` (extend only by editing the policy and its decision log):

| Value | Definition | Required fields |
|---|---|---|
| `public-domain-text` | Historical text whose public-domain basis is recorded | `rights.statement`
(basis: publication date, author's death date, jurisdictions), `rights.recordedAt` |
| `public-domain-image` | A photograph or other image whose public-domain basis is recorded, used
with a credit | `rights.statement` (basis), `rights.source` (archive or catalogue record),
`rights.credit` (archive, photographer where known, date), `rights.recordedAt` |
| `scan-open-terms` | A scan whose stated terms permit reuse and redistribution | `rights.statement`
(verbatim terms), `rights.source` (terms URLs), `originUrl`, `acquisitionDate` |
| `scan-terms-restrict-redistribution` | A scan whose stated terms restrict re-hosting,
redistribution, or commercial use | `rights.statement`, `rights.source`, `originUrl`,
`acquisitionDate` |
| `scan-terms-unknown` | No terms statement found yet | `rights.source` (where terms were sought),
`rights.recordedAt` |
| `site-original-code` | Code written for this site, governed by `LICENSE` | `rights.statement` |
| `site-original-prose` | New prose and the new translation, governed by the license decision |
`rights.statement` |
| `third-party-licensed` | A third-party asset under a named license | `rights.statement` (license
name), `rights.source` (license URL) |
| `in-copyright-witness-only` | Consulted and cited, never copied | `rights.statement` |
| `cleared-image` | An image with a recorded clearance rather than a public-domain basis |
`rights.statement`, `rights.source` (clearance record), `rights.credit` |

`publicationDecision`: `publish` (served from `public/`), `pin-local-only` (pinned bytes retained
outside git and never served), `reference-only` (consulted and cited, never pinned). Every value
other than `publish` requires `publicationReason`.

`cloudProcessing`: `permitted`, `forbidden`, `unknown`. Every value requires `cloudProcessingBasis`
(a verbatim terms excerpt, or a statement that the stated terms place no restriction on processing,
with `rights.recordedAt`).

`rights.reuseTerms`: `pending-decision` (a site-original asset awaiting
`am-gov-decision-license-rights-tps`), `named-license` (reuse under a named license, whose name and
URL are in `rights.statement` and `rights.source`), `source-terms` (reuse governed by the asset's own
stated terms, quoted verbatim in `rights.statement`), or `no-reuse-offered` (the recorded terms do
not support reuse, or the asset is not published). Every value requires `rights.statement`, and
`named-license` also requires `rights.source`.

Constraints (listed in the YAML under `constraints` so the schema can enforce them):
- `scan-terms-restrict-redistribution` implies `publicationDecision` is `pin-local-only` or
`reference-only`.
- `scan-terms-unknown` implies `publicationDecision: reference-only` and `cloudProcessing: unknown`
(not pinned, not published, not sent until resolved).
- `in-copyright-witness-only` implies `reference-only`.
- `publish` requires a status that permits redistribution: `scan-open-terms`, `public-domain-text`,
`public-domain-image`, `site-original-code`, `site-original-prose`, `third-party-licensed` with a
redistribution-permitting license, or `cleared-image`.
- `public-domain-image` and `cleared-image` require a non-empty `rights.credit`, so no image is
displayed without its source credit.
- `cloudProcessing: permitted` is never combined with `scan-terms-unknown`.
- A `publicationDecision` other than `publish` implies `rights.reuseTerms: no-reuse-offered`.
- `site-original-prose` and `site-original-code` assets carry `rights.reuseTerms: pending-decision`
until the license decision is recorded in `docs/DECISIONS.md`, and `named-license` afterwards.
- `rights.reuseTerms: named-license` requires `rights.source`; every value requires
`rights.statement`.

### How to record an asset (checklist in `docs/RIGHTS.md`)

1. Identify the item: institution, host item identifier, file name, and whether the file is the
host's original upload or a derived file that the host may regenerate (prefer originals; derived
files can change bytes later).
2. Record host-published checksums (for example MD5 or SHA-1 in the host's file metadata) and the
retrieval date.
3. Quote every terms statement verbatim with its URL and retrieval date: item page, host-wide terms,
and notices embedded in the file.
4. Classify `rights.status`, `publicationDecision` (with `publicationReason`), and `cloudProcessing`
(with `cloudProcessingBasis`); for an image, write `rights.credit`.
5. Classify `rights.reuseTerms` from the terms just quoted, never from the site's license, and say in
`rights.statement` what a reuser may do. For an instrument embed, record the terms beside the embed
id so the embed snippet and its terms travel together.
6. After pinning: lowercase SHA-256, page count, the parent digest and parent page indices for an
extract, and `embeddedTextLayer` (recorded, never read).
7. State what the classification does not decide: it is an editorial policy, not a legal opinion.
8. Write the record into `docs/provenance/<key>.md` in the receipt format
(`am-src-receipt-format-npo5`).

## Technical Approach

- Write `docs/RIGHTS.md` with numbered sections matching the thirteen policy points, the vocabulary
tables, the constraints, the checklist, and a decision log (date, change, reason, author), whose
first entries are the 2026-09-14 name-and-likeness and photograph decision and this vocabulary's
version 1.
- Write `docs/rights-vocabulary.yaml`: `version`, `rightsStatus[]` (`value`, `definition`,
`requiredFields`, `implies`), `publicationDecision[]` (`value`, `definition`, `requiresReason`),
`cloudProcessing[]` (`value`, `definition`, `requiredFields`), `reuseTerms[]` (`value`, `definition`,
`requiredFields`), `constraints[]` (`id`, `if`, `then`, `message`).
- Add worked classification examples explicitly labeled as illustrations, not determinations about
any real item: a Google-digitized volume whose PDF front page asks for non-commercial use and no
re-hosting (`scan-terms-restrict-redistribution`, `pin-local-only`, `no-reuse-offered`,
`cloudProcessing` decided from the exact wording and escalated as `unknown` if the wording does not
address processing); a university library scan under a public-domain mark with no restrictions
(`scan-open-terms`, `publish`, `source-terms`, `permitted`); an item with no terms found
(`scan-terms-unknown`); an archive portrait whose catalogue records a public-domain status
(`public-domain-image`, `publish`, `source-terms`, with the credit line written out); a
site-original reviewed figure before the license decision (`site-original-prose`, `publish`,
`pending-decision`) and the same figure afterwards (`named-license`); and an instrument embed asset
carrying the embed id, its terms, and the unchanged snippet.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `docs/RIGHTS.md` covers all thirteen policy points above, states that it is an editorial policy
and not a legal opinion, and dates the public-domain statement (as of 2026) with a recheck
instruction.
- [ ] `docs/rights-vocabulary.yaml` exists; every value has a definition, required fields named with
`SourceAsset` field paths, and its implications; the policy tables and the file agree value for
value, including `rights.reuseTerms`.
- [ ] The constraints are listed in both places and each has an identifier and message, including
the image-credit constraint and the three reuse-terms constraints.
- [ ] The checklist exists and names host checksums, original versus derived files, verbatim terms
from every location, `cloudProcessing` with its basis, `rights.credit` for images,
`rights.reuseTerms` classified from the quoted terms, and `embeddedTextLayer`.
- [ ] The policy states that reuse terms are per asset, that attribution is not a grant, that a
non-`publish` asset is never offered for reuse, and that site-original assets read `pending-decision`
until `am-gov-decision-license-rights-tps` is recorded.
- [ ] The policy forbids copying from comparison witnesses and in-copyright translations and defines
the gitignored comparison-work exception.
- [ ] The photograph and likeness sections match the owner's 2026-09-14 decision, with no
reintroduced caveats, and name the required credit fields.
- [ ] The worked examples are marked as illustrations, and include one figure and one instrument
embed with their reuse terms.
- [ ] Voice check: no em dashes and no banned words (`am-edit-voice-lint-trmf` rules), because the
policy is summarized on the public `/sources` page.

## Test Plan

### Unit and integration tests
This bead lands before the application scaffold and ships no executable code. The executable checks
are specified here, delivered by `am-cm-schemas-source-1en`, and may not be weakened there:
- `src/content/schemas/rightsVocabulary.test.ts`: the YAML parses; values are unique kebab-case;
every value has a non-empty definition; every `requiredFields` entry names a real `SourceAsset`
field path; the `SourceAsset` enums for `rights.status`, `publicationDecision`, `cloudProcessing`,
and `rights.reuseTerms` equal the file's value sets exactly; every constraint is enforced by a schema
refinement, each with one valid and one invalid fixture (`scan-terms-restrict-redistribution` with
`publish` fails; `scan-terms-unknown` with `cloudProcessing: permitted` fails; `pin-local-only`
without `publicationReason` fails; `in-copyright-witness-only` with `pin-local-only` fails;
`public-domain-image` without `rights.credit` fails; `pin-local-only` with
`rights.reuseTerms: named-license` fails; `named-license` without `rights.source` fails; a
`rights.reuseTerms` value without `rights.statement` fails; `scan-open-terms` with `publish`,
`source-terms`, and `permitted` passes; `public-domain-image` with a credit, `publish`, and
`source-terms` passes; `site-original-prose` with `publish` and `pending-decision` passes).
- A documentation consistency case in the same file: every vocabulary value and constraint
identifier appears in `docs/RIGHTS.md`, and every value in the policy tables appears in the YAML.
- Until that test exists, this bead's close reason records a manual consistency table: each value,
its definition, its required fields, and the section of `docs/RIGHTS.md` where it appears.

### End-to-end tests
- None directly. `am-design-sources-about-zumd` adds a browser check that the `/sources` page
renders the policy summary without JavaScript, including one image credit and one asset's recorded
reuse terms, and that a `pending-decision` asset is named as pending with no terms offered.

### Structured logging
- The vocabulary test writes JSON lines to
`artifacts/test-logs/rights-vocabulary/<log-run-id>.jsonl` with `timestamp`, `suite:
"rights-vocabulary"`, `logRunId`, `testId`, `beadId`, `value`, `field`, `constraintId`, `check`,
`reuseTerms`, `publicationDecision`, `expected`, `actual`, `outcome`, and `message`. A failing case
retains the offending fixture and the parsed vocabulary under
`artifacts/test-logs/rights-vocabulary/<log-run-id>/evidence/`.

## Considerations and Pitfalls

- The US public-domain cutoff moves every January; phrase it as "as of 2026" and keep the recheck
instruction.
- Whole-issue and whole-volume scans contain other authors' articles; the text is public domain, but
the scan's terms still govern the file. A single whole-volume parent scan that supplies several
papers carries one set of terms for all its extracts.
- Wikisource transcriptions carry community licensing for their editorial layer; they stay
comparison witnesses only.
- Do not let the policy drift into legal advice. It records conservative editorial choices and the
evidence behind each asset decision. Do not conclude that stated terms are unenforceable on the
strength of legal doctrines about reproductions of public-domain works; record the terms and follow
the conservative choice.
- A photograph's public-domain status and the terms of the particular scan of it are two different
questions, exactly as for the papers; record both.
- A host's work-level copyright flag, catalog record, or possession of a file is not a license for
the scan.
- Derived files can be regenerated by the host and change bytes; prefer original uploads and record
host checksums so a later restore can prove byte identity.
- A `cloudProcessing: unknown` determination pauses OCR for that scan until the user decides; it is
never silently treated as permitted.
- Reuse terms are per asset because the rights layers are per asset. A single site-wide reuse
statement would be the exact error this policy exists to prevent: the code license never implies
rights to an embedded scan, dataset, translation, or font.
- Attribution and permission are different things. An embed's footer credits the site; it does not
say what a reuser may do, and only the recorded terms do.
- Publication and reuse are different determinations. An asset can be served to readers and still
carry no reuse offer, and saying so plainly is more useful than an encouraging default.

## Dependencies

Blocked by:
- `am-gov-repo-bootstrap-p5t`: the repository, license, and documentation layout must exist.

Unblocks:
- `am-src-download-script-15ar`, `am-src-facsimile-light-quanta-t4n`,
`am-src-facsimile-brownian-mox`, `am-src-facsimile-relativity-kav`,
`am-src-facsimile-mass-energy-cat`, `am-src-facsimile-dissertation-2mp`: acquisitions record rights
with this vocabulary.
- `am-src-scan-survey-sqnu`: candidate classifications are proposed in this vocabulary.
- `am-src-receipt-format-npo5`: the receipt's rights fields, enums, and constraint checks are built
from `docs/rights-vocabulary.yaml`.
- `am-src-ocr-orchestrator-u1e0`: the `cloudProcessing` refusal reads this vocabulary.
`am-src-ocr-dispatch-interface-m1ur` cites it, but its request to the user does not need to wait for
it.
- `am-cm-schemas-source-1en`: the `SourceAsset` enums and constraints, including `rights.reuseTerms`.
- `am-data-perrin-1909-p7ku`, `am-data-bancelin-1911-94um`, `am-data-millikan-1916-zh2q`,

title: Survey candidate scans, stated terms, and bibliographic identities for the four papers before pinning
description:
# Survey candidate scans, stated terms, and bibliographic identities for the four papers before
pinning

**Epic:** `am-ep-sources-zbs` · **Batch:** A (starts as soon as the rights policy lands; needs no
application code) · **Priority:** P0 · **Plan sections:** §3.1, §4.1, §4.2, §4.3, §19.1
(traceability only)

## Background

Pinning a facsimile needs `scripts/download-facsimiles.ts` (`am-src-download-script-15ar`), which
waits for the application scaffold, which waits for the donor audit and the stack-version decision.
Most of the work behind a good pin needs no code: finding which libraries hold scans of *Annalen der
Physik* volumes 17 and 18 (1905), reading and quoting their terms, telling original uploads from
regenerated derived files, locating each article inside a whole-volume or whole-issue scan, checking
that the mathematics is legible on the pages the transcription depends on, verifying identifiers and
dates, and locating comparison witnesses. This bead does that research in parallel with the scaffold
chain, so that when the download script lands each `src-facsimile-*` bead pins a known, classified
candidate instead of starting its search.

Leads already visible on 2026-09-14 (unevaluated; every one must be verified):
- German Wikisource's Einstein author page links papers 1 and 2 to the Internet Archive item
`annalenderphysi108unkngoog` and paper 4 to `annalenderphysi143unkngoog`. The archive's metadata
describes both as Google-digitized volumes from an unnamed library (collection `americana`), each
with an original "Image Container PDF" of about 29 MB and 36 MB and about 1,181 and 1,254 page
images, plus a larger derived text PDF that the host regenerated years after upload. The metadata
carries a work-level flag `NOT_IN_COPYRIGHT`, which is not a license for the scan.
- The relativity paper's Wikisource transcription (index file `Einstein-Elektrodynamik.djvu` on
Commons) cites the microfilm-derived Internet Archive item `sim_annalen-der-physik_1905_17_5`. The
archive also lists `sim_annalen-der-physik_1905_17_1` to `_5`, `sim_annalen-der-physik_1905_18_1` to
`_5`, and table-of-contents items. Their metadata names the journal's present-day commercial
publisher, which neither makes them publisher PDFs nor establishes open terms. Their "issue" labels
are microfilm segments: Wiley records the relativity paper in issue 10, not 5.
- As of that date German Wikisource had a transcription only for the relativity paper; the other
three papers were listed with scan links only.
- Crossref records (checked 2026-09-14) are in requirement 6, including a correction: the plan
attributes the reissue DOI `10.1002/andp.200590007` to paper 4, but Crossref records it as the 2005
reissue of paper 1.

## Scope

In scope:
- One survey record per paper: `docs/provenance/survey/ap-17-132.md`, `ap-17-549.md`,
`ap-17-891.md`, `ap-18-639.md`, each with YAML front matter and Markdown sections.
- Candidate discovery across the Internet Archive, HathiTrust full view, and at least one national
or university digital library, with searches that found nothing recorded as well.
- Verbatim terms capture and a proposed classification in the vocabulary of
`am-src-rights-policy-1dp`.
- Legibility checks of named pages by visual inspection.
- Identity verification that needs no pinned file, and witness location.
- A recommendation and fallback per paper, with a candidate block ready to paste into
`scripts/sources/facsimile-sources/<key>.yaml`.
- Leads for volumes 19 (1906) and 34 (1911) noticed along the way, recorded without evaluation in
`docs/provenance/survey/companion-leads.md`. This is not companion work and binds nothing.

Out of scope: downloading into the repository or pinning (`src-facsimile-*` beads with the download
script); writing receipts (`src-facsimile-*` beads); final rights determinations (recorded by the
facsimile beads; `unknown` goes to the user); OCR of any kind; the dissertation facsimile
(`am-src-facsimile-dissertation-2mp`).

## Requirements

1. **Coverage of hosts.** Search the Internet Archive (Google-digitized volume items and microfilm
items), HathiTrust (full-view volumes and their rights codes), and at least one national or
university digital library. For every search, record the query, the host, the date, and the result,
including "no candidate found".
2. **Per-candidate record.** Institution; host item identifier; item page URL; downloadable file
names, each marked as an original upload or a derived file; host-published checksums (MD5, SHA-1)
and sizes where listed; page or image count; kind (`whole-volume`, `whole-issue`, `article`); where
the article's first and last printed pages fall, as host viewer page numbers and, where a scratch
inspection copy was taken, as PDF page indices; whether a Google usage-notice page or other front
matter precedes the volume; scan character (bitonal microfilm, grayscale, or color); and whether the
file carries an embedded text layer, recorded as a fact from the host's file description or from the
presence of font resources in a scratch inspection copy. The layer's content is never read, copied,
or quoted (`am-src-rights-policy-1dp`, policy point 12); it is recorded because it tells the OCR
beads that a third-party machine transcription exists and must be ignored.
3. **Terms, verbatim.** Quote every terms statement with URL and retrieval date: rights and license
fields on the item page, the host's general terms, and notices embedded in the file (for example the
first page of a Google-digitized PDF, read by eye from the rendered page and typed; no OCR tool).
Record work-level copyright flags separately and label them as not being licenses. If no terms are
found, write `termsNotFound` with every location searched.
4. **Proposed classification** per candidate, marked "proposed": `rights.status`,
`publicationDecision` with `publicationReason`, and `cloudProcessing` with `cloudProcessingBasis`.
List every `unknown` as a question for the user.
5. **Legibility check** by visual inspection of the host viewer or of pages rendered from a scratch
inspection copy (no OCR, no text-layer reading). Grade each named page `legible`, `partly legible`
(naming the glyphs at risk), or `illegible`:
   - `ap-17-132`: the §2 page with Planck's constants (exponents of $\alpha$ and $\beta$), the §8
   photoelectric page, and the date-line page.
   - `ap-17-549`: the §4 page with $\varphi(\Delta)$ and the integration limits, the §5 page with
   the printed numbers ($k$, $N$, about 0.8 μ, about 6 μ), and the date-line page.
   - `ap-17-891`: the §3 transformation pages (primes, $\xi, \eta, \zeta, \tau$), the §6
   field-component pages, the §8 light-energy pages, the §10 pages with the electron mass $\mu$ and
   its exponents, and the final page with the acknowledgment and date-line.
   - `ap-18-639`: all three pages.
6. **Identity verification** (no pinned file needed). Confirm against Crossref and the publisher
landing page, record the check date, and never copy these values without confirming them:

   | Key | Canonical DOI | Volume (whole-series) | Issue (Wiley) | Pages | 2005 reissue DOI (Annalen
   517, issue S1) |
   |---|---|---|---|---|---|
   | `ap-17-132` | `10.1002/andp.19053220607` | 17 (322) | 6 | 132–148 | `10.1002/andp.200590007`
   (pp. 164–181) |
   | `ap-17-549` | `10.1002/andp.19053220806` | 17 (322) | 8 | 549–560 | `10.1002/andp.2005517s112`
   (pp. 182–193) |
   | `ap-17-891` | `10.1002/andp.19053221004` | 17 (322) | 10 | 891–921 | `10.1002/andp.2005517s113`
   (pp. 194–224) |
   | `ap-18-639` | `10.1002/andp.19053231314` | 18 (323) | 13 | 639–641 | `10.1002/andp.2005517s114`
   (pp. 225–228) |

   Also record the received and issue-publication dates as given by the Einstein Papers Project (18
   March and 9 June; 11 May and 18 July; 30 June and 26 September; 27 September and 21 November
   1905), the Collected Papers Vol. 2 document numbers (14, 16, 23, 24), and the date-line as
   printed, confirmed visually on the candidate scan. Record the reissue-DOI correction to the
   plan's §3.1 in the paper 1 and paper 4 records.
7. **Witnesses.** The Collected Papers documents by bibliographic identity (not deep links); the
Augsburg facsimile records (identity and URL, witness only, never a candidate; record the host name
exactly, because `am-src-download-script-15ar` keeps it on the candidate-host denylist); German
Wikisource per paper (page title, index file, and revision id, or "no transcription found" with the
date); historical translations with their rights status (Perrett and Jeffery, Cowper, Beck, Arons
and Peppard, as applicable), all witness-only.
8. **Shared parents.** Note which candidates serve several papers (a volume 17 scan serves papers 1,
2, and 3), so one parent pin with one terms statement can supply several extracts.
9. **Recommendation and fallback** per paper, reasoned against the plan's order of preference (a
library or archive scan with open terms; whole-issue context preferred), terms, legibility,
availability of an original file, and size, stating whether the published asset should be an article
extract or an issue extract.
10. **Paste-ready candidates**: a fenced YAML block per paper with the `candidates` entries in the
download script's field names (`url`, `kind`, `institution`, `hostItemId`, `hostFileName`,
`hostFileSource`, `derivativeReason`, `hostChecksums`, `termsStatementUrls`,
`expectedPageCountRange`, `maxBytes`), plus a provisional `articlePages` block (`printedFirst`,
`printedLast`, and `parentPageIndices` when a scratch inspection copy established them) marked
"provisional: confirm on the pinned file", because the facsimile bead must fill that block before
extraction and should not repeat the page-finding work.
11. **Front matter** per survey record: `surveyFormatVersion: 1`, `key`, `surveyedAt`, `searches[]`,
`candidates[]` (each with `observations[]` of `{checkedAt, url, method: GET | HEAD | API | viewer,
httpStatus, finding}`), `identityChecks[]`, `witnesses[]`, `legibility[]`, `recommendation:
{candidateId, fallbackCandidateId, publishedAssetKind, reasoning}`, `openQuestionsForUser[]`.

## Technical Approach

- Use host pages, viewers, and metadata interfaces (for example the Internet Archive metadata
endpoint, HathiTrust catalog records, and the Crossref API). Every scripted request sets the user
agent `OpenAI File Downloader, XaiImageApiFetch/1.0`. Do not write helper scripts into the
repository; any throwaway command lives in the session scratch directory.
- An inspection copy of a candidate file may be downloaded to the session scratch directory only,
never into the repository, and is never treated as pinned. Record its SHA-256 as a survey
observation and compare it with host checksums when listed. Avoid repeated downloads of whole
volumes.
- Inspect pages visually. Never run OCR, never read or copy a host's embedded text layer, and never
copy witness text into the survey.
- Commit only the Markdown survey records.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Four survey records exist with valid front matter and the sections above, plus
`companion-leads.md` marked non-binding.
- [ ] Each record documents the Internet Archive, HathiTrust, and at least one other library search,
including searches with no result.
- [ ] Every candidate has verbatim terms with URLs and dates, or `termsNotFound` with the locations
searched; work-level flags are labeled as not licenses.
- [ ] Every candidate has a proposed classification with its basis, and every `unknown` appears in
`openQuestionsForUser`.
- [ ] The legibility grades for the named pages are recorded, and each candidate records whether an
embedded text layer is present, absent, or unknown.
- [ ] The identity table is confirmed with check dates, and the reissue-DOI correction is recorded.
- [ ] Witness availability is recorded for every paper, including "no transcription found" results,
and the Augsburg host name is recorded for the download script's denylist.
- [ ] Each paper has a recommendation, a fallback, a paste-ready candidates block, and a provisional
`articlePages` block.
- [ ] Nothing was downloaded into the repository, nothing was pinned, no OCR ran, and no text layer
or witness text was copied.

## Test Plan

### Unit and integration tests
- This bead writes no code. The receipt-format bead's checker (`am-src-receipt-format-npo5`,
requirement 7) validates survey front matter in `src/content/provenance/receipt.test.ts`: required
keys present; each candidate has terms or `termsNotFound`; proposed classifications use values from
`docs/rights-vocabulary.yaml` and respect its constraints; the recommendation names existing
candidates; every `unknown` classification appears in `openQuestionsForUser`.
- This bead takes no dependency on that checker, so the research can finish while the scaffold chain
is still building. The survey files are checked in practice by every `src-facsimile-*` bead, each of
which depends on both this bead and `am-src-receipt-format-npo5` and runs `bun
scripts/check-receipts.ts --surveys` before pinning.
- Until that checker exists, the close reason contains a per-paper checklist table covering every
acceptance criterion, with the file path and line for each piece of evidence.

### End-to-end tests
- None in this bead. The `src-facsimile-*` beads pin the recommended candidates, and the download
script's host-checksum verification confirms that the pinned bytes are the surveyed file.

### Structured logging
- Each lookup is recorded in the survey front matter as an `observations[]` or `identityChecks[]`
entry (`checkedAt`, `url`, `method`, `httpStatus`, `finding`). When the receipt checker runs over
survey files it writes JSON lines with `timestamp`, `suite: "provenance-survey"`, `logRunId`, `key`,
`rule`, `severity`, `path`, `outcome`, and `message` to
`artifacts/test-logs/provenance-survey/<log-run-id>.jsonl`.

## Considerations and Pitfalls

- Leads are not decisions. A link on Wikisource or a catalog flag establishes nothing about terms,
completeness, or legibility.
- Host viewer page numbers, PDF page indices, and printed journal pages are three different things;
record which one each number is.
- Microfilm item labels are not journal issues, and "unknown library" provenance on a
Google-digitized item should be noted rather than filled in.
- Derived files are regenerated by hosts; prefer original uploads and record host checksums.
- An embedded text layer is noted, never read. A host's OCR is third-party machine output and is
never a transcription source.
- A Wikisource transcription made from a microfilm scan can inherit that scan's misreadings; it
remains a comparison witness only.
- The survey proposes; the facsimile bead records the determination; the user decides `unknown`
cases.
- Companion leads stay non-binding so the four papers are never delayed by dissertation work.

## Dependencies

Blocked by:
- `am-src-rights-policy-1dp`: the vocabulary used for proposed classifications.

Unblocks:
- `am-src-facsimile-light-quanta-t4n`, `am-src-facsimile-brownian-mox`,
`am-src-facsimile-relativity-kav`, `am-src-facsimile-mass-energy-cat`: each pins the recommended
candidate or records why it chose the fallback.

Related (no edge, on purpose): `am-src-receipt-format-npo5` owns `surveySchema.ts`, which validates
these records. No edge is added in either direction, because the survey research must not wait for
the scaffold chain and the checker must not wait for the research; the facsimile beads depend on
both and are where the two meet.
close_reason: Verified by orchestrator SandyCedar against all 9 acceptance criteria at commit 0f967f7. Evidence: docs/provenance/survey/ contains four records (ap-17-132.md 14428B, ap-17-549.md 13938B, ap-17-891.md 15285B, ap-18-639.md 15273B) plus companion-leads.md, each with valid YAML front matter carrying surveyFormatVersion, key, surveyedAt, searches, candidates, identityChecks, witnesses, legibility, recommendation and openQuestionsForUser. Each record documents Internet Archive and HathiTrust plus two or three further hosts (Gallica, DigiZeitschriften, BHL, German Wikisource, Augsburg). Every candidate carries verbatimTerms quoted in full with termsStatementUrls and check dates, or termsNotFound naming the locations searched; the HathiTrust Google-digitized notice is quoted verbatim. Every candidate carries a proposed classification with basis, using the rights.status vocabulary from docs/rights-vocabulary.yaml, and work-level copyright flags are recorded as distinct from a licence grant for the scan file. Legibility audits, witness availability including denylist and null-index qualifications, per-paper recommendation with fallback, and a Paste-Ready Candidate Block are present in all four. The reissue-DOI correction is recorded in both affected records: the master plan section 3.1 attributed 10.1002/andp.200590007 to paper 4, and Crossref confirms it belongs to paper 1, with 10.1002/andp.2005517s114 the true reissue DOI for paper 4. Negative criterion verified independently: no PDF, JP2, TIFF or archive file entered the repository, public/papers/ does not exist, and no local OCR process ran, which AGENTS.md prohibits absolutely. Three owner decisions are raised in openQuestionsForUser rather than decided by the agent. Delivered by agent DarkSnow.
